# Consistency review — the findings in full

The findings of [the 2026-10-26 consistency review](00-summary.md), numbered as its table numbers them.

### 1. The press release says disembark pack runs three agent passes; the disembark chapter says pack is one deterministic run with no model passes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-460cc04582bff3e5 · ledger: iss-2610262030262031 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:23` — “runs three passes (settled artefacts → targeted chat retrieval → distil/compose/audit)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “Packing is one deterministic Go run. It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes: the synthesis artefacts are written later, by the synthesis sub-verbs, over an already-packed lifeboat.”

The press release describes pack as three passes, including targeted chat retrieval and a distil/compose/audit pass. The disembark chapter says packing dispatches no agents, runs no model passes, and leaves synthesis to later sub-verbs over an already-packed lifeboat. A pack cannot both run a distil/compose/audit pass and run no model passes, so anyone building from the press release would build machinery the surface rules out.

### 2. The press release's embark criterion promises an interview, a brief README and memory/docs/terminology; the embark chapter has no interview and writes only record families and the marker block

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-406b78614bbcb598 · ledger: iss-2610262030276998 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:39` — “the user is presented with the press-release interview as the first interaction, the amended press release becomes the new repo's `.abcd/development/brief/README.md`, and all canonical-location files (specs, ADRs, memory, docs, terminology, principles) land at the locations specified in”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:100` — “Embark is a deterministic Go run: it reads the lifeboat, plans, refuses on any conflict, then writes the record families plus the marker block. No interactive scaffolder and no model sit in the write path.”

The press release's acceptance criterion has embark open with the press-release interview, write the amended press release to `.abcd/development/brief/README.md`, and land memory, docs and terminology. The embark chapter says the run is deterministic, with no interactive scaffolder and no model in the write path, and that it writes the record families plus the marker block. The criterion as written cannot pass against the surface as designed.

### 3. Meta says embark writes the new repo's brief by reversing the mapping; the embark chapter says only the record families land and everything else is never written

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-893a6122bdfde0cb · ledger: iss-2610262030273891 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/00-meta.md:42` — “writes a new repo's brief by walking the brief↔lifeboat mapping in reverse — the amended press release becomes the new repo's initial brief.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:201` — “the five record families land at their canonical locations under the target, the current abcd marker block is re-injected into the target `AGENTS.md` (or nowhere, when the target's setup chose no conventions file), and everything else in the lifeboat informs the report but is never written.”

00-meta's brief/lifeboat contract says embark writes a new repo's brief by walking the mapping in reverse, with the amended press release as the initial brief. The embark chapter's acceptance says only the five record families and the marker block land, and everything else in the lifeboat only informs the report. So the 'one skeleton, used three ways' contract has no embark leg as the surface is written.

### 4. Meta says lifeboat-composer agents produce the skeleton's shape; the disembark chapter says pack dispatches no agents

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-918b2100ea9b1784 · ledger: iss-2610262030285264 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/00-meta.md:41` — “uses this skeleton's *shape* as a target schema for what lifeboat-composer agents must produce.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “Packing is one deterministic Go run. It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”

00-meta says disembark uses the brief skeleton as the target schema for what lifeboat-composer agents must produce. The disembark chapter says pack is one deterministic Go run that dispatches no agents and grounds each brief section from the mapping. Neither the skeleton's sections nor any agent named lifeboat-composer is produced by an agent at pack time.

### 5. Platform says past disembarks are recorded with a label; the voyage-log chapter says the entry carries no label

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-5e172db90c736112 · ledger: iss-2610262030288703 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/01-platform.md:23` — “Past disembarks are recorded as manifests (hash + file list + label) at the operator level, not as preserved snapshots”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:302` — “Not a verdict, a label, or a recipient list.”

The platform page says past disembarks are recorded as manifests with a hash, a file list and a label. The embark chapter's voyage layout says the deliberately minimal entry carries no verdict, no label and no recipient list, and its example entry has counts, not a file list. A reader cannot rely on both field sets.

### 6. Platform says the markdown plugin surface is a later front door; the ahoy chapter describes the slash command already dispatching every sub-verb

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b61f1a105b5163b3 · ledger: iss-2610262030290887 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/01-platform.md:17` — “An **MCP server** and a **markdown plugin surface that shells to the Go binary** are later front doors”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:42` — “The slash command dispatches every sub-verb and mode but the identity check, the write verbs included, and each announces that it writes before it runs.”

The platform page says the MCP server and the markdown plugin surface are later front doors, with the CLI the only one shipping in the MVP. The ahoy chapter says the slash command dispatches every sub-verb and mode except the identity check, so the plugin surface is a working front door now. The two cannot both describe the current state.

### 7. The press release says install writes a marker block in AGENTS.md and the prompt-router hook; the ahoy chapter says a default install writes the block nowhere

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8dac513f145098ee · ledger: iss-2610262030294754 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:25` — “`/abcd:ahoy install` bootstraps abcd in any repo (transparent prompts, visibility-driven gitignore, marker block in AGENTS.md, prompt-router hook).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:1070` — “so the docs target defaults to `skip`: a default install writes it into none of the repository's committed conventions files”

The press release says install bootstraps a marker block in AGENTS.md and the prompt-router hook. The ahoy chapter says the docs target defaults to `skip`, so a default install writes the block into no conventions file, and elsewhere says install only verifies the hook manifest and never writes it. The two disagree on what a default install leaves behind.

### 8. The press release lists `/abcd:run` as in-scope operator wiring; the scope page says it is not built and its intent is superseded

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0fac43cb23fe6cbc · ledger: iss-2610262030301816 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:27` — “plus operator-internal command wiring (e.g. `/abcd:run`, the itd-29 autonomous-run operator surface — read-mostly `status`/`pause`/`resume`/`preflight` over the pluggable autonomous-run seam; not part of the user-facing command set)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:19` — “is not built: itd-29 is superseded (by itd-2609201916151817, planned), and no `run` verb or `commands/run.md` is on any shipped surface.”

The press release's 'What's In Scope' lists `/abcd:run`, the itd-29 operator surface with status/pause/resume/preflight, as operator-internal wiring. The scope page says `/abcd:run` is not built, itd-29 is superseded, and no `run` verb or command page is on any shipped surface. A superseded surface cannot also be part of the plumbing the press release delivers.

### 9. The press release calls bare-shows-status a universal convention; the naming page says conformance is partial and several verbs refuse or act instead

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c053753d683dafb4 · ledger: iss-2610262030301422 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:5` — “Bare invocation of any command shows status + suggested next actions; state-mutating actions require an explicit sub-verb (the universal abcd convention).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:105` — “**Conformance is partial, and the gap is the shipped surface's rather than the discipline's.** Several parents print usage with no state, several verbs refuse or act instead of rendering”

The press release says bare invocation of any command shows status and next actions, and that state-mutating actions require a sub-verb, as the universal abcd convention. The naming page says conformance is partial: several parents print usage with no state, and several verbs refuse or act instead of rendering. Both cannot describe the shipped surface.

### 10. Context's lifeboat diagram shows research/ and audit/ as pass B/C outputs; the disembark chapter says pack runs no model passes and its output shape has no such directories

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-da77b2b302b86740 · ledger: iss-2610262030315625 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/02-context.md:31` — “passes B/C outputs + audits”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”

The context page's pack/unpack diagram, which points to the disembark § 5 output shape as the full version, shows `research/` and `audit/` holding pass B and C outputs and audits. The disembark chapter says pack dispatches no agents and runs no model passes, and its § 5 tree has neither directory. The diagram describes outputs no pass produces.

### 11. Context presents `.abcd/corpus.json` as an existing, seeded validation-corpus list; the naming page says the name is reserved and not yet in the tree

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a3a3697cecc0f7aa · ledger: iss-2610262030315186 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/02-context.md:47` — “**Validation corpus:** user-maintained list in `.abcd/corpus.json`, seeded with:”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:80` — “`corpus.json`, which is reserved here as a name and is not yet in the tree”

The context page, which the platform page names as the canonical validation-corpus source, says the corpus is a user-maintained list in `.abcd/corpus.json`, seeded with three repositories. The naming page says `corpus.json` is only a reserved name and not yet in the tree. A list cannot be seeded in a file that does not exist.

### 12. Context keeps `intent ship` as a design target that drives a spec to completion; the scope page says closing the spec ships the intent and there is no separate ship command

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-440184740afdc1cd · ledger: iss-2610262030322001 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/02-context.md:11` — “`ship` drives that spec to completion (or the full pipeline if from drafts/)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:40` — “closing the spec is what ships the intent, and there is no separate ship command.”

The context page describes an `intent ship` sub-verb that drives the spec to completion, or the full pipeline from drafts/, and keeps it among the remaining design targets. Under the truth rule a design target is decided. The scope page says closing the spec is what ships the intent and there is no separate ship command. The record cannot both plan a ship command and rule one out.

### 13. The mental model describes the capture-kind classifier as operating; the naming register marks it staged with no classifier sub-verb registered

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a3375e88a7a40b71 · ledger: iss-2610262030324496 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:74` — “The capture-time classifier (`intent classify-capture-kind`, itd-44) recognises this signature and emits a fourth **verdict**, `decision`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:184` — “Capture-TIME classifier verdict, produced by the capture-kind classifier the intent surface is designed to gain; no classifier sub-verb is registered today.”

The mental model says, without a staged marker, that the capture-time classifier `intent classify-capture-kind` recognises the signature and emits the `decision` verdict. The naming register marks the capture verdict staged and says no classifier sub-verb is registered today. The truth rule needs a staged claim to say so, and here the two pages give the classifier different statuses.

### 14. The mental model gives Modification Grammar three sub-headings; the tradeoffs page records a four-axis section that includes Ripple

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7386cca5921d40bf · ledger: iss-2610262030331903 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:93` — “every spec carries a `## Modification Grammar` section with three sub-headings (`Extends cleanly` / `Breaks the design` / `Why`)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/03-evidence/04-tradeoffs.md:45` — “a 4-axis `## Modification Grammar` section per spec (`Extends cleanly` / `Breaks the design` / `Why` / `Ripple`)”

The mental model says every spec's `## Modification Grammar` section has three sub-headings: Extends cleanly, Breaks the design and Why. The tradeoffs entry records the choice as a four-axis section with Ripple as the fourth, and the mental model itself cites a `## Modification Grammar > Ripple` sub-bullet elsewhere. A spec author cannot follow both counts.

### 15. The mental model defines a standalone intent as shipping as one spec; invariant 17 makes an intent own one or more specs as the normal state

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4c3eff9d1e1226a9 · ledger: iss-2610262030338994 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:64` — “one press-release-shaped user moment, ships as one spec.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:171` — “More than one spec naming one intent is the normal state and not an ambiguity”

The mental model defines the standalone kind as one user moment that ships as one spec. Invariant 17 says the intent-to-spec relation is 1:n, that more than one spec naming one intent is normal, and that the intent ships when its last spec closes. A standalone intent planned as one spec and finished by a remainder spec breaks the mental model's definition but follows the invariant.

### 16. Invariant 8 puts an Acceptance block on every 'brief phase'; the mental model puts it on the press release and surface chapters, with phases retired

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-451dfed62851cdac · ledger: iss-2610262030341371 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:153` — “Every brief phase has an `## Acceptance` block in the same format.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:85` — “The brief's press release and surface chapters carry an `## Acceptance` block in the same format.”

Invariant 8 says every brief phase has an `## Acceptance` block. The mental model says the brief's press release and surface chapters carry that block, and states that the phase is retired. The invariant uses a retired unit for the home of brief-level acceptance, so the invariant and the model name different homes.

### 17. The launch chapter says the repo organises work by phase per adr-9; the mental model says the phase is retired and adr-9 superseded

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8c0e2d349347a169 · ledger: iss-2610262030345408 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:489` — “the repo organises work by **phase** (see [adr-9] (../../decisions/adrs/0009-phase-as-product-layer.md)), and a release number is what falls out when a stretch of that work is published.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:56` — “The phase and the milestone are retired”

The launch chapter's versioning section says the repo organises work by phase, citing adr-9, and that a release number falls out when a stretch of that work is published. The mental model says the phase and the milestone are retired, and its opening paragraph names adr-9 as superseded. The launch chapter's account of what a version measures rests on a unit the record no longer has.

### 18. The naming register still files commands under 'later phases'; the scope page says the phase is retired as a unit of the record

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-bd01696217220132 · ledger: iss-2610262030354678 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:66` — “**Reserved meta-development commands** (later phases; named now to prevent collisions)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:30` — “retired the phase and the milestone as units of the record”

The naming register heads its reserved commands 'later phases' and tags dredge, loot and audit as 'a later phase'. The scope page says adr-2609212115255771 retired the phase and the milestone as units of the record. The register uses a retired term as a live scheduling bucket.

### 19. The constraints index calls the invariants page a placeholder pointer; the page calls itself the canonical register

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b6dc35cfd23f2d0b · ledger: iss-2610262030354870 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/README.md:12` — “Navigational pointer to invariant-shaped rules scattered across the brief (placeholder)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:3` — “This file is the canonical home for the project's invariants”

The constraints README describes `03-invariants.md` as a navigational pointer to invariant-shaped rules scattered across the brief, and marks it a placeholder. The page itself is marked LIVE and says it is the canonical home for the project's invariants, with the other locations as cross-references and not the register. A reader following the index is sent away from the authority.

### 20. The evidence index says every file in the chapter is live; the tradeoffs page is marked PARTIAL

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-f85189e46ebe0d83 · ledger: iss-2610262030357877 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/03-evidence/README.md:4` — “Every file is live — evidence is recorded as it accrues”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/03-evidence/04-tradeoffs.md:3` — “**Status: PARTIAL.** Tradeoff-shaped content (decisions made + alternatives weighed, with rationale) accumulates here as the project progresses.”

The evidence chapter's README says every file is live and records evidence as it accrues. The tradeoffs file opens with a PARTIAL status, and its sibling pages are marked LIVE. The index and the page give two statuses for the same file.

### 21. Dependencies says abcd stamps `schema_version: 1` everywhere; the voyage log's documented entry carries `schema_version` 2

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5c308a125dd502a9 · ledger: iss-2610262030364518 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/02-dependencies.md:95` — “abcd stamps `schema_version: 1` everywhere”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:288` — “"schema_version": 2,”

The dependencies page says abcd stamps `schema_version: 1` everywhere, with migrators added only if a later intent changes the shape. The embark chapter documents the voyage log entry with `schema_version` 2. A shape has already moved past version 1 without the migration stance being updated.

### 22. The naming register defines `managed-repo` as needing `.git/` and accepting an in-tree `.abcd/`; the ahoy chapter rejects both

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4142a6ea8b0943cc · ledger: iss-2610262030363874 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:223` — “Folder kind: a git repo abcd already manages — has an ABCD marker block (or an in-tree `.abcd/`, or an `index.json` entry) and a `.git/` directory.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:568` — “An in-tree `.abcd/` directory is recorded as a signal and reported, but it does not make a folder managed on its own (iss-88): a directory holding nothing but `.abcd/` reports as `unmanaged-folder`. A `.git/` directory means the folder is *a* repo, not that it is *managed*, and a folder carrying a marker block is treated as a managed repo whether or not it is a git checkout at all.”

The reserved-vocabulary row defines `managed-repo` as a git repo with a marker block, an in-tree `.abcd/` or an index entry, and a `.git/` directory. The ahoy chapter, which the row cites as its source, says an in-tree `.abcd/` alone does not make a folder managed, and that a folder with a marker block is managed whether or not it is a git checkout. The register's definition disagrees with the classifier it points to.

### 23. Invariant 3 says every capability is reachable with no plugin host; ahoy says preparing a repository runs only as a host-agent workflow the CLI cannot yet do

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ebd9a9be1defd02f · ledger: iss-2610262030375215 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:13` — “every capability is reachable with no plugin host present”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:275` — “The workflow is an **interim bridge**. abcd cannot yet manage repositories directly, so the page does by hand what the CLI will later take over”

Invariant 3 says every capability is reachable with no plugin host present. The ahoy chapter says abcd cannot yet manage repositories directly, so the preparation workflow (audit, gap report, adoption) runs by hand in the host agent until the CLI takes it over. The repository preparation is a capability with no host-free route, which is the case the invariant forbids.

### 24. The scope page says closing the spec ships the intent; invariant 17 says closing a spec never ships an intent that still has an open spec

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d55da1d9657fad74 · ledger: iss-2610262030374385 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:40` — “It reaches `shipped/` when its linked spec is closed: closing the spec is what ships the intent”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:171` — “closing a spec never ships an intent that still has an open spec”

The scope page says an intent reaches `shipped/` when its linked spec closes, and that closing the spec is what ships it. Invariant 17 says an intent can own several specs, that closing one never ships an intent with another open spec, and that the intent moves only after its last spec closes. The scope page's single-spec rule gives the wrong result for the partial-delivery case.

### 25. The mental model calls the Now / Next / Later status block a planned intent; the scope page says the bare `/abcd` board renders it

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e61cfb0d8aaf58c5 · ledger: iss-2610262030385476 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:3` — “the status block that renders it is itd-2609212103568351, planned”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:3` — “the bare `/abcd` board renders it as the Now / Next / Later block”

The mental model says the status block that renders Now / Next / Later is itd-2609212103568351, which is planned. The scope page says, in the present tense, that the bare `/abcd` board renders the Now / Next / Later block and places each intent in it. One page treats the render as not yet built and the other as current.

### 26. Dependencies names RepoPrompt and codex as oracle adapters; ahoy says host-delegated is the only oracle answer with an adapter

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a63dad9c3cb77366 · ledger: iss-2610262030388384 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/02-dependencies.md:34` — “RepoPrompt and codex are two such adapters; a **direct API oracle is a legitimate adapter** too.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:893` — “The oracle backend is not asked while host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter”

The dependencies page says RepoPrompt and codex are two of the opt-in oracle adapters behind the seam. The ahoy chapter says the oracle backend question is not asked because host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter, and every other answer is recorded without changing how reviews run. Both cannot describe which oracle adapters exist.

### 27. Meta's truth rule bans aspirational maybes from the brief; the press release's open questions carry one outside the registered question homes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-d8712271d2a7c944 · ledger: iss-2610262030391056 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/00-meta.md:9` — “the brief records no proposals, no alternatives still under consideration, no aspirational maybes.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:51` — “A future intent (likely paired with itd-15 self-dogfooded SOTA audit) may quantify it.”

00-meta says the brief records no proposals and no aspirational maybes, and keeps unsettled questions in `03-open-questions.md` or in inline `Open question (adr-35)` notes. The press release carries its own Open Questions section, which neither registers, and it ends on a maybe about a future intent. Under the truth rule that passage has no legitimate home.

### 28. Invariant 18 says surface-chapter prose states no flag the tree registers; the launch chapter's prose names its `dry-run` flag outright

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-704b6b5a7c24d0b7 · ledger: iss-2610262030398252 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:173` — “The prose above the appendix states no flag the tree registers and no sub-verb written as an invocation”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:257` — “**The preview is spelled `dry-run`, and it is a flag, not a sub-verb.**”

Invariant 18 says the prose above a surface chapter's generated appendix states no flag the command tree registers. The launch chapter's prose names the preview's flag directly as `dry-run` and goes on to describe it. The appendix registers that flag, so the chapter's prose states a shape claim the invariant reserves for the appendix.

### 29. The scope page derives build order from dependencies and shelves; the intent chapter names the phase plan as the canonical build order

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-53eeab88b62911ca · ledger: iss-2610262030409180 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:3` — “order comes from each record's dependencies (`blocked_by`, `builds_on`) and its shelf”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:74` — “ID number is *not* an execution-order guarantee — the canonical build order is the phase plan at”

04-scope says order comes from each record's blocked_by/builds_on edges and its shelf, with the phase documents kept only as history, while 05-intent (twice, in Intent IDs and Lifecycle) says the canonical build order is the phase plan under roadmap/phases/. Both cannot be the source of sequence.

### 30. Phases are history on the scope page, yet the intent chapter defines planned/ as scoped into a roadmap phase

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8df5867543c6ec90 · ledger: iss-2610262030401652 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:3` — “The phase documents under `roadmap/phases/` are history.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:12` — “a committed capability, scoped into a roadmap phase and awaiting its Go build”

04-scope states the phase documents under roadmap/phases/ are history (the phase was retired), while 05-intent defines a planned/ intent as one scoped into a roadmap phase whose spec_id is set once the spec layer schedules it in Phase 4, although its own plan step mints the spec at planning. A planned intent cannot be scoped into a unit the record has retired.

### 31. Invariant 17 makes the intent-to-spec relation 1:n; the intent chapter's kinds table maps a standalone intent to one spec (1:1)

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a5143d198ac1dfdc · ledger: iss-2610262030410509 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:171` — “the intent↔spec relation is 1:n: an intent that has been thought through stands as written”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:83` — “One spec (1:1) | itd-3, itd-4, itd-7, most of the corpus”

03-invariants holds that an intent owns one or more specs and ships when its last one closes, while the kinds table in 05-intent states a standalone intent maps to one spec, 1:1. A standalone intent with a remainder spec is legal under the invariant and excluded by the table.

### 32. Invariant 8 requires every intent's press release to carry Acceptance Criteria; the intent chapter says a bench draft may carry none

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5eb0022c36a85741 · ledger: iss-2610262030417187 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:506` — “a draft still on the bench may carry none”

03-invariants lists, as a non-negotiable invariant, that every intent's press release is followed by a Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria block, while 05-intent records as accepted convention that a draft on the bench may carry none, and counts four drafts doing so. A draft with a press release and no criteria violates the invariant yet is admitted by the chapter.

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:335` — “any move into disciplines/, a planned member leaving its bundle's shared spec”

Following the mental model, every shipped route refuses.

### 34. The mental model presents a capture-time classifier that emits the decision verdict; the intent chapter says nothing of it exists or reads the field

03-mental-model states in present tense, with no staged marker, that the capture-time classifier (intent classify-capture-kind, itd-44) recognises a standing choice and emits decision, which plan_single/reclassify refuse. 05-intent says this is a later phase: nothing enforces it, the create seeds suggested_kind null, and no shipped code reads the field.

### 60. The naming register marks the PRD-freeze vocabulary as machinery abcd neither ships nor plans; the intent chapter specifies it as a later-phase plan front end

04-naming marks frozen_content_hash, planning_attempt_id, prd_grandfathered and the planning-attempt modes as predecessor vocabulary for machinery abcd neither ships nor plans, while 05-intent sets out a later-phase PRD-validating and freezing front end for plan that computes frozen_content_hash and writes planning_attempt_id. The same machinery cannot be both unplanned and a later phase.

### 61. The mental model says the intent for the Now / Next / Later status block is still planned; the site chapter describes the status page and the bare board rendering that block as shipped behaviour.

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/22-site.md:111` — “It opens with the Now / Next / Later block the bare `abcd` board carries”

03-mental-model says the status block that renders Now / Next / Later is itd-2609212103568351 and that this intent is planned, meaning not yet delivered. 22-site describes the shipped status page as opening with the Now / Next / Later block the bare `abcd` board carries, rendered from the same read. A reader cannot tell from these two pages whether the block exists, so one of the two lifecycle claims is wrong.

### 62. The mental model calls the itd-60 doc-fidelity loop planned and not yet exercised; the docs chapter describes the itd-60 doc-fidelity gate as a working gate in the present tense.

The doc-fidelity half cannot be both planned and never exercised and also a gate that runs today.

### 63. The mental model says the brief's surface chapters carry an `## Acceptance` block in Given-When-Then format; the identity chapter has no such block and names an issue as its acceptance corpus instead.

Its sections run from Sub-verbs to References, and its only statement of acceptance is a sentence naming iss-143 as its acceptance corpus. None of the twelve surface chapters in this set carries the block either, so the mental model's claim does not hold for them.

### 64. The naming register calls `~/.abcd.noindex/history/` the history store's registry; the history chapter says that directory is ahoy's registry, holds no transcripts, and that the history store lives under `~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/`.

04-naming registers `index.json` as the 'History-store registry at `~/.abcd.noindex/history/index.json`', and its voyage row keys records 'like the history store', so in that page 'history store' names the `history/` directory. 11-history defines the store the `history` verb serves as `~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/<root-sha>/records/`, and says ahoy's registry stays under `~/.abcd.noindex/history/` and holds no transcripts. The one name 'history store' points at two different directories with different contents.

### 65. Invariant 2 says a missing or misbehaving adapter falls back to the native path and abcd never blocks; the reading chapter says a cold-reading dispatch whose provider cannot be reached exits 2 with nothing ingested.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6bc27210b8f9e9f8 · ledger: iss-2610262030564496 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:11` — “A missing or misbehaving adapter degrades to the native path; abcd never blocks on an absent tool.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:377` — “a provider that could not be reached, a run id outside the run-id grammar, a run no assembly parked, and a dispatch that also names an output each exit 2 with nothing ingested.”

03-invariants makes fallback non-negotiable: a missing or misbehaving adapter degrades to the native path, and abcd never blocks on an absent tool. 23-reading routes a position to a provider, which is an opt-in oracle adapter. When that provider could not be reached, the dispatch exits 2 with nothing ingested instead of falling back to the host-delegated harness, and only an explicit `host-decides` override keeps the run on the harness. An unreachable configured provider therefore blocks the reading instead of degrading.

### 66. The mental model gives ADR files the shape `adr-N-<slug>.md`; the decide chapter says an ADR's filename is its stamp followed by its slug.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-bc38578767a69419 · ledger: iss-2610262030578776 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:74` — “routes capture to the existing **ADR store** (`.abcd/development/decisions/adrs/`, `adr-N-<slug>.md`)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/24-decide.md:134` — “The filename is the stamp followed by the slug”

03-mental-model names the ADR store's files `adr-N-<slug>.md`. 24-decide describes the store's minting verb and says the filename is the stamp followed by the slug. It also says the ordinals `0001`–`0058` keep their filenames, so no ADR file carries an `adr-` prefix. A reader looking up an ADR by the mental model's pattern would find no file.

### 67. Invariant 4 says all inter-agent data is JSON and markdown is only a render step; the history chapter's reconstruct artefact is Markdown precisely because a model reads it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-97d08d265a8dd54b · ledger: iss-2610262030576576 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:15` — “all inter-agent data is JSON; markdown is a render step”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:149` — “The artefact is Markdown because its consumer is a model being handed the session as context”

03-invariants says all inter-agent data is JSON and markdown is a render step. 11-history says reconstruct writes one self-contained Markdown artefact as its primary output, and that it is Markdown because its consumer is a model being handed the session as context. Only the telemetry file beside it is JSON. A Markdown document designed as a model's input is inter-agent data that is not JSON, so the invariant's 'all' does not hold.

### 68. The reserved-vocabulary register fixes review verdicts as SHIP / NEEDS_WORK / MAJOR_RETHINK; the docs chapter's saved docs review returns PROMOTE, HOLD or INCONCLUSIVE, which the register does not hold.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-3abc0592b519dd23 · ledger: iss-2610262030580466 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:78` — “A receipt for HEAD that is PROMOTE lets the change proceed.”

04-naming registers review verdicts as the closed enum {SHIP, NEEDS_WORK, MAJOR_RETHINK}, and requires every new term to be registered. 10-docs describes layer 2 of the doc-fidelity gate as a host-delegated docs review whose receipt reads PROMOTE, HOLD or INCONCLUSIVE. A second, unregistered set of review verdicts is in use beside the registered one, so 'review verdict' now names two different closed sets.

### 69. The meta page says unsettled questions are recorded only as registered open questions or as explicit `Open question` notes; the reading chapter carries an owed product-thinker ruling inline, in neither form.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-5c08b09ce7807c77 · ledger: iss-2610262030587661 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/00-meta.md:12` — “Unsettled questions are recorded *as questions*, never as claims — registered in”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:74` — “That is a reading of the rule rather than the rule itself, and the product thinker's ruling on it is owed.”

00-meta's truth rule says the brief records an unsettled question only in 03-open-questions.md or as an explicit `Open question (adr-35)` note. 23-reading says its reach for the comparative run is a reading of the rule rather than the rule itself, and that the product thinker's ruling on it is owed. That is an unsettled question, but it carries no Open question note and is not in the open-questions page. The brief's own record of its unsettled questions is therefore incomplete.

### 70. The reserved review-verdict enum is SHIP/NEEDS_WORK/MAJOR_RETHINK, but the build loop parses SHIP/FIX FIRST and APPROVE/BLOCK/NEEDS-INPUT as review verdicts

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dd270d0d74d01e65 · ledger: iss-2610262030597155 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:187` — “Review verdicts ∈ `{SHIP, NEEDS_WORK, MAJOR_RETHINK}` | Carmack-style review verdicts”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:696` — “stating one verdict of its role (`SHIP` or `FIX FIRST`; `APPROVE`, `BLOCK` or `NEEDS-INPUT`)”

The naming register lists review verdicts as a controlled enum of exactly SHIP, NEEDS_WORK and MAJOR_RETHINK. The build chapter has the loop read each reviewer's one verdict as SHIP or FIX FIRST (and APPROVE, BLOCK or NEEDS-INPUT), tokens the register does not hold. Either the enum is not the closed list of review verdicts, or the loop parses verdicts outside it. A builder working from the register would reject the loop's tokens.

### 71. The mental model calls per-step lanes planned (itd-2609212103565953), while the build chapter describes one lane per spec step as shipped behaviour

The build chapter says it describes the part of the loop that ships, and states as present behaviour that each spec step lands as one lane, citing the same intent's criterion 4 in the brief it renders. The brief's truth rule allows only shipped or explicitly staged claims, so these two documents disagree about whether per-step lanes exist.

### 72. Invariant 19 lists every record filed before the remedy field as ineligible, but the drain reads such a record's suggested_fix as its remedy

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-adfb28697068a717 · ledger: iss-2610262031008610 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:175` — “a record filed before that carries none and is listed as ineligible”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:75` — “record written before the field existed reads its `suggested_fix:` as its remedy”

Invariant 19 states that a record filed before remedies were required carries none and is listed as ineligible. The drain chapter says such a record reads its suggested_fix: as its remedy, so a legacy record that has one can pass the remedy clause and be taken by a machine. The invariant's fixed disposition and the drain's fallback disagree about what happens to the same records.

### 73. /abcd:memory names the itd-36 curated memory substrate with ingest/ask/lint in the tradeoffs record, and a separate memory-notes store with add/list/remove in the memory chapter

### 74. The naming rule forbids `<verb> show` at design time, but the inbox chapter ships a show sub-verb and does not mark it as a gap

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-77c1a868d2dff291 · ledger: iss-2610262031019028 (filed)

The naming convention forbids `<verb> show` at design time instead of leaving it to review. The inbox chapter, designed after the rule, ships `show` as a sub-verb that renders one report by its id. Unlike the memory chapter, which marks its `list` as a gap against the rule, it presents `show` as conforming. The prohibition and the shipped name cannot both hold.

### 75. The dependencies page says abcd needs no external tools beyond the planned runner fence, yet the dashboard verb refuses to start without Tailscale running

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bf8174e3f8051c97 · ledger: iss-2610262031014454 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/36-dashboard.md:96` — “Start refuses outside a checkout abcd manages, when a dashboard already runs on this computer, when Tailscale is not running”

The dependencies constraint says abcd has no required external tools, any present tool being an upgrade and never a prerequisite. The only exception it names is the runner route's fence. The dashboard chapter refuses start when Tailscale is not running or is too old, and the verb has no native path without it. So the dashboard route needs an external program the dependencies page says no route needs.

### 76. Invariant 3 says every capability is reachable with no plugin host present, but the build chapter says a host session always drives the loop and the no-host path is not built

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-92a73d279f95be8f · ledger: iss-2610262031016592 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:13` — “every capability is reachable with no plugin host present”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:537` — “A host session always drives this: the no-host path, where a host-routed role goes to the machine's `runner.fallback_host`, is the process driver's reversal of the host-delegated boundary, and waits on the ADR decision 6 of the intent owes.”

Invariant 3 is a non-negotiable rule: every capability is reachable from the CLI with no plugin host present. The build chapter says a host session always drives the loop, and that the no-host path, where host-routed roles fall to a machine runner, waits on an unwritten ADR. So the build capability, as described, cannot be reached without a host, which the invariant rules out.

### 77. The press release states as universal that a bare command shows status and mutations need a sub-verb, but bare `abcd drain` performs a mutating move

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-57dbeea3097095ba · ledger: iss-2610262031021492 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:5` — “Bare invocation of any command shows status + suggested next actions; state-mutating actions require an explicit sub-verb (the universal abcd convention).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:186` — “each invocation of the bare verb performs one move and exits”

The press release calls it the universal abcd convention that bare invocation of any command shows status and suggested next actions, and that state-mutating actions require an explicit sub-verb. The drain chapter has no sub-verbs. Each bare invocation performs one move: it fetches, reserves on origin, asks judgements and opens lanes. A command whose bare form mutates local and remote state breaks the convention the press release calls universal.

### 78. The press release says bare invocation only shows status, but bare `abcd report` opens an editor and files a report into the inbox

The press release says bare invocation of any command shows status and that state-mutating actions need an explicit sub-verb. The report chapter registers no sub-verb, and its bare form opens the skeleton in an editor and files what is saved into the machine inbox, a state-mutating act with no sub-verb. The two documents disagree on what a bare command may do.

### 79. The register reserves 'claim' vocabulary for itd-33's later-phase coordination unit, while the implement chapter ships a different 'claim' as its unit of exclusion

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f8147f2670d14b85 · ledger: iss-2610262031035884 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:202` — “`claim.status` ∈ `{active, paused, released}` | Three-state claim lifecycle”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:5` — “makes a record the unit of exclusion between them with a claim”

The naming register reserves claim vocabulary for itd-33, a later phase: a three-state claim.status (active, paused, released) beside take/yield/escalate primitives and a work_item claim unit. The register exists so that a name is not re-minted with a different meaning. The implement chapter ships a 'claim' on a record, with a lease, lapse and release and no paused state or those primitives, as the unit of exclusion between sessions. One name now covers two different coordination concepts.

### 80. The meta page says the brief/lifeboat skeleton is the one canonical shape, but the lab chapter calls an intention/method/candidates layout 'the lifeboat's section shape'

### 81. The scope page says blocked_by and builds_on decide when a lane can take an intent, but the build's checks read only blocked_by

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:70` — “nothing the record names in `blocked_by` is unsettled”

The build chapter creates no run until every check passes, and its dependency check reads only blocked_by. No check and no part of the pick's scoring reads builds_on. Under the build chapter, builds_on decides nothing about when a lane takes an intent.

### 82. The mental model defines a step as one of a spec's ordered pieces, while the implement chapter also uses 'step' for the landing's sub-stages

So 'step' carries a sense the defining document does not give it.

### 83. The press release says every state-mutating action needs an explicit sub-verb, but bare `abcd land` pushes and queues with no sub-verb

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-land.md:27` — “The verb takes at most one operand, the branch, and lands the checkout's current branch without one.”

The land chapter says the verb takes at most one operand and, given none, lands the checkout's current branch. So bare `abcd land` runs the gate, pushes the branch to origin and arms its pull request. Either the convention is not universal or the land surface breaks it. A person who trusts the press release would run bare `abcd land` expecting a status render.

### 84. The press release puts `/abcd:run` operator-internal wiring in scope, but the surfaces index lists every registered verb and `run` is not among them

### 85. The press release says `disembark pack` runs three passes, chat retrieval among them, but the agent catalog says the pass A/B/C agents are unbuilt design targets

### 87. The press release's acceptance has capture write an issue file, but universal patterns calls capture (and intent and spec) a read-only render

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-aba87e37c6230e40 · ledger: iss-2610262031062811 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:43` — “a structured issue at `.abcd/work/issues/open/iss-N-<slug>.md` exists with frontmatter populated and source provenance recorded”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:90` — “`capture`, `intent`, `guard`, `--version`, `rules`, `spec`, `identity` and `banlist` are read-only renders”

The press release's acceptance criterion says `/abcd:capture "<text>"` leaves a structured issue file under `.abcd/work/issues/open/`. Universal patterns lists `capture`, `intent` and `spec` with `lint`, `guard` and `banlist` as read-only renders. A verb that writes a record into the ledger is not a read-only render.

### 88. The context page calls the library's curated pages a 'memory store', but the surfaces index gives the name memory to the notes command only

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2592e631a03ee510 · ledger: iss-2610262031070645 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/02-context.md:13` — “curate a queryable memory store (`ingest` external sources / `ask` queries / `lint` health-checks)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:494` — “That merge freed the name `memory`, which now belongs to the notes command”

The context page describes `/abcd:library` as curating a queryable memory store, with ingest/ask/lint over specs, ADRs, reviews and memory. The surfaces index says the library merge freed the name `memory`, which now belongs to the notes command. Its library-versus-memory table puts the cited notes drawn from sources in the library and short agent lessons in memory, and it says the two are not one store with two names. So 'memory store' means the library's curated pages on one page and the notes store on the other.

### 89. The mental model gives intent-auditor a discipline role that checks every spec, but the agent catalog lists three roles and none of them is a discipline role

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c6b5f1fa00b592de · ledger: iss-2610262031074393 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:85` — “the same agent's discipline role checks every spec against the active disciplines”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:135` — “The auditor is one agent with three roles, sharing its prompt scaffolding, oracle resolution and receipts.”

The mental model says the intent-auditor's discipline role checks every spec against the active disciplines. It also says, in the present tense, that the auditor's third role suggests reclassifications as the corpus grows. The agent catalog says the auditor is one agent with three roles: single-document fidelity, cross-document consistency and kind classification (`intent shape`). That third role is marked a design target with no registered sub-verb. No discipline role is among the three, and the reclassification role does not run today.

### 90. The mental model has principle-distiller extract each spec's Modification Grammar at spec completion, but the agent register says it serves only disembark, distilling a packed lifeboat

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-828117d9aff87248 · ledger: iss-2610262031086206 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:93` — “extracted by `principle-distiller` at spec completion into typed memory pages”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:421` — “Distils durable principles from a packed lifeboat's decision record”

The mental model says each spec's Modification Grammar section is extracted by `principle-distiller` at spec completion into typed memory pages, which is how the Modification axis is closed. The surfaces index's agent register says principle-distiller serves `disembark` alone and distils durable principles from a packed lifeboat's decision record. The register's Serves column names the verb that builds the agent's input, so nothing at spec close builds its input. The agent cannot both run only on a packed lifeboat and run at every spec's completion.

### 91. The mental model cites the lint chapter for the reserved code VR001, but the lint chapter says the engine has no numbered code catalogue

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-cb9d86b370657f57 · ledger: iss-2610262031080269 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:103` — “plus the vocabulary-registration requirement (`VR001`, [`05-internals/06-lint.md`] (../05-internals/06-lint.md))”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “The engine carries no numbered code catalogue: rules are named, not numbered”

The mental model points at `05-internals/06-lint.md` for the vocabulary-registration check, reserved as `VR001`. The lint contract says the engine carries no numbered code catalogue: rules are named, not numbered, and are defined only in the two JSON configs. The page the mental model cites has no place for a numbered code, reserved or not.

### 92. The naming register refers to lint rules by numbered codes (GL002, SD001, VR001), but the lint contract says rules are named, not numbered

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7f1147d3a9595a61 · ledger: iss-2610262031092650 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:147` — “and it is what the `GL002` forbidden-synonym rule reads”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “rules are named, not numbered, and their definitions live in the two JSON configs above”

The naming register names a live rule by number, saying the glossary is what the `GL002` forbidden-synonym rule reads. It also reserves `SD001` and `VR001` for unbuilt checks. The lint contract says rules are named, not numbered, are defined only in the record-lint and docs-lint JSON configs, and that the record should not carry a hand-kept enumeration of rules. The two pages identify the same rules by different schemes, so a numbered code in the register maps to nothing in the engine's own vocabulary.

### 93. The naming register relies on Role 2 to verify spec vocabulary registration at every plan-review, but Role 2 reads only the brief and the intents, through its own verb

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7c42e1a37abb3fe3 · ledger: iss-2610262031090459 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:155` — “The Role 2 cross-document audit verifies registration on every plan-review.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:163` — “It reads the brief and every intent outside `superseded/` and reports terminology drift”

The vocabulary-registration requirement applies to terms a spec introduces in its Modification Grammar > Ripple > Vocabulary delta, and the naming register says the Role 2 cross-document audit verifies registration on every plan-review. The agent catalog defines Role 2 as `abcd intent consistency`, which reads the brief and every intent outside `superseded/`. It reads no spec, and it runs as its own verb rather than at plan-review. As written, Role 2 cannot see the spec where the term is introduced, so it cannot meet the dependency the register puts on it.

### 94. The naming register ties the `review` bucket (a change judged) to family-1 verdicts, but the agent catalog says family 1 judges only lifeboats and the change reviewers' verdicts are not family 1

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6b8d360a3ec3eb30 · ledger: iss-2610262031105957 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:181` — “`review` compares a change against judgement (family-1 verdicts)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:236` — “They are each role's own words, not family 1: the ruthless reviewer's `SHIP` shares only its spelling.”

The naming register defines the `review` bucket as comparing a change against judgement, with family-1 verdicts, and glosses that family (`{SHIP, NEEDS_WORK, MAJOR_RETHINK}`) as Carmack-style review verdicts. The agent catalog says family 1 assesses a packed lifeboat only, returned by lifeboat-reviewer to `disembark review`. It says the reviewers that judge a change state words of their own: ruthless-reviewer SHIP/FIX FIRST, security-reviewer APPROVE/BLOCK/NEEDS-INPUT. Those words are not family 1. So 'family-1 verdict' names change review on one page and lifeboat review on the other.

### 95. The naming register says the refresh backstop forces a full re-inject regardless of dedup, but the configuration chapter says a domain still in force is never re-injected unchanged within a session

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4aa7accdb8607ce2 · ledger: iss-2610262031108321 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:208` — “Every N prompts, the prompt-router hook forces a full re-inject regardless of dedup signature match (compaction recovery).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1039` — “a domain that stays in force is still never re-injected unchanged within a session”

The naming register defines `rules.force_refresh_every_n` as forcing a full re-inject every N prompts regardless of the dedup signature match, as compaction recovery. The configuration chapter says compaction recovery is event-driven, on SessionStart and PreCompact, and that the counter only re-injects always-relevant domains. It also says a domain that stays in force is never re-injected unchanged within a session. A full re-inject every N prompts and no unchanged re-inject within a session cannot both hold.

### 96. The naming register says the glossary lives only under `glossary/`, but the designed grill log writes glossary terms to `terminology/`

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e0f22a7c0af23931 · ledger: iss-2610262031105533 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:144` — “is the one canonical glossary and the only place a glossary lives”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:117` — “glossary terms are written inline to terminology/, not batched here”

The naming register says the glossary at `../glossary/` is the one canonical glossary and the only place a glossary lives. The designed `.abcd/.work.local/logs/` layout in universal patterns says a grill session writes its glossary terms inline to `terminology/`. One concept, the canonical glossary, gets two homes under two names.

### 97. The dependencies page presents the run seam (and the spec and history seams) as live, with external loops behind one contract, but the adapters chapter says those seams are design targets

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ba721bcc7ec553f4 · ledger: iss-2610262031110865 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/02-dependencies.md:43` — “Claude Workflows, the companion harness's agent loop, or a thin native Go loop behind one contract.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:34` — “are design targets, each introduced by the first intent that consumes it”

The dependencies page says every capability abcd once delegated to a bundled tool has a native default with the external tool available as an opt-in adapter over the same seam. As live examples it gives the run seam, with Claude Workflows, the companion harness's loop or the native loop behind one contract, the spec seam with ccpm, and the history seam with specstory. The adapters chapter says only `scanner` exists as a seam. It calls `oracle`, `history`, `spec` and `run` design targets, each to be introduced by the first intent that consumes it, and says no registry for choosing a backend exists. External loops cannot be available behind a seam that is not built.

### 98. The dependencies page says abcd stamps `schema_version: 1` everywhere, but the configuration chapter says six of the fourteen committed records carry no stamp

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-47448b6560f4ad1a · ledger: iss-2610262031113826 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/02-dependencies.md:95` — “abcd stamps `schema_version: 1` everywhere”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:431` — “eight of the fourteen committed records carry it, and six do not”

The dependencies page puts cross-version migration out of scope because abcd stamps `schema_version: 1` everywhere. The configuration chapter says the stamp is a convention, not an enforced rule: eight of the fourteen committed records carry it and six do not, the record-lint and docs-lint configuration among them. It notes that a migration would have no version to read on those six. 'Everywhere' and 'six do not' cannot both hold, and the migration plan rests on the stamp.

### 99. The platform page says the markdown plugin surface is a later front door, but the configuration chapter describes it as part of the shipped plugin shape

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-58227ef3ef5e32ff · ledger: iss-2610262031126042 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/01-platform.md:17` — “An **MCP server** and a **markdown plugin surface that shells to the Go binary** are later front doors”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1247` — “A Go binary plus the markdown plugin surface that shells to it”

The platform page sets the CLI against what comes after it. The CLI ships in the MVP, while an MCP server and the markdown plugin surface that shells to the binary are later front doors. The configuration chapter's plugin shape is a Go binary plus the markdown plugin surface that shells to it, with the flat `commands/<verb>.md` pages in the tree. In that chapter the MCP door alone is still to come, as adr-23's third. The plugin surface cannot be both a later front door and present in the shipped layout.

### 100. The platform page says an MCP server is a later front door, but universal patterns says abcd interoperates with the companion harness as an MCP server

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e253661dc49290e9 · ledger: iss-2610262031127666 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/01-platform.md:17` — “An **MCP server** and a **markdown plugin surface that shells to the Go binary** are later front doors”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:73` — “when both are present, abcd and the companion harness interoperate as two independent MCP servers, each a front door over its own core (adr-23)”

The platform page says abcd's MCP server is a later front door, not one that exists now. Universal patterns states, in the present tense and with no staged marker, that MCP is the runtime contract. It says that when both tools are present, abcd and the companion harness interoperate as two independent MCP servers, each a front door over its own core. abcd cannot interoperate as an MCP server while that server is still a later front door.

### 101. Invariant 6 says the voyage record is never committed, but universal patterns says voyage is tracked under the visibility rule

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-06a792042d745545 · ledger: iss-2610262031138510 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:19` — “keyed on the root-commit SHA like the history store — never committed, and never accumulated as stale snapshots”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:161` — “Both are tracked under the visibility rule; they answer different questions”

Invariant 6 says operations history lives at the operator level, `~/.abcd.noindex/voyage/<source-root-sha>/`, and is never committed. Universal patterns compares the log tier with `voyage/` and says both are tracked under the visibility rule. Under that rule the `.abcd/` namespace is committed in a private repository. The voyage store cannot be both outside every commit and tracked under the switch that decides what a repository commits.

### 102. Invariant 4 says all inter-agent data is JSON, but the agent catalog says the implement loop reads the reviewers' prose verdict headings

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5cc8ac0b507d7ffe · ledger: iss-2610262031138048 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:15` — “all inter-agent data is JSON; markdown is a render step.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:57` — “`ruthless-reviewer` and `security-reviewer` return prose ending in a verdict heading the implement loop reads”

Invariant 4, which the invariants page calls non-negotiable, says all inter-agent data is JSON and markdown is only a render step. The agent catalog says four shipped prompts declare no JSON contract. The two loop reviewers return prose ending in a verdict heading that the implement loop reads and records, and the docs reviewer returns a table. The loop takes in agent output as prose, which the invariant rules out.

### 103. The scope page says an intent ships when its linked spec closes, but the spec verb ships it only when no open spec still names it

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-39a0b99324326451 · ledger: iss-2610262031147190 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:40` — “It reaches `shipped/` when its linked spec is closed: closing the spec is what ships the intent, and there is no separate ship command.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:275` — “closes a spec and ships its linked intent (`planned/` → `shipped/`) only when no open spec is left naming it”

The scope page says an intent reaches `shipped/` when its linked spec is closed, so closing the spec is what ships it. The surfaces index's spec verb says `spec close` ships the linked intent only when no open spec is left naming it, because an intent owns one or more specs, and a `--remainder` close leaves it planned. Under the 1:n relation, closing a linked spec does not by itself ship the intent.

### 104. 04-scope counts eighteen agents in the canonical roster; 07-memory says the agent count stays at 15.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-073bbd86f43efab8 · ledger: iss-2610262031141978 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:32` — “eighteen agents — the canonical roster is the catalog in”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:158` — “The agent count stays at 15”

04-scope states the plumbing as 'eighteen agents — the canonical roster is the catalog in' 01-agents.md, while 07-memory asserts 'The agent count stays at 15' as the premise the curator role on principle-distiller is reasoned under. Both state the current size of the one agent roster and give different numbers, so one of them is stale.

### 105. 04-naming registers /abcd:intent grill as a staged sub-verb under itd-27; the build sequence says itd-27's grilling is the planning interview under itd-94, which supersedes it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5b24327cf53233d7 · ledger: iss-2610262031153292 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:117` — “`/abcd:intent grill <itd-N>` (itd-27)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:100` — “the grilling itd-27 asked for is the planning interview”

04-naming lists '`/abcd:intent grill <itd-N>` (itd-27)' among the sub-verbs that are staged, named to hold the shape, which under the truth rule is a decided design target. The build sequence says there is no grill sub-verb because 'the grilling itd-27 asked for is the planning interview', abcd intent interview, under itd-94, which supersedes it. A sub-verb cannot remain the staged target of itd-27 when itd-27 is superseded and its grilling is delivered by another verb.

### 106. 02-context lists grill and ship as remaining intent design targets; the build sequence says there is no intent ship and no grill sub-verb, shipping running through spec close and grilling through the planning interview.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-852a6f85b022375a · ledger: iss-2610262031159277 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/02-context.md:11` — “with `refine` / `grill` / `ship` / `shape` remaining design targets”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:99` — “one or more specs — so there is no `intent ship`. There is no `grill` sub-verb”

02-context gives the intent command its sub-verbs 'with `refine` / `grill` / `ship` / `shape` remaining design targets' and describes ship as driving the spec to completion. The build sequence says an intent moves to shipped/ as the close-hook of abcd spec close, 'so there is no `intent ship`. There is no `grill` sub-verb', the grilling being the planning interview under itd-94. One document holds both verbs as designed and pending; the other holds the design settled without them.

### 107. 04-naming defines force_refresh_every_n as a full re-inject forced every N prompts; the verification matrix says the rules-loader refresh is event-driven and nothing counts prompts.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0bbb2e8f1fd7c735 · ledger: iss-2610262031167048 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:208` — “Every N prompts, the prompt-router hook forces a full re-inject regardless of dedup signature match”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:73` — “Nothing counts prompts”

04-naming's reserved-vocabulary row says 'Every N prompts, the prompt-router hook forces a full re-inject regardless of dedup signature match', with a default of 15. The matrix's Rules-loader dedup row says the refresh is event-driven rather than turn-counted, SessionStart and PreCompact being the two events that clear the ledger, and 'Nothing counts prompts'. A prompt counter that forces a re-inject and the absence of any prompt counter cannot both describe the loader.

### 108. 05-personas says the canonical create picks a persona for each press release; the verification matrix stages persona selection and says nothing selects.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a9d982cd469320ad · ledger: iss-2610262031161961 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/05-personas.md:7` — “picks a persona for the customer quote in each press release”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:59` — “picking a persona from the roster and biasing that pick on a role hint: nothing selects”

The matrix's Persona registry row marks as staged 'picking a persona from the roster and biasing that pick on a role hint: nothing selects', the shipped part being only the lint that refuses an unregistered name. Either the create picks a persona or nothing does.

### 109. The press release's acceptance criteria have the bare quoted create complete an interview, and embark open with a press-release interview; the verification matrix says bare quoted text runs no interview and stages the embark interview.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-59fae98e0c53aee1 · ledger: iss-2610262031168083 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:42` — “(canonical bare quoted create), **when** the interview completes”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:53` — “Bare quoted text runs no interview”

The matrix's Intent capture row says 'Bare quoted text runs no interview': the text becomes the press release and the other sections are seeded as prompts; its Embark press-release interview row is staged, what ships being probe-then-write. The product's own acceptance contract assumes interviews the delivered design rules out.

### 110. 02-dependencies describes the native spec store as directories plus a dependency graph; the verification matrix stages the graph and says the spec core carries none.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f764c997e226cc19 · ledger: iss-2610262031176036 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/02-dependencies.md:39` — “directories whose location encodes status, plus a dependency graph over them.”

02-dependencies gives the spec/task native default as 'directories whose location encodes status, plus a dependency graph over them.' with no staged mark. The matrix's Native spec store row marks as staged the dependency graph over specs and tasks and the sequencing that resolves ready work from it, and says 'the spec core carries no graph'. The store either has a dependency graph or it does not.

### 111. 02-dependencies presents the pluggable run seam, with a native loop as its fallback, as a present native default; the build sequence marks the run seam a design target that does not ship.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-10ae02a1b7f82729 · ledger: iss-2610262031177492 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/02-dependencies.md:45` — “the native loop is the always-available fallback”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:131` — “Autonomous run seam *(design target)*”

The build sequence heads the same seam 'Autonomous run seam *(design target)*' and says the seam does not ship: no run verb is registered and the run adapter is on the planned-seams list. 02-dependencies states as current what the build sequence records as unbuilt, without the staged mark the truth rule requires.

### 112. 02-dependencies includes a thin native Go loop among the run seam's loops; the loop glossary entry says abcd never owns the run loop, an adapter supplying it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9145786f18dc419e · ledger: iss-2610262031186949 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/loop.md:38` — “abcd never owns the run loop.”

02-dependencies lists the run seam's loops as host workflows, the companion harness's agent loop 'or a thin native Go loop behind one' contract, the native loop being the fallback. The glossary's loop entry says 'abcd never owns the run loop.': abcd defines the contract and a pluggable adapter supplies the loop, which it gives as the whole reason the run-loop sense needs its own name. A native Go loop shipped in abcd is a run loop abcd owns, so the two cannot both hold.

### 113. 04-scope defines what has shipped by the intents in shipped/ and the derived release, phases being history; 03-out-of-scope still frames the brief around eight planned phases and defines what has shipped by which phases are complete.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-986a248f630c6bce · ledger: iss-2610262031188637 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/03-out-of-scope.md:174` — “What has shipped is defined by which phases are complete and which intents are in `shipped/`”

### 114. 03-mental-model says planning several intents onto one spec in one act (itd-34) is planned; the verification matrix records the --bundle plan as shipped behaviour.

The matrix's Three intent kinds (itd-34) row, a row describing behaviour the binary carries today, says intent plan with --bundle 'plans several drafts as ONE shared spec' whose close ships every member, while it stages the shape-classification role. The two documents disagree on which halves of itd-34 are delivered.

### 115. 03-mental-model says a bundle's shared spec carries intent: [itd-A, itd-B]; the verification matrix says it carries intents: and bundle:.

The matrix's itd-34 row names the shared spec's fields as '`intents:` and `bundle:` on the spec'. ### 119. 01-platform calls the markdown plugin surface a later front door and a new adapter over the core; the verification matrix treats commands/*.md shelling to the binary through the CLI as delivered wiring.

01-platform says an MCP server and a markdown plugin surface 'are later front doors — each is a new adapter over the unchanged core', the CLI being the door that ships in the MVP. The matrix's front-door wiring row, which describes behaviour the binary carries today, says 'A `commands/*.md` surface shells to the binary → the CLI front door parses input', staging only the MCP half. The plugin surface is thus both a later door over the core and a shipped layer over the CLI.

### 120. 01-platform uses transport for the front doors of a transport-agnostic core; the glossary defines transport only as the mechanism delivering context to an oracle.

The glossary's transport entry has one sense: 'The mechanism by which curated context and artefacts are packaged and delivered to an oracle for review or reasoning.' and records no front-door sense. The constraint chapter uses the term in a sense the canonical glossary does not hold.

### 127. 04-tradeoffs records that a pack either completes or writes nothing, with no state file at any path; the verification matrix stages a forensic checkpoint written on a mid-pack interrupt.

### 142. itd-10's destroy removes an in-tree lifeboat inside .abcd/, but the platform rules say no in-tree lifeboat home exists
