- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:26` — “`/abcd:intent audit` (Role 1 of `intent-auditor`) reviews delivered reality against the press release”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-30-design-fictions-as-intent-format.md:18` — “`intent-fidelity-reviewer` reads either dialect against the same delivered reality”

01-press-release says `/abcd:intent audit` is Role 1 of `intent-auditor`, which reviews delivered reality against the press release. itd-30 gives the same job, reading an intent against delivered reality, to an agent it names `intent-fidelity-reviewer`. That is two agent names for one agent.

### 173. The press release says `/abcd:ahoy install` writes the AGENTS.md marker block, but itd-83 says `prepare-this-repo` owns that section.

- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:25` — “`/abcd:ahoy install` bootstraps abcd in any repo (transparent prompts, visibility-driven gitignore, marker block in AGENTS.md, prompt-router hook)”

The brief registers no `prepare-this-repo` surface, so the one setup surface that owns the marker block has two names.

### 174. Context names `/abcd:ahoy install` as the install surface, but itd-91 puts its setup question in `/abcd:init` / `prepare-this-repo`.

### 175. The naming register makes `/abcd:ahoy` the verb that installs abcd, but itd-57 scaffolds its sentinel with `abcd configure`.

04-naming defines `/abcd:ahoy` as the verb that installs abcd into a project or reports what is installed, and its exempt list has no `configure` verb. itd-57 has `abcd configure` (or 'the equivalent first-run path') plant its sentinel spec, which gives the setup surface a second name.

### 176. The naming rules forbid a plain unfiltered `<verb> list`, but itd-2609091014076309 makes `abcd ahoy worktree list` render the same thing as the bare verb.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6f8a3600f8767dc2 · ledger: iss-2610262031473469 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:100` — “`<verb> show`, `<verb> stats`, `<verb> view` and a plain unfiltered `<verb> list`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609091014076309-session-and-agent-worktrees-live-in-a.md:44` — “**Bare `abcd ahoy worktree` and `abcd ahoy worktree list`** render the lane for this repository”

04-naming forbids `<verb> show`, `stats`, `view` and a plain unfiltered `<verb> list` at design time, because each only renames what the bare invocation already renders. The worktree-store intent has bare `abcd ahoy worktree` and `abcd ahoy worktree list` render the same lane, which is exactly the shape the rule forbids. Only `--all` changes the scope.

### 177. The press release requires an explicit sub-verb for any state-mutating action, but itd-2610031215002409's menu under bare `abcd` starts a build at once.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2ef69087c59646c9 · ledger: iss-2610262031474789 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:5` — “Bare invocation of any command shows status + suggested next actions; state-mutating actions require an explicit sub-verb (the universal abcd convention).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610031215002409-under-the-board-a-short-what-next-menu.md:22` — “Choosing to start building begins at once, because the choice already names what will be built.”

01-press-release states as the universal abcd convention that bare invocation shows status and suggested next actions, and that state-mutating actions require an explicit sub-verb. The menu intent has bare `abcd` start building as soon as the menu choice is made, and set the waiting-on status while the menu waits. The intent records that it reverses 08-abcd.md's zero-writes promise, but the universal convention in the press release still says the opposite.

### 179. GRILL's asking rules say options widen and never recommend, but itd-97's escalation contract hands the product thinker a proposal with a recommendation.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-245d87d510ef5a38 · ledger: iss-2610262031486321 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:221` — “options that widen and never recommend, deferral recorded as an answer”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-97-the-facilitator-is-a-mode-not-a-person.md:67` — “point with a proposal (options, recommendation, price), exactly where duo”

04-naming records GRILL as the asking rules every abcd interview follows, including 'options that widen and never recommend'. itd-97's escalation contract has solo mode stop at every product-thinker decision point with a proposal carrying options, a recommendation and a price. A decision put to the person cannot both carry a recommendation and follow a rule that never recommends.

### 183. Invariant 15 refuses any path at a reading's invocation, but itd-86's cold reading takes exactly one target document.

### 185. Dependencies present RepoPrompt and codex as oracle adapters an operator can select, but itd-2609170822093401 says nothing reads the oracle backend value today.

### 190. itd-7 has disembark's pre-pack step write .abcd/rp/workspace.json into the repository being read; invariant 6 says disembark never writes to the source.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-80b461b8a8f1d36d · ledger: iss-2610262031532231 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-7-rp-workspace-portability.md:20` — “writes it into `.abcd/rp/workspace.json` in the repo”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:19` — “Lifeboat is always *output*, and disembark never writes to the source”

itd-7 says that when dev-sync runs, and as part of /abcd:disembark, abcd reads the RepoPrompt workspace and 'writes it into `.abcd/rp/workspace.json` in the repo', with dev-sync run as a pre-pack step so the file reaches the lifeboat. Invariant 6 states 'Lifeboat is always *output*, and disembark never writes to the source', with the lifeboat written out-of-tree to an operator-chosen destination. A pack path that writes into the source repository breaks that invariant, so the planned intent cannot be built as written unless the write leaves the pack path or the invariant is amended.

### 191. itd-7 depends on a dev-sync pre-pack step it calls 'already in brief'; the brief lists dev-sync only among out-of-scope work not yet under way.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c37daaf29ad4506a · ledger: iss-2610262031537827 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-7-rp-workspace-portability.md:38` — “dev-sync runs as a pre-pack step (already in brief)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:33` — “scheduled `dev-sync`, opencode harness portability”

itd-7 hangs both its pull and its pack on dev-sync: the workspace is written on dev-sync, and 'dev-sync runs as a pre-pack step (already in brief)'. The brief's press release lists 'scheduled `dev-sync`' among the out-of-scope items that are not yet under way and live as draft intents, and describes the pack as three passes with no dev-sync step. As written, the planned intent depends on a verb and a pack step the brief records as unbuilt, and its claim that the step is already in the brief does not hold.

### 192. itd-199 ships a scope operand at invocation that it says was 'carried into brief invariant 15'; invariant 15 says that operand is superseded and the operands are position and target only.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-503260010f74889f · ledger: iss-2610262031532200 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-199-a-reading-is-about-something-narrower.md:19` — “A scope may be widened or narrowed at invocation while calibrating”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:167` — “which supersedes adr-58's scope operand and restores the 2026-08-28 M8 ruling”

itd-199 adds a third operand (a record id, a family or a preset name), says 'A scope may be widened or narrowed at invocation while calibrating', records the ruling as adr-58 and says it was carried into invariant 15; it also has the comparative position refuse because no channel exists. Invariant 15 says the operands are a position and a target state and nothing else, under an ADR 'which supersedes adr-58's scope operand and restores the 2026-08-28 M8 ruling', and has the comparative position derive its widening run from the record. The shipped intent still describes an operand as live that the invariant records as withdrawn.

### 193. itd-147's press release says the generated appendix carries exit codes, schema fields and counts; invariant 18 says flags and sub-verbs only.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-35e556161f829a57 · ledger: iss-2610262031549181 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-147-the-brief-s-surface-chapters-are-a.md:24` — “sub-verbs, exit codes, schema fields and counts, derived from the command tree”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:173` — “The appendix carries flags and sub-verbs only: exit codes, output fields and behavioural claims stay prose and review-grain”

itd-147's press release says each surface chapter's generated block carries the verb's flags, 'sub-verbs, exit codes, schema fields and counts, derived from the command tree'. Invariant 18 states 'The appendix carries flags and sub-verbs only: exit codes, output fields and behavioural claims stay prose and review-grain'. The intent's own decisions narrow to flags and sub-verbs first, but its press release, the part a reader takes as the promise, still claims a wider shipped block than the invariant allows.

### 194. itd-2610161733316518 turns off the host fallback inside a matrix cell; invariant 2 says a missing or failing adapter degrades to the native path, and the brief declares no exception for this.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e77ca7902d3e9263 · ledger: iss-2610262031545672 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610161733316518-a-product-thinker-who-wants-to-know.md:239` — “Inside a matrix cell it switches off the host fallback”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:11` — “A missing or misbehaving adapter degrades to the native path; abcd never blocks on an absent tool.”

The model-matrix intent's decision 4 says 'Inside a matrix cell it switches off the host fallback' that the runners and routing table otherwise take, scores a failed cell as a failure, and argues that invariant 2's purpose still holds. Invariant 2 states 'A missing or misbehaving adapter degrades to the native path; abcd never blocks on an absent tool.' with no carve-out. A route that deliberately does not degrade contradicts the invariant as written until the brief declares the exception, as it declares other exceptions to adr-22.

### 195. itd-117 puts the user-scope rules at ~/.abcd/rules.json; invariant 21 names abcd's user-level home ~/.abcd.noindex.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9b9ca5b2dc722db8 · ledger: iss-2610262031557534 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:179` — “the `.noindex` suffix the home carries, `~/.abcd.noindex`”

itd-117 says a machine's shared conventions 'now live once in `~/.abcd/rules.json`' as the user scope. Invariant 21 says the space abcd owns is the home carrying the .noindex suffix, '`~/.abcd.noindex`', and the brief places every other operator-level path under it. The corpus uses two names for one user-level home, so a reader following itd-117 is sent to a path the brief no longer names.

### 196. itd-200 installs the status-line defaults under ~/.abcd/; invariant 21 names the user-level home ~/.abcd.noindex.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7fa225db94eedb9b · ledger: iss-2610262031557361 (filed)

### 197. itd-39 extends a Python hook, hooks/prompt_router_hook.py; 02-dependencies says abcd ships as a single Go binary with no required external tools.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5ac269b7a8343812 · ledger: iss-2610262031560983 (filed)

### 198. 04-tradeoffs records /abcd:memory as the curated store's command with ingest/ask/lint; itd-39 says memory is now the agents' notes command and the store is reached through library.

### 199. itd-50 calls the per-criterion auditor intent-fidelity-reviewer; the brief names the same role intent-auditor (Role 1).

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8366953637717750 · ledger: iss-2610262031563379 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:26` — “`/abcd:intent audit` (Role 1 of `intent-auditor`)”

itd-50's press release says 'the `intent-fidelity-reviewer` records a `NOT_MET` verdict'. The brief's press release names the same role as '`/abcd:intent audit` (Role 1 of `intent-auditor`)'. That is two names for one agent role, and work built from the planned intent would look for an agent the brief does not name.

### 200. itd-82 requires a remedy on every new issue; the brief's acceptance criterion has /abcd:capture "< text>" alone produce a structured issue.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-cf2f0db47d0c60ba · ledger: iss-2610262031575425 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:44` — “and requires it of every new issue (ruling BX3 of 2026-09-29)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:43` — “the user runs `/abcd:capture "<text>"`, **when** the command completes”

itd-82 says capture gains the remedy field 'and requires it of every new issue (ruling BX3 of 2026-09-29)'. The brief press release's acceptance criterion begins: Given 'the user runs `/abcd:capture "<text>"`, **when** the command completes', then a structured issue exists in open/. No remedy is supplied in that criterion. Under itd-82's rule that invocation is refused, so the criterion cannot pass as written.

### 201. itd-82 makes bare abcd drain the unattended run that changes state; 04-naming rules that a bare invocation renders and that changing state is what a sub-verb is for.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1f594b9998f64c44 · ledger: iss-2610262031575529 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:20` — “`abcd drain` works the open issue ledger unattended”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/04-naming.md:92` — “Every `/abcd:<verb>` treats the bare invocation as status plus help plus a render”

itd-82's press release opens with '`abcd drain` works the open issue ledger unattended': the bare verb opens lanes and pull requests and writes markers, and decision 3 makes it 'all by default, capped by flag'. 04-naming states 'Every `/abcd:<verb>` treats the bare invocation as status plus help plus a render' and that a sub-verb earns its existence by mutating state. The planned verb builds in the bare-acts shape the naming rule excludes at design time; 04-naming treats acting verbs only as a gap in the shipped surface, not as an allowed design.

### 202. 05-personas requires press-release quotes from the persona registry; itd-82's quote is attributed to an unnamed product thinker.

05-personas says 'Customer quotes use placeholder personas from `.abcd/development/personas.json`': the persona is chosen by role and given its registered name rather than generic phrasing. itd-82's press-release quote is attributed with 'said a product thinker who ran the first ledger drains by hand', which names no registered persona. The convention and the record disagree on how a quote is attributed.

### 203. 04-scope defines operator-internal verbs, rules and spec among them, as wiring with no commands/ file; itd-146 says operator_internal only means 'needs no surface chapter' and treats rules as user-facing.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dab67fb82053c4ab · ledger: iss-2610262031582207 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-146-abcd-s-help-renders-in-labelled-command.md:75` — “`record-lint.json` means *needs no surface chapter*, which is a lint”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/04-scope.md:19` — “the class is defined by the absence of a `commands/` file rather than by the presence of one”

04-scope lists rules and spec among the operator-internal verbs, as wiring rather than user-facing surface, and says 'the class is defined by the absence of a `commands/` file rather than by the presence of one'. itd-146 says the operator_internal key in '`record-lint.json` means *needs no surface chapter*, which is a lint' exemption rather than a verdict on user visibility, and keeps rules listed because the marker block tells every managed repository to run it. The term operator-internal has two definitions, and they disagree on whether rules is user-facing.

### 204. itd-146 places a changelog verb in the root help's agent block; 04-naming's register of exempt surfaces, which says every exemption is on the record, does not list it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-ef1c1b3da5eb0c6d · ledger: iss-2610262031588576 (filed)

itd-146's decision 3 says '`changelog` sits in the agent block' of the root help, and the intent keeps changelog a top-level verb rather than folding it under launch. 04-naming introduces its list with 'The remaining surfaces are exempt for the plain reason that no maritime cognate' adds meaning, and says each exemption is registered so that it is a decision rather than an omission; changelog is not in the list. Either the register is incomplete or the help names a verb the register does not know.

### 207. The mental model says the Now/Next/Later status block's intent is planned; that intent is on the shipped shelf and says the board shows the block.

The brief's invariant states that an intent owns one or more specs and ships when its last spec closes. itd-34 asserts that a standalone intent maps one-to-one to a spec. Both make a claim about the same relation and cannot both hold.

The invariants register numbers invariant 3 as 'Native default front door', which is about abcd's logic living in a transport-agnostic Go core and has nothing to do with where config is written. The oracle architecture cannot both keep that cascade and have none, and a builder following itd-6's scope would build the routing that the constraints chapter says does not exist.

### 243. itd-69's checker takes `--tree dev|public`; the platform page says there is no dev→public mirror

### 245. itd-80 moves an intent to shipped when its linked spec closes; invariant 17 says a close never ships an intent that another open spec still names

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e6c41d49576ea307 · ledger: iss-2610262032168367 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-80-intent-lifecycle-automation.md:34` — “on spec close, detect the linked intent via the immutable link, move it `planned → shipped` with an atomic same-filesystem rename”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/02-constraints/03-invariants.md:171` — “closing a spec never ships an intent that still has an open spec, the intent moves `planned/` → `shipped/` on the close after which no open spec names it”

itd-80's reconcile finds the linked intent through the immutable link when a spec closes, and moves it planned → shipped. Invariant 17 makes the intent↔spec relation 1:n: closing a spec never ships an intent that still has an open spec, and the move happens only on the close after which no open spec names it. The two reconcile rules disagree about which close ships the intent.

- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/01-press-release.md:23` — “runs three passes (settled artefacts → targeted chat retrieval → distil/compose/audit) over a project's specs, ADRs, transcripts, oracle reviews, and curated memory”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-88-lifeboat-coverage-experiment.md:46` — “there is no corpus. It ships as a **declared exemption** in `_provenance.json`, never a silent gap, until the transcript store has data.”

The brief's press release scopes `/abcd:disembark pack` as three passes (settled artefacts → targeted chat retrieval → distil/compose/audit) over specs, ADRs and transcripts, with no staged marker. itd-88 says the transcript-mining pass (Pass B) has no corpus and ships as a declared exemption in `_provenance.json` until the transcript store has data. The pack cannot both run the chat-retrieval pass and exempt it.

### 248. itd-88 calls the packer `disembark <repo> to <dest>`; the platform page calls it `disembark pack <source-repo> <dest>`

### 249. itd-89 files transcripts in the local per-repo store; invariant 15 makes the user-level `~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/<root-sha>/` the store, with a per-repo store only for a declared checkout

One puts the default store in the user's home and the other in the repository.

### 250. itd-95 says the richest present tier wins a section; the meta page says tiers are cumulative, so a richer tier can never ground a section worse than a poorer one

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-df0fcfb732add493 · ledger: iss-2610262032182670 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-95-disembark-grounds-a-lifeboat-s-open.md:42` — “it does not change the rule that the richest present tier wins a section”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/00-meta.md:52` — “A richer tier can therefore never ground a section worse than a poorer one.”

itd-95 describes the reduction rule it leaves unchanged as 'the richest present tier wins a section'. Under that rule, an abcd-native tier that finds nothing can override open questions that the conventions tier grounds from TODO markers. 00-meta says a richer tier can never ground a section worse than a poorer one. The first rule lets a section come back worse at a richer tier; the second forbids it.

### 251. itd-96 grounds `internals` from conventions-tier documentation; the generated mapping table caps `internals` at partial for Tier 1 conventions

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c40caa8358a60434 · ledger: iss-2610262032189264 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-96-disembark-reads-a-repo-s-naming-and.md:41` — “Real documentation → grounded; a thin signal (e.g. package dirs but no architecture prose) → partial”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/00-meta.md:76` — “`internals` | `brief/05-internals/` | partial | partial | grounded | package layout, architecture docs, the internals chapters”

itd-96's conventions-tier adapter reports real architecture documentation as grounded. 00-meta's generated mapping table, which states the best status a lifeboat can reach at each tier, gives `internals` partial at Tier 1 conventions and grounded only at Tier 2 abcd-native. The table and the shipped adapter disagree about what the conventions tier can reach.

### 252. The mental model calls itd-60 planned, but itd-60 sits on the shipped shelf

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4debaca702ff2863 · ledger: iss-2610262032193797 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/03-mental-model.md:79` — “This work is governed by the planned itd-60/itd-61 doc-fidelity + derivation loop”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md:32` — “abcd gains a doc-fidelity gate: a change cannot call itself shipped while”

03-mental-model says the framework-provided discipline is governed by 'the planned itd-60/itd-61 doc-fidelity + derivation loop'. itd-60, the doc-fidelity gate, is in `intents/shipped/`. The brief is meant to record the current state, but the lifecycle state it gives for itd-60 is contradicted by the shelf itd-60 sits on.

### 253. itd-46 treats `list` as a corpus-scope intent scan verb that already exists; the context page says there is no plain `list` sub-verb

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-edd55cce9e6d51d9 · ledger: iss-2610262032194841 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:78` — “scan verbs (`list`, `consistency`, `shape`) continue not to require an ID.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/01-product/02-context.md:11` — “There is no plain `list` sub-verb — it is folded into the bare render per SD001.”

itd-46 describes `list`, alongside `consistency` and `shape`, as a scan verb that continues not to require an ID, an already-correct shape it leaves alone. 02-context says there is no plain `list` sub-verb because it is folded into the bare render per SD001. An intent sub-verb cannot both carry on unchanged and not exist.

### 254. Capture says the release guard never blocks a record graded below major; launch says it also blocks an absent or unreadable grade

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7111704d5c136f3a · ledger: iss-2610262032208043 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:334` — “a record whose grade is neither `major` nor `critical`, which the guard never blocks on”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:587` — “is a severity of `major` or `critical`, and also a severity that is absent, misspelled, or outside the ledger's enum”

Launch's unfixed-findings guardrail blocks on a major or critical grade and also on a severity that is absent, misspelled or outside the enum, and names deferral with the waiver pair as one of its routes out. Capture's deferral verb refuses every record whose grade is neither major nor critical, on the stated premise that the guard never blocks on such a record. Both cannot hold: an ungraded record does block the cut, yet the verb that writes the waiver refuses it, so the deferral route launch offers is closed for exactly the records launch counts as unjudged.

### 255. Ahoy says every launch verb refuses an undeclared artefact kind; launch says the cut, the archive render and the receipts check assume the plugin shape

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bb02fca88570f898 · ledger: iss-2610262032208504 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:826` — “withholding the declaration would leave every launch verb refusing the repository”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:46` — “the cut, the archive render and the receipts check read an absent declaration as the plugin shape they have always assumed”

Ahoy justifies declaring application on an unattended install because withholding the declaration would leave every launch verb refusing the repository. Launch says only the preview and the scaffold refuse a repository that declared no kind, while the cut, the archive render and the receipts check read an absent declaration as the plugin shape. Ahoy's premise that every launch verb refuses is false by launch's own account of its verbs.

### 256. Launch says the repo organises work by phase; disembark says sequence is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, with phases retired

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f30736abcaf6c814 · ledger: iss-2610262032214284 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:489` — “the repo organises work by **phase**”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:18` — “sequence is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves ([adr-2609212115255771] (../../decisions/adrs/2609212115255771-phases-and-milestones-are-retired.md))”

Launch's versioning section grounds versions-as-output on the repo organising its work by phase. Disembark records that sequence is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, citing the decision that retires phases and milestones, and calls the phase document it names retired. A reader cannot both organise work by phase and treat phases as retired.

### 257. Launch says intents carry no version label; the intent chapter says a planned intent may name the release vX.Y.Z it must land by

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-749716a32adc8c98 · ledger: iss-2610262032212691 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:491` — “The brief, intents and roadmap carry no version label.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:75` — “A planned intent may name the release it must land by, `vX.Y.Z` or `next`”

Launch states that versions are never a sequencing input on the design record and that the brief, intents and roadmap carry no version label. The intent chapter defines target_release, a planned-intent field naming the release the intent must land by as vX.Y.Z or next, which the preview and the cut report. A release tag carried on an intent as a land-by deadline is a version label used as a sequencing input, so the two statements cannot both hold.

### 258. Ahoy says the docs target defaults to skip, writing no conventions file; embark says no saved choice gives AGENTS.md

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-219e1bfdb5d40c98 · ledger: iss-2610262032225288 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:1070` — “so the docs target defaults to `skip`: a default install writes it into none of the repository's committed conventions files”

Ahoy says the docs target defaults to skip, so a default install plants the marker block in none of the repository's conventions files and a project must name agents_md to get it. Embark reads docs.target with setup's reader yet maps no saved choice to AGENTS.md, so an embark into a target with no saved choice writes the block where a default install would write nothing. The two disagree on what the absent setting means.

### 259. Ahoy calls the remote apply the one verb that mutates state outside the machine; launch says the reservation verb means a push to origin

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a2e7414a99a625bb · ledger: iss-2610262032226321 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:90` — “the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this machine”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:757` — “A push from it would change what the verb means, where the reservation verb already means exactly that push.”

Ahoy says the remote apply is the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this machine. Launch has the cutting session take the release hold with the reservation verb, and says that verb already means exactly a push of the reservation to origin, a remote write every other session's land step then reads. Both cannot be the one remote-mutating verb.

### 260. Ahoy's preparation reads the brief, principles, ADRs and intents from the plugin root; launch says the plugin payload never ships the .abcd/ record

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-596532dfaa74cce5 · ledger: iss-2610262032223832 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:359` — “Read the abcd record from the plugin root: the three-tier README, the brief, principles, ADRs, intents”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:12` — “And it never ships the design record: the payload is default-deny with the whole `.abcd/` namespace excluded structurally, so no include line can put it back.”

The install's preparation workflow opens by reading the abcd record (the brief, principles, ADRs and intents) from the plugin root, and its self-contained boundary says every applied asset resolves from that record or from the binary. Launch says the release payload is default-deny with the whole .abcd/ namespace excluded structurally, and that the catalog pins the cut archive so an install receives the release payload rather than the working tree. A plugin root installed that way holds no design record, so the orient phase depends on files the artefact it reads from cannot carry.

### 261. Library says the memory command merged into library with no surviving name; ahoy names a live memory verb that writes memory notes

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-47630482cff91573 · ledger: iss-2610262032231296 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:463` — “own notes, which agents write through the memory verb”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:11` — “The command merges the two that came before it, `source` and `memory`, under the product thinker's ruling of 2026-10-09”

Library says the command merges the two that came before it, source and memory, and that neither old name survives as an alias, the memory store living at .abcd/memory/ under library's ingest, ask and lint. Ahoy describes the machine's memory.json as notes agents write through the memory verb, recalled beside the project's .abcd/memory.json. The one name memory then denotes both the retired memory-store command and a live notes verb, and two different memory stores in the repository sit under one word.

The board chapter has the session-start hook reserve names in a machine register at ~/.abcd.noindex/sessions/names.json, which appears nowhere in ahoy's inventory. Either the inventory is incomplete or the register lives somewhere the inventory does name.

### 263. Library says embark carrying the memory store forward is designed behaviour; embark says the memory store is not an embark family and does not travel

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-28499d3e8ddd6238 · ledger: iss-2610262032245453 (filed)

Library's composition note says embark carrying the store forward is designed behaviour, with the receiver running the store lint after unpacking. Embark says terminology, docs and the memory store are not embark families and do not travel, and its design-target section lists no memory carry. ### 264. Library defers the lifeboat's memory payload to the spec that wires the packer; disembark has the packer shipped with a fixed file set and no memory section

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-94738d8e275fb65b · ledger: iss-2610262032245680 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:424` — “declaring an exact payload is deferred to the disembark spec that wires the packer (adr-28)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:129` — “Each path derives from the brief-section-to-lifeboat-path mapping in `internal/core/lifeboat/mapping.go`: a section grounds into its file where the source supports it”

Library says disembark is designed to export curated project memory into the lifeboat and that declaring the exact payload is deferred to the disembark spec that wires the packer. Disembark records the pack as shipped, every path derived from the brief-section mapping, and its output shape holds the brief, graveyard, rescue, retrospectives, ADRs and issues with no memory section. The deferral waits on a wiring that, as disembark writes it, has already happened without carrying memory.

### 265. Reflect's set of intents a release shipped follows shipped_in both ways; the cut only drops records whose shipped_in an earlier tag reaches

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c831bcb866195ca5 · ledger: iss-2610262032258227 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:49` — “less any whose `shipped_in` names another release, plus any in `shipped/` now whose `shipped_in` names this one”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:526` — “leaving out an entering record whose `shipped_in:` names a release tag the previous tag already reaches, since that release carried its work; a value that names no such tag keeps the record in”

Launch gathers the records that entered shipped/ since the previous tag, leaving out only one whose shipped_in names a tag the previous tag already reaches and keeping one whose value names no such tag. Reflect takes those that reached shipped/ in the window, less any whose shipped_in names another release, plus any in shipped/ now whose shipped_in names this one. A record stamped for a later release is in the cut but out of reflect's set, and one that entered earlier but is stamped for this release is in reflect's set but not in the cut, so the retrospective's intent table and the changelog section it links can disagree.

### 266. Reflect lists planned intents whose target_release names the release; the cut has already rewritten every such target to next

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-367556ac91e025bc · ledger: iss-2610262032250865 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:59` — “The planned intents whose `target_release` names the release and which **did not ship**”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:790` — “The ingest moves every target the cut passes (`next`, or a tag at or below the derived version) to `next`”

Reflect's seed lists the planned intents whose target_release names the released tag and which did not ship, warns about them, and its write refuses until they are confirmed. Launch's ingest moves every target the cut passes, a tag at or below the derived version, to next in the same write that rolls the changelog. By the time a tag exists for reflect to take, no planned intent's target names it, so the list is empty by construction and the refusal can never fire.

### 267. Launch names its docs-lint gate row the documentation audit; the intent chapter keeps audit and lint as separate verbs, the conformance check being lint

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-b7e32d9d008e16d8 · ledger: iss-2610262032256736 (filed)

The intent chapter's statement of the verb register says the top-level conformance check is abcd lint, the audit name is reserved for other checks, and each verb means one thing. Launch calls its docs-lint engine row the documentation audit, and its acceptance speaks of a documentation-auditor warning, using audit for a lint-bucket conformance check.

### 269. Embark's refresh-audit modifier diffs against a disembark-time audit; disembark produces a review verdict and no audit

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-b138d608193740e6 · ledger: iss-2610262032268272 (filed)

Disembark's pipeline has no audit step: its judgement over the pack is the lifeboat-reviewer's review returning a registered verdict. The modifier depends on an artefact disembark, as written, never produces, or names the review by another verb's word.

### 270. Embark writes the ledger and intent store under a target defaulting to the working directory; capture holds that the root is resolved, never taken to be the working directory

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-152ecf844e942d9f · ledger: iss-2610262032275161 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:366` — “the repository root is **resolved** from the working directory, never taken to be it”

Embark's unpack takes an optional target that defaults to the working directory and writes the issue ledger, intent store and spec store beneath it. Capture says the repository root is resolved from the working directory and never taken to be it, because taking it verbatim minted a second ledger under a subdirectory, out of reach of every gate that reads the real one. An embark run from a subdirectory of a checkout lays exactly the stray store capture describes as the defect.

### 271. lint says the outbound-policy gate is the only surface that judges text before it is public; ahoy says the shell guard also refuses forge text carrying the same two shapes before it is posted

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-da141d4467e0243e · ledger: iss-2610262032272603 (filed)

16-lint.md counts four surfaces that read the harness-leak definition and says the outbound gate is the only one that judges text before it is public. 01-ahoy.md says the outbound opt-in also makes the shell guard refuse a posting gh pr or gh issue command whose title, body or body file carries either shape (forge-text-outbound). That is a judgement of text before it is public. Both cannot hold: either the guard's forge-text check is a fifth pre-public surface, or lint's count and its 'only one' claim are wrong.

### 272. ahoy's inventory of ~/.abcd.noindex/ has no away store; mode keeps the away record in ~/.abcd.noindex/away/< root-sha>/

Either the inventory is incomplete, or the away store lives somewhere else.

### 273. ahoy's inventory of ~/.abcd.noindex/ has no ideas store; ideate writes private verdicts to ~/.abcd.noindex/ideas/< root-sha>/

### 274. ahoy's inventory of ~/.abcd.noindex/ has no after-update store; update's news sub-verb writes under ~/.abcd.noindex/after-update/

### 275. 'history' names two things: ahoy's 'history store' could be the registry directory ~/.abcd.noindex/history/ or the history verb's transcript store

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-d87fecf34a711c14 · ledger: iss-2610262032291598 (filed)

So 'history' names both the registry directory and the transcript store, and ahoy's phrase does not say whether uninstall keeps the transcript corpus, the registry, or both.

### 276. ahoy's setup mints the drain rule as an accepted record carrying drain_ fields through the decision store's seam; decide says a minted record lands empty and proposed, and names embark, a restore, as the only other writer

It names embark, a restore rather than a mint, as the store's only other writer, and a decision (dcn) record carries no status and no extra fields. No writer decide describes produces the accepted, field-carrying record ahoy says it mints, and decide does not list setup as a minting writer.

### 277. launch's citation-baseline row refuses on an overdue citation; docs says the launch preflight only names what would stop a release, while the release still cuts

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-43836ca0dc59ebb6 · ledger: iss-2610262032307333 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:338` — “against their receipts and refuses on a broken, unreceipted or overdue one.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:228` — “which names what the citation baseline would stop a release on while a release still cuts.”

04-launch.md says the citation-baseline row of the pre-flight suite refuses on a broken, unreceipted or overdue citation. 10-docs.md says launch computes its own citation preflight and that this preflight names what the citation baseline would stop a release on, while a release still cuts. In docs, only the lint's release-gate flag, passed by the release workflow, makes an overdue citation a blocker, and no committed config can arm it. Either the cut refuses on an overdue citation without that flag, or it still cuts.

### 278. docs and launch each own a change-narration check over the same doc bodies and give opposite verdicts on an ambiguous phrase: a warning in the docs lint, a refusal in launch

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8dbe1c46c7bdf182 · ledger: iss-2610262032308835 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:140` — “Unambiguous change-narration blocks; phrases that can also describe present state warn advisorily rather than block.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:304` — “A pair the words cannot tell apart is refused, not passed: the tier is a release gate”

10-docs.md gives change-narration to the currency lint, which it presents as the check that gates a release, and says phrases that can also describe present state only warn. 04-launch.md runs its own hard-fail change-narration gate over the shipped doc bodies and refuses any pair the words cannot tell apart. The same ground is covered twice with contradictory outcomes, so a sentence that passes CI's docs lint with a warning refuses the cut. Neither chapter names the other's rule as the authority.

### 279. docs says the release workflow runs the lint's release-gate mode while the scaffolded release template never names the verb; launch says abcd's own release workflows are regenerated byte-exact from those templates

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b5647a6675ab11d9 · ledger: iss-2610262032317368 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:131` — “The release workflow's docs-currency step runs the lint in its release-gate mode; CI's step and the `docs-lint` make target each run the lint in its plain mode, the scaffolded release template names the verb nowhere”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:216` — “The workflows ship from embedded templates, one per file, that abcd's own release workflows are regenerated from, proved byte-exact by a test, so a scaffolded repo and this one cannot drift.”

10-docs.md says the release workflow's docs-currency step runs the lint in its release-gate mode, and that the scaffolded release template names the verb nowhere. 04-launch.md says abcd's own release workflows are regenerated from the embedded templates and a test proves them byte-exact, so a scaffolded repo and abcd cannot drift. If abcd's workflow is byte-exact with the template, the template carries the release-gate step and names the verb. If the template names no such step, abcd's workflow is not byte-exact or does not carry it.

### 280. launch's artefact declaration reserves an inert opt-in for the release-rendered site; site describes a shipped setup that already writes a workflow rendering the site from each published release

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-574e18fe83dc9685 · ledger: iss-2610262032310109 (filed)

The release-rendered site is therefore already acted on, and it is opted into through the site verb, not artefact.json. Two declarations claim the same opt-in, and the one launch names does nothing.

### 281. Ahoy's history store is a registry that holds no transcripts; build's history store is where a runner's transcript lands

### 282. Implement's record verb captures transcripts into the history store, which ahoy says holds no transcripts

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-02ad13ba10da62fe · ledger: iss-2610262032328073 (filed)
