Both documents cannot be right about where a run's transcripts go.

### 283. Ahoy says the prompt router recalls memory notes now; memory says recall through the prompt hook is a later step

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9ca45a6daf628da8 · ledger: iss-2610151422092354 (already open)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:466` — “The prompt router recalls them beside the project's .abcd/memory.json”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:6` — “Recall of a note through the prompt hook is the same spec's later step”

01-ahoy describes ~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json as notes the prompt router recalls beside the project's .abcd/memory.json, the project's note winning an id both hold, and states this as present behaviour. 37-memory says recall of a note through the prompt hook is its spec's later step, and that the chapter covers only the store and the verb. Recall cannot be both shipped and still to come.

### 284. Ahoy calls the remote apply the one verb that mutates state off this machine; reserve exists to write a branch on the shared remote

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-be4689508c61d8ae · ledger: iss-2610262032326065 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:90` — “the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this machine”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-reserve.md:4` — “it reserves the record on the shared remote as a branch nobody merges”

01-ahoy states that the remote apply is the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this machine. 37-reserve's whole purpose is to write the reservation, as a branch, on the shared remote that other people and computers read. That is a push to origin, which is state outside this machine. A reader who trusts ahoy's claim would not count the reservation verb among abcd's outward writes.

### 285. Implement says abcd calls no model; ahoy has a delegating verb send its step to a configured provider itself

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8464a591409084be · ledger: iss-2610262032338974 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:507` — “the model service only by the verdict of a canary agent the lead runs, since abcd calls no model”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:204` — “A delegating verb whose agent's `oracle.roles` entry points at a configured provider sends the step there itself”

27-implement probes the model service only through a canary agent the lead runs, and gives the reason that abcd calls no model. 01-ahoy says a delegating verb whose agent's oracle.roles entry points at a configured provider sends the step there itself, so abcd does call a model whenever a provider is configured. The premise the outage probe rests on is false in that case.

### 286. Ahoy says only host-delegated has a reviewer adapter; build routes lane reviews to RepoPrompt

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-289e83a7f56d74f0 · ledger: iss-2610262032331100 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:893` — “The oracle backend is not asked while host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:542` — “A build lane's ruthless and security reviews can go to RepoPrompt over MCP instead of the host's own agents”

01-ahoy's install does not ask for the oracle backend, because host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter, and it says other reviewers arrive later. 34-build's reviewer route sends a lane's ruthless and security reviews to RepoPrompt over MCP through oracle.review. So either a second reviewer already has an adapter, which contradicts ahoy, or two different settings choose the reviewer and neither document says how they relate.

### 287. Lab says its harvest takes the lifeboat's section shape, but disembark gives the lifeboat a different set of sections

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-97916ed151c6ff3f · ledger: iss-2610262032345454 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/31-lab.md:99` — “assembles the lab's harvest in the lifeboat's section shape — intention, method, what worked, what is open, candidates, coverage”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:129` — “Each path derives from the brief-section-to-lifeboat-path mapping”

31-lab says the harvest is assembled in the lifeboat's section shape: intention, method, what worked, what is open, candidates and coverage. 02-disembark derives every lifeboat path from the brief-section-to-lifeboat-path mapping, which yields brief sections, a graveyard, a rescue spine, retrospectives, ADRs and an issue snapshot alongside coverage. Of lab's six sections only coverage is a lifeboat part, so a builder who follows lab's pointer to the lifeboat finds a different shape.

### 288. Ahoy's inventory of ~/.abcd.noindex has no dashboard/ entry, but the dashboard keeps its run file and device list there

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0879a000841522cb · ledger: iss-2610262032346952 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:420` — “~/.abcd.noindex/ USER SCOPE — one per machine (machine-local state only)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/36-dashboard.md:127` — “The run file and the devices list live in `~/.abcd.noindex/dashboard/`”

01-ahoy lists the user-scope directory entry by entry as the machine-local state abcd keeps, and says this inventory and the configuration chapter's are one list that must agree. 36-dashboard puts its run file and device list in ~/.abcd.noindex/dashboard/, which the inventory does not include. Either the inventory is incomplete, or the dashboard writes state outside what abcd says it keeps.

### 289. Build's landing relies on the spec close to ship the intent, but no build check secures the impact that launch says the close requires

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-042ea5abe3c2df26 · ledger: iss-2610262032353042 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:743` — “In the lane's worktree it runs the spec's close (which ships the intent and parks the fidelity receipt)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:516` — “the spec verb's close refuses to ship an intent that records none when none is given on the close, and moves nothing”

34-build's landing runs the spec's close in the lane's worktree as the step that ships the intent. None of its start checks (key, ready, open questions, claim sections, hold, blocked, steps, peers) asks for an impact, and the close it runs is given none. 04-launch says the spec verb's close refuses to ship an intent that records no impact when none is given on the close, and moves nothing; it also says a planned intent may still lack an impact. As written, a planned intent with no impact passes every build check and its run then cannot ship at the landing.

### 290. ahoy calls the remote apply the one abcd verb that mutates state outside the machine; land pushes branches to origin and queues pull requests

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1c4698c18919957c · ledger: iss-2610262032354048 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:90` — “the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-land.md:4` — “pushes the branch to `origin`, and queues its open pull request where the merge gate allows”

The ahoy chapter says the remote apply is the only abcd verb that changes anything outside this machine. The land chapter describes a shipped verb that pushes the branch to origin and arms and queues its pull request on the forge. Both are writes outside the machine, so the remote apply cannot be the only one.

### 291. configuration says install asks about the oracle backend; ahoy says the oracle backend is not asked

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4c476ce17c61f7f3 · ledger: iss-2610262032368674 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:33` — “Install asks about visibility, the docs target, the oracle backend”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:893` — “The oracle backend is not asked while host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter”

The configuration chapter lists the oracle backend among the values install asks about. The ahoy chapter says that question is not put to the person while host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter, and that install records host-delegated with a note. Install cannot both ask the question and skip it.

### 292. the ~/.abcd.noindex inventory is stated twice and says load-limits holds three limits in ahoy but two in configuration

- class: scope leakage · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-a5017834b2874c2f · ledger: iss-2610262032368998 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:476` — “the load check's per-machine limits (stray-minutes, extreme-load, wait-load)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:661` — “the load check's two limits in `load-limits`”

Both chapters say their two inventories of ~/.abcd.noindex are one list and must agree. The ahoy tree says load-limits holds three limits (stray-minutes, extreme-load, wait-load), while the configuration prose says it holds two. Because the same ground is covered twice, the two copies now disagree.

### 293. 'decision log' is the live shared-tier store in configuration, but in ahoy it is a legacy single file kept as frozen history

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7f3626302a5444b7 · ledger: iss-2610262032365346 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:805` — “current orientation, the append-only decision log, the external-contribution runbook”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:295` — “any single decisions log the repository already keeps left untouched as frozen history”

The configuration chapter's tier table says the shared work tier holds an append-only decision log. The ahoy chapter seeds a decisions folder with one file per decision, and treats any single decisions log as frozen history that is left untouched. One name points to two different things: the current decision store in one chapter and the retired legacy file in the other.

### 294. adapters has ahoy redirecting prompt exports into ~/.abcd.noindex/history/< root-sha>/; ahoy says history/ holds the registry only

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c1ffd3841d8cae0d · ledger: iss-2610262032379645 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:289` — “which ahoy redirects into `~/.abcd.noindex/history/<root-sha>/prompt-exports/` via the `<repo>/prompt-exports` symlink”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:427` — “the REGISTRY only: identity and lineage keyed on the”

The adapters chapter says ahoy redirects RepoPrompt prompt exports into a prompt-exports folder under ~/.abcd.noindex/history/< root-sha>/, through a symlink in the repository. The ahoy chapter defines history/ as the registry only, holding identity and lineage, and its inventory has no prompt-exports entry and no such symlink. Both cannot be true.

### 295. ahoy says the docs check with empty roots warns at exit 0; the lint contract says a warning raises the exit code to 1

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-378f137505137b22 · ledger: iss-2610262032378831 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:1017` — “document and warns that nothing was checked, at exit 0”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:34` — “Raises the exit code to 1 on an otherwise-clean run”

The ahoy chapter says a seeded docs-lint config with roots [] runs, warns that nothing was checked, and exits 0. The lint contract says the docs gate follows the tri-state exit rule, where a warning raises the exit code to 1 on an otherwise clean run. Under that rule, the same run cannot both warn and exit 0.

### 296. universal patterns puts the record of setup questions and answers in logs/ahoy/< timestamp>/prompts.json; ahoy writes it to .abcd/.work.local/interviews/

- class: scope leakage · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-22c3f84ba8c2dfd4 · ledger: iss-2610262032383787 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:101` — “what was asked, what was answered”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:879` — “The repository's answers go to `.abcd/.work.local/interviews/setup-<stamp>.json`”

The universal-patterns log layout puts the record of what ahoy asked and what was answered in a prompts.json under logs/ahoy/< timestamp>/. The ahoy chapter writes that same record, each question as asked with its answer, to .abcd/.work.local/interviews/setup-< stamp>.json. The same artefact has two homes that do not agree.

### 297. agents puts press-release-composer under cite-or-be-dropped validation; disembark says the press release is accepted or refused as a whole

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-08b1eb1c28a8a307 · ledger: iss-2610262032381678 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:20` — “each feeding one verb that validates its output under a cite-or-be-dropped rule”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:185` — “The document stands or falls whole”

The agent catalog groups press-release-composer with the agents whose output is validated under a cite-or-be-dropped rule, and contrasts that with the changelog composer, whose payload is refused whole. The disembark chapter says the press release stands or falls whole: a payload citing none of the required paths is refused with exit 2. By the catalog's own terms, that is refusal as a whole, not cite-or-be-dropped.

### 298. the lint contract says documentation-auditor audits it on every disembark; disembark says packing dispatches no agents

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c92970006c432a65 · ledger: iss-2610262032399609 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:70` — “The `documentation-auditor` agent (per `01-agents.md`) audits this contract on every disembark”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “Packing is one deterministic Go run. It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”

The lint contract says, in the present tense, that the documentation-auditor agent audits the contract on every disembark, and its acceptance depends on that run. The disembark chapter says packing is one deterministic Go run that dispatches no agents. Its only agents are the four synthesis agents, and documentation-auditor is not one of them. No disembark step runs the audit the lint contract relies on.

### 299. adapters says a user_docs reader copies the user docs verbatim into the lifeboat; disembark's output shape has only ADRs under docs/

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-35e6a8982d86d03b · ledger: iss-2610262032399341 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:357` — “`docs/{tutorials,guides,reference,explanation}/` | Mirror verbatim”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:152` — “ADRs copied verbatim”

The adapters chapter lists a disembark source reader that copies docs/{tutorials,guides,reference,explanation}/ verbatim. The disembark chapter says the plan lists every file a pack writes, and its output tree carries only ADRs under docs/. A user-docs copy would be a path the output shape does not have.

### 300. adapters lists a transcript reader that disembark packs from; embark says no source tier reads a transcript store

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5df5eaf7ecefb0c4 · ledger: iss-2610262032390626 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:350` — “Reads the root-SHA-keyed local corpus; merge by timestamp/content hash when an imported specstory source is also present”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:177` — “No source tier this build packs reads a transcript store”

The adapters chapter says disembark reads into the lifeboat through source readers, including a transcript reader over the root-SHA-keyed local corpus. The embark chapter says no source tier this build packs reads a transcript store, which is why every pack declares the pass B exemption. If the transcript reader existed, that exemption would be false.

### 301. embark treats an unset docs.target as agents_md; configuration says skip is the default

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-808bde266ee53627 · ledger: iss-2610262032400782 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:131` — “`agents_md` or no choice saved gives `AGENTS.md`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:66` — “"skip" is the default, so a default install names abcd”

The embark chapter says that, read with setup's reader, a target with no docs.target saved gets the marker block in AGENTS.md. The configuration chapter says skip is the default, so a default install names abcd in no conventions file. The same reader cannot give agents_md for an unset key in one place and skip in the other. Embark would plant abcd's block in a repository that never chose one.

### 302. universal patterns says the voyage store is tracked under the visibility rule; embark says it is never committed

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-beeb05409782f6ca · ledger: iss-2610262032400242 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:161` — “Both are tracked under the visibility rule”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:264` — “root-commit SHA exactly as the history store is, and therefore never committed”

Universal patterns cites embark section 7 and says both the log tier and ~/.abcd.noindex/voyage/< source-root-sha>/ are tracked under the visibility rule. The embark chapter says the voyage store lives at the operator level, keyed on the root commit, and is therefore never committed. A store outside every repository cannot be committed, or ignored, under a repository's visibility rule.

### 303. launch uses 'documentation-auditor' for its docs-lint warning gate; the agent catalog uses it for an unbuilt agent that audits docs

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ea76a5241abd3c58 · ledger: iss-2610262032415141 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:890` — “a documentation-auditor or hook-compliance warning”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:95` — “a documentation audit over a source or lifeboat `docs/` tree, invoked by other verbs rather than by a user”

Launch's acceptance speaks of a documentation-auditor warning, and its gate list defines the documentation audit as the docs-lint engine run over the configured doc roots. The agent catalog uses the name documentation-auditor for a design-target agent, absent from agents/, that would audit a source or lifeboat docs/ tree when other verbs call it. One name covers two different things.

### 304. the lint contract counts 'previously' as change narration; launch's change-narration gate passes a bare 'previously' as present-tense prose

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4cff3fe8fc53ee98 · ledger: iss-2610262032410731 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:10` — “change-narration (past-tense drift such as "previously" or "formerly")”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:303` — “Bare "now" and bare "previously" are present-tense prose and pass”

The lint contract defines the change narration it lints in docs/ as past-tense drift and gives 'previously' as an example. Launch's change-narration gate, run over the same Markdown under docs/, says a bare 'previously' is present-tense prose and passes. The term means different things in the two chapters, so the same sentence is drift to one check and acceptable to the other.

### 305. universal patterns says issue-ledger entries cannot change after creation; launch has the deferral verb write a waiver into an open record

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1eefd1f7f776665d · ledger: iss-2610262032428223 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:195` — “capture issue-ledger entries (immutable post-create)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:598` — “`deferral_reason`, both schema-accepted keys, written by the ledger's deferral verb”

The artefact-lifecycle table puts issue-ledger entries in the append-only class: never modified after creation. Launch's findings gate depends on records being changed after capture: the ledger's deferral verb writes the deferred_after and deferral_reason pair into the record's frontmatter, and a record may be re-graded. A ledger whose entries never change could not hold either.

### 306. configuration lists every .abcd/config.json key the binary reads, without release.digest; launch's cut reads release.digest from that file

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3fe2a75d9e49c394 · ledger: iss-2610262032429930 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:7` — “Beyond those sixteen, the binary reads only keys a person opts into”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:118` — “`release.digest`, a repository-relative path to a `.json` file”

The configuration chapter names the sixteen keys and then says that beyond them the binary reads only an enumerated set of opt-in keys. release.digest is in neither list. The launch chapter says the cut reads release.digest from the repository's own .abcd/config.json and appends the release to that file, and that abcd itself declares one. The binary therefore reads a config.json key the configuration chapter says it does not.

### 307. ahoy says the user-scope ~/.abcd.noindex/memory/ resolves nothing today; 07-memory has the prompt hook querying the index of both the repo and the user memory scope

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-52daa7c00e2bfbc2 · ledger: iss-2610262032437661 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:470` — “curated cross-project memory pages (a later phase; nothing resolves it today)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:193` — “The hook queries the `index.md` of both memory scopes (repo / user — § 0).”

01-ahoy's inventory of the user-scope home marks memory/ as curated cross-project pages of a later phase that nothing resolves, and puts the person's own recalled notes in memory.json beside the project's .abcd/memory.json. 07-memory states as current that personal preferences land in ~/.abcd.noindex/memory/ and that the hook queries the index.md of both the repo and the user scope. Both cannot describe the same machine: either the hook reads a user-scope memory/ index or nothing resolves that directory.

### 308. 07-memory relies on the first /abcd:ahoy after itd-36 backfilling memory pages' source class; ahoy's detection and apply passes carry no such step

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e6b3b1048d8f53f6 · ledger: iss-2610262032431692 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:42` — “backfilled with `source.class: session_memory` as the default on first `/abcd:ahoy` after itd-36 ships”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:591` — “What it probes, in behaviour rather than in step order: the folder's kind and the plugin root”

07-memory makes ahoy the step that backfills source.class: session_memory onto pre-existing memory pages. 01-ahoy enumerates everything its one detection pass probes and every gap category the apply pass acts on, and an install with no detected gap writes nothing; none of those names the memory store or a source-class backfill. As written, ahoy cannot perform the step 07-memory depends on.

### 309. ahoy calls the library's store 'the local sources corpus'; the library glossary entry forbids 'corpus' as a synonym

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-4f9c91725a376b78 · ledger: iss-2610262032432036 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:472` — “the local sources corpus the library verb maintains and /abcd:library reads”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/library.md:6` — “forbidden_synonyms: ["corpus", "knowledge base"]”

core/library lists 'corpus' among the forbidden synonyms for the library, the person's collection of outside material. 01-ahoy's inventory describes sources/ as the local sources corpus the library verb maintains and /abcd:library reads, substituting the forbidden word for that same collection.

### 310. ahoy calls the setup answers file in the local tier an 'answers record'; the record entry says an artefact with no id and no minting command is not a record

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-d2fa072897f6c63c · ledger: iss-2610262032441828 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:874` — “answers file write one answers record through `interview.Write`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record.md:57` — “an artefact with no id and no minting command is neither”

core/record reserves 'record' for an identified, filed document a command mints and a lint gate reads, and says a working-tier note or a local scratch file, having no id and no minting command, is not one. 01-ahoy calls the setup answers written into .abcd/.work.local/interviews/ an answers record, and its path-entry and provenance files records too, though none carries an id.

### 311. the oracle glossary says a native, CLI, API or MCP oracle adapter is wired behind the seam; ahoy says every backend answer but host-delegated changes nothing about how reviews run

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e3e3d4e386b2fe3b · ledger: iss-2610262032445652 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:898` — “every answer but host-delegated is recorded without changing how reviews run”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/oracle.md:28` — “a concrete **oracle adapter** — native, CLI, API, or MCP — is wired behind the same seam.”

core/oracle defines the alternative to host delegation as a concrete oracle adapter, native, CLI, API or MCP, wired behind the same seam. 01-ahoy says the oracle backend is not asked because host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter, and that every other answer is recorded without changing how reviews run. A reader cannot both wire such an adapter and find that choosing one does nothing.

### 312. the verification matrix checks that ahoy's rules-loader install injects the marker block; ahoy's default docs target writes the block into no conventions file

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-36af3cf1f3c88b6d · ledger: iss-2610262032458879 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:1070` — “a default install writes it into none of the repository's committed conventions files”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:30` — “Marker block from the bundled defaults injected; the rules override skeleton written”

02-verification-matrix's ahoy rules-loader install row, unstaged and so a claim about shipped behaviour, asserts the marker block from the bundled defaults is injected. 01-ahoy says the docs target defaults to skip, so a default install writes the block into none of the repository's committed conventions files and only an agents_md choice plants it. A default-install test written from the matrix row would fail against the behaviour ahoy specifies.

### 313. ahoy calls the remote apply the one abcd verb that mutates state outside the machine; 10-site has abcd site setup configuring forge environments through gh and the host through the hosting adapter

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f5d8c97424387890 · ledger: iss-2610262032458294 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:90` — “the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this machine”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/10-site.md:88` — “The forge environments go through `gh` as the invoking person, and the host through the hosting adapter seam”

01-ahoy asserts that the remote apply is the one abcd verb that mutates state outside this machine. 10-site describes abcd site setup sending the forge environments through gh as the invoking person and the provider's host configuration through the hosting adapter seam, both writes to remote services. Either site setup writes nothing remote or the remote apply is not the only outward-mutating verb.

### 314. the build sequence says ahoy install carries its configuration as flags rather than a wizard; ahoy draws each value question and approval one at a time at a terminal

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d4d5717d70fa1e17 · ledger: iss-2610262032465065 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:848` — “the install asks through the drawn door instead of the line reader”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:55` — “carrying its configuration as flags rather than a wizard”

01-build-sequence describes abcd ahoy install as carrying its configuration as flags rather than a wizard. 01-ahoy specifies that at a terminal the install asks through the drawn door, putting each value question and each approval as a numbered Setup question through an answer loop, with flags only pre-answering those prompts. A question-by-question interactive setup is a wizard, so the two accounts of the install's shape disagree.

### 315. the build sequence has the disembark pack run the host-delegated audit; disembark says packing dispatches no agents and runs no model passes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-387bc770caa83b30 · ledger: iss-2610262032464642 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:155` — “synthesises the lifeboat at the operator-chosen destination, and runs the host-delegated audit”

01-build-sequence's lifeboat milestone says the pack synthesises the lifeboat at the destination and runs the host-delegated audit. 02-disembark says packing is one deterministic Go run that dispatches no agents and runs no model passes, the review and every synthesis artefact being written later by separate sub-verbs over an already-packed lifeboat. The pack cannot both run the audit and dispatch nothing.

### 316. the matrix says the disembark read-only test hashes the source and asserts it byte-identical; disembark says the evidence is a fingerprint of path, mode and size, not a content hash

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-48bc0762da27533a · ledger: iss-2610262032467744 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:234` — “The evidence is a fingerprint, not a content hash”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:38` — “a test hashes the source tree before and after the run and asserts it is byte-identical”

02-verification-matrix's Disembark read-only row states that a test hashes the source tree before and after the run and asserts byte-identity. 02-disembark says the evidence is a fingerprint, not a content hash: it accumulates each entry's path, mode and size and skips .git, so a size-preserving rewrite or a write under .git escapes it. The matrix claims a stronger guarantee than the test the surface chapter describes.

### 317. the matrix's multi-repo corpus check needs a validation corpus; disembark says the corpus manifest is not yet in the tree

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a766bed60e2b5e3d · ledger: iss-2610262032478338 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:216` — “The corpus manifest (`.abcd/corpus.json`) is not yet in the tree.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:45` — “Every milestone acceptance gate passes on each corpus repo, with documented exemptions”

02-verification-matrix carries an unstaged row requiring every acceptance gate to pass on each corpus repo with documented exemptions. 02-disembark says acceptance is checked across a validation corpus but that the corpus manifest (.abcd/corpus.json) is not yet in the tree. The matrix's check depends on a corpus definition the surface chapter says does not exist, so it cannot be run as written.

### 318. the voyage glossary's example has the voyage log record the host oracle a lifeboat was packed with; disembark says the voyage line carries no oracle backend

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1d16b1cbc0660ebe · ledger: iss-2610262032470373 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:276` — “The line carries no oracle backend and no verdict, because nothing produces them yet and an empty field would be a lie.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/voyage.md:53` — “The voyage log says this lifeboat was packed from root SHA `3f9a…` with the host oracle.”

core/voyage's usage example says the voyage log records that a lifeboat was packed from a root SHA with the host oracle. 02-disembark specifies that the voyage line deliberately carries no oracle backend and no verdict, because nothing produces them at pack time and an empty field would be a lie. The log cannot both name the oracle that packed the lifeboat and carry no oracle field.

### 319. disembark calls the packed lifeboat a 'snapshot'; the lifeboat glossary entry forbids 'snapshot' as a synonym

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-80697634ac786a14 · ledger: iss-2610262032482122 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:280` — “the previous snapshot is replaced and its manifest remains in the voyage log”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/lifeboat.md:6` — “forbidden_synonyms: ["backup", "archive", "snapshot", "checkpoint"]”

core/lifeboat lists snapshot among the words that must not substitute for lifeboat. 02-disembark's acceptance says a new snapshot lands at the destination and the previous snapshot is replaced, using the forbidden word for the lifeboat itself.

### 320. the lifeboat glossary says a pack carries a logbook summary and configuration; disembark's output shape carries neither

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f0178017e6ebd8a8 · ledger: iss-2610262032480986 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:121` — “The plan lists the file set a pack writes, and a pack that completes writes that same tree.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/lifeboat.md:20` — “packs the grounded brief, a coverage report, a graveyard, key decisions, logbook summary, and configuration”

core/lifeboat says disembark packs the grounded brief, a coverage report, a graveyard, key decisions, a logbook summary and configuration. 02-disembark says the file set a pack writes is its output shape, which holds _provenance.json, coverage, brief/, graveyard/, rescue/ (intents, specs, spine), retrospectives/, docs/adrs/ and activity/issues/, and no logbook summary or configuration. The glossary describes contents the packer does not write.

### 321. 07-memory names the lifeboat the surface that publishes curated project memory; disembark's pack inventory walks record families and brief sections and writes no memory

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d9baf26f1d1778d7 · ledger: iss-2610262032491690 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:81` — “walk the source and its record families → the planned lifeboat file set”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:118` — “its real consumer is the lifeboat, the surface that publishes curated project memory/provenance (adr-35)”

07-memory routes the restrictive-licence gate to the lifeboat because it is the surface that publishes curated project memory and provenance. 02-disembark's pack inventory walks the source's record families and grounds brief sections into a planned file set whose output shape carries no memory store, and the pack runs only a destination gate and a secret scan before it writes. The lifeboat as packed publishes no curated memory for that gate to judge.

### 322. the matrix's round-trip check expects the embarked repo's memory to be a faithful subset; embark says the memory store does not travel

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ca4fcb40917e7aa3 · ledger: iss-2610262032499433 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:126` — “Terminology, docs and the memory store are **not** embark families; they do not travel.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:44` — “the new repo's memory and decisions are a faithful subset”

02-verification-matrix's Round-trip row, unstaged, checks that after a disembark and an embark the new repo's memory and decisions are a faithful subset of the source's. 03-embark says terminology, docs and the memory store are not embark families and do not travel, so an embarked target receives no memory at all. The row checks for something embark is specified never to write.

### 323. the record glossary says embark writes four record families; embark reads and writes five, adding release retrospectives

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c40d8e5e8fb3dcf4 · ledger: iss-2610262032506491 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:104` — “The five record families — ADRs, issues, intents, specs, release retrospectives — plus the report-only files that inform the run.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record.md:32` — “the four families `embark` writes”

core/record defines 'a record family' by pointing at the four families embark writes in 03-embark, and its disagreement note quotes that chapter as counting four (ADRs, issues, intents, specs). 03-embark reads the lifeboat's five record families, adding release retrospectives, and lands all five. The glossary's anchoring example describes a chapter that no longer says what it cites.

### 324. record-families maps intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release and status; embark's 'record families' are ADRs, issues, intents, specs and release retrospectives

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-42abf5288ffdc283 · ledger: iss-2610262032509493 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:201` — “the five record families land at their canonical locations under the target”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:4` — “The one page that maps abcd's record families (intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release, status)”

core/record-families is the one map of abcd's record families, and a name with no row on it is one nobody has justified; its rows are intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release and status. 03-embark uses 'the five record families' for ADRs, issues, intents, specs and release retrospectives, two of which have no row on the map, so the term names a different set in each document.

### 325. the voyage glossary says the voyage records every embark run; embark says voyage provenance on embark is not built

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b58173cf71021357 · ledger: iss-2610262032502060 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:251` — “an `embark/provenance.json` under the voyage store recording the source path, the source manifest hash, the timestamp and the files written”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/voyage.md:4` — “an append-only record of what abcd *did* to produce a lifeboat (every disembark and embark run)”

core/voyage defines the voyage as an append-only record of every disembark and embark run, and lists embark/provenance.json in its layout. 03-embark places voyage provenance on embark in its design-target surface, none of which is built, and marks the embark/ subtree of the voyage layout not built yet. An embark run today leaves no voyage record, so the definition overstates what the namespace holds.

### 326. embark's lessons speak of 'the previous voyage' and 'the new voyage's brief'; the voyage glossary restricts the word to the operations namespace and forbids it for a project

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a1655910dea6bf42 · ledger: iss-2610262032516143 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:57` — “answer what the previous voyage learned (itd-24)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/voyage.md:59` — “Do not use it for a "project" (too generic)”

core/voyage fixes voyage as the operations namespace that records disembark and embark runs, says not to use it for a project, and leaves the end-to-end project-lifecycle sense unnamed after adr-35. 03-embark's lessons sub-verb answers what the previous voyage learned and ranks lessons against the new voyage's brief, using voyage for a project's lifecycle, the retired sense.

### 327. 'embark' names the grill session's unshipped opening move in the interview glossary and the shipped lifeboat-unpack command in 03-embark

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-982f17602f37b073 · ledger: iss-2610262032517943 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:3` — “Point embark at a packed lifeboat and it writes that project's decisions, issues, intents, specs and release retrospectives into their canonical places in your repo”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/interview/embark.md:4` — “The opening move of a grill session, a design target that does not ship”

The glossary's only embark entry, interview/embark, defines embark as the opening move of a grill session, a design target that does not ship. 03-embark uses embark for the shipped /abcd:embark surface that unpacks a lifeboat into a repository. One name carries two unrelated concepts, and the shipped one has no glossary entry of its own, so a reader resolving the term through the glossary reaches the wrong concept.

### 328. launch says the repo organises work by phase; the phase entry is superseded, sequencing being dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-869ce71352fbb5aa · ledger: iss-2610262032521502 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:489` — “the repo organises work by **phase** (see”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/phase.md:18` — “the sequencing layer is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves”

04-launch's versioning section says versions are an output because the repo organises work by phase, a release number falling out when a stretch of that work is published. core/phase is superseded: the sequencing layer is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, and the phase documents stay only as history. Launch states a retired unit as the live organiser of work.

### 329. the phase glossary names Phase 1 'Substrate'; launch links Phase 1 as the ahoy phase document

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-825ea187a21cedbf · ledger: iss-2610262032520382 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:64` — “ships in [Phase 1] (../../roadmap/phases/phase-1-ahoy.md)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/phase.md:72` — “Phase 1 — Substrate ends when the oracle backend ships and project state is reconciled.”

core/phase's example gives Phase 1 the name Substrate. 04-launch's ownership note says the curated-release cut ships in Phase 1 and links phase-1-ahoy.md for it. One phase number carries two names, so a reader cannot tell which history document Phase 1 is.

### 330. launch lists the roadmap among the record's live documents; the roadmap entry says the status block replaces the roadmap document and the word

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-047107112b5050d3 · ledger: iss-2610262032536646 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:491` — “The brief, intents and roadmap carry no version label.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/roadmap.md:18` — “replaces the roadmap document and the word”

core/roadmap is superseded: the rendered Now / Next / Later status block replaces the roadmap document and the word. 04-launch says the brief, intents and roadmap carry no version label, naming the roadmap as a live part of the design record beside the brief and the intents.

### 331. the version glossary's example has launch ship tag the repo; launch says the verb neither commits, tags nor publishes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c80a09389acb5a87 · ledger: iss-2610262032530356 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:180` — “verb neither commits, tags, nor publishes”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/distribution/version.md:47` — “`launch ship` stamps the release artifact `0.2.0` (strict SemVer, no leading `v`) and tags the repo `v0.2.0`.”

distribution/version's example says launch ship stamps the release artifact and tags the repo v0.2.0. 04-launch says the verb neither commits, tags nor publishes: it writes the dated changelog heading and the release page, and every step past them, the tag included, is performed by a human and by CI. The two disagree on whether launch ship creates the tag.

### 332. the release glossary says a release is published via launch ship; launch says the verb publishes nothing

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d79dbae3a1563dd8 · ledger: iss-2610262032545565 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:10` — “It publishes nothing: the shipped verb writes a dated changelog heading and the release page and stops”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/distribution/release.md:35` — “and for the act of publishing one via `launch ship`”

distribution/release tells the reader to use 'release' for the act of publishing one via launch ship. 04-launch says launch publishes nothing: the shipped verb writes a dated changelog heading and the release page and stops, and CI and a human take it from there. The glossary attributes publication to a verb whose chapter says it never publishes.

### 333. the lifeboat licence gate's allowlist is named .abcd/launch-allowlist.json; launch says that allowlist and release packaging are two mechanisms never given one name

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-b95bb4d4aa6a7848 · ledger: iss-2610262032542009 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:483` — “Two mechanisms, never one name.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/09-provenance-substrate.md:89` — “unless `.abcd/launch-allowlist.json` explicitly names it”

04-launch says the restrictive-licence gate is the lifeboat's, not the release artefact's, and that the gate's evaluation-input allowlist and packaging are two mechanisms, never one name. 09-provenance names that lifeboat gate's allowlist .abcd/launch-allowlist.json, beside a .abcd/launch.allow, so the lifeboat's mechanism carries launch's name, the conflation launch's rule exists to prevent.

### 334. itd-10 lists a lifeboat among the .abcd/ contents destroy deletes; disembark always writes the lifeboat out-of-tree

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-455a5a933ded9090 · ledger: iss-2610262032548523 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-10-purge-uninstall.md:16` — “AND the entire `.abcd/` namespace (including lifeboat, dev artefacts, logbook, and config)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:198` — “The lifeboat is written out-of-tree, so the source repo has nothing to gitignore.”

itd-10's destroy promises to delete the .abcd/ namespace 'including lifeboat'. The disembark chapter writes every lifeboat to an operator-chosen destination outside the source repository, so the source has nothing to gitignore. That leaves no lifeboat under .abcd/ for destroy to remove, and the draft's list of what it deletes names an artefact the surface never puts there.

### 335. itd-106 has abcd switch on auto-deletion of merged branches; ahoy says abcd only mirrors the repository's merge-hygiene settings and never sets them

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-271bfec0afca9b81 · ledger: iss-2610262032556158 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-106-abcd-sets-up-the-ci-a-repo-requires-and.md:70` — “Repository-settings reconciliation: auto-deletion of merged branches”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:85` — “the repository's merge hygiene, which abcd mirrors and never sets: those settings encode the technical facilitator's workflow”

Deleting a branch when it merges is one of the repository's merge-hygiene settings. The ahoy chapter rules that abcd reads those settings into an observed block and never sets them, because they encode the technical facilitator's workflow. itd-106 puts writing that same setting in scope. The two cannot both stand: either the draft drops the write, or the ahoy stance and its split between managed and observed settings change.

### 336. itd-81 names an embark-scaffolder agent; embark says no scaffolder and no model sit in its write path

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-482ecd2873a56f29 · ledger: iss-2610262032558851 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-81-judge-calibration.md:126` — “Agents that transform or scaffold rather than render a verdict (`chat-distiller`, `embark-scaffolder`) remain under itd-5 only.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:101` — “No interactive scaffolder and no model sit in the write path.”

itd-81 exempts `embark-scaffolder` from calibration as an agent that scaffolds rather than judges, which assumes embark runs such an agent. The embark chapter says embark is a deterministic Go run with no interactive scaffolder and no model in its write path. The discipline classifies an agent that the surface it is named for does not have.

### 337. itd-5 applies its rule to a Pass A spine agent spec; disembark packs the spine in one deterministic run that dispatches no agents

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-378a76eababddbfe · ledger: iss-2610262032566420 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:25` — “Pass A spine, Pass B chat-distiller, Pass C principle / artefact / brief / press-release agents”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “Packing is one deterministic Go run. It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”

itd-5's rule lists the agent specs it governs, beginning with a Pass A spine agent. The disembark chapter says packing, which writes the rescue/spine.md commit-history spine, dispatches no agents and runs no model passes. Its only agents are the ones the later synthesis sub-verbs delegate to. The discipline's scope names a lifeboat agent that the lifeboat surface says never runs.

### 338. itd-11 gives the lifeboat audit to a lifeboat-oracle; disembark's lifeboat review agent is lifeboat-reviewer, and no lifeboat-oracle appears

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-de28ee82b65f569c · ledger: iss-2610262032561511 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-11-pass-b-pitfall-mitigation.md:15` — “the lifeboat-oracle's audit catches and quarantines low-confidence Pass B output”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:178` — “the principles to `principle-distiller` and the review to `lifeboat-reviewer`”

The disembark chapter names the four agents its synthesis steps hand work to, and the one that reviews a lifeboat is `lifeboat-reviewer`. No agent by the other name appears. Either one agent goes by two names, or the draft depends on an agent the surface does not have.

### 339. itd-11 hardens an existing chat-distiller; disembark says the transcript-reading distiller is not built and waits on itd-11

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-493be1d7112c6274 · ledger: iss-2610262032572271 (filed)
