- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:114` — “Not built yet: routing such disagreements to a transcript-reading distiller that emits a finding for the unrecorded-decisions report. Viability is gated on itd-11 (draft)”

itd-11 is scoped as hardening a chat-distiller that already reads transcripts, and it rules out a redesign. The disembark chapter says that distiller is not built yet and that whether it is viable waits on itd-11. Each document waits on the other: the draft assumes the distiller exists, and the surface holds off building it until the draft lands.

### 340. itd-12 has the principle distiller weigh .abcd/work/notes/, reviews and memory; disembark's agents read only packed lifeboat files, and the pack carries none of those sources

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d20d64374dcf128f · ledger: iss-2610262032577014 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-12-work-adapter-weighting.md:15` — “abcd weights `.abcd/work/notes/` (shared working scratch) below ADRs, specs, and memory in the principle distiller”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:307` — “The four lifeboat agents read the packed lifeboat's files”

itd-12 ranks ADRs, specs, memory, reviews and notes as the principle distiller's inputs. The disembark chapter says its lifeboat agents, principle-distiller among them, read the packed lifeboat's files. The pack holds the brief, graveyard, intents, specs, retrospectives, ADRs and an issue snapshot, but no notes, reviews or memory. As the pack is written, the weighting the draft depends on has nothing to weigh.

### 341. itd-15 has every disembark of abcd-cli run an agent audit pass automatically; disembark's pack dispatches no agents, and synthesis runs only as later sub-verbs

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-113d63e32ac5298b · ledger: iss-2610262032578385 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-15-self-dogfooded-sota-audit.md:16` — “Pass C automatically runs a SOTA-prompt-audit pass over every `agents/*.md` file in the repo”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “Packing is one deterministic Go run. It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”

itd-15 makes a Pass C agent run automatically whenever abcd-cli is disembarked, with its findings shipped in the lifeboat. The disembark chapter says packing dispatches no agents and runs no model passes. Synthesis artefacts are written afterwards by explicit sub-verbs over an already-packed lifeboat. An automatic agent pass inside disembark breaks that architecture.

### 342. itd-37 extends principle-distiller into a curator that writes memory pages from specs when they complete; disembark says its lifeboat agents, principle-distiller among them, read the packed lifeboat's files

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8b3b271fa8056cb2 · ledger: iss-2610262032580449 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-37-modification-grammar.md:25` — “At spec completion, `principle-distiller` (the role-extended curator from [itd-36] (../shipped/itd-36-memory-unification.md)) extracts the `## Modification Grammar` section into two memory pages”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:307` — “The four lifeboat agents read the packed lifeboat's files”

itd-37 has `principle-distiller` read a spec's Modification Grammar section when the spec completes and write two memory pages from it. That role needs no lifeboat. The disembark chapter counts principle-distiller among the four lifeboat agents and says they read the packed lifeboat's files. One agent cannot both work only from a packed lifeboat and curate specs in the live repository unless one of the two descriptions changes.

### 343. itd-26 calls the licence gate a launch gate; launch says the restrictive-licence gate is not the release artefact's gate, and that its consumer is the lifeboat

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b8e6ef50824453be · ledger: iss-2610262032585048 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-26-loot-oss-vendor.md:70` — “launch-gate-licence-gate machinery itd-26 needs is the **same** machinery memory ingest needs”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:477` — “The restrictive-licence gate over kept originals is likewise **not this artefact's gate**. Its real consumer is the lifeboat”

itd-26 builds on a substrate it names as including the 'launch-gate-licence-gate'. The launch chapter says the restrictive-licence gate is not this artefact's gate: its real consumer is the lifeboat, it is future and inert at launch, and it insists on 'two mechanisms, never one name'. Calling it a launch gate attaches the gate to the surface that says it is not there.

### 344. itd-2609292107351737 has transcripts captured into the history store; ahoy says history/ is the registry only and holds no transcripts

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1bd3c9a7c2e753e0 · ledger: iss-2610262032595554 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609292107351737-every-development-session-records-what.md:21` — “When a transcript is captured into the history store, abcd keeps the per-message token counts”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:428` — “ahoy owns it; it holds no transcripts”

The draft measures token cost 'when a transcript is captured into the history store', which uses 'history store' to mean the transcript corpus. The ahoy chapter's inventory says history/ is the registry of identity and lineage and holds no transcripts, and that the transcript corpus is a separate sibling under transcripts/. The same term names two different stores across the two documents.

### 345. The lab discipline says a lifeboat's sections are intention, method, what worked, what is open, candidates and coverage; disembark takes a lifeboat's sections from the brief-section mapping

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-eef5a47e33646a86 · ledger: iss-2610262032597891 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2609251624540864-a-lab-runs-one-procedure-from-intention.md:40` — “The harvest is assembled in the lifeboat's section shape — intention, method, what worked, what is open, candidates, coverage”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:129` — “Each path derives from the brief-section-to-lifeboat-path mapping in `internal/core/lifeboat/mapping.go`”

The lab procedure assembles its harvest 'in the lifeboat's section shape' and lists six sections. The disembark chapter derives every lifeboat path from the brief-section-to-lifeboat-path mapping, giving brief sections, graveyard, rescue, retrospectives, ADRs, activity and coverage. Only coverage appears in both. 'Lifeboat' names one shape in one document and a different shape in the other.

### 346. The glossary calls a phase the retired sequencing unit; launch says the repo organises its work by phase

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-fad23e81814901a1 · ledger: iss-2610262033003041 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/position.md:25` — “Do not call a position a phase (the retired sequencing unit)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:489` — “the repo organises work by **phase**”

The ledger glossary's position entry describes 'phase' as the retired sequencing unit, which is delivery vocabulary no longer in use. The launch chapter still states that the repo organises work by phase, citing adr-9, and treats a release as what falls out when a stretch of phase work is published. A reader cannot tell from the two documents whether phases are the live unit of work.

### 347. The glossary keeps 'disposition' apart from 'fixed'; launch uses fixed, invalid and deferred as the dispositions of a release-gate finding

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2031e21b3947f005 · ledger: iss-2610262033006141 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:25` — “Do not call a disposition a resolution: resolved means fixed”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:151` — “disposition every finding as fixed, invalid or deferred”

The glossary limits disposition to answering a reading item, in four states (accepted, rejected, declined, held), or to a scope condition, and it warns against calling a disposition a resolution because 'resolved means fixed'. The launch receipts protocol has every finding dispositioned as fixed, invalid or deferred. That is a third vocabulary for the term, and it includes the one value the glossary sets against it.

### 348. itd-59 puts the transcript corpus at ~/.abcd.noindex/history/< root_sha>/; the ahoy page says history/ is the registry only and holds no transcripts.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-988c0d136c6f70ed · ledger: iss-2610262033019185 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-59-autonomous-worker-transcript-capture.md:36` — “every autonomous-run pass's instructions + reasoning lands in the native transcript corpus under `~/.abcd.noindex/history/<root_sha>/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:427` — “the REGISTRY only: identity and lineage keyed on the root-commit SHA. ahoy owns it; it holds no transcripts”

itd-59's whole scope is landing autonomous-run transcripts in the native transcript corpus under ~/.abcd.noindex/history/< root_sha>/, and it treats that store as fixed. The ahoy page's inventory says history/ is the registry only, owned by ahoy, and holds no transcripts, and it puts the corpus in a sibling directory, transcripts/< root-sha>/. The two cannot both be right about where the corpus lives. Built from itd-59 as written, capture would write into the registry directory.

### 349. itd-83 puts a pointer to abcd's reviewer agents in the AGENTS.md conventions section that prepare-this-repo owns; the ahoy page says that block never mentions abcd, and the prepare page is retired.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9fb2bd9c1fb75fe0 · ledger: iss-2610262033012386 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-83-review-bar-fires-itself.md:66` — “a one-line pointer in the marked conventions section of `AGENTS.md` that `prepare-this-repo` already owns”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:385` — “The working-conventions block written into `AGENTS.md` never mentions abcd, the page, or any private repository”

itd-83's fallback for a harness that does not run the hook is a one-line pointer naming abcd's reviewer agents, placed in the marked conventions section of AGENTS.md owned by prepare-this-repo. The ahoy page says the working-conventions block written into AGENTS.md never mentions abcd. It also says the preparation was folded into the install and the retired page's name is gone. A pointer that names abcd's agents cannot sit in a block that never names abcd, and the owner itd-83 relies on no longer exists. The other marked block, the marker block, does name abcd, but at the default docs target it is written into no conventions file. So 'install abcd and the review bar is simply on' fails for a harness without hooks either way.

### 350. itd-85 wires a new abcd audit verb into prepare-this-repo's Phase 2 as the conformance report; the ahoy page already gives that phase to abcd lint's JSON form.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dcd70b7d63c801da · ledger: iss-2610262033013099 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-85-audit-verb.md:31` — “Wiring: `prepare-this-repo` Phase 2 consumes `abcd audit --json` in place of the hand-produced gap report.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:362` — “Run `abcd lint` in its JSON form, supplement it, write the gap report to the target's `.abcd/.work.local/scratch/`”

itd-85 makes `abcd audit` the read-only check of repository conformance (three-tier layout, conventions router, decision durability, docs currency) and has prepare-this-repo's Phase 2 consume `abcd audit --json` in place of the hand-produced gap report. The ahoy page says the preparation, now part of the install's plugin page, runs `abcd lint` in its JSON form at its conformance-lint phase, as the engine-backed conformance core, and writes the gap report from that. Two verbs claim the same conformance report for the same phase, and the page itd-85 wires into is retired.

### 351. itd-91 adds a setup question that chooses an AI-acknowledgement convention; the ahoy page already has the install's attribution opt-in, a hook that asks each commit to declare assistance.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-32f923352a02ae56 · ledger: iss-2610262033022683 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-91-ai-attribution-preference.md:31` — “in the onboarding surface (`/abcd:init` / `prepare-this-repo`) offering a selection of acknowledgement conventions”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:317` — “that run installs the committed `prepare-commit-msg` prompt asking every commit to declare whether a tool assisted it, and the choice is recorded”

itd-91 puts one setup question in the onboarding surface (/abcd:init or prepare-this-repo). It offers none, Assisted-by, Co-Authored-By, Generated-by or a custom wording, and applies the answer to every trailer. The ahoy page covers the same ground in the install. An opt-in attribution run installs the committed prepare-commit-msg prompt, which asks every commit to declare whether a tool assisted it, and the choice is recorded. It runs only where the user says the repository requires AI disclosure. The two describe the same setup choice in incompatible shapes: a yes/no hook against a choice among conventions. itd-91 also names a page the ahoy page says is retired.

### 352. itd-62 calls CI, pre-commit and runtime hooks 'the same three-tier model abcd uses elsewhere'; on the ahoy page, the three tiers are the .abcd/ record layout.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-78ea07a08d31217d · ledger: iss-2610262033027180 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-62-pluggable-safety-gate.md:40` — “invocable from CI, pre-commit, and runtime hooks — the same three-tier model abcd uses elsewhere”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:259` — “only then adopts the three-tier `.abcd/` layout”

On the ahoy page, 'three-tier' names the .abcd/ layout that the preparation adopts. itd-62 uses 'the same three-tier model abcd uses elsewhere' for three invocation points: CI, pre-commit and runtime hooks. One name now carries two concepts, and the precedent itd-62 claims points a reader at the record layout, which says nothing about where a gate is invoked.

### 353. itd-8 has a code-rescuer agent decide what code the pack copies; the disembark page says pack is one deterministic run that dispatches no agents.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d97b88475a6ed430 · ledger: iss-2610262033030496 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-8-with-code-bundling.md:31` — “`code-rescuer` agent extended (currently principle-only) to make scope-aware copy decisions”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:75` — “Packing is one deterministic Go run. It dispatches no agents and runs no model passes”

itd-8 says that `disembark pack --with-code` packs the synthesised brief, principles and reviews along with the code, and that a `code-rescuer` agent, described as currently principle-only, makes the scope-aware copy decisions. The disembark page says packing is one deterministic Go run that dispatches no agents and runs no model passes. The principles, press release and review are written afterwards by the synthesis sub-verbs and do not exist at pack time. Its agent roster has no code-rescuer: principles go to principle-distiller. An agent choosing the copy set inside pack cannot coexist with a pack that dispatches no agents.

### 354. itd-90 relies on embark to write the product thinker's answers into the target; embark writes only its record families and never writes anything else from the lifeboat.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-94400eb0e0738111 · ledger: iss-2610262033033258 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-90-brief-interview-for-the-blanks.md:43` — “Embark (itd-88, M5) owns reconciling answers into a target; this intent produces the answers, it does not scaffold the destination.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:204` — “and everything else in the lifeboat informs the report but is never written”

itd-90 produces answers that are ingested back into the brief, and it leaves the write path to embark: 'Embark (itd-88, M5) owns reconciling answers into a target'. The embark page's unpack writes ADRs, issues, intents, specs and release retrospectives, plus the marker block. Everything else in the lifeboat, the brief included, informs the report but is never written, and no interview answers enter its plan. As written, embark's scope cannot carry the dependency itd-90 hands it.

### 355. itd-35 writes its lifeboat report in the repository under .abcd/logbook/audit/; the embark page says lifeboat operations record at the operator level under ~/.abcd.noindex/voyage/, never committed.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b01c709d57778adb · ledger: iss-2610262033042911 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-35-lifeboat-integrity-audit.md:42` — “Verification report output**: `.abcd/logbook/audit/lifeboat-<ts>/report.{json,md}`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:262` — “Lifeboat *operations* write provenance and history to **`~/.abcd.noindex/voyage/<source-root-sha>/`**: the operator level”

itd-35's check of a lifeboat is a lifeboat operation, and it writes its report inside the repository, at .abcd/logbook/audit/lifeboat-< ts>/report.{json,md}. The embark page says lifeboat operations write provenance and history to ~/.abcd.noindex/voyage/< source-root-sha>/, at the operator level and never committed, under adr-35, which superseded the earlier in-repository location of adr-4. The two documents give incompatible homes for the record of a lifeboat operation.

### 356. itd-41 builds a negotiator over ordered phases with Expectation, Milestone and Phase Acceptance; the disembark page says sequence is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, and phases and milestones are retired.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-eb21ca85a2d5beca · ledger: iss-2610262033041268 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-41-phase-negotiator.md:30` — “proposes an ordered set of phases, each with a draft `## Expectation`, `## Milestone`, and `## Phase Acceptance`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:18` — “sequence is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves ([adr-2609212115255771] (../../decisions/adrs/2609212115255771-phases-and-milestones-are-retired.md))”

Everything itd-41 outputs is a phase plan. It proposes ordered phases, each with a draft ## Expectation, ## Milestone and ## Phase Acceptance, grounds costs in phase-acceptance bullets, and leaves the product thinker to write the roadmap/phases/phase-N files under adr-9. The disembark page says sequence is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, citing adr-2609212115255771 (phases and milestones are retired), and calls the Phase 6 document retired. A negotiator over phases presupposes a layer the brief says is gone.

### 357. The announcements intent promises that nobody's session merges into a release being cut; the launch page says the release hold does not stop a merge armed or queued before the reservation.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7edc531cd739ffc4 · ledger: iss-2610262033053387 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609151838312703-sessions-announce-what-they-are-doing.md:24` — “and when I cut a release, nobody's session merges into it.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:770` — “The hold stops a merge from being armed; it does not stop a merge armed, or queued, before the release was reserved”

itd-2609151838312703 promises that while a release is cut, nobody's session merges into it, because every session's merge step waits on the release reservation. The launch page describes the same hold (rel-vX.Y.Z, read by the land step, citing this intent's C7 and C8) and says it only stops a merge being armed. A pull request with auto-merge already on, or already in the merge queue, lands when its checks pass. The runbook has to check for such merges by hand. The intent's guarantee is stronger than the mechanism the launch page says it delivers.

### 358. The routing intent has the install render the proposal, a table with one row per agent, before consent; the ahoy page states the proposal in counts and names no agent.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-c14c99b8068308e9 · ledger: iss-2610262033059301 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609170822093401-the-oracle-choice-is-one-repo-wide-value.md:101` — “Rendering the proposal and writing it only on consent, at machine level”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:765` — “the proposal said in counts (how many agents, how many at each tier, their fan-out bounds), naming no agent so the question fits”

itd-2609170822093401 defines the proposal as a table with one row per agent, and has the install render it and write it only on consent. The ahoy page's oracle-routing offer states the proposal in counts (agents, agents at each tier, fan-out bounds) and names no agent, so that the question fits. The person therefore consents to a table whose rows they are not shown. The two documents describe different things being consented to.

### 359. The decision-adapter intent treats embark's lesson ranking as a judgement the host answers by default; the embark page ranks lessons by term overlap, with no judgement in that step.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-0fa68fc1ec4b7f88 · ledger: iss-2610262033055327 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609221009495079-abcd-s-typed-judgements-can-run-through.md:28` — “the docs lint's present-tense advisory, embark's lesson ranking”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:59` — “ranked by term overlap against the new voyage's brief”

itd-2609221009495079's interface is (state, typed question) to (value, probability), and by default the host's own judgement answers it. Embark's lesson ranking is among the judgement types it can be configured for. The embark page says the lessons sub-verb ranks every retrospective lesson by term overlap against the new voyage's brief and writes nothing. That ranking is a deterministic computation, not a host judgement, so the shadow lab has no host answer to pair with the adapter's, and turning the type on would replace a computation rather than a judgement.

### 360. The harness-version intent names a harness whose version cannot be read as not checked, never as current; the ahoy page's floor warning stays silent when it cannot read a version.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-55acc0e3c1bded81 · ledger: iss-2610262033066869 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610031026190632-when-a-person-runs-abcd-s-check-on.md:19` — “A harness abcd cannot read a version from is named as not checked, with the reason, and never as up to date.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:963` — “No command, no answer, an error exit or no parsable version raises nothing.”

itd-2610031026190632 reuses the installed-harness version reading that setup's floor warning already uses (its decisions 7 and 8), and it says, citing brief invariant 16, that a harness whose version cannot be read is named as not checked, never as up to date. The ahoy page describes that same setup warning: it asks the claude command for its version and warns below the floor. But it raises nothing when there is no command, no answer, an error exit or no parsable version. The same reading against the same floor treats an unreadable version in opposite ways, and the setup's silence is what the invariant forbids.

### 361. itd-30 lets a user-facing intent carry a design fiction in place of a press release; the launch page composes the release page from the press releases of the user-facing intents shipped.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a4d6cb4f156a42f9 · ledger: iss-2610262033062965 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-30-design-fictions-as-intent-format.md:18` — “abcd lets intent authors choose between a press release and a design fiction when capturing a user-facing change.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:103` — “composed from the press releases of the user-facing intents shipped since the last tag”

itd-30 lets the author of a user-facing change choose a design fiction instead of a press release, with one format per intent and no automatic conversion between the two, so a fiction intent has no press release. The launch page composes RELEASE.md from the press releases of the user-facing intents shipped since the last tag. Each intent in that set must be cited once, and persona quotes are carried word for word and checked against their source. A shipped fiction intent leaves the release page nothing to compose from, so the cut's rule cannot be met for it.

### 362. itd-7 relies on disembark running dev-sync before the pack and writing a workspace file into the repo; the disembark chapter has no such step and never writes to the source

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-75a5ceac395beff7 · ledger: iss-2610262033075573 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/02-disembark.md:11` — “writes to the source, and a test fingerprints the source tree before and after”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-7-rp-workspace-portability.md:38` — “dev-sync runs as a pre-pack step (already in brief). Workspace state goes into the lifeboat naturally.”

itd-7 says dev-sync runs as a pre-pack step of disembark, that this step is already in the brief, and (in its press release) that it writes `.abcd/rp/workspace.json` into the repository so the workspace reaches the lifeboat. The disembark chapter says the packer never writes to the source, which a before-and-after fingerprint of the source tree proves. It describes packing as one deterministic pass (inventory, destination gate, secret scan, write, voyage line) whose output paths come from the brief-section mapping, with no pre-pack step and no place in the lifeboat for a workspace file. As written, disembark cannot provide the step itd-7 depends on.

### 363. The embark chapter still calls the judgement over a lifeboat an 'oracle product audit'; itd-125 renamed it a review everywhere

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bc73b0ee06202284 · ledger: iss-2610262033072029 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:248` — “would re-run the oracle product audit against the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-125-the-lifeboat-verdict-says-what-it-is.md:22` — “produced by an oracle, holding a review verdict — three words for one thing.”

itd-125 says the judgement over a packed lifeboat is a review (`abcd disembark review`, returning SHIP, NEEDS_WORK or MAJOR_RETHINK). It says the old wording, an audit produced by an oracle holding a review verdict, was three words for one thing and is now one word in the verb, the flag, the artefact and the prose. The embark chapter's refresh-audit modifier would re-run the oracle product audit and report drift against the disembark-time audit, and its probe 'runs no product audit'. That is the retired wording, still used for the same judgement.

### 364. itd-24 has the embark unpack show earlier retrospectives in the press-release interview; the embark chapter gives that job to the separate lessons sub-verb

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c498e8e2d3efa487 · ledger: iss-2610262033081135 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/03-embark.md:61` — “for the press-release interview to ask which apply”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:55` — “`/abcd:embark from <path>` surfaces predecessor retrospectives during the press-release interview”

itd-24 says `/abcd:embark from <path>` (the unpack) surfaces earlier retrospectives during the press-release interview, and its press release says embark surfaced them in the lifeboat unpack. In the embark chapter, the unpack writes retrospectives verbatim and reports blanks, writes, counts and the marker action. Surfacing them belongs to `lessons`, a separate read-only sub-verb that ranks the retrospectives' lessons for the press-release interview. The two documents disagree on which verb a person runs to see what the previous voyage learned.

### 365. itd-24 says reflect reads a release's intents the way the cut does, but its shipped_in rule is not the one the launch chapter's cut applies

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e01be210324dc27e · ledger: iss-2610262033086503 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:526` — “leaving out an entering record whose `shipped_in:` names a release tag the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:45` — “less any whose `shipped_in` names another release, plus any whose `shipped_in` names this one”

In the launch chapter, the cut gathers records that entered `intents/shipped/` since the previous tag. It leaves out only an entering record whose `shipped_in:` names a release the previous tag already reaches, keeps a record whose value names no such tag, and adds nothing from outside the window. itd-24 claims to read the intents 'the way the release cut reads them', yet it drops any record whose `shipped_in` names another release, a later one included. It also adds any record whose `shipped_in` names this release, even one that entered outside the window. For those records the retrospective's seed and the cut's record set differ, so the claim that both read the same way cannot hold.

### 366. The launch chapter says the repo organises work by phase; itd-24 records that phases are retired and the release is the unit

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b53564d053da2e42 · ledger: iss-2610262033096678 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/04-launch.md:489` — “the repo organises work by **phase**”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:90` — “phases are retired, so `<phase-id>` reads as the release tag”

The launch chapter's versioning section says versions are an output and that the repo organises work by phase (adr-9). Its ownership note also places the release cut in Phase 1. itd-24 rules, citing adr-2609212115255771, that phases are retired, so its `<phase-id>` reads as the release tag and the release is the unit of work. One document treats 'phase' as a live organising unit and the other treats it as a retired word.

### 368. itd-122 says a shipped sub-verb with no table row fails the build; the launch chapter ships `smoke-pages` with no row

### 374. itd-39 names a 'workspace' memory scope; the ahoy chapter says abcd has no workspace layer, only the repository and the user scope

itd-39 queries memory across two scopes, the workspace and the user's personal store, and `<workspace>/.abcd/memory/` wins a conflict over the user scope. The ahoy chapter says abcd manages exactly one kind of folder, a repository, plus one user-scope directory. It says there is no workspace, host or development-environment layer, and that a folder grouping repositories gets no special treatment. ### 384. itd-67 has launch ship write plugin.json and tag the repo; 04-launch says the verb neither commits, tags nor publishes

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:47` — “`/abcd:launch ship` auto-selects the bump tier (patch/minor/major) via the brief §4 phase-completion detection, writes the new version into `plugin.json`, updates `marketplace.json` (version + changelog entry), tags the repo”

### 385. itd-67 keeps a `--version <x.y.z>` override on ship; 04-launch says there is no version flag at all

### 387. itd-67 has the catalog list the plugin with `source: "./"`; 04-launch has the cut replace the catalog's source with the pinned release archive

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4f9008ca74a8f7ad · ledger: iss-2610262033185478 (filed)

itd-67 defines `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with one plugin whose source is `./`, the repository itself. 04-launch says the cut turns the catalog's plugin source into the release's pinned archive wherever the version-location contract declares `publishes_plugin_archive`, which abcd does, so an install receives the cut release and not the working tree. The catalog cannot name both the repository root and a pinned archive as abcd's plugin source.

### 388. itd-73 derives a major bump from any breaking intent; 04-launch says no set of records derives 1.0.0 from a 0.y.z base

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-73-derived-versioning.md:30` — “take the highest-severity `impact`, and compute the next SemVer — any `breaking` → major, else any `additive` → minor, else patch”

At a 0.y.z version, a breaking intent gives 1.0.0 under itd-73 and a minor bump under 04-launch, so the two rules cannot both hold.

### 389. itd-69 says the version lives in both plugin.json locations plus marketplace.json; 04-launch says two locations are the whole of it

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-69-plugin-metadata-lockstep-update.md:31` — “both `plugin.json` locations and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`”

The checker's path set cannot be both three surfaces and two.

### 390. itd-88 names the packer `disembark <repo> to <dest>`; 02-disembark makes bare disembark a read-only listing and packing the `pack` sub-verb

### 391. itd-48 calls the lifeboat review agent `lifeboat-oracle`; 02-disembark calls it `lifeboat-reviewer`

### 392. itd-6 says abcd makes no direct LLM API calls, only RP over MCP; 01-ahoy has delegating verbs send steps straight to a configured provider

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5cb379aa151ac1e2 · ledger: iss-2610262033202441 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:38` — “abcd calls RP via `mcp__RepoPrompt__*` tools. Period. No subprocess spawning of `claude -p`, no direct LLM API calls”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:204` — “A delegating verb whose agent's `oracle.roles` entry points at a configured provider sends the step there itself”

itd-6 makes RepoPrompt over MCP abcd's single integration point, with no direct LLM API calls, and puts direct OpenAI, Google and Anthropic integrations out of scope. 01-ahoy describes an OpenAI-compatible provider adapter: a delegating verb whose `oracle.roles` entry points at a configured provider sends the step there itself, after the provider setup has checked the provider with a real call. abcd cannot both never call an LLM API directly and send steps to a provider it calls.

### 393. itd-6 has ahoy discover RP and lock `oracle.backend = "rp"`; 01-ahoy records host-delegated without asking, as the only answer with an adapter

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a9406ff69dce6b76 · ledger: iss-2610262033219255 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:43` — “and tests reachability. If reachable: lock `oracle.backend = "rp"`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:893` — “The oracle backend is not asked while host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter”

itd-6 scopes a one-time RP setup discovery in ahoy that tests reachability and then locks `oracle.backend` to `rp` (or `codex` or `in-session`). 01-ahoy says the oracle backend is not asked while host-delegated is the only answer with an adapter, and the install records host-delegated. Yet itd-6's status says the RP adapter has been built. ahoy cannot both lock the backend to rp when it finds RP and treat host-delegated as the only backend with an adapter.

### 394. itd-89 files SessionEnd transcripts in the local per-repo store; 01-ahoy keeps the per-repo transcripts folder for opted-in checkouts only

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-25b4d25db5aef0b2 · ledger: iss-2610262033217382 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-89-start-the-transcript-clock.md:18` — “files it in the local per-repo store”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:515` — “local-transcript-roots checkouts whose transcripts are pulled in to < repo>/.abcd/.work.local/transcripts/ instead”

itd-89 says the SessionEnd hook files each transcript in the local per-repo store. 01-ahoy lists the default corpus as `transcripts/<root-sha>/` in the user-scope `~/.abcd.noindex/` home, and says that only checkouts named in `local-transcript-roots` have their transcripts pulled into `<repo>/.abcd/.work.local/transcripts/` instead. A default capture cannot land in both the per-repo store and the user-scope corpus.

### 395. itd-76 places the sources corpus at `~/.abcd/sources/`; 01-ahoy lists it under the user-scope home `~/.abcd.noindex/`

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dfa5b365b2fd5173 · ledger: iss-2610262033224778 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-76-source-provenance-ledger.md:18` — “abcd's user-level home, `~/.abcd/sources/` by default, itself a no-remote git repository”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/01-ahoy.md:472` — “the local sources corpus the library verb maintains”

itd-76 calls abcd's user-level home `~/.abcd/` and puts the local-only sources corpus at `~/.abcd/sources/` by default. 01-ahoy's inventory of the user-scope directory, `~/.abcd.noindex/`, lists `sources/` as the local sources corpus the library verb maintains. Two names for one user-level home send a builder to two different directories for the same corpus.

### 396. 05-intent's cut rewrites every passed target_release to next, so 09-reflect's list of a cut release's unshipped targeted intents is always empty.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-219fac169619d87b · ledger: iss-2610262033228511 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:75` — “The cut moves every target it passes — `next`, or a tag at or below the release it cuts — to `next`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:59` — “The planned intents whose `target_release` names the release and which”

05-intent says the cut moves every target at or below the release it cuts to `next`, in the same write as the dated changelog section, which is before the tag exists. 09-reflect runs only on a release tag the repository already holds and lists the planned intents whose `target_release` names that release. By then no planned intent can still name it. So the seed's list, the interview's warning and the write's `unshipped_targets` refusal (with its proceed flag) can never fire as written.

### 397. 05-intent defers the honoured/diverged/missing gap buckets, but 09-reflect reads gap counts from every ingested review.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-272747155f5b21ec · ledger: iss-2610262033223107 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:553` — “(the `honoured` / `diverged` / `missing` buckets below) and other prose/terminology/PRD-fidelity outputs are **deferred** to a later spec”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:54` — “rollup an ingested review writes, and the honoured / diverged / missing gap”

05-intent records that the press-release prose review, meaning the honoured / diverged / missing buckets, is deferred to a later spec. It describes the audit ingest as writing only per-criterion verdicts and scope-condition dispositions. 09-reflect's seed takes, for each shipped intent, the acceptance rollup an ingested review writes plus the honoured / diverged / missing gap counts, and its metrics report the gap distribution. Either ingested reviews carry gap buckets or the seed has no gap counts to read.

### 398. 05-intent keeps a re-run owed on an ingested review that left a check owed, but 08-abcd says an ingested review leaves nothing to do.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-54033ef1764f0f97 · ledger: iss-2610262033235782 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:327` — “An ingested review whose verdict left a check owed (ruling DQ1c) is listed under its own heading as reviewed and flagged”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:100` — “is reported unreviewed with its reason; an ingested one leaves nothing to do.”

05-intent treats an ingested review whose verdict left a check owed (ruling DQ1c) as a separate case. It is listed as reviewed and flagged, it carries a remedy and a re-emit that rewrites its request for the re-run, and the same reader supplies the record dispatcher's next move for a shipped intent. 08-abcd's account of `abcd <itd-N>` for a shipped intent says an ingested review leaves nothing to do. That drops the re-run still owed after a NOT_MET or INCONCLUSIVE verdict.

### 399. 05-intent gives ADR files as zero-padded NNNN-< slug>.md, but 24-decide mints adr-< yymmddHHMMSS>< rrrr> ids with stamp-named files.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-534472ddc8b0a364 · ledger: iss-2610262033239291 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:93` — “(`.abcd/development/decisions/adrs/`, `NNNN-<slug>.md`, zero-padded)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/24-decide.md:124` — “The id is `adr-<yymmddHHMMSS><rrrr>` — the twelve-digit UTC second stamp and the”

05-intent's itd-44 decision verdict sends capture to 'the existing ADR store' and gives its files as `NNNN-<slug>.md`, zero-padded. 24-decide says new ADR ids come from a timestamp mint that reads no maximum, with files named stamp then slug. Only 0001-0058 keep ordinal names, and a hand-numbered ordinal is exactly the collision the mint was adopted to close. A builder following 05-intent would write the retired filename shape.

### 400. 05-intent names the phase plan as the canonical build order, but 08-abcd orders what gets built by build next's pick order.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6e0be541d84f19ce · ledger: iss-2610262033248041 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:74` — “ID number is *not* an execution-order guarantee — the canonical build order is the phase plan at”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:338` — “read in build next's pick order (itd-2609211116005482): each READY intent is”

05-intent says the canonical build order is the phase plan at `roadmap/phases/`, although elsewhere it records that phases are retired. 08-abcd says the head of Now and the Next list are read in build next's pick order (readiness score, then age), and that the head is the intent the pick would start. The build order cannot be both the phase plan and the pick order.

### 401. 06-capture expects `abcd lint` to count a widening run's admitted, declined and held proposals, but 16-lint's rule set has no such check.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0f1a5e6141cf8b27 · ledger: iss-2610262033241465 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:570` — “**Given** a run of widening items, **when** the bare board or `abcd lint`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:28` — “judges the repository, each as one rule of the set below: the docs through”

One of 06-capture's acceptance criteria expects `abcd lint` to count a widening run's admitted, declined and held proposals, and to name each one that has neither an admission nor a declined or held disposition. 16-lint says bare `abcd lint` runs every target that judges the repository, each as one rule of its v1 set: three-tier-layout, conventions-router, decision-durability, docs-currency, privacy-hygiene, site-gates and identity-positioning. None of those reads the readings store or the admission records.

### 402. 06-capture says the filing-time match runs on the ledger's two unattended writers, but 05-intent's audit ingest is a third writer that files through the match.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-678f6b912630b161 · ledger: iss-2610262033250826 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:123` — “The same match runs on the ledger's two unattended writers, through the same”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:330` — “related to the intent, with the filing-time match”

06-capture names exactly two unattended writers that run the match (promoted inbox reports and the consistency pass) and says what each must leave out of the comparison. 05-intent says a failed or undecided audit ingest captures an issue through the ledger's filer, related to the intent, with the filing-time match. 06-capture's list omits that writer, and with it any rule on which of its fixed lines stay out of the comparison.

### 403. 'Standing disposition' means a reading item's answer in 06-capture and a scope condition's current standing in 05-intent.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-a6d851b0cc3922c0 · ledger: iss-2610262033252259 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:331` — “every scope condition the intent carries, with its standing disposition and the block that disposition came from”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:217` — “makes the standing disposition the one no sibling supersedes”

In 06-capture a disposition is a record answering one reading item (accepted, declined, held, rejected), and the standing disposition is the one no sibling supersedes. In 05-intent a condition disposition is a dated Audit Notes block on a shipped intent's scope condition (survived, narrowed, falsified, untested), read back as its standing disposition. Such a block can be occasioned by a reading item that has a disposition of its own. So one term names two records with different state sets, and they meet at the same reading item.

### 404. 08-abcd says questions in a repository abcd does not manage are not gated, but 17-guard checks abcd's questions against the field limits whether the repository is managed or not.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e2375669e4f7f51b · ledger: iss-2610262033260205 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:184` — “questions are not gated.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:137` — “`question.Default`) wherever the hook runs, managed or not: the setup interview”

08-abcd says a repository abcd does not manage, or one without the local tier, has no badge and its questions are not gated. 17-guard says abcd's question is held to the field limits wherever the hook runs, managed or not, because the setup interview asks its questions before a repository is managed. Under 17-guard a limit finding refuses the question with the host's deny, so only the badge and mode part is skipped in such a repository.

### 405. 18-ideate says capture friction stays at one line, but 06-capture makes a capture one line of text plus one line of remedy.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-e5fb94e7c0b1c3bd · ledger: iss-2610262033262866 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/18-ideate.md:14` — “and capture friction stays at one line”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:71` — “is one line of text and one line of remedy.”

18-ideate says ideate costs capture nothing because capture friction stays at one line. 06-capture says the remedy is required and has no default, and that this tightens the one-line capture on purpose: a capture is one line of text and one line of remedy, and a capture without the remedy is refused with nothing written.

### 406. The intent chapter's audit-loop table never iterates on an INCONCLUSIVE verdict and never rolls it up as UNACHIEVABLE; the build chapter's fix loop fails the round on INCONCLUSIVE exactly as on NOT_MET.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-369c31f201d4177f · ledger: iss-2610262033260091 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:592` — “Fail-closed: recorded as the shipped audit records it, no iterate, no summons, no replan; never flips to `UNACHIEVABLE`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:712` — “a criterion it could not decide (`INCONCLUSIVE`) fails the round exactly as a `NOT_MET` one does”

05-intent's state-coverage table for the loop-to-acceptance audit loop says an INCONCLUSIVE rollup is fail-closed: no iterate, no replan, and it never flips to UNACHIEVABLE (the table is headed 'the loop trigger is NOT_MET only'). 34-build realises that same loop as the build lane's fix-round bound. There an INCONCLUSIVE criterion fails the round and goes to a fresh implementer, using up fix rounds. A lane out of rounds is handed back with the verdict `unachievable`, which lists the criteria the audit could not decide. One page says undecided criteria never drive re-work or an unachievable end; the other makes them do both. 05-intent says its per-intent shape predates the loop's re-scope into build, but its table still states the opposite policy.

### 407. The build's landing runs the spec close as an automatic stage, but the close refuses without an impact judgement that no build check requires and no stage supplies.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-cc6323a3060cef58 · ledger: iss-2610262033277086 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:518` — “the impact is demanded at the close that ships and refused at any earlier one”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:743` — “In the lane's worktree it runs the spec's close (which ships the intent and parks the fidelity receipt)”

05-intent says the impact is demanded at the close that ships the intent: a close with neither a recorded impact nor one given on the call is refused, and planning leaves the judgement owed when none is given. 34-build's landing runs the spec's close in the lane's worktree to ship the intent. Yet none of its start checks (key, ready, open questions, claim sections, hold, blocked, steps, peers) asks for an impact, and the landing passes none to the close. A READY intent planned without an impact therefore builds through every lane and is refused at its last landing. As written, the build cannot finish such an intent.

### 408. 'drain' names both the intent audit's owed-review queue and the top-level verb that works the issue ledger.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-01b2499c7920cf18 · ledger: iss-2610262033270378 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:553` — “the owed set is paid on demand by the bounded drain”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:3` — “`/abcd:drain` is the verb a person types to have the open issue ledger worked unattended”

05-intent calls the capped owed form of the intent audit 'the bounded drain': the command that pays the fidelity-review debt, one audit at a time. 35-drain gives the same word to a different verb, `/abcd:drain`, which works the open issue ledger unattended through implement-loop lanes and never audits. 05-intent has to say 'the top-level drain verb' to tell the two apart, and 35-drain never mentions the other use. Across the two pages, 'drain' names two different things.

### 409. Capture defines 'promoted' as the two-ended join between an issue and an intent; drain hands back as `promoted` any issue whose related_intents names an intent.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0528cc238f5d5ee1 · ledger: iss-2610262033286211 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:189` — “the pair is what "promoted" means: an issue may name an intent it is only related to, and it is promoted into the one that names it back”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:93` — “An issue whose `related_intents` names an intent is handed back under `promoted`, naming each intent: an intent already owns it”

06-capture says 'promoted' means the pair: the issue's related_intents and the intent's related_issues naming each other. An issue may name an intent it is only related to without being promoted. 35-drain hands back under `promoted` every issue whose related_intents names an intent, even when only the issue names it. That includes the audit-check issues the verdict ingest files as merely related to an intent, and 35-drain says an intent already owns them. The same word means a two-way join on one page and a one-way relation on the other.

### 410. The library chapter says the `memory` command was merged into `library`; the memory chapter documents a live `/abcd:memory` verb for a different store.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-09d2e3715bfed6a3 · ledger: iss-2610262033287288 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:11` — “The command merges the two that came before it, `source` and `memory`, under the product thinker's ruling of 2026-10-09”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:3` — “`/abcd:memory` keeps memory notes: short lessons an agent writes so that a later session does not learn them again”

07-library says `library` merges the two commands that came before it, `source` and `memory`, and calls `.abcd/memory/` (distilled, cited pages) 'the memory store'. 37-memory documents `/abcd:memory` as a shipped verb for memory notes kept in `memory.json` layers (`~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json` and `.abcd/memory.json`), a different store with a different shape. So 'memory' and the memory store each name two concepts. 07-library also lists user-scope memory outside the repo as not built, yet 37-memory's machine layer is exactly that.

### 411. The board restates the pick's candidate rule to choose its next-up head, but leaves out the pick's footprint exclusion.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e69b1431dcdec54a · ledger: iss-2610262033292397 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:349` — “so the head is always the intent the pick would choose”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:172` — “less one whose spec's `## Footprint` names no packages to reserve it with (the check `footprint`)”

08-abcd chooses the status block's head from the readiness gate, the build's record-only start checks, the lanes and the peers check, and concludes that the head is always the intent the pick would choose. 34-build's pick also excludes, in a checkout with an `origin` remote, any planned intent whose spec's Footprint names no packages, and the planning verb mints every spec with that section empty. Both pages cover how the head is chosen, and they disagree. An intent with an empty footprint is shown as next up on the board while `abcd build next` passes over it.

### 412. The record page names closing the spec as a READY planned intent's next move; the build chapter makes READY the state from which an intent is built.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-2b21202c8bb04a8d · ledger: iss-2610262033299542 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:101` — “For a ready planned intent, and for its open spec, the move is closing the spec”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:48` — “the implement-readiness gate the intent verb reports: planned, criteria written, the spec linked both ways and written past its stub”

08-abcd says that, for a ready planned intent and for its open spec, the next move `abcd <record-id>` reports is closing the spec, which ships the intent. 34-build defines READY through the implement-readiness gate (planned, criteria written, spec linked both ways and written past its stub) as the condition for starting a build. The close happens only at the landing of the lane that delivers the last step. Following the record page for a READY intent would close its spec and ship it before any of it is built.

### 413. The board's Now row shows one lane and one awaited role per run; the implement chapter runs a run's lanes in parallel up to its ceiling.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6456226a2d16226f · ledger: iss-2610262033301184 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:325` — “a run in progress, with the lane the loop works on, its next stage and the role it waits on”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:386` — “A run works in parallel up to its ceiling (ruling DR6)”

08-abcd's status block lists each intent in a lane as a run in progress, with the lane the loop works on, its next stage and the role it waits on, and its JSON carries a single `lane` object. 27-implement says a run works in parallel up to its ceiling: a stage moves on any lane, several lanes can each await agents, and the status render names every lane alive with each agent it awaits. A run with several lanes alive has no single lane the loop works on. The board's row shape assumes the one-lane-at-a-time loop that the implement chapter replaced.

### 414. Reflect's plain-Terminal interview treats a configured fallback host as a working route; the build chapter says the fallback-host path still waits on a decision.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-915dcc6ebae66b24 · ledger: iss-2610262033306077 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:143` — “when no route of the person's reaches a runner: the role's route is the host, no fallback host is set”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:538` — “the no-host path, where a host-routed role goes to the machine's `runner.fallback_host`, is the process driver's reversal of the host-delegated boundary, and waits on the ADR decision 6 of the intent owes”

09-reflect's interview refuses only when the role's route is the host and no fallback host is set. So a host-routed role with a fallback host configured runs there, with no host session. 34-build describes exactly that no-host path, a host-routed role going to the machine's `runner.fallback_host`, as a reversal of the host-delegated design that waits on an ADR decision the runner intent still owes. One page relies on the path as shipped; the other says it has not been decided.

### 415. The report chapter says the sources store is keyed by the full root-commit SHA; the library chapter names a repository's sources ledger by the first twelve hex digits of its root commit.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-f1519bb6179d5ad8 · ledger: iss-2610262033311711 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:109` — “A repository's ledger is named by the first twelve hex digits of its root commit”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/29-report.md:95` — “The inbox is a machine-scoped store beside the history, transcript, worktree, sources, labs and run stores. The sender key is the reporting repository's full root-commit SHA, the key those stores use”

29-report lists the sources store among the machine-scoped stores and says the full root-commit SHA is 'the key those stores use'. 07-library says a repository's ledger in the sources corpus is named by the first twelve hex digits of its root commit. The two pages cannot both describe the sources store's key correctly.

### 416. The intent chapter defers the honoured/diverged/missing prose audit, while the agent catalogue says the shipped fidelity role returns it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f0058a3c774fe96b · ledger: iss-2610262033319993 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:553` — “The broader **press-release prose review** (the `honoured` / `diverged` / `missing` buckets below) and other prose/terminology/PRD-fidelity outputs are **deferred** to a later spec.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:141` — “per-criterion verdicts plus a three-bucket prose audit (honoured / diverged / missing), each claim carrying a cited evidence pointer.”

05-intent states that the press-release prose review, with its honoured, diverged and missing buckets, is deferred to a later spec. 01-agents describes the shipped single-document fidelity role as returning per-criterion verdicts plus that same three-bucket prose audit, each claim cited. Both documents describe the same shipped role, so they cannot both be right about whether the gap audit is part of its verdict.

### 417. The intent chapter ships a bounded drain for owed audits, while the configuration chapter says nothing drains today.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-de5f62fdc784540c · ledger: iss-2610262033322455 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:328` — “The bounded command that pays the review debt”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:408` — “No `run` seam ships, so nothing drains today.”

05-intent describes the audit sub-verb's owed form as the shipped bounded command that pays the review debt: oldest shipped first, up to a cap. 03-configuration says that because no run seam ships, nothing drains today. Owed fidelity reviews either have a shipped drain or have none.

### 418. The intent chapter says the audit loop was re-scoped into the last stage of the build, while the configuration chapter still stages it as a per-intent mode.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f94f53f1a6997d34 · ledger: iss-2610262033328180 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:578` — “This per-intent shape predates itd-50's 2026-09-21 re-scope, which makes the loop the last stage of `abcd build` rather than a per-intent mode”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:415` — “**Audit-loop mode and budget (staged: itd-50)** are elected **per intent**, in the intent's own frontmatter rather than in `config.json`”

05-intent records that the per-intent audit-mode shape predates a re-scope that makes the loop the last stage of abcd build rather than a per-intent mode. 03-configuration presents the staged audit-loop mode and budget as chosen per intent, in each intent's own frontmatter. Anyone building the loop from the configuration chapter would build the shape the intent chapter calls superseded.

### 419. The intent chapter runs the doc-fidelity gate on every close that ships an intent, while universal patterns calls that pass a draft that is not yet built.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-08b3bbf946b441af · ledger: iss-2610262033335346 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:518` — “A close that ships an intent first runs the doc-fidelity gate over it”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:144` — “the doc-fidelity anti-drift pass planned under **draft intent itd-60** (`intents/planned/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md`; not yet built)”

05-intent says a close that ships an intent first runs the doc-fidelity gate, and that the gate refuses the close on a missing or stale docs review. 04-universal-patterns describes the same doc-fidelity anti-drift pass as planned under a draft intent and not yet built. The gate cannot both run on every close that ships an intent and be unbuilt.

### 420. The intent chapter's issue-drift form writes a report.json in the log tier, while universal patterns says the intent verb writes no report at all.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b6677e5186d5f034 · ledger: iss-2610262033340952 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:329` — “Findings land in `.abcd/.work.local/logs/audit/issue-drift-<ts>/report.json`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:90` — “Most verbs write no report at all: `lint` and its targets, `capture`, `intent`, `guard`”

05-intent states that the issue-drift check's findings land in a report.json under the log tier's audit directory. 04-universal-patterns, describing what ships today, lists intent among the verbs that write no report at all. One of the two statements about what the shipped intent verb writes is false.

### 421. The intent chapter stages the fidelity audit's request under the local reviews directory, while universal patterns puts the same audit's output in a review sub-tier of the log tier.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-7a6ac4997ce3fef8 · ledger: iss-2610262033346897 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:651` — “the emit path stages an ephemeral review request under `.abcd/.work.local/reviews/` (gitignored, report-only)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:120` — “audit/review-< ts>/ (Role 1 itd-1 pass / /abcd:intent audit, itd-1)”

05-intent says the shipped audit keeps its verdict in the intent's Audit Notes, and that its emit stages an ephemeral review request under .abcd/.work.local/reviews/. 04-universal-patterns gives the single-document audit pass a per-run directory, audit/review-< ts>/, in the log tier. The two documents put the same audit's per-run artefact in different directories.

### 422. The intent chapter reserves the word review for change-judgement, while universal patterns calls the audit and consistency sub-verbs review sub-verbs.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-38353fa1648aa045 · ledger: iss-2610262033354966 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:534` — “the four-bucket vocabulary reserves *review* for family-1 change-judgement”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:130` — “registered review sub-verbs of /abcd:intent”

05-intent says the four-bucket vocabulary reserves review for family-1 change-judgement, and its table files audit and consistency under the audit bucket. 04-universal-patterns calls audit and consistency the registered review sub-verbs of /abcd:intent. It applies the reserved word to the promise-versus-reality verbs that the vocabulary keeps out of it.

### 423. The capture chapter edits ledger records after they are filed, while universal patterns classes ledger entries as append-only and unchangeable once created.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f8d61c3fc2aff4a3 · ledger: iss-2610262033366548 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:160` — “a resolved record's edges are history and stay editable”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:195` — “capture issue-ledger entries (immutable post-create)”

06-capture has linking rewrite a record's blocked_by in place, in any status folder, because a resolved record's edges stay editable. Resolving, wontfix, the remedy verb and deferral rewrite records too. 04-universal-patterns puts capture issue-ledger entries in the append-only class, never changed after creation. A lifecycle rule built on that taxonomy would refuse edits the capture verbs make by design.

### 424. The capture chapter keeps a scratch-to-ledger migration as owed design, while the configuration chapter says that migration has nothing left to migrate.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-27e272564119cfa7 · ledger: iss-2610262033374109 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:521` — “The migration rides the `dev-sync work` surface”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1200` — “so the migration this design was drawn around has nothing left to migrate”

06-capture describes a legacy scratch migration, not yet built, that rides the dev-sync work surface and has a migrator seam reserved for it. 03-configuration says capture writes the ledger directly, so the migration the dev-sync design was drawn around has nothing left to migrate. One document treats the migration as pending work and the other treats it as moot.

### 425. The library chapter calls its distilled-pages half the memory store, while the surfaces register says the merge freed the name memory for the notes command.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3afc5377ee653fc8 · ledger: iss-2610262033372159 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:50` — “memory store: ingesting a source, asking a question and the store lint.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:494` — “That merge freed the name `memory`, which now belongs to the notes command”

07-library calls the half of /abcd:library that ingests, asks and lints distilled pages the memory store. The surfaces README says the merge that created library freed the name memory, which now belongs to the notes command and its short lessons. The two documents use the same word for two different stores.

### 426. Exit code 3 means an absent corpus in the library chapter and contention in the land chapter.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c720291535aa09f8 · ledger: iss-2610262033385114 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:210` — “exits 3, a code distinct from a refusal, so a script can tell”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-land.md:201` — “A landing a release cut holds exits 3, contention, as every verb that backs off does”

07-library has every corpus verb exit 3 when no corpus exists, as a code distinct from a refusal. 38-land says exit 3 is contention, used by every verb that backs off, and keeps a failed fetch off 3 because an automation backing off on 3 would wait on no one. An automation that follows the land chapter would wait indefinitely on a library verb whose corpus is simply missing.

### 427. The intent chapter has an armed record-lint rule that checks the promote back-link, while the lint contract lists that check as an unbuilt full-corpus tier.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-212c7a84451f35e8 · ledger: iss-2610262033399864 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:511` — “`related_issues_backlink` flags an intent's `related_issues` entry whose issue's `related_intents` omits the intent”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:54` — “for example a promote back-link between an intent and its source issue, which needs both files in view”

05-intent names related_issues_backlink as an armed record-lint rule. It flags an intent's related_issues entry when that issue's related_intents leaves the intent out. 06-lint gives that same promote back-link as its example of a check for a full-corpus tier that is a design target and not yet built. The check is either armed in the record gate or not yet built.

### 428. The intent chapter lists the armed record-lint rules and their severities by hand, while the lint contract says any literal list of rules belongs in a generated, gated region.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6231d5016eb62a52 · ledger: iss-2610262033407239 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:502` — “The armed record-lint rules that bear on the intent tree are `intent_lifecycle`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “Any literal enumeration of rules in the record belongs in a generated, gated region”

06-lint gives the armed rule set to the JSON configs, and says a literal list of rules in the record belongs only in a generated, gated region, never in a hand-kept table. 05-intent keeps its own hand-typed list of the armed record-lint rules that bear on the intent tree, with their severities. The same ground is covered twice, and the hand-kept copy can drift from the config.

### 429. The intent chapter describes numbered lint codes such as GL005, while the lint contract says rules are named, not numbered.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-3e2f283d6cc1ada7 · ledger: iss-2610262033404989 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:472` — “Lint extractor for GL005 knows both shapes”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “The engine carries no numbered code catalogue: rules are named, not numbered”

05-intent describes, in the present tense, a lint extractor for GL005, beside the codes GL003 and GR002. 06-lint says the engine carries no numbered code catalogue and that rules are named, not numbered. Anyone following the intent chapter would create numbered codes that the lint contract rules out.

### 430. The intent chapter says itd-to-spc link drift warns and never blocks; the verification matrix says the same disagreement is a blocker that refuses to lint.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-764359008b818b00 · ledger: iss-2610262033418681 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:528` — “Drift triggers a warning, not a block (since spec-store state may legitimately lag intent state during work in progress).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:60` — “when an intent's spec reference and the spec's intent reference disagree: the pair refuses to lint until they agree”

05-intent states that link drift 'triggers a warning, not a block' because spec-store state may lag intent state during work in progress. The matrix's Bidirectional link drift row says that when an intent's spec reference and the spec's intent reference disagree 'the pair refuses to lint until they agree', calls it a blocker, and places it in the pre-push gate and CI. One rule cannot both warn and refuse on the same disagreement, so a contributor cannot tell from the record whether a mismatched link stops a push.

### 431. The intent chapter defers the honoured/diverged/missing prose review to a later spec; the verification matrix says the shipped auditor prompt already emits it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3ee8aa951e299a99 · ledger: iss-2610262033425782 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:553` — “and other prose/terminology/PRD-fidelity outputs are **deferred** to a later spec.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:58` — “The shipped auditor prompt emits both halves: per-criterion verdicts over the acceptance criteria, each with a cited evidence pointer and a concerns verdict refused unless it names its concern, **and** the three-bucket prose audit.”

05-intent says the press-release prose review, with its honoured / diverged / missing buckets, and the other prose outputs 'are deferred to a later spec'. The matrix's Intent audit (Role 1) row is not marked staged, so it describes what the binary carries today, and it says the shipped auditor prompt emits per-criterion verdicts 'and the three-bucket prose audit'. The bucket audit cannot be both deferred and shipped.

### 432. The intent chapter says the quoted-text create seeds Why This Matters and Acceptance Criteria; the verification matrix says it also seeds Mechanism and Scope Conditions.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2de1a33b0185f7a8 · ledger: iss-2610262033433919 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:318` — “with Why This Matters and Acceptance Criteria seeded as prompts for the human to fill; assigns `itd-N` and derives the slug from the text”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:53` — “with Why This Matters, Mechanism, Scope Conditions and Acceptance Criteria seeded as prompts to be replaced”

05-intent's create row gives Why This Matters and Acceptance Criteria as the prompts seeded into the new draft. The matrix's Intent capture row says the same create seeds 'Why This Matters, Mechanism, Scope Conditions and Acceptance Criteria'. The seed either carries the two claim sections or it does not, so a test written from one page fails against the other.

### 433. The out-of-scope page says itd-27 (the grill sub-verb) is scoped into the planned phases; the intent chapter says itd-27 is superseded by itd-94 and no grill sub-verb ships.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4c241131bd4cdba6 · ledger: iss-2610262033434648 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/03-out-of-scope.md:166` — “itd-27 (`/abcd:intent grill` sub-verb + glossary), itd-28 (spec-tied reviews in the native spec review store), and itd-34 (three intent kinds with three lifecycle paths) were captured after this brief was written and are scoped into the planned phases.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:319` — “per itd-27, `intents/superseded/`, superseded by itd-94; no grill sub-verb ships”

03-out-of-scope lists itd-27 ('/abcd:intent grill' sub-verb + glossary) among additions that 'are scoped into the planned phases', which presents it as live, scheduled work. 05-intent records itd-27 as sitting in intents/superseded/, superseded by itd-94, with no grill sub-verb shipping. A superseded intent is not scheduled work, so the out-of-scope note cannot hold as written.

### 434. The out-of-scope page frames the brief as the work of eight planned phases; the reflect chapter says adr-2609212115255771 retired the phase.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f2b96b1b8605f602 · ledger: iss-2610262033444397 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/03-out-of-scope.md:3` — “This brief describes the work bundled into the eight planned phases”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:13` — “2609212115255771-phases-and-milestones-are-retired.md) retired the phase; itd-24 decisions 4 and 5)”

03-out-of-scope opens by saying the brief describes the work bundled into the eight planned phases, and later has an intent enter work by being scoped into a phase. 09-reflect says adr-2609212115255771 retired the phase, which is why a retrospective's grain is the release. If the phase is retired there are no planned phases for the brief's work to be bundled into, so one of the two premises is stale.

### 435. The intent chapter names the phase plan under roadmap/phases/ as the canonical build order; the glossary marks phase superseded, with sequencing now dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e5058b642b326bc7 · ledger: iss-2610262033451641 (filed)
