- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:74` — “the canonical build order is the phase plan at”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/phase.md:18` — “the sequencing layer is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, rendered as the Now / Next / Later status block; the phase documents stay as history.”

05-intent says 'the canonical build order is the phase plan at roadmap/phases/', and elsewhere that a planned intent is 'scoped into a roadmap phase', so it uses phase as the live sequencing unit. The glossary's phase entry has status superseded and says the sequencing layer is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, rendered as Now / Next / Later, with the phase documents kept as history. The intent chapter states a retired term in its retired sense as current fact.

### 436. The glossary forbids 'corpus' as a synonym for the library; the library chapter calls the person's collection the 'sources corpus' throughout.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-87e633a72b69d531 · ledger: iss-2610262033467091 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/library.md:6` — “forbidden_synonyms: ["corpus", "knowledge base"]”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:48` — “Six of the verbs act on the sources corpus: creating it, adding a source,”

glossary/core/library.md defines the library as the person's collection of outside material and lists 'corpus' among its forbidden_synonyms. 07-library calls exactly that collection 'the sources corpus' (six verbs 'act on the sources corpus'), and uses 'library' for the command over two stores, the corpus and the in-repo memory store. The record cannot both forbid the word and use it as the canonical name, and the two pages also disagree on what 'library' names.

### 437. 'memory' names two things: the library's in-repo memory store, whose old memory command the library chapter says was merged away, and the glossary's memory note, written with /abcd:memory add and kept on the person's machine.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e165534b0e2013d5 · ledger: iss-2610262033478703 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/memory-note.md:18` — “An agent writes one with `/abcd:memory add` when it learns something worth keeping”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:11` — “The command merges the two that came before it, `source` and `memory`, under”

07-library says the library command merged the earlier source and memory commands, with neither old name surviving as an alias, and calls its in-repo .abcd/memory/ pages 'the memory store'. glossary/core/memory-note.md, whose alias is 'memory', says an agent writes a memory note with /abcd:memory add and that the note stays on the person's machine until promoted. One word names a repository store of distilled source pages and a machine-local store of agent lessons, and the two pages disagree on whether a memory command exists.

### 438. The memory substrate says abcd library's shipped surface is ingest, ask and lint and nothing else; the library chapter's generated appendix lists nine shipped sub-verbs.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2b42c53fea333ce2 · ledger: iss-2610262033471150 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:197` — “The shipped surface carries `ingest`, `ask` and `lint` and nothing else.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:500` — “Sub-verbs: `abcd library add`, `abcd library ask`, `abcd library cite-check`, `abcd library declassify`, `abcd library ingest`, `abcd library init`, `abcd library ledger`, `abcd library lint`, `abcd library sync-banlist`.”

07-memory, describing a would-be recall sub-verb of abcd library, says 'The shipped surface carries ingest, ask and lint and nothing else'. 07-library's appendix, generated from the command tree, lists add, ask, cite-check, declassify, ingest, init, ledger, lint and sync-banlist. The 'nothing else' claim cannot hold beside six further shipped verbs.

### 439. The memory substrate has principle-distiller route pages between a repo scope and a user scope; the library chapter says the curator role and user-scope memory are not built.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4397f5d197a7001e · ledger: iss-2610262033488570 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:16` — “Which scope a curated page lands in is decided by `principle-distiller` at curation time”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:413` — “Not built: a curator role on the `principle-distiller` agent (the agent and the disembark sub-verb it feeds ship; this role does not), ingest and ask run reports, user-scope memory outside the repo, and the automatic extraction of a spec's modification grammar into the store at spec completion.”

07-memory says the scope a curated page lands in is decided by principle-distiller at curation time, across a repo scope and a user scope at ~/.abcd.noindex/memory/, and describes retrieval querying both. 07-library lists as not built 'a curator role on the principle-distiller agent', 'user-scope memory outside the repo', and the modification-grammar extraction 07-memory also describes. A routing decision made by a role that does not exist, into a scope that does not exist, cannot be current behaviour.

### 440. The memory substrate lists external_pdf pages as ingested through abcd library ingest; the library chapter says the binary rejects PDF sources.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-59e891f126aedae0 · ledger: iss-2610262033494841 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:51` — “User-ingested PDF via `/abcd:library ingest <path>`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:355` — “And PDF is a later seam: the binary rejects PDF sources with a clear error until a text-extraction dependency is wired.”

07-memory's closed source-class enum carries external_pdf, described as 'User-ingested PDF via /abcd:library ingest < path>' and immutable after ingest. 07-library says PDF is a later seam and the binary rejects PDF sources with a clear error until a text-extraction dependency is wired. No page can carry a class whose only producer refuses its input.

### 441. The memory substrate says a failed coverage check refuses the next quotation block from that source; the library chapter says nothing enforces the budget at ingest.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-791a99c89edbe335 · ledger: iss-2610262033503137 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:140` — “On fail: refuses next quotation block from that source until coverage drops via summarisation rewrite of existing pages.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:405` — “computed at lint time. Nothing enforces it at ingest.”

07-memory says that when the cumulative coverage check fails, abcd 'refuses next quotation block from that source until coverage drops'. 07-library says the budget is computed at lint time and 'Nothing enforces it at ingest', and that the lint mutates no store state. With ingest unenforced and the lint write-free, nothing is left to make the refusal 07-memory describes.

### 442. The verification matrix says the lifeboat licence gate refuses to publish a kept original without an allowlist entry; the library chapter says that gate is not built.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a911326ab8560f8f · ledger: iss-2610262033500384 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:86` — “and the lifeboat licence gate refuses to publish it without an explicit allowlist entry”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:361` — “That gate is not built, and the shipped ingest classifies restrictive licences without ever refusing on them.”

The matrix's Memory ingest row is not marked staged, so it describes what the binary carries today, and it says the lifeboat licence gate refuses to publish a kept original without an explicit allowlist entry. 07-library says 'That gate is not built' and that the shipped ingest classifies restrictive licences without ever refusing on them. A gate cannot both refuse today and not exist.

### 443. The memory substrate has session_memory pages distilled via dev-sync memory; the board chapter says no dev-sync verb ships and no dev-sync code exists.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7e29ed375ac87a9f · ledger: iss-2610262033514039 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:50` — “distilled by the `internal/core/memory` adapter via `dev-sync memory`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:583` — “no `dev-sync` verb is on any shipped surface, and no dev-sync code exists in the tree.”

07-memory's source-class enum has session_memory pages 'distilled by the internal/core/memory adapter via dev-sync memory', re-distilled on each sync, and names the vendor memory directory as a harvest source for dev-sync memory. 08-abcd states that no dev-sync verb is on any shipped surface and no dev-sync code exists in the tree. A page class produced only through a verb that does not exist cannot be described as working, so one of the two pages is wrong about the tree.

### 444. The board's six-section design reads a recent-logbook section; the build sequence says the logbook location is retired and a detector fails the build on any internal Go source that names it.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-53c3325912099409 · ledger: iss-2610262033526755 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:543` — “**Recent logbook**: the last five entries by modification time”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:176` — “`.abcd/logbook/` is a retired location, held retired by an armed detector: `TestNoRetiredLogbookLocationInSource` fails the build if any non-test Go source under `internal/` so much as names it.”

08-abcd's design target renders section 4, 'Recent logbook: the last five entries by modification time', from the core renderer internal/core/board, and lists only the last-disembark and dev-sync sections as open questions. 01-build-sequence says .abcd/logbook/ is retired and TestNoRetiredLogbookLocationInSource fails the build if any non-test Go source under internal/ names it. Section 4 cannot be built as designed without tripping that detector, and the design does not record that it has lost its source.

### 445. The reflect chapter uses 'voyage' for a project's lifetime ('every retrospective the voyage produced', 'the new voyage's store'); the glossary fixes voyage as the operator-level log of disembark and embark runs.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e4102e56c9c60775 · ledger: iss-2610262033521157 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:201` — “A lifeboat pack carries every retrospective the voyage produced, verbatim, as”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/voyage.md:4` — “an append-only record of what abcd *did* to produce a lifeboat (every disembark and embark run)”

glossary/core/voyage.md defines a voyage as the operations namespace under ~/.abcd.noindex/voyage/< source-root-sha>/, an append-only record of what abcd did to produce a lifeboat. It warns against using the word for a project, and records the end-to-end lifecycle sense as retired by adr-35 and unsettled. 09-reflect says a lifeboat carries every retrospective 'the voyage produced', and that embark writes them into 'the new voyage's store' and ranks lessons against 'the new voyage's brief'. A run log produces no retrospectives and has no store or brief, so the chapter is using the retired lifecycle sense.

### 446. The glossary says embark writes only the four record families; the reflect chapter says embark also writes retrospectives back, sealed with the other record families.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1f1d1935dae770b2 · ledger: iss-2610262033534032 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record.md:66` — “`embark` writes only the four record families, verbatim, into their canonical locations.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:203` — “the other record families. The embark write puts them back into the new”

glossary/core/record.md fixes 'a record family' as one of the four families embark writes (ADRs, issues, intents, specs), with the example that embark writes only those four. 09-reflect says a lifeboat carries retrospectives sealed 'with the other record families' and that 'The embark write puts them back into the new voyage's store'. Either retrospectives are a fifth family that embark writes, or embark writes only four.

### 447. The board chapter calls admissions and surprises 'the issue ledger's two folderless families'; the glossary's one map of record families lists no such families.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-804e7482d38f6bc5 · ledger: iss-2610262033533504 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:85` — “An admission and a surprise are the issue ledger's two folderless families”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:4` — “The one page that maps abcd's record families (intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release, status) and how they relate”

glossary/core/record-families.md presents itself as 'The one page that maps abcd's record families (intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release, status)' and says a name with no row there is a name nobody has justified. 08-abcd names admissions and surprises as two further families of the issue ledger. Either the map is incomplete or the board chapter uses 'family' outside the glossary's closed set.

### 448. The glossary defines a record as an itd, spc, adr, iss or rdg document; the record dispatcher treats dcn, adm, srp and rfm ids as records and gives rdg no dispatch.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-9b80a35daf87d651 · ledger: iss-2610262033548897 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record.md:4` — “One identified, filed document that a command mints and a lint gate reads — an itd-N, spc-N, adr-N, iss-N or rdg-id.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:83` — “`spc-N`, `adr-N`, `dcn-N`, `adm-N`, `srp-N` or `rfm-N` and reports, read-only, what that”

glossary/core/record.md defines a record as one identified, filed document, 'an itd-N, spc-N, adr-N, iss-N or rdg-id'. 08-abcd's abcd < record-id> takes iss, itd, spc, adr, dcn, adm, srp and rfm ids and reports 'what that record is', and says the reading families have no record dispatch. The two pages give different sets as what 'record' covers, so the term's extent is not fixed.

### 449. The glossary defines an intent as a press-release-shaped description of a feature; the intent chapter's discipline kind of intent skips the press release entirely.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-cd946e61da8f705f · ledger: iss-2610262033543354 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/intent.md:4` — “A press-release-shaped description of a feature written before implementation begins, capturing the user problem, proposed solution, and success criteria.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:99` — “Discipline-kind intents skip the press release entirely (no user moment to describe; no customer quote to attribute).”

glossary/core/intent.md defines an intent as 'A press-release-shaped description of a feature written before implementation begins'. 05-intent declares discipline as one of three intent kinds, and says discipline-kind intents skip the press release entirely, state a rule rather than a feature, and never get a spec. The glossary's definition leaves out one of the three kinds the intent chapter declares, so the chapter uses 'intent' more widely than the glossary allows.

### 450. The intent chapter's kinds table maps a standalone intent to one spec (1:1); the record-families map says an intent has one or more specs.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8ffb357cb9856868 · ledger: iss-2610262033557020 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:83` — “One spec (1:1) | itd-3, itd-4, itd-7, most of the corpus”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:23` — “its intent (one or more specs per intent)”

05-intent's kinds table gives standalone the mapping 'One spec (1:1)'. glossary/core/record-families.md says a spec is grouped by 'its intent (one or more specs per intent)', the 1:n relation a remainder spec depends on. A standalone intent with an open remainder spec breaks the 1:1 cell, so the two cannot both describe the relation.

### 451. The glossary says a spec is broken into ordered tasks with acceptance criteria; the intent chapter's spec stub carries Summary, Footprint and Steps sections and no criteria.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c0b08563c9500da2 · ledger: iss-2610262033556324 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/spec.md:4` — “broken into ordered tasks with acceptance criteria”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:203` — “an empty `## Steps` section (a spec listing no step is built as one step)”

glossary/core/spec.md defines a spec as 'broken into ordered tasks with acceptance criteria', decomposed into numbered tasks. 05-intent says planning mints a stub with a Summary placeholder, a Footprint section and 'an empty ## Steps section (a spec listing no step is built as one step)'. One page calls the unit below a spec a task and the other a step, which the glossary's own step entry forbids calling a task, and the stub carries no acceptance criteria.

### 452. The intent chapter makes the grill glossary-aware once a terminology/ directory exists; the glossary's home is .abcd/development/brief/glossary/.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-c231d8c4e992f9f2 · ledger: iss-2610262033559124 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:319` — “Glossary-aware once `terminology/` exists.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/README.md:66` — “The glossary lives at `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/` (the home, per adr-30).”

05-intent says the grill step is 'Glossary-aware once terminology/ exists'. The glossary README says the one canonical glossary lives at .abcd/development/brief/glossary/ (the home, per adr-30), and its grill design keys glossary-aware mode on that directory. Two names point at one directory, and a builder following 05-intent would test for a directory the record does not use.

### 453. The capture chapter lists issues in derived-priority order; the verification matrix says the filtered list is sorted by id.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-77e197a5fc784198 · ledger: iss-2610151422140743 (already open)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:589` — “unblocked first, then severity, with rows blocked by an open dependency”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:67` — “`abcd capture list` with a state filter prints one line per issue, sorted by id.”

06-capture's acceptance says a listing prints its rows in derived-priority order, 'unblocked first, then severity, with rows blocked by an open dependency demoted'. The matrix's Capture filtered list row says abcd capture list with a state filter prints one line per issue, 'sorted by id'. A list cannot be ordered both ways, so a test written from one page fails against the other.

### 454. The glossary allows bare 'the ledger' only for the issue ledger; the library chapter uses bare 'the ledger' for the sources ledger.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-e24eac9749ba609a · ledger: iss-2610262033569882 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/ledger.md:44` — “Use bare "the ledger" only where the issue ledger is unambiguous — inside `capture` surface”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:246` — “the host records the influence through the ledger and tells the person which key was recorded against which decision”

glossary/core/ledger.md says to use bare 'the ledger' only where the issue ledger is unambiguous and to name every other ledger in full, and lists the sources ledger as one of those others. 07-library says the host 'records the influence through the ledger', meaning the per-repository sources ledger. The chapter uses the bare form for a sense the glossary says must always be named in full.

### 455. itd-1 says plan's acceptance-criteria refusal is a record-lint hard block; the intent surface says it is the intent package's own check, not internal/core/lint

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-d0d9ff460ff62f1c · ledger: iss-2610262033567089 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:17` — “`/abcd:intent plan` refuses to promote an intent without it (hard block via the record lint, `internal/core/lint`).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:198` — “Refuses to promote if `## Acceptance Criteria` is missing/malformed (the intent package's own hasAcceptanceCriteria check, not internal/core/lint)”

itd-1 places the refusal to promote an intent without acceptance criteria in the record lint (`internal/core/lint`). The intent surface's lifecycle says the plan step's refusal is the intent package's own hasAcceptanceCriteria check and explicitly not internal/core/lint. Both cannot say where the gate lives: a reader trusting itd-1 expects the record lint to hold committed intents to the section, which the intent surface says no record-lint rule does.

### 456. itd-190 makes a present-but-empty Mechanism section a readiness-gate fault; the intent template says a blank section passes the readiness gate with the nullity recorded

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-82c0658081edca7a · ledger: iss-2610262033578037 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-190-the-claim-recording-gradient-an-intent-s.md:24` — “Prompted, nullable — declined with the nullity token; a present-but-empty section is a gate fault”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:411` — “A blank section passes the readiness gate with the nullity recorded”

itd-190 separates three byte states for a claim section (absent; present but empty, which is a gate fault; the nullity token, which is a claim declined) and says they are never collapsed. The intent surface's template says a blank Mechanism section passes the readiness gate with the nullity recorded, which treats empty as the nullity. One gate cannot both fault and pass the same empty section.

### 457. itd-84 calls the intent_sota gate unbuilt; the intent surface lists intent_sota as an armed record-lint rule at warn

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c17a80f83537f3ac · ledger: iss-2610262033577968 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-84-intent-decomposition.md:122` — “the unbuilt `intent_sota` gate wanted”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:502` — “`intent_sota` (a `planned/` intent carries a non-empty `## SOTA` declaration, armed at warn)”

itd-84 takes SOTA-rooting into its validator as the enforcement that 'the unbuilt intent_sota gate wanted'. The intent surface lists intent_sota among the armed record-lint rules on the intent tree, flagging a planned intent with no non-empty SOTA section at warn. The gate is either unbuilt or armed, and itd-84's scope item rests on it being unbuilt.

### 458. itd-81 requires judge agents, intent-auditor named first, to emit binary verdicts; the intent surface has intent-auditor emit four-valued per-criterion verdicts

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-55a654c7f2118da9 · ledger: iss-2610262033588599 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-81-judge-calibration.md:102` — “Binary verdicts. Severity is structural (a FIX-FIRST list vs a NOTES list)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:326` — “Per-criterion verdicts (`MET` / `MET_WITH_CONCERNS` / `NOT_MET` / `INCONCLUSIVE`) appended to the intent's `## Audit Notes`.”

itd-81 names intent-auditor as the verdict-rendering agent of today and puts binary verdicts, with severity carried structurally rather than graded, into the output contract its calibration scores. The intent surface's audit records each criterion as one of four verdicts, MET, MET_WITH_CONCERNS, NOT_MET or INCONCLUSIVE, including a graded middle. The same agent's output cannot be both binary and four-valued, so a calibration built to itd-81 cannot score the audit as the intent surface specifies it.

### 459. itd-5 relies on intent-auditor's single-document role checking delivery against itd-5's own criteria; the audit refuses any record in disciplines/

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dcc9823dbb4870a1 · ledger: iss-2610262033586792 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:102` — “checks delivered reality against this discipline's acceptance criteria when each agent spec ships”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:326` — “Takes a **shipped** intent and nothing else: a record still in `drafts/`, `planned/`, `disciplines/` or `superseded/` is refused by name”

itd-5, a discipline, says the auditor's single-document role checks delivered reality against this discipline's acceptance criteria when each agent spec ships. The intent surface's audit takes a shipped intent and nothing else and refuses a record in disciplines/ by name. No audit run can judge a discipline's criteria, so the check itd-5 depends on cannot be issued by the surface as written.

### 460. itd-192 decides a verdict by whether 'this phase' wires the producer; the intent surface says phases are retired

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e8aad8da9953893f · ledger: iss-2610262033593092 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-192-an-acceptance-criterion-whose-producer.md:16` — “An acceptance criterion whose producer does not exist is judged by whether this phase wires it”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:95` — “Phases are retired, and this check is what replaces the same-phase rule a bundle once carried”

itd-192's rule turns on one question, whether this phase wires the missing producer, and grades MET_WITH_CONCERNS or NOT_MET on the answer. The intent surface says phases are retired and that the bundle check replaces the old same-phase rule. With no phase as a delivery unit, the discipline's deciding term has no referent, and an auditor cannot apply it as written.

### 461. itd-196 keys its cumulative and closing rehearsals on the phase; the reflect surface says the phase was retired and the release is the grain

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-476366dbfe40d769 · ledger: iss-2610262033596296 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-196-a-capability-is-rehearsed-end-to-end.md:36` — “One full run of everything the phase set out to”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:14` — “retired the phase; itd-24 decisions 4 and 5)”

itd-196 sets its second and third rehearsal rungs on the phase, ending with one full run of everything the phase set out to deliver. The reflect surface records that adr-2609212115255771 retired the phase and makes the release the unit a delivery is closed on. The discipline's rungs are keyed on a unit the brief says no longer exists, so when its closing rung is owed is undefined.

### 462. itd-25 extends an 'intent-fidelity-reviewer'; the intent surface names the one agent that owns intent fidelity intent-auditor

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-30145ff70db326c9 · ledger: iss-2610262034005768 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-25-dredge-cross-corpus-synthesist.md:46` — “`intent-fidelity-reviewer` extension”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:532` — “`intent-auditor` is a single agent in the catalog”

itd-25 extends an intent-fidelity-reviewer to check, when an intent promoted from an issue cluster ships, whether the cluster's issues moved to resolved/. The intent surface says intent fidelity belongs to a single catalog agent, intent-auditor, with three roles. Two names for one agent leave the itd-25 extension without a defined home.

### 463. itd-25 grounds dredge's bare status+help in 'the universal convention'; the intent surface says bare-command-as-help is common, not universal

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-9feb95f02b831800 · ledger: iss-2610262034012499 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-25-dredge-cross-corpus-synthesist.md:34` — “bare invocation = status+help only per the universal convention”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:344` — “Bare-command-as-help is a common abcd convention, not a universal one”

itd-25 justifies its bare invocation as status and help per the universal convention. The intent surface states that bare-command-as-help is a common abcd convention and not a universal one, naming verbs whose bare form prints a plain block or help instead. The convention cannot be both universal and not.

### 464. itd-25 keys the intent side of an issue-to-intent link resolves_issues; the capture surface's promote join writes that side as related_issues

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f00bc507a6dfd19b · ledger: iss-2610262034017438 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-25-dredge-cross-corpus-synthesist.md:44` — “the intent's frontmatter gains `resolves_issues: [iss-N, iss-NM, iss-NO]` reciprocally”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:187` — “the issue in the draft's `related_issues`, and appends the minted id to the”

itd-25's N:1 promotion stamps resolves_issues on the intent as the reciprocal of the issues' related_intents. The capture surface defines the intent half of the same join as related_issues, written when a draft is minted from an issue and read from both ends. Two keys for one back-link would split the join between two fields.

### 465. itd-16 writes the chain verification report under .abcd/logbook/audit/; the intent surface puts the chain sub-verb's receipts in the local ephemeral logs tier

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-51b28cfc2a2db28f · ledger: iss-2610262034027543 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-16-hash-chain-merkle-audit.md:50` — “writes a report to `.abcd/logbook/audit/chain-<ts>/report.{json,md}`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:653` — “The later-phase review/audit verbs write their per-run receipts under the local ephemeral logs tier, `.abcd/.work.local/logs/audit/<sub-tier>-<ts>/`”

itd-16 has the chain sub-verb write its verification report to .abcd/logbook/audit/chain-< ts>/. The intent surface's audit-trail layout says the later-phase audit verbs, the chain sub-verb among them, write their per-run receipts under .abcd/.work.local/logs/audit/< sub-tier>-< ts>/. The same output cannot live in both places, which sit in different tiers.

### 466. itd-21 has the scaffold's starter intent captured as itd-1; the intent create mints a timestamp-numeric id

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7ada5e8184cb0a19 · ledger: iss-2610262034034042 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-21-no-lifeboat-scaffolding.md:32` — “capturing the project's mission as `itd-1`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:185` — “Mints a timestamp-numeric itd-N id through the shared record-id seam”

itd-21 promises a starter intent, kicked off through the intent interview, that captures the project's mission as itd-1. The intent surface's create mints a timestamp-numeric itd-N through the shared record-id seam, so an intent created through it is never itd-1. The scaffold could keep its promise only by bypassing the create path.

### 467. draft itd-165 promises that a failed fidelity verdict becomes visible work; the intent surface's audit ingest already files an issue for every failed or undecided check

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-789e69b5eb7d3ad8 · ledger: iss-2610262034042710 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-165-an-intent-that-fails-its-own-fidelity.md:12` — “A failed fidelity verdict becomes work somebody can see”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:330` — “That issue is captured through the ledger's one filer”

itd-165 claims, as a capability still to be planned, that a failed fidelity verdict becomes work somebody can see. The intent surface says an ingested verdict judging any criterion NOT_MET or INCONCLUSIVE flags the block and captures an issue carrying the check through the ledger's one filer. The same ground is covered twice, once as shipped and once as a draft.

### 468. draft itd-175 promises the product thinker writes down how an intent could be wrong; the readiness gate's grounds already record what would show the conjecture wrong

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5064ad9e362bb5de · ledger: iss-2610262034045777 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-175-the-product-thinker-writes-down-how-this.md:12` — “The product thinker writes down how this could be wrong, and what would show it”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:325` — “it appends the conjecture behind this decision — what is expected, and what would show it wrong — to the intent's `## Grounds` section”

itd-175 claims, as a draft, that the product thinker writes down how this could be wrong and what would show it. The intent surface says the readiness gate's grounds append the conjecture behind each decision, what is expected and what would show it wrong, to the intent's Grounds section. Both documents claim the same recorded falsifier, one as shipped and one as yet to be built.

### 469. draft itd-2609292108373494 hands over 'abcd's grill'; the intent surface says no grill sub-verb ships

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5163e6843f760021 · ledger: iss-2610262034051312 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609292108373494-when-the-person-has-installed-an.md:22` — “abcd's grill hands the interview to it”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:319` — “no grill sub-verb ships”

The draft has abcd's grill hand its interview to an installed interviewing skill, and run abcd's own when there is none. The intent surface records the grill step as superseded and says no grill sub-verb ships; the interview it does ship is the planning interview. The draft names a surface the intent chapter says does not exist, so which interview it hands over is ambiguous.

### 470. draft itd-143 says the brief gains a framing chapter whose position and filename are still to be fixed; the capture surface's reframe reads that chapter's Construal section as a committed surface at a fixed path

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d423ef11f13c580b · ledger: iss-2610262034068157 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-143-the-brief-gains-a-framing-chapter-under.md:47` — “The new section under `01-product/` (position and filename fixed at the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:264` — “The frame is three committed surfaces at fixed paths:”

itd-143 describes the framing section under 01-product/ as work to be done, its position and filename fixed only at its planning interview. The capture surface's reframe record fingerprints the framing chapter's Construal section as one of three committed surfaces at fixed paths. The chapter cannot be both an unbuilt draft deliverable with no fixed path and a committed surface at a fixed path.

### 471. itd-2610141956319695 names a release-receipt finding's fixed/invalid/deferred state its 'disposition'; the capture surface's disposition is the researcher's record answering a reading item

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6e428f1139acd000 · ledger: iss-2610262034072525 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2610141956319695-a-deferred-finding-is-its-own-captured.md:36` — “`disposition`, spelled exactly, and a deferred finding carries a separate field”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:211` — “records the researcher's answer to one reading”

itd-2610141956319695 spells a reviewed finding's three states, fixed, invalid and deferred, in a release receipt field called disposition. The capture surface uses disposition for a separate record type keyed to one reading item, written by its own verb with its own states. One name now covers two unrelated things a reader of the ledger and the receipts must tell apart.

### 472. itd-2610141956319695 defines a deferral as capturing a finding as its own record; the capture surface's deferral is a waiver written onto an existing open record past one cut

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d485a013e97a132a · ledger: iss-2610262034081102 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2610141956319695-a-deferred-finding-is-its-own-captured.md:20` — “A deferral is always a capture. There is no exception.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:327` — “writes the release cut's waiver onto an open record”

Under itd-2610141956319695 a deferral is always a capture: a deferred finding becomes an open issue of its own. The capture surface's deferring writes the release cut's waiver onto an open record that already exists, for a major or critical grade only, and carries it past one cut. A receipt reading deferred and a record carrying a deferral therefore name different acts under one word.

### 473. the disposition glossary keeps disposition vocabulary apart from the issue ledger's wontfix; the capture surface records a wontfix under the token declined, a disposition state

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-2b6fc77cc48c6c3e · ledger: iss-2610262034081412 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:25` — “Do not reuse the issue ledger's open, resolved and wontfix.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:344` — “the token stays `declined`, because a wontfix **is** that non-action”

The glossary gives a disposition four states, declined among them, and says not to reuse the issue ledger's open, resolved and wontfix. The capture surface writes every wontfix's grounds under the token declined, because a wontfix is that non-action. So declined names both a reading-item disposition state and an issue wontfix, the crossing of the two vocabularies the glossary rules out.

### 474. itd-37 has principle-distiller, as itd-36's role-extended curator, extract each spec's Modification Grammar into memory pages at spec completion; the library surface says that curator role is not built

### 504. The intent chapter keeps an UNACHIEVABLE intent in shipped/ and calls a drafts/ move a lifecycle break; itd-50 rules that unachievable reopens the intent to drafts.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-6743d234834a67bc · ledger: iss-2610262034333292 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:596` — “a `drafts/` move would break the lifecycle invariant”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-50-loop-toward-acceptance.md:100` — “Unachievable reopens the intent to drafts”

05-intent's replan surface says a terminal UNACHIEVABLE leaves the intent in shipped/ with its directory byte-untouched, because a drafts/ move would break the lifecycle invariant and read as a partial un-ship. itd-50's decision 3 (product thinker, 2026-09-21) rules the opposite outcome: unachievable reopens the intent to drafts with the reason and its audit notes. A builder of the loop cannot both leave the record where it is and move it to drafts/; the chapter's note that the per-intent shape predates the re-scope does not cover this outcome, which its table and replan paragraph still state as the design.

### 505. The intent chapter's loop treats INCONCLUSIVE as fail-closed with no iteration; itd-50 rules that an undecided criterion fails the round and reopens the work as NOT_MET does.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-ad04bc203acdcc51 · ledger: iss-2610262034335136 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:592` — “no iterate, no summons, no replan; never flips to `UNACHIEVABLE`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-50-loop-toward-acceptance.md:105` — “a criterion the audit could not decide fails the round exactly as a not-met one does”

05-intent's state-coverage table maps INCONCLUSIVE to no iterate, no summons and no replan, never flipping to UNACHIEVABLE, and states the loop trigger is NOT_MET only. itd-50's decision 5 (ruling DQ1a) says a criterion the audit could not decide fails the round exactly as a not-met one does, sending the lane back to a fresh implementer, and records that it supersedes the fail-closed reading. The two cannot both describe what the loop does on an undecided verdict.

### 506. The intent chapter records hand verification as a separate JSON verification receipt; itd-50 rules it is a grounds entry, not a separate receipt.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-059ab2ef4fb136d3 · ledger: iss-2610262034345807 (filed)

One design keeps the sign-off in a local-tier receipt with its own states, the other in the record's append-only grounds; both cannot be what the loop delivers.

### 507. The intent chapter names the Role 1 fidelity agent intent-auditor; itd-50 calls the same actor intent-fidelity-reviewer.

Two names for one agent, one of them in the register the chapter reserves for change review, leaves a builder of the loop unsure which agent it dispatches.

### 508. itd-7 builds its workspace pull on dev-sync, a pre-pack step it says is already in the brief; the board chapter says no dev-sync verb or code exists anywhere.

The planned intent depends on a surface no record here delivers, and its own scope does not build it.

A disembark that writes a file into the source repository is not read-only.

### 514. itd-201 says the itd-200 mode records which hat the human wears so it is not asked again; the board chapter says answering any abcd question resets the mode to managed.

### 515. itd-122 says surface_coverage checks every surface file's sub-verb rows both ways; the board chapter says its table is compared with the command tree in neither direction.

### 516. itd-179 says a capture triage without grounds is refused; the capture chapter says resolving records grounds only when given, their absence parked.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5fcc4ce01dcd6115 · ledger: iss-2610262034428117 (filed)

itd-179 promises that capture's triage routes (promote, resolve, wontfix) take a grounds argument and that a triage without grounds is refused. 06-capture states that resolving records grounds when given with their absence parked by iss-2609091009111294, that grounds are optional on a wontfix, and that a promotion's missing grounds are reported rather than refused. The shipped intent's refusal and the chapter's acceptance of a groundless triage cannot both describe the verbs.

### 517. itd-179 has intent ready refuse when grounds are absent; the intent chapter reports the readiness gate's grounds row as advisory, never withholding readiness.

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-179-the-reasoning-behind-what-was-pursued-no.md:27` — “A grounds argument on `intent ready` and on the capture triage routes (promote / resolve / wontfix), refusal on absence.”

itd-179's scope puts a grounds argument on intent ready with refusal on absence. 05-intent's readiness gate lists the grounds row among the rows reported as advisory that never withhold readiness, their refusals parked, and makes recording grounds an optional write of the gate. A gate that refuses without grounds and one that reports READY without them are different gates.

### 518. itd-177 has the readiness gate refuse an intent that leaves a context claim unrecorded; the intent chapter reports the claim rows as advisory, never withholding readiness.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-532cc7d83ab20756 · ledger: iss-2610262034437300 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-177-an-intent-s-claims-are-typed-and-its.md:13` — “the readiness gate refuses an intent that leaves a context claim unrecorded”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:325` — “are reported as advisory and never withhold readiness, their refusals parked by iss-2609091009111294”

itd-177's title and scope promise readiness-gate refusals per the claim gradient: an intent leaving its scope-condition claim unrecorded is refused, and so is a duplicated or missing condition marker, by name. 05-intent's readiness gate reports the mechanism and scope-condition rows as advisory rows that never withhold readiness, their refusals parked. An intent the shipped intent says the gate refuses is READY under the chapter.

### 519. itd-2609020625405251 makes a condition's standing the latest block naming it; the intent chapter lets a reading-occasioned block stand over a later verdict that does not name its occasion.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bc724d151cf07a78 · ledger: iss-2610262034445775 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609020625405251-a-scope-condition-is-dispositioned-from.md:34` — “A condition's standing disposition is the one in the latest block that names it”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:331` — “A condition's standing is its latest reading-occasioned block where it has one, and otherwise its latest verdict block”

The condition intent says a condition's standing disposition is the one in the latest block that names it, whichever writer wrote that block. 05-intent says the standing is the latest reading-occasioned block where one exists, otherwise the latest verdict block, and that a verdict overrides a reading-occasioned block only where its rationale names that block's occasion, wherever the two sit in the section. A later verdict that does not name the occasion is the standing under the first rule and is overridden under the second, so the fold, and whatever reads a condition's standing from it, differs.

### 520. The intent chapter says only the reading-ingest verb writes origin contributed-by-reading; itd-2609020625400169 has the capture promote path stamp it on the draft it mints.

### 521. itd-2609020625400169 has the reading-item promote link mode write promoted_from and promoted_to; the capture chapter calls those retired names that no reader tolerates.

### 522. itd-104 says abcd gates an idea and only a survivor graduates to a draft intent; the intent chapter calls ideate optional beside a create that drafts any quoted text.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a4eae4cd83da88e3 · ledger: iss-2610262034513980 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:61` — “Moves the file between directories as the new kind dictates”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:301` — “no reclassify writes a discipline, on any shelf”

itd-34 scopes the reclassify subcommand to late kind changes, a draft realised to be a discipline among them, and says it moves the file between directories as the new kind dictates. 05-intent.md says no reclassify writes a discipline on any shelf, that any move into disciplines/ is refused with nothing written, and that a kind change on a draft or planned record leaves the shelf where it is. The two cannot both describe the shipped verb. The same intent also says the plan step proposes a kind for the user to confirm and that the shape role runs continuously from a pre-commit hook, where the surface page says the shipped plan step neither infers nor asks for a kind and no hook invokes the shape scan.

### 529. itd-34 links a bundle member to its shared spec through epic_id and an epic.intent list; the intent surface page links it through spec_id and the spec's intents list.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dce44517292ba38b · ledger: iss-2610262034528274 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:52` — “each intent's `epic_id: spc-N` and `bundle: <bundle-id>`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:235` — “links each spec_id to the shared spec”

itd-34 says each bundle member carries an `epic_id` naming the shared spec, beside `bundle`, and that the spec lists its members as `epic.intent`. 05-intent.md says the bundle command links each member's spec_id to the shared spec and mints the spec with an `intents:` list beside `intent:`. Two names for the one intent-to-spec link: a member written to itd-34's shape carries a key the lifecycle rules and the readers described on the surface page do not read.

### 530. itd-34 calls the three-role fidelity agent intent-fidelity-reviewer; the intent surface page calls the same agent intent-auditor.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-deb52e454f961e73 · ledger: iss-2610262034520240 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:88` — “`intent-fidelity-reviewer` shape-classification role (third role)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:532` — “`intent-auditor` is a single agent in the catalog”

itd-34 attaches the shape-classification role as the third role of `intent-fidelity-reviewer`, the agent it says performs the single-document and cross-document fidelity audits. 05-intent.md says `intent-auditor` is the single agent in the catalog that owns those three roles. The old name survives in a shipped record and names no agent the catalogue holds, so a reader looking it up finds nothing.

### 531. itd-36 calls bare-command-as-render a universal discipline; the intent surface page says it is a common convention, not a universal one.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-efbb03d750b2a83f · ledger: iss-2610262034535349 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-36-memory-unification.md:41` — “Bare invocation renders state per the universal bare-command-as-render discipline.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:344` — “Bare-command-as-help is a common abcd convention, not a universal one”

itd-36 justifies the memory command's bare render as following the universal bare-command-as-render discipline. 05-intent.md states outright that bare-command-as-help is a common abcd convention and not a universal one, naming commands whose bare form prints help or a version block instead of a board. Both cannot hold: either every bare command renders state or some do not.

### 532. itd-28 says no abcd verb files a dated review folder; the intent surface page has the consistency pass write a dated report under .abcd/work/reviews/.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2e4f6b8b4abb2c4d · ledger: iss-2610262034543078 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-28-rp-reviews-into-flow.md:117` — “No abcd verb files a dated review folder: the semantic-gate receipts are abcd's only writer under `.abcd/work/reviews/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:622` — “The report lands at `.abcd/work/reviews/<date>-consistency/00-summary.md` for the corpus”

itd-28's decision 3 states that the semantic-gate receipts are abcd's only writer under .abcd/work/reviews/ and that no abcd verb files a dated review folder, so the dated folders are commissioned by hand. 05-intent.md says the consistency pass's report lands at .abcd/work/reviews/< date>-consistency/00-summary.md, written by its ingest with a review_of_commit pin. Either the consistency ingest is an abcd writer of dated review folders or no such writer exists; the shipped record's account of who writes the reviews shelf no longer matches the surface.

### 533. itd-4 has capture promote call intent new with the issue's body; the capture surface page says promotion mints the draft natively with a by-id pointer, not a copy.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-614971807885a7c4 · ledger: iss-2610262034550860 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-4-issue-capture.md:35` — “promote an `iss-N` entry to an intent draft (calls `/abcd:intent new` with the entry body + bidirectional link)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:186` — “with the slug reused and the body a by-id pointer rather than a copy”

itd-4 scopes `capture promote` as calling `/abcd:intent new` with the entry body and a bidirectional link. 06-capture.md says one invocation mints the draft itself, with the slug reused and the body a by-id pointer rather than a copy, and that this native promotion superseded an earlier command-orchestrated flow; `intent new` was also removed by itd-2609212130136102. A promoted draft cannot both carry the issue's body through intent new and only point at the issue by id.

### 534. itd-4 names the issue ledger's spec-link field related_epics; the capture surface page's schema names it related_specs.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-444d146472d1a82e · ledger: iss-2610262034566586 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-4-issue-capture.md:42` — “`related_epics` (list of `spc-N`)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:417` — “related_specs: [spc-N, ...]”

itd-4 lists the issue frontmatter field holding spec links as `related_epics`. 06-capture.md gives the schema that the writer and the committed-ledger gate share, and there the field is `related_specs`. Two names for one field: a record written to itd-4's schema carries a key the shipped schema does not define.

### 535. itd-4's shipped scope migrates scratch issues through dev-sync; the capture surface page says that migration is not built and rides a dev-sync surface that is only a design target.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4fd3b29ba3ef5db8 · ledger: iss-2610262034567348 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-4-issue-capture.md:46` — “`dev-sync` promotes existing `.abcd/.work.local/issues.md` entries to the structured ledger on first run after install”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:521` — “**Not built yet.** The migration rides the `dev-sync work` surface”

itd-4 places in scope a migration path in which `dev-sync` promotes the entries of .abcd/.work.local/issues.md into the ledger on the first run after install. 06-capture.md says the legacy scratch migration is not built, that it rides the `dev-sync work` surface, and that this surface is itself a design target. A shipped intent's scope rests on a verb that, as the surface page states it, does not exist, so that part of the intent cannot have been delivered.

### 536. The capture surface page counts a promoted inbox report among abcd's automatic filers; itd-2609221656361680 says nothing is filed until a person or a session acts and rules automatic filing out.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a1867b1f355abd1e · ledger: iss-2610262034572130 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:74` — “abcd's own automatic filers: the consistency pass, every”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609221656361680-a-repository-abcd-manages-reports-back.md:45` — “nothing is filed until a person or a session acts”

06-capture.md lists, among abcd's own automatic filers, every promoted inbox report, whose remedy is written as `none (filed automatically)`, a value it says always means a machine filed the record; it also calls the inbox one of the ledger's two unattended writers. The inbox intent says nothing is filed until a person or a session acts and puts any automatic filing out of scope. The word is used in two senses, a record abcd composes versus a filing nobody asked for, so the record a person's promote writes states that it was filed automatically, which the intent says never happens.

### 537. itd-36 says the lifeboat licence gate refuses to surface kept originals; the library surface page says that gate is not built and the ingest never refuses on a licence.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-222c3f31e71772e7 · ledger: iss-2610262034587290 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-36-memory-unification.md:44` — “the lifeboat licence gate refuses to surface `sources/` files without an explicit allowlist entry”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:362` — “is not built, and the shipped ingest classifies restrictive licences without”

itd-36 scopes keeping originals under .abcd/memory/sources/ behind a lifeboat licence gate that refuses to surface those files without an explicit allowlist entry. 07-library.md says the licence gate belongs to the lifeboat, that the gate is not built, and that the shipped ingest classifies restrictive licences without ever refusing on them. The intent's scope likewise lists a curator role on principle-distiller that the library page lists as not built, while the same page calls itd-36 non-decomposable. A shipped intent cannot rely on a gate the surface page says does not exist.

### 538. itd-2609212130146198 has the guard refuse a question while the mode reads managed; the board's surface page has the guard admit abcd's chipped question and set the state from it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a6f26ccfbd2c6f68 · ledger: iss-2610262034582374 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212130146198-the-status-line-badge-is-true-at-every.md:40` — “a question to the human through the host's question tool is refused while the mode reads managed”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:172` — “guard hook, on the host's question tool, admits abcd's own question”

The badge intent says a question to the human through the host's question tool is refused while the mode reads managed, and that the mode verb sets the state. 08-abcd.md says the guard hook admits abcd's own question headed in the chip grammar, sets the state from the chip's role itself, and that a chipped question is never refused on the mode; it also has the answer reset the state through the question tool's PostToolUse hook, not only on the next prompt. A chipped question asked while the mode reads managed is refused under one and admitted under the other.

### 539. itd-2610111707085098 says a hand-given session name is never replaced; the board's surface page replaces it in a fork once abcd has given that name to another session.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-68fdfd4429b55fdf · ledger: iss-2610262034598939 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610111707085098-the-status-line-should-show-which.md:68` — “A name the person gave by hand is never replaced.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:198` — “gave is never replaced, except in a fork of it once abcd has given another”

The session-name intent's decision 10 says a name the person gave by hand is never replaced, and its decision 5 that the person's name always wins. 08-abcd.md says a name the person gave is never replaced except in a fork of it once abcd has given another session that name, where the fork reads the name as abcd's and takes the next free name. A forked, hand-named session whose name abcd has handed out elsewhere keeps it under the intent and loses it under the surface page.

### 540. itd-28's press release lands spec-tied reviews in a store under .abcd/reviews/< spec-id>/; the board reads reviews as dated folders under .abcd/work/reviews/.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0e05abead341e990 · ledger: iss-2610262035005988 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-28-rp-reviews-into-flow.md:33` — “in a per-review directory at `.abcd/reviews/<spec-id>/<NNNN>-<slug>-<ref>/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:290` — “Every folder under `.abcd/work/reviews/` is a row: a dated”

itd-28's press release and scope say every spec-tied review lands as review.json and review.md in a per-review directory at .abcd/reviews/< spec-id>/< NNNN>-< slug>-< ref>/, with an index command and a CI check over that tree. 08-abcd.md says every folder under .abcd/work/reviews/ is a review row, a spec's review carrying its id in a dated folder name. The intent's own decision 1 drops that store, but its press release and scope still state it, so the shipped record describes a review location the surface does not read.

### 541. itd-2609231013154443 names abcd changelog as the release preview; the board's surface page lists changelog as a retired name the launch preview replaced.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-201612db7c4afedf · ledger: iss-2610262035015704 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609231013154443-every-release-arrives-with-its-own-press.md:94` — “The read-only preview (`abcd changelog`, or the `launch` dry run)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:458` — “`version`, whose page retired when the board took the version; `changelog`,”

The release press-release intent scopes the read-only preview as `abcd changelog` or the launch dry run. 08-abcd.md lists `changelog` among the names retired with no alias, answered with the launch preview that replaced it. A reader following the intent types a verb the binary now answers only with its replacement.

### 542. itd-2609212103568351 lists every READY intent under Next; the board's surface page lists the pick's head under Now alone and never under Next.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-04b7b41ec865ffd2 · ledger: iss-2610262035028747 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212103568351-the-bare-abcd-status-board-and-the-site.md:40` — “every planned intent the readiness gate reports READY, in pick order”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:329` — “intent the readiness gate reports READY: the head is listed under Now alone,”

The status-board intent says Next is every planned intent the readiness gate reports READY, in pick order, and that Now is never empty while anything is READY. 08-abcd.md says Next lists every other READY intent because the head is listed under Now alone, never also under Next, and that Now is empty only when no READY intent may start. Under the intent the head appears in both lists and Now is never empty beside a READY intent; under the surface page neither holds.

### 543. The retrospective seed lists planned intents whose target_release names the cut release; itd-2609212103572513's cut has already moved every such target to next.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-db86283e2a09c562 · ledger: iss-2610262035030115 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/09-reflect.md:59` — “The planned intents whose `target_release` names the release and which”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212103572513-an-intent-names-the-release-it-must-land.md:41` — “at the cut, each unshipped target the cut passes becomes `next` (whatever the following release is numbered) in the change that rolls the changelog”

09-reflect.md takes a release tag that has been cut and lists the planned intents whose target_release names that release and did not ship, and its write refuses until they are confirmed. The target intent says that at the cut each unshipped target the cut passes becomes `next`, in the change that rolls the changelog. By the time reflect can run, no planned intent's target still names the release, so the seed's list and the write's unshipped-targets refusal depend on a value the cut has already rewritten.

### 544. itd-48's press release says the shape role went live as a working verb; the intent chapter says itd-48 did not build the shape role

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4845ed4f03727f67 · ledger: iss-2610262035033556 (filed)

itd-48 announces that with all three roles live, /abcd:intent shape moves to a working command surface. The intent chapter says the shape role is not built by itd-48 and was re-homed to itd-34's kinds lint. Both cannot be true of the same shipped record: one says the shape verb exists because of itd-48, the other says itd-48 never delivered it.

### 545. itd-48 puts consistency reports under .abcd/logbook/audit/; the intent chapter puts them on the reviews shelf under .abcd/work/reviews/

These are two different locations and file shapes for the same report, so a reader or builder following one will not find it where the other says it is.

### 546. itd-48 calls the three-role agent intent-fidelity-reviewer (agents/intent-fidelity-reviewer.md); the intent chapter calls the same agent intent-auditor

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3ddcc62a3cf0003d · ledger: iss-2610262035056745 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-48-intent-fidelity-reviewer-roles-2-3.md:54` — “Extend `agents/intent-fidelity-reviewer.md` with a Role 2 prompt section”

Both documents describe one agent that owns the per-intent fidelity role, the cross-document role and the kind-classification role. itd-48 names it intent-fidelity-reviewer and its file agents/intent-fidelity-reviewer.md. The intent chapter names it intent-auditor. That is two names for one concept, and the file path itd-48 asks to extend does not match the agent the chapter describes.

### 547. itd-80 names the verdict-ingest verb abcd intent review ingest; the intent chapter's command tree names it abcd intent audit ingest

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-436e6f36daa44e9c · ledger: iss-2610262035065340 (filed)

The chapter also keeps the word review for change-judgement verbs, apart from the audit verb that writes these verdicts. So one operation carries two verb names.

### 548. itd-42 is scoped as a capability of an existing /abcd:intent grill sub-verb; the intent chapter says no grill sub-verb ships

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ae0ebb823223711d · ledger: iss-2610262035075414 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-42-coherence-aware-grill.md:71` — “this is a capability of the existing `/abcd:intent grill`, not a sibling verb.”
