### 549. itd-42's full grill loads the naming, scope and out-of-scope chapters as well as the invariants and principles; the intent chapter's pre-pass assembles four inputs and nothing else

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9cd6b222b73b99a8 · ledger: iss-2610262035071845 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-42-coherence-aware-grill.md:58` — “A full grill always loads `02-constraints/03-invariants.md`, `02-constraints/04-naming.md`, `01-product/04-scope.md`, `06-delivery/03-out-of-scope.md`, and the `principles/` set”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:320` — “Assembles the four inputs and nothing else, which is the budget: the draft, the brief's numbered invariants (`02-constraints/03-invariants.md`), each principle's rule paragraph, and a one-line index of every other intent (id, title, shelf) on every shelf.”

itd-42 says a full grill always loads 02-constraints/03-invariants.md, 02-constraints/04-naming.md, 01-product/04-scope.md, 06-delivery/03-out-of-scope.md and the principles set. The chapter says the pre-pass assembles four inputs and nothing else: the draft, the invariants, each principle's rule paragraph and a one-line index. The naming, scope and out-of-scope chapters are in one context set and explicitly excluded from the other. The index fields differ too: id, slug, headline and state over three shelves in one, against id, title and shelf over every shelf in the other.

### 550. itd-46 calls bare-command-as-status a universal abcd convention; the intent chapter says it is a common convention, not a universal one

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-65b28dcb4a852949 · ledger: iss-2610262035089991 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:18` — “The bare command (zero arguments) keeps doing what the universal abcd convention says it must: shows status and help, never mutates state.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:344` — “Bare-command-as-help is a common abcd convention, not a universal one”

itd-46 rests its bare-form behaviour on what the universal abcd convention says it must do. The intent chapter says outright that bare-command-as-help is a common abcd convention, not a universal one, and names commands that print help or a version block instead of a board. One document asserts a rule with no exceptions and the other asserts that exceptions exist.

### 551. itd-46 has promotion pass the issue text to the quoted-text create; the capture chapter has promotion mint a draft whose body is a by-id pointer, not a copy

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7346d5cfdab63cb9 · ledger: iss-2610262035091535 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:58` — “change it to call `/abcd:intent` directly with the issue text as the quoted-text argument.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:185` — “One invocation mints the draft under `intents/drafts/` with the slug reused and the body a by-id pointer rather than a copy”

itd-46 changes the promote path to call /abcd:intent directly with the issue text as the quoted-text argument, which would copy the text into the press release. The capture chapter says one invocation mints the draft with the body as a by-id pointer rather than a copy, and records its origin as extracted-from-record rather than through the create path. The promoted draft cannot be both a copy of the issue text and a pointer to it.

### 552. itd-53's press release has an opt-in drainer run owed reviews at loop ends, session edges and pre-commit or CI steps; the intent chapter says nothing starts the drain on its own

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-521fc743d3d347c3 · ledger: iss-2610262035104777 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-53-review-queue-auto-drain-fidelity-gate.md:22` — “This intent adds an opt-in drainer that runs queued reviews at a safe boundary (after a loop, at a session edge, in a pre-commit or CI step — never inside the pure close hook)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:328` — “Nothing starts the drain on its own: no hook, gate or schedule”

itd-53 announces a drainer that runs queued reviews automatically at a safe boundary: after a loop, at a session edge, or in a pre-commit or CI step. The intent chapter says nothing starts the drain on its own, with no hook, gate or schedule. Automatic boundary-triggered draining and a drain that only runs when asked are incompatible descriptions of one surface.

### 553. itd-53 calls the shipped-but-unreviewed listing a consistency gate; the intent chapter uses Consistency for the Role 2 cross-document pass

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c1111b29b12f064c · ledger: iss-2610262035102052 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-53-review-queue-auto-drain-fidelity-gate.md:36` — “A consistency gate / report that lists shipped intents whose latest fidelity review is missing or not-met”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:332` — “Consistency (the whole corpus, or one intent id)”

itd-53 names its list of shipped intents whose fidelity review is missing or not met a consistency gate. In the intent chapter, Consistency is the Role 2 cross-document pass over the whole corpus or one intent, and the shipped-but-unreviewed listing is the owed-reviews form of the audit sub-verb. One name covers two concepts, so a reader cannot tell which surface consistency means.

### 554. itd-53 says entries with no backend stay deferred; the intent chapter says such entries stay owed

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-028e6b59d1ecda3a · ledger: iss-2610262035112905 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-53-review-queue-auto-drain-fidelity-gate.md:35` — “No-backend behavior: entries stay `deferred` (not failed), so a headless run never blocks on an unreachable backend.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:328` — “with no auditor available every entry stays owed and the summary says why nothing ran”

itd-53 names the no-backend state of a queued review deferred. The intent chapter describes the same situation, no auditor available, as every entry staying owed, and its receipt vocabulary (owed, ingested, dead-lettered) has no deferred state. The same state is named with two different words.

### 555. itd-94 says autonomous drain runs are held by the intent readiness gate; the intent chapter says the drain verb's lanes are issues

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ee296f65d70bbebc · ledger: iss-2610262035127167 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-94-an-intent-that-is-not-planned-cannot-be.md:25` — “Autonomous drain runs get the same gate for free: exit 1 is a journaled SKIP, never a guess.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:278` — “a run of the top-level drain verb never does, since its lanes are issues and an issue has no criteria.”

itd-94 says autonomous drain runs get the implement-readiness gate for free, so exit 1 becomes a journaled SKIP. The intent chapter says the lanes of the top-level drain verb are issues, which have no acceptance criteria. An intent readiness gate has no intent to judge in a run whose lanes are issues, so the two documents disagree about what drain runs work on.

### 556. itd-76 puts the sources corpus at ~/.abcd/sources/ by default; the library chapter puts it at ~/.abcd.noindex/sources

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5d164db05a8635b8 · ledger: iss-2610262035135419 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-76-source-provenance-ledger.md:18` — “abcd's user-level home, `~/.abcd/sources/` by default, itself a no-remote git repository”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/07-library.md:64` — “The corpus is the default one under the user-level home, `~/.abcd.noindex/sources`, unless the invocation names another directory.”

Both documents name the default location of the same user-level sources corpus. itd-76 gives ~/.abcd/sources/ and the library chapter gives ~/.abcd.noindex/sources. Only one can be the default, so a person or tool following the other will look in the wrong directory.

### 557. itd-67 picks the release bump tier from phase-completion detection; the intent chapter derives the version from each intent's impact judgement

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-61e6fb596ac25b4f · ledger: iss-2610262035142666 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:47` — “`/abcd:launch ship` auto-selects the bump tier (patch/minor/major) via the brief §4 phase-completion detection”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:393` — “the compatibility judgement the derived version is computed from”

itd-67 has /abcd:launch ship choose patch, minor or major through the brief's phase-completion detection. The intent chapter says the intent's impact field is the compatibility judgement the derived version is computed from, and elsewhere says phases are retired. Two incompatible inputs are named for the same bump decision.

### 558. itd-67 keeps a hand-typed --version override for a release; the status-board chapter says the version is derived and never hand-authored

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b5469dc8bc1e7648 · ledger: iss-2610262035153070 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:56` — “`--version <x.y.z>` remains the override / major-bump escape hatch, not the norm.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:511` — “The version is **derived, never hand-authored**: it is read from the shipped build, not from a literal in the record”

itd-67 keeps --version < x.y.z> as the override and major-bump escape hatch, a version a person types. The status-board chapter says the version is derived and never hand-authored, read from the shipped build and not from a literal. A version a human can set by hand contradicts a version that is never hand-authored.

### 559. itd-67 generates the changelog from git tags, commit and spec history and the launch report; the intent chapter says the cut composes only from terminal record folders

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-04ba2e2d8a0f86ad · ledger: iss-2610262035169561 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:48` — “generated from the canonical history (git tags + commit/spec history + launch report)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/05-intent.md:245` — “only from terminal folders — the cut exits 0 without it”

itd-67 says the changelog is generated from git tags, commit and spec history and the launch report. The intent chapter says the launch cut composes only from terminal folders, so a planned intent whose code is already on main is left out and the cut still exits 0. A changelog built from commit history would include that work. A changelog built from terminal folders leaves it out. The two sources give different changelogs for the same release.

### 560. itd-73 derives the release version from the shipped intents alone; the capture chapter says a resolved issue's impact drives the derived version too

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-35611e742150dfc6 · ledger: iss-2610262035168556 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-73-derived-versioning.md:30` — “gather the intents shipped since the previous release, take the highest-severity `impact`, and compute the next SemVer”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/06-capture.md:405` — “required in resolved/; drives the derived version and changelog inclusion”

itd-73 computes the next SemVer by gathering the intents shipped since the previous release and taking their highest impact. The capture chapter says an issue's impact, required in resolved/, drives the derived version and changelog inclusion. Take a release with a breaking resolved issue and no breaking intent: itd-73 would not bump the major version, and the capture chapter would. The two documents name different inputs for one computation.

### 561. itd-6's scope makes RepoPrompt over MCP the preferred oracle transport ahead of a Codex CLI and the in-session agent; the status-board chapter says every delegated step runs through the harness unless a routing table is accepted

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6a8be1b3c848b43f · ledger: iss-2610262035171024 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:41` — “RP MCP (preferred) → Codex CLI subprocess (alternative for non-Mac / no-RP users — RP is macOS-only) → in-session subagent (final fallback)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:283` — “With no table accepted the lines are absent and every delegated step runs through the harness at `host-decides`.”

itd-6 keeps a three-transport chain with RepoPrompt over MCP preferred, a Codex CLI subprocess second and the in-session subagent as the last fallback. The status-board chapter says that with no routing table accepted, every delegated step runs through the harness at host-decides. One document puts an external route first by default and the other makes the harness the default.

### 562. itd-43 rules its reviews rename moot because no reviews subsystem classifies reviews by kind; the status-board chapter describes a reviews reader whose rows carry a kind and a spec

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-c3c17a64efa1df26 · ledger: iss-2610262035181369 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-43-epic-to-spec-terminology.md:41` — “the Go tree has no reviews subsystem that classifies reviews by kind, so none of these surfaces exists to rename.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/08-abcd.md:311` — “each row `folder`, `kind` (`review` or `receipt`), `scope`, `spec` when the name carries one”

itd-43 says the Go tree has no reviews subsystem that classifies reviews by kind, so there is nothing to rename. The status-board chapter describes a reviews reader whose rows each carry a kind (review or receipt) and a spec read from the folder name. The premise behind the moot ruling no longer matches the surface the brief documents.

### 563. The docs chapter has the spec close refuse without a saved docs review for HEAD, but the build chapter's unattended landing runs that close with no stage that records one

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-8eaff51bf8bff544 · ledger: iss-2610262035195318 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:92` — “The spec close runs it over the intents the close would ship, before anything moves”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:743` — “In the lane's worktree it runs the spec's close (which ships the intent”

10-docs says the doc-fidelity gate runs at the spec close over the intents it would ship, and a missing receipt for HEAD refuses with 'run the docs review first'. 34-build's landing runs the spec close in the lane's worktree to ship the intent, but its lane stages (worktree, brief, implementer, validators: ruthless, security, intent-auditor; landing) never run a docs review or record a docs-fidelity receipt for the lane's head. In a repository where the gate is armed, every spec-closing landing would be refused, so the loop as written cannot deliver an intent unattended.

### 564. The reading chapter's ingest sends a position's input to a model provider, but the implement chapter rests its outage probe on abcd calling no model

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b2493d88530ace92 · ledger: iss-2610262035201511 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:363` — “A position routed to a provider runs there.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:508` — “only by the verdict of a canary agent the lead runs, since abcd calls no model.”

23-reading says a position routed to a provider runs there: the ingest's dispatch form sends the definition and the parked bundle to the provider and ingests the answer, which is abcd itself calling a model service. 27-implement says the model service can be probed only through a canary agent the lead runs, 'since abcd calls no model'. Both cannot be true. A provider-routed dispatch is an abcd call whose loss of the model service the outage design does not account for.

### 565. The guard chapter describes agents abcd starts through its claude runner, but the implement chapter counts agents against the ceiling on the premise that abcd runs no agent

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-297b72709229390c · ledger: iss-2610262035213062 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:385` — “An agent abcd starts through its claude runner has no terminal, so nobody can”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:129` — “abcd runs no agent, so the count it holds”

17-guard describes 'an agent abcd starts through its claude runner', launched with the lane's base commit. 27-implement holds a session's agent ceiling only against the session's own agent_start lines 'because abcd runs no agent'. If abcd starts agents itself, that premise is false, and agents abcd launches can sit outside the count the ceiling is held against.

### 566. The scribe chapter says a reading receives no ledger, but the reading chapter hands the comparative position a prior widening run's ledger items

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-95a407deafc6e442 · ledger: iss-2610262035213176 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/32-scribe.md:6` — “a reading receives a positively included slice of the shipped repository and no ledger”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:62` — “its object is a prior widening run's pre-admission output”

32-scribe states the reading assembler's access rule as absolute: a reading receives a slice of the shipped repository and no ledger, and it counts reading records among the issue ledger's own directories. 23-reading says the comparative position's object is a prior widening run's pre-admission output, those reading records projected to two body fields, and calls this the one positional exception. The scribe chapter's inverse-access premise leaves that exception out.

### 567. The lint chapter calls the outbound gate the only surface that judges harness-leak text before it is public, but the guard enforces a forge-text check on gh pr and gh issue text before it is posted

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-32d25be7f7be7a6c · ledger: iss-2610262035222673 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:91` — “This is the fourth, and it is the only one that judges text BEFORE it is”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:102` — “(a posting `gh pr` or `gh issue` command whose title or body carries a live”

16-lint counts four surfaces that judge the session-URL and tool-footer class and calls `abcd lint outbound` the fourth and the only one that judges text before it is public. 17-guard enforces `forge-text-outbound`, which refuses a posting gh pr or gh issue command whose title or body carries a live agent-session URL or a tool attribution footer. That check also judges the class before the text is public, so the count and the 'only one' claim cannot both hold.

### 568. The identity chapter says bare abcd lint is the gate for positioning drift, but the lint chapter says no gate invokes bare abcd lint and the identity target runs in no gate

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-12a2d39634113eea · ledger: iss-2610262035238503 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/19-identity.md:89` — “and exits `0` even when it reports drift: it is a status render, and the gate is”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:144` — “No gate in this repository invokes bare `abcd lint`.”

19-identity justifies the identity report's exit 0 on drift by saying the gate is bare `abcd lint`, and says the `blocker` severity turns the family into a hard lint gate. 16-lint says no gate in this repository invokes bare `abcd lint` and that the identity target runs in no gate. The drift the identity chapter treats as gated is therefore gated nowhere, and a `blocker` severity has nothing to block.

### 569. 'The memory store' names a store whose ingest takes documents and web addresses in the history chapter, but the memory chapter's store takes notes on stdin and has no ingest

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8f3ebf8c3c9cffbe · ledger: iss-2610262035249588 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:394` — “the memory store's ingest takes a document or a web address”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:74` — “Adding takes no path: the text arrives on stdin, so the verb never opens the”

11-history says the memory store's ingest takes a document or a web address and never a stored transcript. 37-memory describes `/abcd:memory`, whose store is the two memory.json layers. Adding to it takes no path, only text on stdin, and it has no ingest of documents or addresses. One name is used for two stores: the history chapter's is evidently the library corpus, and the memory chapter's is the notes store.

### 570. The history chapter keeps the history directory for ahoy's registry with no transcripts, but the build chapter calls the transcript store 'abcd's history store'

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dca7a4690ca08b74 · ledger: iss-2610262035256103 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:15` — “ahoy's registry stays under `~/.abcd.noindex/history/` and holds no transcripts.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:500` — “transcript lands in abcd's history store, keyed on the repository's root”

11-history places transcripts under ~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/< root-sha>/records/ and says ahoy's registry stays under ~/.abcd.noindex/history/ and holds no transcripts. 34-build says the runner's transcript lands in abcd's history store. 'History store' therefore names both the registry, which holds no transcripts, and the transcript store, so a builder could write transcripts into the wrong tree.

### 571. 'Checked nothing' means a lint that exits 0 in the docs chapter and a refused check that must never exit 0 in the lint chapter

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-e828c45a707bfded · ledger: iss-2610262035256968 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:39` — “A lint that checked nothing (no rule armed,”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:35` — “exits 2 as the target alone does, never `0` over a check that never ran”

10-docs uses 'a lint that checked nothing' for a run with no rule armed or roots holding no document, and keeps its exit at 0. 16-lint uses 'checked nothing' for a target that refused, raises an error and exits 2, 'never 0 over a check that never ran'. The same phrase names two states with opposite exit codes, so a reader cannot tell whether a docs lint with nothing armed is a check that never ran.

### 572. The docs chapter ships the itd-60 doc-fidelity gate, saving receipts keyed by commit; universal patterns calls the itd-60 pass a draft that is not yet built, keyed by input fingerprint.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-98edc4939d947f12 · ledger: iss-2610262035265656 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:76` — “labelled with the commit the checkout stands at, under `.abcd/.work.local/doc-fidelity/<commit>/`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:144` — “the doc-fidelity anti-drift pass planned under **draft intent itd-60** (`intents/planned/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md`; not yet built)”

10-docs lists `fidelity` and `fidelity record` as shipped and says the record sub-verb saves the docs review as a receipt under `.abcd/.work.local/doc-fidelity/<commit>/`. The spec close and the release cut both wait on that receipt. 04-universal-patterns describes the same itd-60 pass as planned under a draft intent and 'not yet built', with a different on-disk contract: a content-addressed `doc-fidelity/<input_fingerprint>/` tier under the log tier. Both cannot hold. Someone building from the patterns chapter would treat a gate that already blocks closes and cuts as future work, and would lay out a second, incompatible store for it.

### 573. The reading chapter derives a position's definition file from its name instead of looking it up; the agent catalogue says the locator finds the definition by its `position` frontmatter field.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ba15b3bc97f11d24 · ledger: iss-2610262035274211 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:187` — “The file is derived from the position, `agents/cold-reading-<position>.md`,”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:317` — “the locator resolves a position to its definition by this field”

23-reading says the definition file is derived from the position as `agents/cold-reading-<position>.md`, 'rather than looked up', and that the frontmatter's `position` is only checked against it afterwards. 01-agents' frontmatter table says the locator resolves a position to its definition by the `position` field, which is a lookup over the prompts. A definition whose filename and frontmatter disagree would be found by one mechanism and missed by the other, so both accounts of resolution cannot be right.

### 574. The decide chapter says a decision record is never edited; the lifecycle taxonomy puts the decisions folder in the compounding-curated class, whose pages are modified, contradicted and deprecated.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-41b679b1f51bc544 · ledger: iss-2610262035280605 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/24-decide.md:68` — “A record is never edited; a correction is a new”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:196` — “Accumulates across sessions/runs; pages added, modified, contradicted, deprecated by curator. Carries provenance per entry; lint surfaces drift between curated form and source-of-truth. | `.abcd/memory/` (multi-upstream knowledge substrate per itd-36), `.abcd/work/` (shared working record — CONTEXT.md, the `.abcd/work/decisions/` folder”

24-decide states that a decision record is never edited and that a correction is a new record, which is the append-only class's behaviour. 04-universal-patterns places `.abcd/work/decisions/` under Compounding-curated, defined as pages added, modified, contradicted and deprecated by a curator. The taxonomy says lint blocks a namespace whose curation behaviour disagrees with its declared class, so the folder cannot be both.

### 575. The lint chapter runs its site and outbound targets as CI gates; the lint contract says record-lint and docs-lint are the whole of CI's lint coverage.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-205ef65dce0c8191 · ledger: iss-2610262035294777 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:147` — “the docs target runs in the `docs-lint` make target and in CI, the site target in the `site-render` make target and in CI”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:56` — “Until those ship, the two armed gates above are the whole of CI's lint coverage”

16-lint says three `abcd lint` targets are gated: the docs target in CI, the site target in the `site-render` make target and in CI, and the outbound target in CI's attribution workflow. 06-lint, the canonical lint contract, says that until the planned tiers ship, the two armed gates (record-lint and docs-lint) are the whole of CI's lint coverage. The site and outbound targets running in CI contradict 'the whole'.

### 576. The lint chapter gives the record-lint engine two severities, `blocker|warn`; the lint contract gives the same engine three, `blocker`, `warn` and `info`.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-8b1aec720d7040f4 · ledger: iss-2610262035308321 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:168` — “That is a different vocabulary from the record-lint engine's (`internal/core/lint`) `blocker|warn`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:12` — “Each rule carries a severity (`blocker`, `warn`, or `info`) resolved from its config entry”

16-lint contrasts its own `error|warn|off` vocabulary with the `internal/core/lint` engine's `blocker|warn`. 06-lint says every rule of that engine carries `blocker`, `warn` or `info`, and gives `info` its own row in the severity model. A rule set at `info` has no place in 16-lint's account of the vocabulary its boundary mapping translates.

### 577. The docs chapter's lint walks its roots and prunes only git-ignored untracked paths; the lint contract says the tree gates read git-tracked bytes.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dd8a1ddcc3dbfb87 · ledger: iss-2610262035302318 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:202` — “the lint asks git once per root which untracked paths it ignores and reads none of them”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:48` — “The two tree gates read git-tracked bytes through `internal/core/lint`”

10-docs says the walk asks git which untracked paths it ignores and skips only those. A committed file is never pruned, and outside a repository nothing is pruned, so untracked files that are not ignored are read, and so is a tree with no git at all. 06-lint says the two tree gates read git-tracked bytes. If only tracked bytes were read, there would be no ignored untracked path to prune and nothing to read outside a repository. The two describe different input sets.

### 578. The banlist chapter says this repository's docs-lint `names/` entries read `name_roots` that include `.abcd`; the lint contract limits docs-currency to `docs/` and the repo-root prose.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-11d838950e712344 · ledger: iss-2610262035312375 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/20-banlist.md:79` — “This repository's `name_roots` are `.abcd`, `AGENTS.md`,”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:10` — “lints `docs/` and the repo-root prose for change-narration”

20-banlist says the `names/` entries of `.abcd/docs-lint.json` also read the configuration's `name_roots`, and that this repository's are `.abcd`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts` and the other shipped surfaces. 06-lint describes the docs-currency gate, configured by that same file, as linting `docs/` and the repo-root prose, and assigns `.abcd/development/` to record-currency. Both cannot describe the docs gate's reach: by the banlist chapter it reads the design record, and by the lint contract it does not.

### 579. The lint chapter says the outbound gate is the fourth surface for its class and the only one that judges text before it is public; the configuration chapter has the shell guard refusing a posting gh pr/issue command over the same shapes.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8167fb4d64f8a002 · ledger: iss-2610262035329500 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:91` — “This is the fourth, and it is the only one that judges text BEFORE it is”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:89` — “the shell guard refuses a posting gh pr/issue command whose title,”

16-lint counts four surfaces that judge the outbound policy's class. It says `abcd lint outbound` is the only one that judges text before it is public. 03-configuration's `outbound.forge` key has the shell guard refuse a posting `gh pr`/`gh issue` command whose title, body or body file carries either shape. That is a further surface, and it judges text before it is posted. So the count of four and the claim 'the only one' cannot both stand.

### 580. The docs chapter says the release gate runs the docs-currency-reviewer; the agent catalogue says no verb starts that reviewer: the operator runs it and the gate only checks its receipt.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-36660cb300dfd052 · ledger: iss-2610262035332173 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:223` — “The release gate runs both.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:45` — “for the operator to run, and `launch receipts` and the release workflow check its receipt, but no verb starts it or records its verdict”

10-docs presents the docs-currency-reviewer as the semantic complement of the currency lint and says 'The release gate runs both.' 01-agents says `launch ship` names the reviewer in a checklist for the operator to run. `launch receipts` and the release workflow only check its receipt, and no verb starts it or records its verdict. A gate that runs the reviewer and a gate that only checks a receipt the operator produced are different designs.

### 581. The history chapter says no shipped surface but `history` reads the transcript store; the adapters chapter gives disembark a transcript reader that reads the same corpus.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a7b47d0893821ab1 · ledger: iss-2610262035341739 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:393` — “No shipped surface reads the store but `history` itself”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:350` — “Reads the root-SHA-keyed local corpus; merge by timestamp/content hash when an imported specstory source is also present”

11-history says that nothing distils the store yet and that no shipped surface reads it except `history` itself. 02-adapters lists, among the source readers disembark uses to fill a lifeboat, a transcript reader over the native transcript store (`internal/core/history`). It describes that reader in the present tense and does not mark it as a design target, as it does for the `claude_md` reader's git history. Disembark is shipped, so either it reads the transcript store or the reader is unbuilt. The two chapters cannot both be right.

A store that one chapter writes and the authoritative inventory omits is missed by anything built from the inventory, such as a backup or a cleanup.

### 585. The land chapter calls itd-97's auto/human merge toggle 'the facilitator mode'; the mode chapter uses `facilitator` as a value of `abcd mode`'s waiting-on state.

So 'facilitator mode' names two concepts: a merge toggle, and the mode state that says the loop waits on the facilitator. Its partner 'human mode' reads like the badge parked on a person.

### 590. The lint chapter says bare `abcd lint` runs when a human types it; the surfaces register lists `lint` with the agents, a block it reserves for commands no person types.

### 592. The reading-position glossary entry says the comparative position does not assemble and refuses; the reading chapter says it assembles from a prior widening run

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-40af2c5a36de4619 · ledger: iss-2610262035439719 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/reading-position.md:60` — “does not assemble and refuses: its object has no channel”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:61` — “derives its candidate set from the record”

The glossary's worked example states that `comparative` does not assemble and refuses because its object has no channel. The reading surface chapter states that the comparative position derives its candidate set from the record: it selects the one committed widening run at the target and hands the reading that run's items. One position cannot both refuse to assemble and assemble from a derived candidate set. The same glossary entry also still describes a position as reading 'the scope it was commissioned about', the model the chapter says its two-operand invocation superseded.

### 593. The glossary says the reading chapter writes 'reading position' in full on first use; the chapter opens with bare 'position' and never writes the full phrase

The reading-position entry describes how the record spells the term: the full phrase on first use, then bare 'position' inside the reading chapter. The reading chapter's first use is bare ('Assembly takes a position and a target state') and the phrase 'reading position' does not appear in it, so the spelling convention the glossary records for this chapter is not the one the chapter follows.

### 594. The glossary reserves bare 'surface' for a verb's front door and 'rendered surface' for identity-held text; the identity chapter uses bare 'surface' for identity-held text throughout

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8b95fce550438343 · ledger: iss-2610262035440979 (filed)

surface.md says the noun without a qualifier always means the front door, and names 19-identity.md as the home of the qualified sense 'a rendered surface'. The identity chapter calls the README strapline, plugin manifest and conventions-file opening 'surfaces' with no qualifier ('which surfaces have drifted', 'A surface can also come back unlocatable') and never writes 'rendered surface', so a reader applying the glossary would read those sentences as about command front doors.

### 595. The glossary forbids bare 'the loop' for the agent loop; the mode chapter's title uses bare 'the Loop' for exactly that loop

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/26-mode.md:1` — “Whose Answer the Loop Waits On, and the Away Mode”

loop.md reserves 'the loop' for the record loop and says not to use it for the agent loop of the wider literature, with the other loops always named in full. The mode chapter is titled 'Whose Answer the Loop Waits On' and its first line says the facts it holds are what 'the agent loop' is judged by, so its bare 'Loop' means the agent loop. That is the substitution the glossary rules out.

### 596. The glossary says abcd never owns the run loop; the site chapter reads the state file of abcd's own implement loop

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-56c4c3786bd91129 · ledger: iss-2610262035468845 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/loop.md:38` — “abcd never owns the run loop.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/22-site.md:118` — “implement loop's state file for Now's lane rows through the reader its front door hands it, the loop's own”

loop.md states that abcd never owns the run loop: it defines the contract and a pluggable adapter supplies the loop. The site chapter says the site build reads the implement loop's state file through the loop's own reader to render Now's lane rows. That is abcd's own loop, with its own state file and reader, iterating over ready work. The two statements cannot both hold, and 'the implement loop' is also a fourth loop sense the glossary's senses table does not carry.

### 597. The glossary allows bare 'the ledger' only for the issue ledger and spells the source-provenance store 'the sources ledger'; the guard chapter writes 'source-ledger' and then bare 'the ledger' for it

ledger.md says bare 'the ledger' is used only where the issue ledger is unambiguous, and every other ledger is named in full ('the sources ledger' for the corpus's source-to-decision provenance). The guard chapter calls it a 'source-ledger line' and then says 'the ledger records that a person chose to cite the source', so the bare form there means the sources ledger, not the issue ledger.

### 598. The glossary lists 'corpus' as a forbidden synonym for the library; the banlist chapter calls the library 'the sources corpus'

The banlist chapter describes that same collection by its confidential entries and points to the library chapter, but names it 'the sources corpus', 'the corpus sync' and 'the corpus writer'. ### 600. The glossary says a record, an ADR included, carries no status field; the decide chapter mints ADRs with a `status: proposed` field the author later changes

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/24-decide.md:160` — “and the record lands with `status: proposed`”

record.md names an ADR (adr-N) as a record and states that lifecycle is directory-as-truth, with a record moving between buckets rather than carrying a status field. The decide chapter says a freshly minted ADR lands with `status: proposed`, that the author sets `accepted` when the decision is in force, and that the index row's status comes from the record's frontmatter. So ADR lifecycle is held in a status field, not in a folder.

### 602. The voyage entry calls privacy-hygiene an 'audit rule' run by abcd's 'own audit'; the lint chapter says that verb is a lint and that 'audit' is reserved

### 603. The glossary says forbidden synonyms are registered there and nowhere else; the docs chapter registers the retired role word as a docs-lint banned token

### 609. The out-of-scope list holds 'abcd Can Read Its Own Design Documents As A Stranger Would' as later-phase work; the reading chapter ships exactly that outside reading of the design

The same ground is claimed as shipped by one document and as unscheduled later-phase work by the other.

### 610. The brief index says spc-N references trace the predecessor implementation's spec store and are not delivery claims; the update chapter cites spc-32 as a closed spec in this repository's own store, paired with a shipped intent

The brief README says `spc-N` references throughout the brief trace the predecessor implementation's spec store, are carried as design input for the Go rebuild, and are not delivery claims. The update chapter's references give 'Intent / spec' as shipped itd-130 and spc-32 at this repository's `specs/closed/` path, so spc-32 is this repository's delivered spec, not the predecessor's. Other chapters cite timestamp-minted ids such as spc-2610030944505997 the same way.

### 611. The brief index says delivery state never lives in brief prose; every surface chapter records each verb's shipped or staged existence in its prose table

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-ce90d36fc9a3e643 · ledger: iss-2610262035572805 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:17` — “non-assessment verb) and its existence (`shipped` / `staged`)”

The brief README says current delivery state lives in the roadmap dashboard, never in brief prose. The docs chapter, like every surface chapter, carries a machine-checked table whose rows record each verb's existence as `shipped` or `staged`, verified against the command-tree snapshot. That is per-verb delivery state stated in brief prose.

### 612. The verification matrix says an imported transcript merges by timestamp and content hash; the history chapter keys identity on content hash, session id and source labels, so the same content under another session is a new record

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9e6f404c12389b1c · ledger: iss-2610262035583798 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:32` — “an optional import merges by timestamp and content hash over the same store”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:58` — “the same content under a different session id writes a new record”

The matrix's native-transcript-capture row says an optional import merges by timestamp and content hash over the same store. The history chapter says capture, the path an import takes under the `import` route, is idempotent on the content hash, session id and source labels together, and that the same content under a different session id writes a new record. A merge keyed on timestamp and hash would fold together two sessions' identical content, which the history chapter forbids.

### 613. The verification matrix says an unreachable provider falls back to the harness rather than failing; the reading chapter's dispatch form exits 2 with nothing ingested when the provider cannot be reached

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:377` — “a provider that could not be reached, a run id outside the run-id grammar, a run no assembly parked, and a dispatch that also names an output each exit 2 with nothing ingested”

The matrix's oracle-adapter-degrade row says a step routed to a provider connection that cannot be reached, nothing having been sent, runs through the harness rather than failing the run, and the receipt names the harness used. The reading chapter says that for its dispatch form a provider that could not be reached exits 2 with nothing ingested. It also refuses an output the host produced while the position is routed to a provider, so the step cannot fall back to the harness.

### 614. itd-140 puts the landing page on the opt-in composition side, never a default; 22-site gives every repository a landing page it cannot switch off.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-94c09065a9e4ee7f · ledger: iss-2610151422085155 (already open)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-140-the-generic-specific-boundary-of-the.md:28` — “Specific side — the composition.** The landing page, the cast imagery,”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/22-site.md:103` — “Every repository gets the same pages: the landing page, the record explorer,”

itd-140 rule 2 lists the landing page, with install.sh and the deploy workflow, on the specific side: opt-in, declared in the repo's .abcd/site.json, never a default. 22-site says every repository gets the same pages, the landing page first, and refuses a declaration that switches the landing page off beneath the explorer. A landing page cannot be both an opt-in composition never given by default and a page every repository receives and cannot remove. The same 22-site sentence also states the page set is the same for every repository, a genericity claim itd-140 rule 3 forbids until a sparse fixture instance demonstrates it.

### 615. itd-140's armed-detector rung lives in `abcd site check`; 16-lint says the site verb's former check sub-verb is an unknown command.

The discipline names a verb that no longer exists as the home of its enforcement, so one gate carries two names and the one the discipline uses cannot be built on.

### 616. A draft filed for later wants every managed project to publish the public record site; 22-site already sets up and publishes that site for any managed repository.

The same ground is claimed by a shipped surface and by an unplanned draft, so it is either delivered or still owed, and the record says both.

### 617. The read-block glossary keeps every reading record of a prior run out of the next run; 23-reading hands the comparative reading a prior widening run's items.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6463abb262682173 · ledger: iss-2610262036018615 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/read-block.md:17` — “The instrument's own outputs, manifests and reading records, sit inside the read-block on the next run.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:82` — “This is the one positional exception to the prior-run exhaust”

read-block.md states without exception that the instrument's own outputs, manifests and reading records, sit inside the read-block on the next run. 23-reading's comparative position receives the items of one committed widening run, projected to two body fields, and calls this the one positional exception to the prior-run exhaust. The glossary's unconditional statement and the surface's exception cannot both describe the block; a builder reading the glossary would wall off exactly the input the comparative position must receive.

### 618. The regime glossary says the supply-regime check validates at ingest what a reading may produce; 23-reading says the generative regime's constraint falls at admission, not ingest.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-2ff5b5aeb903a352 · ledger: iss-2610262036027822 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:250` — “the generative licence is the widest of the four, with its constraint falling at”

regime.md says the supply-regime check validates at ingest what a reading was licensed to produce, and its definition has the ingest verb refusing or flagging. 23-reading says the generative regime declares no reserved names, that the generative licence is the widest of the four with its constraint falling at admission rather than at ingest, so at that position the gate performs no check of its own, and the prose layer that could flag was removed. The glossary's claim holds at three positions, not four.

### 619. 23-reading uses disposition for the researcher's recorded answer to a reading item; the deferred-finding discipline uses it for a review finding's fixed/invalid/deferred field in a release receipt.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6d1c5a87f82f4824 · ledger: iss-2610262036024309 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:319` — “the confirmed form of a recurrence stays the disposition's `recurs` citation”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2610141956319695-a-deferred-finding-is-its-own-captured.md:36` — “`disposition`, spelled exactly, and a deferred finding carries a separate field”

In 23-reading a disposition is the ledger record answering a reading item: the confirmed form of a recurrence stays the disposition's recurs citation, and the comparative position selects items carrying no disposition and no admission. itd-2610141956319695 makes disposition the field of a release-receipt finding whose three words are fixed, invalid and deferred, with a separate field naming the deferred finding's record. One word carries two state vocabularies on two different objects, so the term alone no longer says which record or which state set is meant.

### 620. itd-142 names entailment as one of four question regimes; 23-reading makes entailment a position whose regime is explicative.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6d91d5f979534594 · ledger: iss-2610262036033754 (filed)

itd-142 lists four question regimes: narrative, options, entailment and defaults. In 23-reading a regime is the supply regime a reading's definition declares, and the entailment position's row gives its regime as explicative, so entailment is a position and not a regime. The two documents use regime for different things and put entailment on opposite sides of the position/regime distinction.

### 621. itd-195 forbids an unexecuted list of which readers do what; 24-decide lists which readers call the ADR derivation and which carry their own, agreeing by inspection.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5546cd9ed7243e31 · ledger: iss-2610262036040955 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-195-a-claim-about-how-the-code-behaves-is.md:21` — “is backed by something that runs, or it is not written.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/24-decide.md:144` — “Three readers still carry their own”

itd-195's rule is that a statement of how the codebase behaves is backed by something that runs, or it is not written, and it names a list of the readers and what each does as the forbidden shape. 24-decide enumerates the readers that call recordid.CanonADRID and recordid.ADRFileID, says three readers still carry their own derivation, and notes the derivations agree by inspection. The brief carries exactly the list the discipline says must not be written unless a test establishes it.

### 622. itd-21's scaffold files the starter intent as `itd-1`; 24-decide says every minting family draws timestamp ids through one mint that reads no maximum.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-82a7c5cc300232a8 · ledger: iss-2610262036053576 (filed)

itd-21 has the scaffold's starter intent capture the project's mission as itd-1. 24-decide describes ids as the twelve-digit UTC stamp plus the four-digit uniform suffix every other minting family draws through recordid.Minter, a mint that reads no maximum. Under that mint no newly created intent can carry the ordinal id itd-1, so the scaffold as written cannot produce what it promises.

### 623. itd-16 makes /abcd:audit an open umbrella a schema or prompt-quality audit can join; 16-lint reserves it for hash-chain fidelity and calls a check of form a lint.

### 624. itd-11 hardens a Pass B chat-distiller that reads the transcript store; 11-history says no shipped surface reads the store but history itself.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bc0b76e7688d9463 · ledger: iss-2610262036068415 (filed)

itd-11 is framed as hardening, not redesign, of a pipeline in which Pass B's chat-distiller reads the native redacted transcript store and has produced noisy findings. 11-history says the harvest out of the store is only a design: nothing does that yet, and no shipped surface reads the store but history itself. The hardening depends on a reader of the store that, as the history surface is written, does not exist.

### 625. The token-cost draft adds per-session token accounting at capture; 11-history already reports per-session token usage in reconstruct telemetry, with its own counting rule.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9b0b7a135dcf3abc · ledger: iss-2610262036076395 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609292107351737-every-development-session-records-what.md:21` — “keeps the per-message token counts and the model id the transcript itself carries”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:168` — “The telemetry file carries the span, turn counts, token usage, a per-tool”

itd-2609292107351737 keeps the per-message token counts and the model id the transcript carries at capture and sums them per session. 11-history's reconstruct already writes a telemetry file carrying the span, turn counts, token usage, per-tool call counts and models per session and per agent, counting tokens once per response id because a per-line sum inflates by 2.44x to 5.28x. Two surfaces claim per-session token cost, and the draft names neither the existing telemetry nor its counting rule, so the two counts can diverge.

### 626. itd-134 renders a banner from the identity block's name, tagline and version; 19-identity's block holds a title, a tagline and an optional pitch, and no version.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d2d16231fd872e8f · ledger: iss-2610262036082275 (filed)

itd-134 scaffolds a banner rendered from the repo's canonical identity block, naming its fields as name, tagline and version. 19-identity defines the block's fields as Title, Tagline and Pitch, with title and tagline required and the pitch optional. The block carries no version and calls the name a title, so a banner sourced from the block as itd-134 describes cannot take its version from it.

### 627. Draft itd-169 asks that a stopped agent loop say who it is asking; 26-mode already records whom the loop waits on in the badge's waiting-on state.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5614f667275e2f73 · ledger: iss-2610262036097307 (filed)

The core of the draft is ground a shipped surface already covers, and neither document names the other, so the ground is claimed twice.

### 628. The rewriter draft rests on abcd being unable to start an agent; 17-guard describes agents abcd starts through its claude runner.

The premise that rules out an abcd-started rewriter is contradicted by a surface that starts agents.

### 629. itd-84 types a proposal's relation to existing records as supersedes/reverses/duplicates/refines; ideate's record grill types the same relation as covered/contradicted/superseded.

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/18-ideate.md:46` — “carrying a relation (`covered` / `contradicted` / `superseded`)”

itd-84 requires typed cross-record links (supersedes, reverses, duplicates, refines) for the existing records a new proposal touches. 18-ideate's record grill records hits on the existing record carrying a relation of covered, contradicted or superseded. Both judge a new proposal against the existing record, yet name the same relation with two closed vocabularies (duplicates and covered, reverses and contradicted).

### 630. The history chapter puts the transcript corpus under ~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/ and keeps ~/.abcd.noindex/history/ for ahoy's registry, holding no transcripts; itd-59 places the corpus at ~/.abcd.noindex/history/< root_sha>/.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-26b7c7fe587a560b · ledger: iss-2610262036113224 (filed)

11-history says the store is ~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/< root-sha>/records/ and that ahoy's registry stays under ~/.abcd.noindex/history/ and holds no transcripts. itd-59 says interactive sessions are redirected into the native transcript corpus at ~/.abcd.noindex/history/< root_sha>/, and its whole scope is to feed that directory. Both cannot say where the corpus lives. Building itd-59 as written would put transcripts into the registry directory that the brief says holds none.

### 631. itd-59 claims, as missing work, the capture of autonomous-run transcripts into the corpus; the history chapter says abcd build's delegated agent transcripts already reach the store through capture.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9f67ebabcc3035d6 · ledger: iss-2610262036129928 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-59-autonomous-worker-transcript-capture.md:36` — “every autonomous-run pass's instructions + reasoning lands in the native transcript corpus”

11-history lists, among the write paths into the corpus, a delegated agent's transcript that abcd build stores through the same capture. itd-59's stated gap is that every autonomous-run pass's instructions and reasoning should land in the native transcript corpus, on the premise that the unattended worker leaves only an ephemeral log. The same ground is claimed twice, once as shipped and once as unbuilt, and the draft does not say what it adds to the build capture that already exists.

### 632. The history chapter's 'memory store' is the store whose ingest takes documents and web addresses; itd-2610091918433290 says the name memory was freed into library, and gives /abcd:memory to agents' memory notes.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4e9497a27d77e25d · ledger: iss-2610262036131057 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610091918433290-an-agent-working-in-an-abcd-managed.md:58` — “freed the name `memory` by merging the sources and memory commands into `library`”

11-history says the memory store's ingest takes a document or a web address, and names it as the store that is meant to distil curated knowledge from transcripts. itd-2610091918433290 records that the sources and memory commands were merged into library, which freed the name memory, and uses /abcd:memory for agents' recall notes kept in memory.json. One name now points at two stores, so a reader of the history chapter cannot tell whether the transcript harvest feeds library's store or the agents' notes.

### 633. The lint chapter reserves /abcd:audit for itd-16's hash-chain fidelity surface and calls the conformance check abcd lint; itd-85, the intent the chapter cites, ships that same check as abcd audit.

- class: naming conflict · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-9e702702904fde00 · ledger: iss-2610262036142715 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:20` — “`/abcd:audit` stays reserved for itd-16's hash-chain fidelity surface.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-85-audit-verb.md:16` — “**abcd ships `abcd audit`** — a read-only check that tells you, in one command, whether a repository follows the working conventions”

16-lint says the conformance verb applies rules about form and so is a lint, and that /abcd:audit stays reserved for itd-16's hash-chain fidelity surface, where the staged chain and lifeboat verbs belong. itd-85 announces the same read-only repo-conformance check, with the same five v1 rules, as a new abcd audit verb with its own commands/audit.md. So one name, audit, is given to two different surfaces, and building itd-85 as written would collide with the reserved one.

### 634. itd-86 defines the cold reading as one target document read against its own constraints; the reading chapter's detection position reads the shipped tree against the claim record, assembled at a commit from an include table.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-5606991aae838f69 · ledger: iss-2610262036146367 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:193` — “Where is the shipped tree in tension with the claim record?”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-86-cold-reading-surface.md:29` — “A surface that takes exactly one target document and produces candidate detections against the constraints visible in that document alone.”

In 23-reading, the detection agent answers where the shipped tree is in tension with the claim record. Assembly takes only a position and a commit, and the reader gets what the committed include table admits. itd-86 instead scopes the cold reading as a surface that takes exactly one target document and detects only against constraints visible in that document. It also lands detections in the issue tier, while the chapter keeps reading records in the readings store, separate from the issue ledger. The two give incompatible objects for the same reading.

### 635. itd-87 treats matching captures against dispositioned entries, not only open ones, as new work; the reading chapter says capture's filing-time match already compares with open and resolved issues.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ef72e8c0b2792391 · ledger: iss-2610262036157324 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:314` — “with the open and resolved issues, the intents and every earlier reading item”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-87-recurrence-escalation-in-capture.md:31` — “Matching an incoming capture against **dispositioned** entries (`resolve`, `wontfix`), not merely against open ones.”

23-reading says the ingest runs capture's filing-time match, with capture's threshold and configuration, comparing each item with the open and resolved issues, and that a confirmed recurrence is the disposition's recurs citation. itd-87 scopes as new work the matching of an incoming capture against dispositioned entries, not merely against open ones. Both cannot describe today's matcher: either it already reaches resolved records or it does not.

### 636. itd-2609170822093401's press release says the oracle choice is one repo-wide value that nothing reads; the reading chapter has the ingest resolve that intent's model-tier route before anything runs.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a419def550c2e767 · ledger: iss-2610262036163231 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609170822093401-the-oracle-choice-is-one-repo-wide-value.md:26` — “backend is one repo-wide value that nothing reads, and every delegated step”

23-reading says the ingest resolves the model-tier route of itd-2609170822093401 and spc-2609180535002478 through the shared resolver, over the repo, machine and bundled tables, and records it on a route receipt. The planned intent states as present fact that the oracle backend is one repo-wide value that nothing reads. One of them misstates the current surface: either the reading ingest runs the routing or nothing reads it.

### 637. itd-44 has capture write an ADR as adr-< next-free>-< slug>.md; the decide chapter mints ADR ids from a timestamp that reads no maximum, and names the file < stamp>-< slug>.md.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-3367b576bf40ac01 · ledger: iss-2610262036171679 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/24-decide.md:127` — “The mint reads **no maximum**: not the store's, not the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-44-fourth-intent-kind-decision.md:122` — “`adr-<next-free>-<slug>.md` into `.abcd/development/decisions/adrs/`”

24-decide says an ADR id is adr-< yymmddHHMMSS>< rrrr> and the mint reads no maximum, neither the store's nor the citations'. It also says a hand-numbered ordinal allocated by reading the directory is exactly the collision the ruling closed. itd-44 allocates adr-< next-free> and writes adr-< next-free>-< slug>.md into the same store. That is allocation by reading the directory, and a filename shape the store does not use. Building itd-44 as written brings back the duplicate-number collision.

### 638. The decide chapter makes abcd decide with the ADR flag the ADR store's minting verb, with embark counting only as a restore; itd-44 adds capture as a second path that writes new ADRs into the store.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f182f4fbc29c6252 · ledger: iss-2610262036186092 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-44-fourth-intent-kind-decision.md:120` — “A confirmed `decision` verdict DIVERTS capture”

24-decide names abcd decide with the ADR flag as the store's minting verb, the counterpart of the read-only adr dispatch, and accepts embark as another writer only because embark restores rather than mints. itd-44 has capture, on a confirmed decision verdict, write a new ADR into .abcd/development/decisions/adrs/. Two verbs would then mint ADRs, and the draft does not route through the decide mint.

### 639. The site chapter's setup takes any managed repository's site live and gives every repository the same pages; itd-2610032150577708 rules that the record site is promised for abcd's own record only.

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610032150577708-a-product-thinker-opens-abcd-s-dashboard.md:47` — “The record site and the dashboard are promised for abcd's own record only”

22-site says setup takes a repository abcd manages from the checkout to a live address in three stages, and that every repository gets the same page set. Decision 13 of itd-2610032150577708 gives up itd-140's promise that the record site works for any project, and says the record site and the dashboard are promised for abcd's own record only. The shipped surface promises what the ruling withdraws.

### 640. The site chapter's setup publishes a managed repository's site through a hosting provider adapter on a custom domain; itd-2610091010348892 publishes the same per-release record on the project's own GitHub Pages, with abcd running nothing.
