22-site's setup writes a workflow that renders on each release, and at its host stage the provider adapter creates the host, routes the custom domain to it and reports the live address. itd-2610091010348892 claims the same ground, a per-release build of an opted-in project's record, but has GitHub host it on the project's own Pages and moves abcd's own record to that route. The two describe one publication in contradictory ways, and the intent does not say what becomes of setup's host stage.

### 641. The site chapter's 'status page' renders the board's Now/Next/Later block; itd-2609151838312703 renames the board so that the word status is free for abcd status, the view of announcements and reservations.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-9848ee40938cdd86 · ledger: iss-2610262036208370 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/22-site.md:111` — “The status page is the record health page, `/record/health/`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609151838312703-sessions-announce-what-they-are-doing.md:120` — “The status board's rename also frees the word "status" for this command.”

22-site calls the record health page the status page and opens it with the block the bare abcd board carries. itd-2609151838312703 gives the word status to the people's view of announcements, reservations and release cuts, and renames the status board to the dashboard to free the word. After that rename, the site's status page shows the dashboard's block while status names a different view.

### 642. In the mode chapter, mode means the waiting-on badge (managed, facilitator, product-thinker) and the away mode set by abcd mode autonomous; itd-2610150602547271 adds 'the facilitator's mode', facilitator.mode human|auto, shown on the same board.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5114c49234f6b384 · ledger: iss-2610262036211949 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/26-mode.md:4` — “waiting-on state behind the status line's badge: `managed`, `facilitator` or”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610150602547271-a-repository-declares-whether-its.md:15` — “The facilitator's mode gates the merge”

26-mode stores the waiting-on state as the mode that abcd mode prints and sets, and one of its values is facilitator; its away mode is entered with the autonomous sub-verb. itd-2610150602547271 names a separate per-repository setting, the facilitator's mode, whose values human and auto decide who merges, and has the bare board name 'the mode'. On one board, mode and facilitator would then name two different facts, and auto sits next to autonomous with an unrelated meaning.

### 643. itd-2610170638184486 lets the person set away open-ended, ending only when they say they are back; the mode chapter caps every away record at seven days.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6b6dc8246061b639 · ledger: iss-2610262036224651 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/26-mode.md:41` — “ends seven days after it was set at most, so an end past that, or one already”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610170638184486-every-abcd-session-keeps-a-checklist-on.md:296` — “in the app, either until a set time or open-ended; open-ended, they say when”

26-mode allows an away record with no end, but says every record ends at most seven days after it was set and refuses any later end. The checklist draft's product-thinker decision says the person sets away either until a time or open-ended, and that when it is open-ended they say when they are back. An open-ended away that only the person's word ends cannot also lapse by itself after seven days.

### 644. The guard's question gate assumes only abcd mode and the gate itself set a mode that names somebody; itd-2610031215002409 has bare abcd's Terminal menu set that waiting-on state too.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0c85a14992d529ee · ledger: iss-2610262036232872 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:127` — “naming somebody, which only `abcd mode` and this gate set and the answer resets”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610031215002409-under-the-board-a-short-what-next-menu.md:22` — “While the menu waits, the status line says an answer is waiting on whoever the view is for, and it clears when you answer or leave; in a Terminal this is the one thing opening the board ever changes.”

17-guard treats a question without an abcd chip as abcd's when the mode names somebody, and states the premise behind that: only abcd mode and the gate set the mode, and the answer resets it. itd-2610031215002409 has the 'what next?' menu under bare abcd set the status line's waiting-on state in a Terminal while it waits, and clear it on the answer. That is a third setter outside the host's question tool, so the premise behind the gate's ownership test no longer holds.

### 645. itd-185 has reading ingest check prose that ranks, settles or proposes; the reading chapter says that prose-signature layer was removed and only fields are refused

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-0d18ebfb5a2640c7 · ledger: iss-2610262036243501 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-185-one-ingest-verb-validates-every-cold.md:57` — “Semantic violations — prose that ranks, settles, or proposes without the fields — are checked too”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:262` — “It is gone rather than softened, because a gate that reads prose is still reading prose.”

itd-185's scope ships semantic checks over an item's prose beside the structural regime table, to degrade only on observed noise. 23-reading says the regime gate refuses only a real decision field, and that the second layer, a registry of named signatures over an item's prose, is gone outright. Ingest cannot both read item prose for ranking, settling or proposing and not read it.

### 646. itd-185 says every refused run writes a refusal record; the reading chapter says refusals made before the run's identity is proven, a hash disagreement among them, leave none

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d93a259fdae28947 · ledger: iss-2610262036257320 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-185-one-ingest-verb-validates-every-cold.md:85` — “A refused run still writes a refusal record — run metadata and the named reason, no items”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:276` — “A malformed envelope, a run id nothing is parked under, a hash disagreement, and a manifest naming another run or another position each refuse before that point and leave no refusal record at all.”

itd-185 makes a list-level refusal always durable through a refusal record, and counts a manifest reference whose hash disagrees as one of the refusals of the run. 23-reading says a malformed envelope, an unparked run id, a hash disagreement or a manifest naming another run refuses before identity is proven and leaves no refusal record at all. The two give opposite answers for what a hash-mismatched run leaves behind.

### 647. itd-199 lets a reading's scope be widened or narrowed at invocation and records the override; the reading chapter says the invocation is a position and a target with no override and nothing to stamp

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-fd467e20bfe7b653 · ledger: iss-2610262036260273 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-199-a-reading-is-about-something-narrower.md:19` — “A scope may be widened or narrowed at invocation while calibrating, and the manifest then records the scope a run actually had”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:59` — “There is no override at the invocation and nothing to stamp.”

itd-199, in shipped/, adds a scope operand the verb refuses to run without, lets it be widened or narrowed at invocation, and stamps an overridden run in the manifest. 23-reading says assembly takes a position and a target state and nothing else, that what a run is handed is not an operand, and that there is no override at the invocation. An assembler cannot both require and refuse a third operand.

### 648. itd-199 has the comparative position refuse because it has no channel; the reading chapter has it derive its candidate set from a committed widening run

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2059870ccfc5a7c1 · ledger: iss-2610262036267743 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-199-a-reading-is-about-something-narrower.md:55` — “The comparative position REFUSES, naming the channel it lacks”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:61` — “The comparative position derives its candidate set from the record”

itd-199 rules that the comparative position refuses, naming the channel it lacks, because no repository material can be its object. 23-reading says the comparative position derives its candidate set from the record, selecting the one committed widening run at the target and handing its items to the reading. A comparative assembly either refuses or assembles; the two documents state the opposite outcome.

### 649. itd-198 says the assembler states no size figure of its own; the reading chapter has every assembly report against a standing size target

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-60d098de15cd4ed8 · ledger: iss-2610262036279746 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-198-an-assembly-reports-what-it-would-cost.md:19` — “No budget is enforced and none is invented: the assembler cannot know what a given reader accepts, and a number it made up would be wrong for someone.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:172` — “A standing size target, stated and never enforced.”

itd-198 rules out any budget the assembler supplies, enforced or not, because it cannot know what a reader accepts and a number it made up would be wrong for someone. 23-reading has every assembly report a standing size target the tool states, naming both figures when the estimate runs over it. The two agree that nothing is enforced but disagree on whether the tool states its own size figure.

### 650. itd-166 says a field a route cannot show is recorded as unpinned or self-reported, never left out; the reading chapter's route receipt leaves model_reported empty when the payload names no model

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ffcbd9bde1eac6c8 · ledger: iss-2610262036286227 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-166-each-run-should-record-the-model.md:18` — “Whatever the route cannot show is written down as unpinned or self-reported, never left out and never guessed.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:355` — “`model_reported`, the last read from the payload's own `model` field (a reading's `instrument.model`) and empty when the payload names none”

itd-166 extends the override's route receipt so that every model call records the served side, with a missing field written down under a stated reason and never omitted. 23-reading describes the ingest's route receipt as carrying model_reported read from the payload and empty when the payload names none, with no reason recorded. An empty field is what itd-166 says the receipt never holds.

### 651. itd-2609020625407419's press release has the comparative assembly refuse when the widening run returned fewer than two configurations; the reading chapter has it stage an empty comparative run

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e9f1f6b9e227415b · ledger: iss-2610262036293167 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609020625407419-a-comparative-reading-receives-the.md:21` — “If the run returned fewer than two configurations, the assembly refuses and records that the position was not exercised”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:80` — “the position is not exercised, and the assembly stages a run whose ingest commits that outcome as an empty comparative run naming the widening run”

The intent's press release says that with fewer than two configurations the assembly refuses and records that the position was not exercised. 23-reading says the assembly stages a run whose ingest commits that outcome as an empty comparative run naming the widening run. One describes a refusal and the other a successful staging for the same case.

### 652. itd-201 uses the itd-200 mode to remember which role the person holds across questions; the guard chapter resets that mode to managed when each question is answered

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1c0feaf43c2fa4d9 · ledger: iss-2610262036304277 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-201-every-question-abcd-s-agents-put-to-a.md:65` — “the itd-200 mode records the answer so the next question does not ask again”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:197` — “The answer resets the state to managed and clears the marker”

itd-201 says that once the first question establishes the person's role, the mode records it so the next question does not ask again. 17-guard says the question gate sets the mode from the question's chip and the answer resets it to managed and clears the marker, so nothing about the person's role survives the answer. The mode cannot both persist the role and be reset at every answer.

### 653. itd-104 says an idea is gated before it can mint any record; the ideate chapter says ideate is optional, never a gate, and required by no other verb

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ce33ea60f3b54291 · ledger: iss-2610262036303950 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-104-abcd-gates-a-new-idea-before-it-becomes.md:17` — “abcd gates a new idea before it can mint a single record”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/18-ideate.md:13` — “No other verb requires it, nothing warns when it is skipped”

itd-104's press release makes the gauntlet a precondition: an idea is gated before it can mint a single record. 18-ideate says ideate is optional and never a gate, that no other verb requires it and nothing warns when it is skipped. An idea cannot be both barred from minting a record until ideated and free to be captured without it.

### 654. itd-104 says every ideate run outputs a verdict and a recorded decision; the ideate chapter writes no decision for a private verdict

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ce6174e190a607a8 · ledger: iss-2610262036312405 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-104-abcd-gates-a-new-idea-before-it-becomes.md:17` — “The output is a verdict and a recorded decision that keeps the rejected alternatives”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/18-ideate.md:88` — “no decision points at it, because the decisions folder is committed”

itd-104 states the output of the admission interview as a verdict plus a recorded decision keeping the rejected alternatives. 18-ideate writes a private verdict only under the home store, with no decision pointing at it because the decisions folder is committed. For a private run the recorded decision itd-104 promises does not exist.

### 655. itd-101 says the offline lint enforces no stale citation entries alongside no broken ones; the docs chapter says staleness only warns and never blocks an ordinary commit

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-50f2517ae1136483 · ledger: iss-2610262036322416 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-101-every-citation-abcd-publishes-is.md:14` — “no broken entries, no stale entries, no cited URL without a receipt”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:130` — “an ordinary commit is never blocked by the calendar”

itd-101 lists stale entries among what the offline lint enforces against, next to broken entries and missing receipts. 10-docs records staleness as a warning past 180 days, promoted to a blocker only in the release-gate mode, so that an ordinary commit is never blocked by the calendar. The two disagree on whether a stale entry is refused by the lint a commit runs.

### 656. itd-102 calls the positioning check part of every audit; the identity chapter runs it as a rule of abcd lint

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-c4dcdde0a6079b9b · ledger: iss-2610262036330589 (filed)

itd-102 says the positioning check compares each surface on every audit. 19-identity runs the same drift check as the identity-positioning rule on every abcd lint, and the lint chapter keeps the word audit for the hash-chain fidelity surface. The same check is named by two verbs whose vocabulary the record keeps apart.

### 657. itd-117 puts the user-scope rules file under ~/.abcd/; the history chapter calls ~/.abcd a legacy location

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7b3aa3fb08c13b1d · ledger: iss-2610262036343040 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-117-development-instructions-live-in-the.md:19` — “now live once in `~/.abcd/rules.json` and inject into every”

Two names are given for the one user-level home, and a reader following itd-117 writes the rules file where the brief says nothing current lives.

### 658. itd-200 puts the status-line defaults in the user-level home under ~/.abcd/; the history chapter calls ~/.abcd a legacy location

### 659. itd-130 names the staleness check abcd version --check; the update chapter makes the check a flag of abcd update

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8b12a31c0e8a005b · ledger: iss-2610262036353820 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-130-abcd-update-completes-a-chosen-update-in.md:32` — “typed `abcd version --check` on the machine where they first installed the”

### 660. itd-147 says a chapter's prose above the generated appendix never states a flag or sub-verb; the docs chapter's prose states which of its verbs take the configuration and root

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-aa5593a1cd7366a1 · ledger: iss-2610262036368072 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-147-the-brief-s-surface-chapters-are-a.md:90` — “the prose above it never states a flag or sub-verb”

itd-147 rules that shape claims live only in the generated appendix and the prose above its marker states no flag and no sub-verb. 10-docs, above its marker, says by hand which citation leaves accept the docs-lint configuration and the repo, and that the citation parent and the fidelity verbs take neither. That is a flag-shape claim in hand-written prose.

### 661. itd-122 says surface_coverage checks every sub-verb row against the command tree; the lint chapter's table note says a row's bucket cell is not checked against the tree

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-59976fb16e363090 · ledger: iss-2610262036376225 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-122-the-registry-cannot-wave-its-hands-every.md:19` — “`surface_coverage` now checks every row against the binary's own command tree, both ways”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:56` — “wrong but legal passes, and that cell stays a review-grain claim”

itd-122 presents the sub-verb table as recording each verb's bucket and existence, with surface_coverage checking every row against the binary's command tree. The machine-checked note in 16-lint says only existence is verified against the snapshot, and a wrong but legal bucket passes and stays a review-grain claim. Half of each row is not checked as itd-122 says.

### 662. The badge intent refuses a question to the human while the mode reads managed; the guard chapter says abcd's question is never refused on the mode.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-add309ce56add5cc · ledger: iss-2610262036376499 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212130146198-the-status-line-badge-is-true-at-every.md:40` — “a question to the human through the host's question tool is refused while the mode reads managed”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:183` — “In a repository abcd manages, abcd's question is never refused on the mode”

The badge intent's guard refuses any question put through the host's question tool while the mode reads managed, and leaves naming the addressee to the agent, since deriving it from the question's text is out of its scope. The guard chapter says that in a managed repository abcd's question is never refused on the mode. Instead the gate derives the state from the chip's role and sets it, and an unchipped question asked while the mode reads managed runs unchecked. One gate cannot both refuse on the managed mode and never refuse on it.

### 663. The question-layout intent refuses every question that breaks the asking rules; the guard admits a question whose only fault is going over the rows limit.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ac83840b3b505e4f · ledger: iss-2610262036380647 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610030810350727-every-question-abcd-puts-to-a-person.md:32` — “A question that breaks these rules is refused before it reaches you, naming the part and the limit”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:153` — “The rows limit is the one finding that does not refuse on its own”

The intent promises that a question breaking its rules is refused before it reaches the person, and that such a question reads at 80 columns without scrolling, with height handled by tabs. The guard chapter makes the rows limit the one finding that does not refuse on its own. A question whose only findings are tabs over the rows limit is admitted and marked open, and the agent is told only after it returns. So an over-tall question does reach the person, which the intent says cannot happen.

### 664. The reconstruction intent says reconstruction makes no write to the store; the history chapter says every history verb's resolve seam creates the store chain and moves a legacy corpus.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d90b00ba4a18522a · ledger: iss-2610262036392981 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609091718595846-any-captured-session-can-be-handed-to-an.md:57` — “Reconstruction reads records and writes only its two output files.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:186` — “Every history verb reaches the store through one resolve seam, and that seam creates the store chain when it is absent and moves”

The intent puts any write to the store out of scope and says reconstruction reads records and writes only its artefact and its telemetry file. The history chapter says every history verb reaches the store through one resolve seam. That seam creates the store chain when it is absent and moves a corpus left at the legacy location into it, leaving a tombstone. `history reconstruct` is one of those verbs, so either it writes to the store or the seam statement does not hold for it.

### 665. The verb-consolidation intent makes bare `abcd lint` run all targets; the lint chapter keeps the outbound target out of the bare run.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d27fa985eea18f41 · ledger: iss-2610262036404974 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212130136102-abcd-s-verbs-consolidate-ahoy-s-three.md:41` — “`abcd lint` (all), `lint docs`, `lint outbound`, `lint site`, `lint identity`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:36` — “The outbound target alone stays out of the bare run”

The intent labels bare `abcd lint` as running all targets, listed beside `lint outbound` among the four targets. The lint chapter says the bare run covers every target that judges the repository, and that the outbound target alone stays out because its subject is text the caller hands it. A bare run cannot both run all targets and leave outbound out.

### 666. The site-setup intent says a result followed by the error envelope is the repository-wide JSON convention; the update chapter emits a refusal as a single document.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-eb96e282b0cfeeae · ledger: iss-2610262036415345 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609061543533170-abcd-sets-up-a-managed-repository-s.md:70` — “A `--json` run that exits 1 prints two JSON documents, the result and then the CLI's error envelope; that is the repository-wide convention”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/21-update.md:238` — “In the JSON form a refusal of either kind is one document on stdout”

The site-setup intent tells a strict `--json` consumer that a run exiting 1 prints two documents, the result and then the CLI's error envelope, and calls this the convention across the repository. The update chapter says a refusal in JSON is one document on stdout, carrying the envelope's fields beside its own, so that no receipt is followed by a second envelope. A consumer built to the claimed repository-wide convention would misread update's refusals. So the convention is either not repository-wide or update breaks it.

### 667. The decision-log intent has the site list every decision from `.abcd/work/decisions/`; the site chapter says its one working-tier input is the issue ledger, off by default.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f236e5bb797ea55c · ledger: iss-2610262036429463 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609151138388536-append-only-logs-conflict-on-every-merge.md:28` — “A command and the site list every decision in date order.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/22-site.md:199` — “One input reaches past the durable record into the working tier, and it is off”

The intent writes each decision to its own file in `.abcd/work/decisions/` and says the site lists every decision in date order, on a page its 2026-10-14 ruling names the Decision log. The site chapter says one input reaches past the durable record into the working tier: the issue ledger, and only when a repository turns it on. The chapter's fixed page set names no decision log and cannot be added to. A site that lists the decisions would read a second working-tier input, and one that is always on.

### 668. The folder-classification intent calls ahoy's registry of managed repositories "the history store"; in the history chapter that store is the transcript store, kept apart from the registry.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-70ab1952c588673f · ledger: iss-2610262036424620 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-40-folder-classification.md:16` — “the history store's `index.json` keyed on each repo's root-commit SHA”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:15` — “ahoy's registry stays under `~/.abcd.noindex/history/` and holds no transcripts.”

itd-40 names the machine-wide registry of managed repositories the history store's `index.json`, under a scope heading "The history-store registry". The history chapter makes the `history` verb's store the session-transcript store under `transcripts/<root-sha>/records/`. It says ahoy's registry under `history/` holds no transcripts, and that install provisions the registry, not the store. The one name "history store" therefore stands for two different stores.

### 669. The rules-loader intent rejects a user-level rules.json and keeps rules per repository; the guard chapter counts a rules.json in abcd's home folder as part of the user layer.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f7d51eed8e4b8eee · ledger: iss-2610262036437864 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-3-modular-rules-loader.md:41` — “explicitly rejected. Keeping a personal cross-repo rules file recreates exactly the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:452` — “its trusted-roots, rules.json, config.json and the rest of the user layer”

itd-3 marks a global rules.json in abcd's home as explicitly rejected and keeps rules per repository only, because a cross-repository rules file recreates the failure the loader exists to fix. The guard chapter names rules.json, beside trusted-roots and config.json, among the files of abcd's own folder in the home directory, part of the user layer. One document says the file must not exist and the other treats it as part of abcd's home.

### 670. The conventions-file intent removes the CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md links; the docs chapter still justifies its root-symlink rule by the bridge files it lets pass.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-db646f5068efb090 · ledger: iss-2610262036446593 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610030814013772-evaluate-whether-claude-md-can-be.md:84` — “this repository's CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md links are removed whichever way the rest falls”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:160` — “what lets the bridge files pass while appearing in no allowlist”

The intent removes this repository's CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md links, and has abcd write no separate conventions copy for any tool. The docs chapter judges a root markdown symlink by its target's stem, and gives as the reason that this is what lets the bridge files pass while appearing in no allowlist. That reason assumes bridge files still stand at the root, and the intent says they were removed.

### 671. The menu intent hides the guard as a command only agents run; the guard chapter says a person or a script asks the guard about a command line.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0f6bb1a10932a662 · ledger: iss-2610262036453716 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610090831227812-a-person-who-types-abcd-sees-only-the.md:21` — “Commands only agents run, such as the guard that judges a shell command, are hidden from the menu”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:11` — “A person or a script asks it about one command line.”

The intent's press release gives the guard as its example of a command only agents run, and its ruling is that only commands no person types leave the person's menu. The guard chapter says two things use the guard: a person or a script asking about one command line, and an agent harness through the hook. It sets out the verdicts a person gets back. If a person asks it, the guard is a person's command by the intent's own rule.

### 672. The menu intent puts lint among the commands no person types; the lint chapter says bare lint runs when a human types it.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-26f337e78febb84e · ledger: iss-2610262036460690 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610090831227812-a-person-who-types-abcd-sees-only-the.md:94` — “Agent-only: lint, reflect, inbox, implement, history, site, docs, scribe, identity, guard, hook and statusline.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:145` — “onboarding and runs when a human types it”

The intent puts lint on the agent-only list, under the ruling that only commands no person types leave the person's menu. The lint chapter says no gate invokes bare `abcd lint`, and that its rule set backs onboarding and runs when a human types it. A command a human types is a person's command by the intent's own rule, so it cannot be on the agent-only list.

### 673. itd-89 files session transcripts in a local per-repo store; the history chapter says the store is user-level and the per-repo location is only an opt-in

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9ac40bce975e9e91 · ledger: iss-2610262036461110 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:338` — “The per-repo location is an opt-in pull.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-89-start-the-transcript-clock.md:18` — “files it in the local per-repo store”

itd-89's press release says the SessionEnd hook files the transcript 'in the local per-repo store', presenting per-repo as where every capture lands. The history chapter says the store is user-level, outside every repo, under ~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts/< root-sha>/records/, and that 'The per-repo location is an opt-in pull' honoured only for checkouts declared in ~/.abcd.noindex/local-transcript-roots. Both cannot describe the default destination of a captured transcript.

### 674. itd-76 puts abcd's user-level home at ~/.abcd/; the history chapter treats ~/.abcd as a legacy location

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-67d2fc170e920638 · ledger: iss-2610262036474703 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/11-history.md:216` — “or a legacy `~/.abcd` standing with no plugin binary in the plugin root”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-76-source-provenance-ledger.md:18` — “abcd's user-level home, `~/.abcd/sources/` by default”

itd-76 names abcd's user-level home as ~/.abcd/ and puts the sources corpus at ~/.abcd/sources/ by default. The history chapter puts its user-level store under ~/.abcd.noindex/ and calls a standing ~/.abcd 'legacy', a state its hook wrappers refuse when no plugin binary is in the plugin root. A builder following itd-76 would create the corpus in the directory the brief treats as left behind.

### 675. itd-60 names the shipped docs-currency lint `abcd docs lint`; the lint chapter says the docs verb's former check sub-verb is an unknown command

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-283e1f9fc8ecbe10 · ledger: iss-2610262036483439 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/16-lint.md:44` — “The docs and site verbs' former check sub-verbs are unknown commands”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md:151` — “`abcd docs lint` — change-narration, resolvable cross-links, no stray root documents”

itd-60 calls the docs-currency lint `abcd docs lint` and says it 'runs everywhere already'. The lint chapter makes that lint the docs target of the one lint (`abcd lint docs`) and says the docs and site verbs' former check sub-verbs are unknown commands. So the spelling itd-60 gives is the one the binary refuses: one surface, two command names, and only one of them resolves.

### 676. itd-60 says the gate writes its drafted brief edit into the shipping change itself; the docs chapter says the gate only proposes the edit and still refuses

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f3016389b5be6acb · ledger: iss-2610262036495984 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:104` — “The gate proposes that edit and still refuses.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md:130` — “When the gate finds the brief lagging, the pass writes the brief edit into the shipping change itself”

In itd-60, when the brief lags, the pass writes the brief edit into the shipping change and flags it, so the change is not held up by the paragraph. The docs chapter says a drafted replacement is only proposed by the gate, which 'still refuses'. Only a separate apply form, or the autonomous form, writes the sentence and lets the change through. One says drift is fixed and the change proceeds by default; the other says drift refuses by default until a second invocation applies the fix.

### 677. itd-65 calls its change-narration detector the `doc_fidelity` surface; the docs chapter uses doc-fidelity for the gate that checks the brief against the shipped surface

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-7f3d2b77403694a2 · ledger: iss-2610262036509587 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:66` — “(itd-60) judges whether the brief describes every surface that ships”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-65-launch-preflight-gate-suite.md:52` — “Reuses the spc-74 `doc_fidelity` surface as the detector.”

itd-65's doc-history gate finds change-history narration in shipped doc bodies and says it reuses the spc-74 `doc_fidelity` surface as its detector. The docs chapter uses 'doc-fidelity' for a different mechanism: the itd-60 gate that judges whether the brief describes every shipped surface. In that chapter, change-narration is a rule of the currency lint. One name now covers two concepts, so a reader of itd-65 would look for the narration detector in the wrong place.

### 678. itd-93 says abcd's release workflows are generated from the one scaffold template, so abcd runs exactly what a managed repo gets; the docs chapter says abcd's release workflow has a docs-currency step that the scaffolded template never names

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e25cb0993b6b705e · ledger: iss-2610262036512603 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/10-docs.md:131` — “The release workflow's docs-currency step runs the lint in its release-gate mode; CI's step and the `docs-lint` make target each run the lint in its plain mode, the scaffolded release template names the verb nowhere”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-93-abcd-scaffolds-a-hardened-changelog.md:79` — “The proven pattern and the shipped template are one artifact by construction, so every abcd release exercises the exact machinery a managed repo receives.”

itd-93 says abcd's own release.yml and auto-release.yml are regenerated from the single scaffold template, so every abcd release runs 'the exact machinery a managed repo receives'. The docs chapter says abcd's release workflow has a docs-currency step that runs the lint in release-gate mode, while 'the scaffolded release template names the verb nowhere'. If the template lacks that step, abcd's release machinery is not the scaffolded one. If abcd's release machinery is the scaffolded one, the template would have to name the verb.

### 679. itd-6 says abcd never spawns Claude Code subprocesses; the guard chapter describes agents that abcd starts through its claude runner

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b602dc555ff5fc97 · ledger: iss-2610262036514870 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/17-guard.md:385` — “An agent abcd starts through its claude runner has no terminal”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:53` — “Spawning Claude Code subprocesses with `claude -p` — explicitly NOT how abcd works; abcd is the consumer, not the spawner”

itd-6 rules out spawning Claude Code subprocesses with `claude -p` as 'explicitly NOT how abcd works', saying abcd is the consumer and not the spawner. The guard chapter describes agents abcd starts through its own claude runner: headless launches carrying their own command line, settings and MCP server, plus a second, opencode, runner. The two disagree on whether abcd launches harness processes at all.

### 680. itd-6 rules out direct provider integrations and sends everything through RP; the reading chapter routes a cold-reading position straight to a configured provider through abcd's own tier routing

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-05c13042a58d76bf · ledger: iss-2610262036529540 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/23-reading.md:365` — “when the person's `oracle.roles.cold-reading-<position>` points at a provider it sends the position's definition as the instructions and the parked bundle”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:54` — “Direct OpenAI / Google / Anthropic API integrations — out of scope; route everything through RP”

itd-6 rules out direct OpenAI, Google and Anthropic API integrations and says to route everything through RP, with no abcd-side oracle selection. The reading chapter has abcd resolve a model-tier route per agent from layered oracle-routing tables. When `oracle.roles.cold-reading-<position>` names a provider, the ingest's dispatch form sends the definition and bundle directly to that provider and ingests the answer. abcd choosing a provider and calling it directly is what itd-6 excludes.

### 681. The surfaces register lists drain among the verbs no person types, while the drain chapter calls it the verb a person types

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-55bdc530ed28563b · ledger: iss-2610262036532725 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:152` — “agents and hosts | — | `announce`, `banlist`, `docs`, `drain`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:3` — “`/abcd:drain` is the verb a person types to have the open issue ledger worked unattended”

The register's help table puts `drain` in the agents-and-hosts block, and the same page says the product thinker placed verbs by who types them, listing with the agents only a command no person types. The drain chapter opens by calling `/abcd:drain` the verb a person types to have the ledger worked unattended. A verb cannot be both one no person types and the one a person types, so either its placement or the chapter's framing is wrong.

### 682. The memory chapter defers recall through the prompt hook to a later step, while the configuration chapter has the prompt router already injecting recalled notes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9a483656852bf8ab · ledger: iss-2610151422092354 (already open)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:6` — “Recall of a note through the prompt hook is the same spec's later step; this chapter covers the store and the verb.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:976` — “followed by a `## MEMORY` block of the memory notes the prompt recalls that this session has not yet been given”

37-memory says recalling a note through the prompt hook is the spec's later step and that the chapter covers only the store and the verb. The configuration chapter's prompt-router output table says stdout already carries a `## MEMORY` block of the notes the prompt recalls, read from both memory.json layers. Recall either ships with the router or is still a later step. It cannot be both.

### 683. 'Memory verbs' names the library's curation of `.abcd/memory/`, while `/abcd:memory` is a separate verb over memory notes

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ac9b32a165d1bf3a · ledger: iss-2610262036545848 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1139` — “New projects use `.abcd/memory/`, the substrate `abcd library` curates through its memory verbs.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:3` — “`/abcd:memory` keeps memory notes: short lessons an agent writes so that a later session does not learn them again”

The configuration chapter says the repository's `.abcd/memory/` substrate is curated by `abcd library` through its memory verbs. The memory chapter gives the name `memory` to a top-level verb that keeps short notes in `memory.json` files. The one name now covers two different stores side by side in `.abcd/`. A reader looking for the memory verbs that curate `.abcd/memory/` lands on a verb that writes a different file for a different purpose.

### 684. The build chapter refuses any key under `pace` the loop does not read, while the drain reads two more keys from that namespace

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c72b79054080fdbd · ledger: iss-2610262036554739 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:231` — “the reader claims the `pace` namespace, so a key under it the loop does not read is refused rather than ignored”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:233` — “both bounds are read from the pace's layers (`pace.stuck_refusals`, `pace.stuck_minutes`) at every move”

34-build resolves four pace keys (work_minutes, pause_minutes, sub_agents, fix_rounds) and says the reader claims the `pace` namespace, refusing any key under it the loop does not read. 35-drain reads its stuck bounds from `pace.stuck_refusals` and `pace.stuck_minutes` in the pace's layers. As written, a repository that sets a stuck bound for its drain holds a key under `pace` that the build chapter says is refused.

### 685. The configuration chapter counts two limits in load-limits, while the implement chapter names three keys in that file

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1df57a93e1507cd9 · ledger: iss-2610262036569134 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:661` — “the load check's two limits in `load-limits` (read-only and never created, itd-2609231434459890)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:253` — “The limits live in the caller's machine tier, `~/.abcd.noindex/load-limits` (`stray-minutes`, default 30; `extreme-load`, default four times the online core count; `wait-load`, default twice it)”

27-implement lists three keys in `~/.abcd.noindex/load-limits`: stray-minutes, extreme-load, and wait-load, the limit the wait gate opens below. The user-scope inventory in 03-configuration describes the same file as holding the load check's two limits. A reader building the file from the configuration chapter would leave out the wait limit the gate depends on.

### 686. Multi-agent claims live in-tree under `.abcd/coordination/` per the universal patterns, but in the machine-scoped run store per the implement chapter

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ad09e984cb3b7cba · ledger: iss-2610262036565450 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:139` — “Coordination state (file locks like `shape.lock`, multi-agent claims per itd-33) lives at `.abcd/coordination/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:3` — “It holds a run's shared state in the machine-scoped store, records the sessions that join it, makes a record the unit of exclusion between them with a claim”

04-universal-patterns places multi-agent claims (itd-33) under `.abcd/coordination/`, beside a committed coordination append-log with daily UTC rotation. 27-implement keeps the claim that makes a record the unit of exclusion between concurrent sessions in the machine-scoped store, with its own per-UTC-day run log, and has the sessions write no repository file. Both documents claim the same ground, the exclusion record between concurrent agents, and give it incompatible homes.

### 687. The lifecycle taxonomy calls issue-ledger entries immutable after creation, while the drain's user-visible route writes `related_intents` into the issue

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a1847199eaf5935b · ledger: iss-2610262036573008 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:195` — “capture issue-ledger entries (immutable post-create)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:579` — “the draft, and the issue's `related_intents` naming it; nothing else”

04-universal-patterns puts capture issue-ledger entries in the append-only class, never modified after creation. The drain's hand-back table says a user-visible hand-back writes the intent draft and adds `related_intents` to the issue, which edits an existing issue record. The drain chapter also re-admits a handed-back issue only once a person changes its record. If the taxonomy holds, the drain's routing breaks it by design.

### 688. The register says chapters point to its bare-invocation list instead of restating it, but the announce chapter restates its bare behaviour

- class: scope leakage · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-2b065f822d5d3b59 · ledger: iss-2610262036589915 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:248` — “This paragraph is the one enumeration of the exceptions; the chapters point here rather than restating it.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-announce.md:34` — “Bare `abcd announce` refuses as a usage error naming the kinds.”

README says its bare-invocation paragraph is the one enumeration of the exceptions and that the chapters point there rather than restate it. 38-announce states the exception itself: bare `abcd announce` refuses as a usage error naming the kinds. The same behaviour is therefore written in two places, which is the second copy the register says it avoids.

### 689. The user-scope inventory has no dashboard store, while the dashboard chapter keeps its run file and devices list in `~/.abcd.noindex/dashboard/`

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-35d393e3f9db697e · ledger: iss-2610262036597501 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:621` — “one per machine, machine-local shared state only: the history registry, the transcript corpus, the voyage operations namespace, the lab store”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/36-dashboard.md:127` — “The run file and the devices list live in `~/.abcd.noindex/dashboard/` and name no project content.”

03-configuration lists, store by store, what the user scope holds and says the ahoy tree must agree with that list. No `dashboard/` store is on it. 36-dashboard writes its run file and the list of devices that opened it under `~/.abcd.noindex/dashboard/`. Either the inventory is incomplete or the dashboard keeps a store the inventory does not admit.

### 690. The agent register says intent-auditor serves `intent` alone, while the build loop composes its request and validates its verdict

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-6aecefdab4925277 · ledger: iss-2610262037002531 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:417` — “`intent` | [`05-intent.md`] (05-intent.md) | Audits a shipping intent's promise against the delivered code”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:697` — “the auditor's fidelity verdict checked against the request (its receipt, both provenance hashes, every criterion and scope condition)”

README's Serves column names the verb that builds an agent's input or validates what it returns. It lists only `intent` for intent-auditor, while it lists `build` and `drain` for the two reviewers. 34-build has the validate stage hand the closing lane to an intent-auditor and check its fidelity verdict against the request before the loop records it. By the column's own definition, `build` serves the auditor as well.

### 691. The loop glossary says abcd never owns the run loop; the build chapter ships abcd's own implement loop.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-fa10e0c80a5b36e6 · ledger: iss-2610262037018200 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/loop.md:38` — “abcd never owns the run loop.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:5` — “It starts the implement loop: a loop over a state file, not a model, where every invocation reads the state, does at most one stage, writes the state and exits.”

loop.md says abcd never owns the run loop (the iteration that picks up ready work and gates each step on a receipt): abcd defines the contract and a pluggable adapter supplies the loop. 34-build.md says `abcd build` starts abcd's own implement loop, a loop over a state file that the binary advances one stage per invocation. The glossary rule and the shipped loop cannot both hold.

### 692. The memory internals chapter homes keyword-recalled personal and project memory in ~/.abcd.noindex/memory/ and .abcd/memory/; the memory verb homes the same in two memory.json layers.

- class: scope leakage · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-4c3c52a11a36d0b8 · ledger: iss-2610262037016704 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:14` — “| **user** | `~/.abcd.noindex/memory/` | **Personal preferences** and cross-project principles that have no single repo home”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:26` — “The machine's `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json` holds the person's own notes; a repository's `.abcd/memory.json` holds the notes a person promoted into the project.”

07-memory.md puts personal preferences and lessons that apply to every project in the user scope `~/.abcd.noindex/memory/`, with project knowledge in `.abcd/memory/`, curated by principle-distiller and injected by the prompt hook through each page's recall keywords. 37-memory.md puts the person's own lessons in `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json` and promoted project notes in `.abcd/memory.json`, written by agents with recall words for the same prompt hook. Two stores, with different writers and different precedence, claim the same ground.

### 693. The step glossary says the build loop takes a spec's steps one lane at a time; the build chapter runs lanes in parallel up to a ceiling.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9aede0d48387e65d · ledger: iss-2610262037021391 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/step.md:18` — “the build loop (`abcd build`) takes them one lane at a time, the spec's next pending step opening the next lane when a lane is done”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:406` — “A run works in parallel up to its ceiling (ruling DR6, spc-2609202134341288).”

step.md says `abcd build` takes a spec's steps one lane at a time, the next pending step opening the next lane only when a lane is done. 34-build.md says a run works in parallel up to its ceiling (ruling DR6), so several of a spec's steps can be in lanes at once. A reader building from the glossary would serialise what the loop runs in parallel.

### 694. The spec glossary says a spec is broken into ordered tasks; the build chapter breaks a spec into steps.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b0de33c0e9aa372b · ledger: iss-2610262037031364 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/spec.md:4` — “A specced block of work in abcd's native spec store that implements one or more intents, broken into ordered tasks with acceptance criteria.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:84` — “the open spec's `## Steps`, read through the spec store's own reader, parses and leaves at least one step unlanded”

spec.md defines a spec as broken into ordered tasks. 34-build.md reads the spec's `## Steps` section and lands the spec step by step. The unit below a spec is named task in one document and step in the other.

### 695. The out-of-scope page says the spec close that ships an intent is a manual step; the build loop's landing runs the close itself.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-510efab1af9b5dab · ledger: iss-2610262037049481 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/03-out-of-scope.md:172` — “the close is a manual step run in the change that lands the work”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:743` — “In the lane's worktree it runs the spec's close (which ships the intent and parks the fidelity receipt)”

03-out-of-scope.md says nothing promotes a record on its own and the close is a manual step run in the change that lands the work. 34-build.md says the landing stage runs the spec's close in the lane's worktree, which ships the intent with no person running it. A build run does promote a record on its own, so the manual-step claim does not hold.

### 696. The build sequence says the dependency graph and the sequencing over it are a design target; the build loop sequences a spec's steps by their declared needs.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e71c7ec81e46e25d · ledger: iss-2610262037059425 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:123` — “The dependency graph and the sequencing over it are a **design target**; readiness today is per-intent, through `abcd intent ready`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:417` — “A lane opens for a spec step once every step it needs has landed (its `- needs:` line, or by default every step before it, ruling DR6b)”

01-build-sequence.md says the dependency graph over specs and tasks and the sequencing over it are a design target, with readiness today per-intent through `abcd intent ready`. 34-build.md says a lane opens for a spec step only once every step it needs has landed, read from each step's `- needs:` line: a dependency graph over a spec's steps, with sequencing over it, that ships. One of the two describes the shipped state wrongly.

### 697. The brief index says spc references trace the predecessor's spec store and are not delivery claims; the build chapter cites a spec of this repository for what has landed.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-526d8c75e53c26e0 · ledger: iss-2610262037066238 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/README.md:7` — “`spc-N` references throughout the brief trace”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:860` — “the design record: spc-2609202134338445, whose Progress section says which pieces have landed.”

README.md says `spc-N` references throughout the brief trace the predecessor implementation's spec store, as design input and not as delivery claims. 34-build.md cites spc-2609202134338445 as its design record, whose Progress section says which pieces have landed: a spec in this repository's own store, used as a delivery reference. The README's blanket rule misdescribes the spec ids this repository mints.

### 698. The brief glossary says a project has exactly one brief; the build chapter gives every lane a brief of its own.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-fb02a2b297b98e4e · ledger: iss-2610262037067804 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/brief.md:28` — “A project has exactly one brief.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:617` — “The brief is rendered from the lane's base commit, read out of git's objects rather than the worktree's files”

brief.md keeps "brief" for the project-level document under `.abcd/development/brief/` and says a project has exactly one. 34-build.md uses "the brief", unqualified, for the per-lane document rendered for the implementer from the lane's base commit, and names a lane stage after it. The word carries a second sense the brief entry does not allow.

### 699. The memory-note glossary says the rules loader brings a note back when a prompt matches; the memory chapter says prompt-hook recall is a later step.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-03a8eb4809b15cc1 · ledger: iss-2610151422092354 (already open)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/memory-note.md:18` — “The same loader that brings in the project's rules brings the note back when a prompt matches those words, so no one has to remember to look it up.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:6` — “Recall of a note through the prompt hook is the same spec's later step; this chapter covers the store and the verb.”

memory-note.md says, in the present tense, that the loader that brings in the project's rules brings a note back when a prompt matches its words. 37-memory.md says recall of a note through the prompt hook is the spec's later step and the chapter covers only the store and the verb. A note written today is not recalled automatically, so the glossary describes behaviour that does not ship.

### 700. The record-families page says batch is not a term of the record; the implement chapter makes batch a named window mode.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9a5989670e3a8ecc · ledger: iss-2610262037072482 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:32` — “is the autonomous run's internal order, derived from dependencies and the pick, and is not a term of the record”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:87` — “single, claim, batch or split-roles”

record-families.md says a batch is the autonomous run's internal order, derived from dependencies and the pick, and not a term of the record. 27-implement.md lists batch as one of the window's modes (single, claim, batch or split-roles), set by a sub-verb and logged in the run log. The record uses as a named mode a word the glossary says it does not use, in a sense other than the internal order the glossary describes.

### 701. The record-families page names status as a computed Now / Next / Later view; the announce chapter names a stored per-person branch of announcements status.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2d26a5b9c039d8bf · ledger: iss-2610262037080548 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:28` — “Now / Next / Later, rendered from the shelves, the gate and the build's state”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-announce.md:39` — “The announcement is one empty-tree commit on the sender's own status branch”

record-families.md defines the status family as Now / Next / Later, rendered from the shelves, the gate and the build's state: a view that is computed and never stored. 38-announce.md calls each person's branch of announcement commits on origin their status branch, read by `abcd status`. One name covers a computed view of the record and a stored message channel.

### 702. The record-families page lists the record families as intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release and status; the inbox chapter calls adr, itd, iss, spc and dcn the record families.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-49b4bb784f7496f2 · ledger: iss-2610262037095269 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:4` — “The one page that maps abcd's record families (intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release, status)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/30-inbox.md:108` — “a record family abcd resolves (`adr`, `itd`, `iss`, `spc` and `dcn`) followed by a number”

record-families.md is the one page that maps the record families and lists intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release and status, with no ADR or decision family. 30-inbox.md uses "record family" for the id prefixes the citation grammar resolves, adr, itd, iss, spc and dcn, two of which have no row on that page. The term names lifecycle groupings in one document and id prefixes in the other.

### 703. The plan glossary keeps bare "plan" for the intent sign-off verb; the drain chapter uses bare "the plan" for a drain move's ordering of the ledger.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-93b36b318e9a3fe9 · ledger: iss-2610262037099879 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/plan.md:51` — “only for the intent verb and its sign-off. Qualify every other use”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:194` — “The plan, the lane's start check, the judgement's remedy digest and the reservation's footprint all read that snapshot”

plan.md says bare "plan" is used only for the intent verb and its sign-off, every other sense qualified, and never for the order of work. 35-drain.md writes "The plan", unqualified, for the classification and ordering a drain move derives from its snapshot of origin's ledger. The bare word carries a sense the glossary withholds from it.

### 704. The loop glossary keeps bare "the loop" for the record loop; the build chapter uses it bare for its run iteration.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-0cbe8fd62b187dc2 · ledger: iss-2610262037101841 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/loop.md:50` — “for the record loop, and only where no run loop or round-trip is in view”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:694` — “Only the loop writes a verdict (decision 9)”

loop.md allows bare "the loop" for the record loop only where no run loop or round-trip is in view, and requires the other senses to be named in full. 34-build.md, whose subject is the build run's own loop, writes "Only the loop writes a verdict", the bare form for the run iteration.

### 705. The only glossary entry for session is the unshipped grill exchange, which it says not to use generically; the implement chapter's session is a host agent session.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-179ad29f7ffae124 · ledger: iss-2610262037119222 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/interview/session.md:29` — “Do not import it into HTTP/auth contexts or use it generically”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:71` — “A session joins under its id, in the role `first` or `second`, optionally stating an agent ceiling.”

session.md defines a session as one grill interview exchange, a design target, and says not to import the term or use it generically. 27-implement.md uses session throughout for a host agent session that joins a shared run in a role, a concept with no glossary entry. The same word names two concepts, and the sense the record operates on is the unregistered one.

### 706. The release glossary accepts snapshot as an alias for a release; the lab chapter defines a snapshot as a standalone clone pinned at one commit.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-51df57a6afc4f748 · ledger: iss-2610262037128325 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/distribution/release.md:5` — “aliases: ["published snapshot", "plugin release", "snapshot"]”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/31-lab.md:48` — “lays down a **snapshot**: a standalone clone of the repository detached at the pin”

release.md lists snapshot among a release's aliases, so a snapshot is a published, version-tagged cut of abcd. 31-lab.md defines a lab's snapshot as a standalone clone of the repository detached at the pin. The word is an accepted name for two different things.

### 707. The lab discipline lets no candidate into a harvest before a refutation pass; the lab verb's harvest lists candidates nobody tried to refute and only flags them.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1ef617386e86c7e1 · ledger: iss-2610262037133461 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/31-lab.md:103` — “and flagged where no refutation was attempted”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2609251624540864-a-lab-runs-one-procedure-from-intention.md:119` — “no candidate enters the harvest before a refutation pass”

itd-2609251624540864 makes a refutation pass a precondition for a candidate entering the harvest. 31-lab says its procedure is that discipline, yet its harvest lists every product finding as a capture candidate and only flags those where no refutation was attempted. So the harvest the verb builds can hold exactly the candidates the procedure forbids.

### 708. itd-1 says a shipped intent's Audit Notes come only from an audit run by hand, because the automatic audit at ship time is deferred; the build loop already runs that audit and ingests it when the intent ships.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0a121e9d2d4adede · ledger: iss-2610262037138873 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:45` — “Until that lands, a shipped intent's `## Audit Notes` is populated only when `/abcd:intent audit` is run by hand.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:743` — “runs the spec's close (which ships the intent and parks the fidelity receipt) and ingests the verdict of the audit the lane took into that receipt”

itd-1 defers automatic invocation on the planned-to-shipped move and says that until then, Audit Notes are filled only when /abcd:intent audit is run by hand. In 34-build, the landing runs the spec close that ships the intent, then ingests the verdict of the intent-auditor the lane already ran. That is an automatic audit at exactly that move, so 'only when run by hand' cannot also hold.

### 709. itd-1 says reviews of implementations return SHIP / NEEDS_WORK / MAJOR_RETHINK; the build's implementation reviewers return SHIP or FIX FIRST.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6c071faeba99b9d5 · ledger: iss-2610262037142878 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:47` — “(`SHIP` / `NEEDS_WORK` / `MAJOR_RETHINK`) which score *changes/runs*”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:696` — “stating one verdict of its role (`SHIP` or `FIX FIRST`”

itd-1 fixes one set of review verdicts, kept separate from criterion verdicts, for reviews of plans, implementations and completions: SHIP / NEEDS_WORK / MAJOR_RETHINK. In 34-build the validators review a lane's implementation, and the loop reads one verdict per role: SHIP or FIX FIRST. The two documents give different words for the same set of verdicts, so a reader built from itd-1 would reject what the build's reviewers return.

### 710. itd-190 says the readiness gate enforces the claim-recording rules; 34-build says the readiness gate only reports them as advisory and enforcement happens at a run.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4dda363b4287b78c · ledger: iss-2610262037151611 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-190-the-claim-recording-gradient-an-intent-s.md:39` — “the gradient binds standalone intents at the readiness gate from adoption on”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:65` — “The readiness gate reports both as advisory; a run is where they bind”

itd-190's rule says the gradient binds standalone intents at the readiness gate, and that a blank scope-conditions section or an empty mechanism section is a gate fault. 34-build says the readiness gate reports the mechanism prompt and the scope conditions as advisory, and that they bind only when a build starts. Either the gate refuses, or it only advises; the two pages say opposite things.

### 711. itd-191 allows selection only on its declared criteria, with the final choice made by the maintainer; the build pick chooses an intent itself on three computed scores and records that as a pursued: grounds entry.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-147390af5a44ab66 · ledger: iss-2610262037160502 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-191-the-selection-criteria-are-a-declared.md:18` — “Selection at the gate weighs candidates against the criteria this record declares, and only these.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:176` — “three parts of 0 to 100 at equal weight (decision 7, the bundled default): criteria clarity”

itd-191 limits selection to plausibility, generativity, cost, risk, learning value and practical importance, and says combining them into a choice is the maintainer's act, on recorded grounds. 34-build's pick instead scores candidates on criteria clarity, test path and footprint at equal weight, takes the readiest, and appends a 'picked by run' pursued: grounds entry. That is a machine-made selection on criteria the discipline does not declare.

### 712. itd-2609292107351737 treats refusing to start a run on a budget as abandoned ground from a superseded intent; the build ships a budget check that refuses a run whose estimate is over quota.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-353732922a3a7f9e · ledger: iss-2610262037171531 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609292107351737-every-development-session-records-what.md:57` — “Budget enforcement: refusing to start a run on a budget is itd-29's superseded ground and is not revived here.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:258` — “an estimate over the quota is refused at the `budget` check”

The draft says refusing to start a run on a budget belongs to superseded itd-29 and is not brought back. 34-build's start runs a budget check that compares the run's estimate with each runner's remaining quota and refuses the run at the budget check when it is over. A builder cannot treat budget refusal both as abandoned and as a shipped start check.

### 713. itd-107 keeps forge calls (arming auto-merge, re-reading created items) out of the binary so it needs no forge command-line tool; the build loop's binary already makes those calls through gh.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-74f8ccee9ac5dcf6 · ledger: iss-2610262037186224 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-107-autonomous-routines-assemble-from-one.md:145` — “so the binary acquires no platform CLI dependency”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:768` — “It opens the pull request through the forge client the repository already uses (`gh`)”

itd-107 justifies leaving forge calls to the host by saying the binary then acquires no platform CLI dependency. In 34-build's landing, the binary opens the pull request through gh, asks gh pr view whether it merges, arms auto-merge and re-reads the body the forge holds. So the binary already depends on gh, and the draft's reason does not hold.

### 714. The bump re-authoring workflow stamps a commit message a machine wrote with Assisted-by: None; 34-build treats None as meaning human-only, which is false for machine-written text.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-74124b83a7988f46 · ledger: iss-2610262037198530 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609301020001595-a-dependabot-bump-of-a-pinned-action-in.md:73` — “a message naming the bot, its commit and the workflow, and `Assisted-by: None`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:196` — “so neither a model's trailer nor the human-only `None` would be true of it”

In itd-2609301020001595, a workflow writes the landed commit's message (naming the bot, its commit and the workflow) and declares Assisted-by: None. 34-build says a commit whose message abcd computed takes abcd's own label, because 'the human-only None' would not be true of it. The two documents give the None trailer incompatible meanings: no AI involved, versus written by a person.

### 715. itd-2610070550516046 requires the pick's intent to be reconciled with it before either is built; the pick is already built and shipped as build next.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-786fa57f6ab3137c · ledger: iss-2610262037208650 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610070550516046-on-abcd-s-dashboard-a-product-thinker.md:44` — “that intent must be reconciled with this one before either is built”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:168` — “The pick sub-verb chooses the intent instead of taking one named”

The draft requires itd-2609211116005482 (the pick) to be reconciled with it before either is built. 34-build documents the pick sub-verb (build next, shipped) already choosing intents by their scores. So the 'before either is built' order can no longer be met: reconciling now means changing shipped behaviour, not settling a design.

### 716. itd-19's per-stage defaults set the oracle to in-session, rp or rp+codex; the oracle.review key accepts only host or rp.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-93ca02f0c8aa300c · ledger: iss-2610262037211310 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-19-stage-aware-behaviour.md:31` — “oracle=in-session (fast iteration)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:544` — “`oracle.review` in the layered configuration names `host`, the bundled default, or `rp`”

34-build gives the review route's values in .abcd/config.json as host (the bundled default) or rp, and refuses any fault in oracle.review before anything moves. itd-19 calls the same host route in-session and adds rp+codex. A stage default written from the draft would use a second name for the default route and a value the reader refuses.

### 717. itd-2609091416304128 treats 'the default branch' as refs/remotes/origin/main; 34-build defines it as origin's HEAD, falling back to main, master, trunk, then develop.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-41c652746ea25b0f · ledger: iss-2610262037219105 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609091416304128-capture-resolve-refuses-a-record-the.md:35` — “The verb reads the ledger at `refs/remotes/origin/main` through git's object store”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:599` — “cut from the default branch (origin's `HEAD` as last fetched, else the first of `main`, `master`, `trunk` and `develop`)”

The draft promises a refusal when the default branch has already closed the record, but reads only origin/main. In a repository whose default branch is master or trunk, it would carry on as if there were no upstream ref, while 34-build's definition would find that repository's real default branch. The draft uses the term more narrowly than the brief defines it.

### 718. itd-25 calls an intent's back-link to its issues resolves_issues; 35-drain reads that same back-link as related_issues.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ab0c8b419a49cf94 · ledger: iss-2610262037227384 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-25-dredge-cross-corpus-synthesist.md:44` — “the intent's frontmatter gains `resolves_issues: [iss-N, iss-NM, iss-NO]` reciprocally”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:101` — “An intent it was promoted into, one that names it back in `related_issues`, still owns it”

Both name the intent-side field that lists the issues an intent took on, the counterpart of an issue's related_intents. A dredge promotion writes resolves_issues, but the drain decides that an intent still owns a promoted issue by reading related_issues. Under one of the two names, the drain would not see that ownership.

### 719. itd-26 names /abcd:memory ingest as a user-facing verb for taking in knowledge; in 37-memory, /abcd:memory is an agents' command whose only sub-verbs are add, list and remove.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-60a0d4448279e91f · ledger: iss-2610262037238195 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-26-loot-oss-vendor.md:70` — “Two distinct user-facing verbs (`/abcd:loot` for code, `/abcd:memory ingest` for knowledge)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:5` — “It is an agents' command: its page is hidden from a person's menu”

37-memory makes /abcd:memory a command for agents' memory notes, hidden from a person's menu, with sub-verbs add, list and remove. itd-26 uses the same name for a user-facing verb that takes knowledge into a shared source registry. One command name now covers two different things for two different audiences.

### 720. itd-37 has an agent (principle-distiller) write memory pages into the repository's .abcd/memory/; 37-memory says agents write only the machine layer.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-58e0c1b06c34a57a · ledger: iss-2610262037246775 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-37-modification-grammar.md:63` — “Writes append-only `spec_modification_grammar_<spec_id>.md` to `.abcd/memory/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:50` — “Agents write only the machine layer, and only through one gate”
