37-memory lets agents write only the machine file, through one gate; the repository's memory changes only by a reviewed edit, and there is no promote operation. itd-37 has the principle-distiller agent write append-only and curated pages into the repository's .abcd/memory/ at every spec completion. Either agents write repository memory or they do not.

### 721. itd-2610170634394993 calls the hold on the shared remote a claim; in 27-implement, a claim is the run-state lock on this machine that keeps sessions apart.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-13c5b34ca50ef6eb · ledger: iss-2610262037257443 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610170634394993-several-headless-agents-work-one.md:22` — “Each agent takes a piece of work by a claim on the shared remote”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:5` — “makes a record the unit of exclusion between them with a claim”

27-implement's claim is the per-record file in the machine-scoped run state that keeps one person's sessions apart. The coordination intent says each agent takes work 'by a claim on the shared remote' and re-checks 'a claim's generation number', meaning the hold on origin (which shipped as reservations). One name now covers two mechanisms with different scope, lease and failure behaviour.

### 722. itd-57 says nothing holds a planned item back from autonomous pickup today; the build brief's hold check already refuses any record carrying held:

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-59bfd06f3cbf4a37 · ledger: iss-2610262037255566 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-57-manual-hold-sentinel.md:17` — “Today, holding a spec back from the run seam means either deleting it (loses the work), leaving `plan_review_status` open (fragile — a reviewer can flip it), or hand-rolling a never-`done` dependency each time.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:68` — “the record carries no `held:`, well formed or not”

itd-57 assumes that today the only ways to keep work from an autonomous run are deleting it, leaving a review status open, or hand-rolling a never-done dependency, and that the selector skips specs by native spec dependency. The build chapter says no run starts, and the pick passes over, any record that carries `held:` in any form, and that blocking is read from the intent's `blocked_by`. The hold that itd-57 sets out to invent already exists on the record, so the two documents describe different pickup mechanisms for the same autonomous run.

### 723. itd-59 says the autonomous worker leaves only an ephemeral, pruned log; the build brief says a runner's transcript lands in the history store

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-fb6d9b2b499ad6f8 · ledger: iss-2610262037262122 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-59-autonomous-worker-transcript-capture.md:19` — “emits its instructions and reasoning only to an ephemeral per-pass log that run-dir hygiene prunes”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:499` — “the runner's transcript lands in abcd's history store, keyed on the repository's root commit”

itd-59 aims to close a gap. Its premise is that the unattended worker writes its instructions and reasoning only to a per-pass log that run-dir hygiene prunes. The build chapter says the transcript of a runner the step verb starts lands in abcd's history store, keyed on the repository's root commit, and that the record verb stores the run's transcripts there at the end. If the build chapter is right, the gap itd-59 describes is already closed for the loop that ships.

### 724. The sessions-announce intent promises every session's merge waits out a release cut; the reserve brief says merges armed before the hold still land

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-cd3c36c0dbed36e9 · ledger: iss-2610262037274982 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609151838312703-sessions-announce-what-they-are-doing.md:22` — “A session cutting a release holds merges with a reservation everyone sees, and every session's merge step waits until the cut is done.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-reserve.md:357` — “A merge armed, or queued, before the release was reserved (a pull request with auto-merge on, or an entry already in the merge queue) is not stopped by it and lands when its checks pass.”

The intent's press release says a release reservation makes every session's merge step wait until the cut is done. The reserve chapter says the hold only stops a merge from being armed. A pull request with auto-merge already armed, or already in the merge queue, when the release is reserved is not stopped and lands when its checks pass. Someone building from the intent would expect no merge to land during a cut, but the brief says some can.

### 725. The sessions-announce intent plans to rename the status board (bare abcd) to the dashboard; the dashboard brief already uses that name for the Tailscale web server

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f9d68b54a6967953 · ledger: iss-2610262037281449 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609151838312703-sessions-announce-what-they-are-doing.md:120` — “that change and renaming the status board to the dashboard are captured as their own records”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/36-dashboard.md:3` — “`/abcd:dashboard` runs the one network listener abcd has: a server on this computer that the product thinker opens from a phone”

Decision 21 of the intent records that the status board, which bare `abcd` renders, is to be renamed the dashboard. The dashboard chapter gives `/abcd:dashboard` to something else: abcd's one network listener, a server on this computer that the product thinker opens from another device. If the rename goes ahead, one name will cover two different surfaces.

### 726. The worktree-store intent calls a pruned worktree's archived local tier its notes and keeps it under ~/.abcd.noindex/notes/; the memory brief's notes are the memory notes in memory.json

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-5720d4198d0524cc · ledger: iss-2610262037293150 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609091014076309-session-and-agent-worktrees-live-in-a.md:46` — “it moves the tier into a sibling store, `~/.abcd.noindex/notes/<root-sha>/<UTC timestamp>-<worktree name>/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-memory.md:26` — “The machine's `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json` holds the person's own notes”

The memory chapter calls the person's own notes the memory notes kept in `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json`. The worktree-store intent moves a pruned worktree's local tier into a store named `~/.abcd.noindex/notes/` and calls it the notes archive. Under one abcd home, two different stores would both be called notes, and the one named `notes/` would not hold the memory notes.

### 727. The build intent arms auto-merge wherever a queue gates the default branch; the build brief arms it only when a ruleset also requires a person's approval

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-053d456c2b6e64fd · ledger: iss-2610262037294601 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:62` — “A pull request with auto-merge armed where the ruleset gates it through a queue, a pull request left open where it does not.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:785` — “where an active ruleset gates the default branch through a merge queue and an active ruleset on it requires a person's approval, it arms auto-merge with the queue's method; otherwise it leaves the pull request open for a person to merge (ruling AM1)”

Decision 3 of the build intent arms auto-merge wherever the ruleset gates the default branch through a queue, and leaves the pull request open otherwise. The build chapter cites decision 3 and ruling AM1. It arms auto-merge only where a queue gates the branch and a ruleset also requires a person's approval, and otherwise leaves the pull request open for a person. For a repository with a queue and no required approval, the two documents give opposite answers.

### 728. The build intent says each invocation does one step; the build brief keeps 'step' for a spec's steps and calls one invocation's work a stage

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-6bd3c576f4651693 · ledger: iss-2610262037301480 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:21` — “every invocation reads the state, does one step, writes the state and exits”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:388` — “A spec's steps and a lane's stages are two words for two things”

The build intent says every invocation does one step and exits. Under BU1, the build chapter keeps 'step' for a spec's steps only, and what one invocation performs is a lane's stage, one move of the run. Read with the brief's vocabulary, the intent says each invocation lands a whole spec step, which the loop does not do.

### 729. The build intent puts an issue lane's hand-back in the lane report; the drain brief puts handback in the receipt

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-8958d586530edc12 · ledger: iss-2610262037311796 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:76` — “the lane report carries a `handback:` field the loop reads as a first-class outcome”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:572` — “A lane that finds a decision in its issue writes `handback` (a kind, a reason and, where the kind needs one, a home) in its receipt instead of resolving it.”

Decision 10 of the build intent says the lane report carries a `handback:` field that the loop reads. The drain chapter says the lane writes `handback` (kind, reason, home) in its receipt instead. The brief treats the receipt and the implementer's report as two separate things, so the two documents put the field in different places.

### 730. The build brief says the no-host runner.fallback_host path waits on the ADR owed by the build intent's decision 6; the drive draft records the same reversal in an ADR of its own

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f8f437dafca4cea6 · ledger: iss-2610262037323830 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:539` — “is the process driver's reversal of the host-delegated boundary, and waits on the ADR decision 6 of the intent owes”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610222215485265-abcd-drain-run-from-a-plain-terminal.md:78` — “The reversal of the host-delegated boundary it carries is recorded as adr-2610222222326104, proposed.”

The build chapter says that sending a host-routed role to `runner.fallback_host` reverses the host-delegated boundary. It says that path waits on the ADR owed by decision 6 of the build intent, the `--auto-plan` record. The drive draft uses the same no-host path and records the same reversal as adr-2610222222326104, proposed. Two records now claim the decision that unlocks the no-host path, and the corpus does not say which one governs it.

### 731. itd-30 calls the fidelity auditor intent-fidelity-reviewer; the build brief calls that validator intent-auditor

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-392f79ac0824978c · ledger: iss-2610262037339788 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-30-design-fictions-as-intent-format.md:18` — “`intent-fidelity-reviewer` reads either dialect against the same delivered reality”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:683` — “on the lane whose landing closes the spec, an `intent-auditor`”

itd-30 says an agent named `intent-fidelity-reviewer` reads an intent of either format against delivered reality. The build chapter gives the fidelity audit to `intent-auditor`, on the lane whose landing closes the spec. One role has two names, and a format built from itd-30 would be aimed at an agent the build loop never dispatches.

### 732. itd-44 files ADRs as adr-< next-free>-< slug>.md; the drain brief cites the store's ADRs as < timestamp id>-< slug>.md

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-bdbba32cbf114cfd · ledger: iss-2610262037334466 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-44-fourth-intent-kind-decision.md:121` — “capture writes `adr-<next-free>-<slug>.md` into `.abcd/development/decisions/adrs/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:46` — “decisions/adrs/2609291342092738-a-drain-takes-an-issue-alone-only-when.md”

itd-44 sends a decision capture into `.abcd/development/decisions/adrs/` as `adr-<next-free>-<slug>.md`, which is a prefixed, sequentially numbered name. The drain chapter cites the record its rule is read from as a file in that store named with the bare timestamp id and slug, with no `adr-` prefix. An ADR filed the way itd-44 describes would be named in a form the store's own records do not use.

### 733. The decision-adapter intent needs lab harvest to report agreement rates with probability bands; the lab brief's harvest only assembles prose sections from findings and probe records

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-98716f3a82450774 · ledger: iss-2610262037348735 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609221009495079-abcd-s-typed-judgements-can-run-through.md:45` — “`abcd lab harvest` produces agreement rates per type with counts and probability bands”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/31-lab.md:99` — “assembles the lab's harvest in the lifeboat's section shape — intention, method, what worked, what is open, candidates, coverage — from the INTENTION, the findings log and the probe records”

The intent's evidence for turning a judgement type on is the agreement rates per type, with counts and probability bands, that `abcd lab harvest` produces from pairs the adapter recorded. In the lab chapter, the harvest assembles the lifeboat's sections from the INTENTION, the findings log and the probe records, and computes no statistics. The lab verbs run nothing either, because whoever runs the lab runs each probe. As the lab is written, its harvest cannot produce the figures this intent depends on.

### 734. itd-86's cold reading takes exactly one target document; the implement brief says a cold reading is handed the union of every position's paths

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bfb7ab7a36b8e890 · ledger: iss-2610262037357893 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-86-cold-reading-surface.md:29` — “A surface that takes exactly one target document and produces candidate detections against the constraints visible in that document alone.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:154` — “The reading corpus is derived, never restated: the union of every position's `object.paths` in the checkout's committed `.abcd/config/reading-presets.json`”

itd-86 defines the cold reading as a pass over exactly one document, judged against the constraints visible in that document alone. The implement chapter derives what a cold reading is handed as the union of every position's `object.paths` in the reading presets, and an entry there may be a directory that covers everything beneath it. The two documents disagree on what the cold reading's input is.

### 735. The model-tier intent says nothing reads the oracle setting and every delegated step goes where the harness picks; the build brief reads oracle.review to route a lane's reviews

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b45de80ed8e456d0 · ledger: iss-2610262037365749 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609170822093401-the-oracle-choice-is-one-repo-wide-value.md:26` — “backend is one repo-wide value that nothing reads, and every delegated step”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:544` — “`oracle.review` in the layered configuration names `host`, the bundled default, or `rp`”

The intent's press release starts from the premise that the oracle backend is a single repo-wide value nothing reads, so every delegated step reaches whatever model the harness picks. The build chapter says `oracle.review` in the layered configuration sends a build lane's ruthless and security reviews to `rp` instead of the host. The setting is read, and not every delegated step goes to the harness's choice.

### 736. The cloud-session intent admits work-in-progress branches without a receipt as an entry in the reservation build's list; the reserve brief admits receipt-less pushes only when every commit has the empty tree

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8e2a30d209681b6d · ledger: iss-2610262037376558 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610120738075547-a-person-hands-an-item-from-their.md:129` — “the push hook admits such a branch without a preflight receipt as one entry of its declared list of receipt-less prefixes (the list the reservation build introduces)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-reserve.md:111` — “The committed pre-push hook lets a push under the prefix through without a preflight receipt only when every commit it moves has the empty tree.”

The cloud intent lets a cloud session's work-in-progress branch past the push hook without a preflight receipt by adding it to the receipt-less prefix list that the reservation build introduced. That branch carries the session's actual changes. The reserve chapter says what that admission requires: a push under the prefix passes without a receipt only when every commit it moves has the empty tree. A branch of real changes fails that condition, so the dependency as written cannot admit it.

### 737. itd-91 has every commit trailer follow the project's chosen AI-credit convention; the announce brief requires an announcement's Assisted-by to be abcd's own label and nothing else

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8d755d4ed7c45e1e · ledger: iss-2610262037372402 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-91-ai-attribution-preference.md:17` — “Your answer is recorded once, in the repo, and from then on every commit trailer, pull-request body, and generated record uses exactly that convention.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-announce.md:84` — “its `Assisted-by` abcd's own `abcd:<version>` label and no other value”

itd-91 records a per-project choice of convention, from none to `Co-Authored-By:` to custom wording, and says every commit trailer, pull-request body and generated record then uses exactly that convention. The announce chapter checks every announcement against a validator that requires its `Assisted-by` trailer to be abcd's own `abcd:<version>` label and no other value. In a project that chose a different convention, announcement commits either fail the validator or ignore the project's choice.

### 738. itd-82 says a record filed before the remedy rule has no remedy and is ineligible; 35-drain reads such a record's legacy suggested_fix as its remedy

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2b96752b08a4f98c · ledger: iss-2610262037387137 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:44` — “a record filed before the rule carries none, and is ineligible and listed as such”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:75` — “record written before the field existed reads its `suggested_fix:` as its remedy.”

In itd-82 a remedy is only the remedy: field, so a record filed before the rule carries none and is ineligible and listed as such until a person adds one. 35-drain uses remedy in a wider sense: a record written before the field existed has its suggested_fix: read as its remedy, so it can pass the remedy test and be drained. A builder cannot follow both for the older backlog. Under one reading those records are listed as ineligible, and under the other they are worked unattended.

### 739. itd-82 declares the drain order ends oldest first; 35-drain orders each group by a rendezvous hash on origin, with file paths ahead of directories

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3dee3f366ce2a5e2 · ledger: iss-2610262037392162 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:49` — “then `nitpick` before `minor`, then oldest first; the run's summary states the rule”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:156` — “drain on `origin` takes each part in its own order instead: a rendezvous”

itd-82 fixes the order as category, then nitpick before minor, then oldest first, and declares it so that no implementer decides it alone. 35-drain adds a rule that puts issues whose found_at names a file before those naming a directory or no path. It keeps oldest first only in a checkout with no origin. On origin each part is taken in a per-holder, per-copy rendezvous-hash order instead. The two documents give different orders for the same eligible set, and a summary that states the itd-82 rule would describe an order the shipped drain does not follow.

### 740. itd-82's --max caps issues attempted and names --until-empty as the drain default's flag; 35-drain's cap counts lanes opened, and the drain has no --until-empty

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a65dcb9b54783fce · ledger: iss-2610262037409579 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:50` — “`--max <n>` caps issues attempted and `--until-empty` is the default's own name”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:254` — “When the drain has opened as many lanes as its cap, it ends and says so.”

In itd-82 --max counts issues attempted and --until-empty is the name of the default. In 35-drain the drain's cap ends the drain once it has opened that many lanes. Issues that the rule or the host judgement hand back open no lane, so they do not count toward that cap. The shipped flag list in the 35-drain appendix has --max and no --until-empty. So one flag name stands for two different counts, and the other name has no flag behind it.

### 741. 35-drain counts spend only in agent runs because no runner reports tokens or money; itd-166 has every route record token counts and cost

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b271cc6b5dcea03a · ledger: iss-2610262037413056 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:606` — “reports tokens or money, so neither is counted.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-166-each-run-should-record-the-model.md:18` — “then the model, provider, token counts and cost the answer reported”

35-drain counts the drain's spend in agent runs and says no runner reports tokens or money, so neither is counted. Shipped itd-166 says every role run through the host, a command-line runner or a provider connection records the model, provider, token counts and cost. For the claude and opencode runners the cost is computed by the harness. The drain summary's stated reason for leaving tokens and cost out is therefore false of the delivered runner record.

### 742. 27-implement says the model service can only be probed through a canary agent because abcd calls no model; itd-166 records every model call abcd makes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3879fcdbbccd694c · ledger: iss-2610262037410328 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/27-implement.md:508` — “only by the verdict of a canary agent the lead runs, since abcd calls no model.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-166-each-run-should-record-the-model.md:18` — “Every model call abcd makes now records two sides”

27-implement limits the outage probe of the model service to a canary agent the lead runs, on the ground that abcd calls no model. The same page says abcd runs no agent. Shipped itd-166 says abcd makes model calls through provider connections and runners, and records two sides for each. Its adapter streams usage from the provider, and the runners are launched by abcd. The premise the probe design rests on no longer holds for the delivered surface.

### 743. itd-177 says the readiness gate refuses an intent with an unrecorded context claim; 34-build says the readiness gate only reports scope conditions and the mechanism prompt as advisory

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7edaf0cf6bdafae2 · ledger: iss-2610262037423257 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:66` — “advisory; a run is where they bind, because an autonomous lane has nobody to”

Shipped itd-177 is titled as making the readiness gate refuse an intent that leaves a context claim, its scope conditions, unrecorded. 34-build describes the claim-sections check differently. There the readiness gate reports the mechanism prompt and the scope conditions as advisory, and they bind only when a build run starts. The two documents disagree on whether intent ready refuses such an intent or merely reports it.

### 744. itd-50 calls the fidelity verdict's agent intent-fidelity-reviewer; 34-build names the same validator intent-auditor

itd-50's press release says the intent-fidelity-reviewer records the NOT_MET verdict that its loop acts on. 34-build gives that role on the closing lane, which writes the per-criterion fidelity verdict, to an agent named intent-auditor. itd-50 models its intent-grain loop on an implementation-grain SHIP/NEEDS_WORK fix loop. In the build loop it would extend, 34-build names the verdicts that fail a round: FIX FIRST, BLOCK, NEEDS-INPUT, or a criterion NOT_MET. No validator there returns NEEDS_WORK. The verdict vocabulary that itd-50 assumes is not the one the shipped loop parses.

### 749. itd-147 rules that a surface chapter's hand-written prose never states a sub-verb; 27-implement states its sub-verbs above the generated appendix in a table and in prose

Shipped itd-147 makes the generated appendix the only place a chapter states flags and sub-verbs: the prose above it never states a flag or sub-verb. 27-implement keeps a hand-maintained sub-verb table above the appendix marker. itd-2609201916056194, filed in shipped/, places in scope, and rules in its decision 2, that where abcd runs as the binary with no host session the fallback is a host the operator configured, so there is always a landing. 34-build.md says a host session always drives the runner, and that the no-host path, which routes a host-routed role to runner.fallback_host, is a reversal of the host-delegated boundary still waiting on an ADR. Both cannot describe what shipped: either the no-host fallback was delivered with the intent, or the intent shipped without part of its scope and its record does not say so.

One document makes the shared word the rule; the other removes it as a confusion.

### 753. The spec-steps intent starts each step's lane only after the previous step merged; the build chapter opens a lane once the steps its needs line names have landed, so lanes can run side by side.

itd-2609212103565953 says the loop runs one lane per step in order and the next step's lane starts after the previous has merged. 34-build.md opens a lane once every step it needs has landed, read from the step's - needs: line, with every earlier step only as the default, and runs lanes in parallel up to the ceiling. The two agree for a spec that declares no needs. They disagree for one that does: there the brief opens a later step's lane before the previous one merges.

itd-2609091034175565 decision 31, and its In Scope 'Only origin' line, refuse any other remote layout, naming the remotes found, and its spec 2 has abcd build reserve the intent when it starts. 34-build.md says that in a checkout with no remote named origin nothing is reserved, and no build check refuses the run for it. 27-implement.md and 35-drain.md say the same of the land fence and the drain. ### 755. The stuck-lane intent sends a conflict on generated files back to the implementer as a fix round; the build chapter says a sync counts no fix round.

itd-2610161016391855 records that a conflict on declared generated files during a lane's sync goes back to the implementer as a fix round. 34-build.md sends a conflicting sync merge to a fresh implementer with a sync brief and states that a sync counts no fix round. ### 757. The load-check intent says the check never refuses and never waits; the implement chapter's load check, with its wait flag, holds make preflight's test stages until the load falls.

itd-2609231434459890 puts refusing and waiting out of scope outright: the check never refuses and never waits. 27-implement.md keeps that only for the plain form. With its wait flag the same check is the waiter concurrent sessions gate a preflight with, make preflight runs its test stages through it, and it blocks until the one-minute load is below the wait limit, exiting 1 when it gives up at its timeout. A preflight on a loaded machine carries on by the intent and is held by the brief.

### 758. The load-check intent defines a stray as a process outside abcd's lanes at near full CPU; the implement chapter defines it by a share of the process's fair share, a 0.4-core loop included, with nothing exempt by name.

itd-2609231434459890 defines the stray trigger as a process outside abcd's own lanes at near full CPU for longer than the stray limit. 27-implement.md defines a stray as a process whose lifetime CPU share reaches 0.9 of its fair share of the machine as loaded, so forty loops at 0.4 of a core each on 16 cores are all strays, and it exempts nothing by name: abcd's own lanes are exempt only by time. The word stray names a different set of processes in each document.

itd-2609211913453478 puts status on the record-families page as Now / Next / Later, the block the bare board renders. 38-announce.md names abcd status as the reader of the fixed-form announcements posted on the shared remote, and 37-reserve.md has it show the release holds as well. One word names the computed board block and also a separate verb that lists other sessions' announcements, so a reader who looks up status in the glossary runs a verb that does not show it.

### 768. itd-6 selects the reviewer route with `oracle.backend` (rp, codex, in-session); 34-build selects it with `oracle.review` (host, rp)

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f28b9427cdae4f31 · ledger: iss-2610262038033829 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:43` — “If reachable: lock `oracle.backend = "rp"`. If not: lock `oracle.backend = "codex"` (if Codex CLI present) or `"in-session"` (final fallback)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:544` — “`oracle.review` in the layered configuration names `host`, the bundled default, or `rp`”

itd-6 has the route locked as `oracle.backend` with the values `rp`, `codex` or `in-session`, while 34-build reads the same choice of reviewer route from `oracle.review`, whose only values are `host` (the bundled default) and `rp`. One setting carries two key names and two value sets, so a configuration written to one document's key is not the one the other reads.

### 769. itd-6 falls an unreachable RepoPrompt through Codex and then an in-session subagent; 34-build falls a review the rp route does not return straight back to the host

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-51f55dfcbe265c84 · ledger: iss-2610262038043808 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:42` — “if RP MCP is unreachable, abcd falls through to Codex if configured, then in-session subagent. Three-step cascade.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:566` — “the call records one fallback receipt (the role, `asked: rp`, the reason, abcd's detail, `ran: host`) in the state and the record”

itd-6 states a three-step cascade when RP MCP is unreachable: Codex if configured, then an in-session subagent. 34-build states that a review the `rp` route does not return records one fallback receipt with `ran: host` and hands the host the same brief and return path, with no Codex step between. The two cannot both describe what happens when RepoPrompt cannot be reached.

### 770. itd-6 says abcd never spawns Claude Code subprocesses; 35-drain has the drain move start the claude runner for the drain judge itself

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d3a85b684caa0211 · ledger: iss-2610262038052818 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:53` — “Spawning Claude Code subprocesses with `claude -p` — explicitly NOT how abcd works; abcd is the consumer, not the spawner”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:522` — “When the person's own layer routes `roles.drain-judge.runner` to the claude runner, the move that writes the host's request also writes the runner a brief of its own, the same question over the same quoted record with an answer shape that carries no digest, and starts the runner on it through the dispatch every routed role takes”

itd-6 records that spawning Claude Code subprocesses with `claude -p` is not how abcd works, abcd being the consumer and never the spawner. 35-drain states that when `roles.drain-judge.runner` is routed to the claude runner, the drain move writes the runner a brief and starts the runner through the dispatch every routed role takes. Either abcd starts a claude runner process or it never spawns one; both cannot stand as written.

### 771. itd-94 says autonomous drain runs inherit the implement-readiness gate, exit 1 a journaled SKIP; 35-drain's lanes are issue runs checked only by the drain rule and the peers check

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-95376c04c0ff6daf · ledger: iss-2610262038051992 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-94-an-intent-that-is-not-planned-cannot-be.md:25` — “Autonomous drain runs get the same gate for free: exit 1 is a journaled SKIP, never a guess.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/35-drain.md:561` — “Its checks are the rule above, read the same way, and the peers check”

itd-94 presents the intent implement-readiness gate (`abcd intent ready`) as one autonomous drain runs get for free, a NOT READY exit 1 becoming a journaled SKIP. 35-drain's drain works open issues, each lane being the run `abcd build <iss-N>` starts, whose checks are the drain rule and the peers check; no readiness gate applies to such a lane, and the drain as written has no intent run for itd-94's gate to stop.

### 772. itd-67 has `/abcd:launch ship` tag the repo; 37-reserve has the release workflow push the release tag after the merge

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ad4593a3247f040c · ledger: iss-2610262038066422 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:47` — “`/abcd:launch ship` auto-selects the bump tier (patch/minor/major) via the brief §4 phase-completion detection, writes the new version into `plugin.json`, updates `marketplace.json` (version + changelog entry), tags the repo”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/37-reserve.md:311` — “the release tag is pushed by the release workflow after the merge, so a two-hour hold could lapse in the middle of a cut.”

itd-67 puts tagging the repository in `/abcd:launch ship` itself, beside writing the new version. 37-reserve states the release tag is pushed by the release workflow after the merge, which is why the release hold lasts a day and ends when the tag appears on origin. The tag cannot be both the cut verb's own act and a workflow's act after a merge the cut waits on.

### 773. itd-89 files SessionEnd transcripts in the local per-repo store; 31-lab says the transcript store is machine-scoped and keyed on the root commit

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-297105ea8a1f4b3e · ledger: iss-2610262038074426 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-89-start-the-transcript-clock.md:18` — “files it in the local per-repo store”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/31-lab.md:30` — “The lab store is machine-scoped and keyed on the repository's root commit, as the transcript store is”

itd-89 states the SessionEnd hook files each session's transcript in the local per-repo store. 31-lab states the lab store is machine-scoped and keyed on the repository's root commit, as the transcript store is, so the transcript store is a machine-level store keyed per repository rather than a store local to the repository. The two place the captured transcript in different stores.

### 774. itd-76 puts the sources corpus under `~/.abcd/sources/`, abcd's user-level home; 29-report puts the sources store beside the inbox in the machine-scoped store

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-69836f6a0ccaecee · ledger: iss-2610262038084949 (filed)

The two give the same store different homes.

### 775. itd-60 makes `abcd spec close` refuse while the brief lags, failing closed without a reviewer; 34-build's closing lane runs the spec's close with no doc-fidelity review among its stages

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ed05aadd9c1412da · ledger: iss-2610262038097833 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md:124` — “`abcd spec close`, the verb that moves a planned intent to `shipped/`, refuses per intent while the brief lags the surface that intent delivered”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/34-build.md:743` — “In the lane's worktree it runs the spec's close (which ships the intent and parks the fidelity receipt)”

itd-60 makes the close that moves a planned intent to `shipped/` refuse per intent while the brief lags the delivered surface, its semantic layer host-delegated and failing closed when no reviewer runs. 34-build's closing lane runs the spec's close in its worktree to ship the intent, and its validate stage hands the lane only to the ruthless reviewer, the security reviewer and the intent-auditor, so nothing the lane runs produces the doc-fidelity verdict that close requires. As written, the closing landing depends on a close itd-60's gate refuses.

### 776. itd-80 names the Role 1 fidelity agent `intent-fidelity-reviewer`; 34-build gives the same closing-lane fidelity audit to `intent-auditor`

itd-80 specifies a host-delegated `intent-fidelity-reviewer` agent that reads an intent's acceptance criteria and the delivered diff and returns the per-criterion verdict the spec close ingests. 34-build hands that same audit, whose verdict the landing's close consumes, to an agent named `intent-auditor`. One agent carries two names across the record.

### 796. The glossary defines a step as a landable piece of a spec; the land chapter uses "step" for its own gate, push and enqueue acts while also citing a spec's step.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-f86aca1aac0fc17e · ledger: iss-2610262038278710 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/step.md:4` — “One of the ordered, independently landable pieces a spec lists under its Steps section”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-land.md:30` — “Every step is idempotent, so running the verb again resumes where it stopped.”

step.md gives step one sense: an ordered, independently landable piece a spec lists. 38-land calls its gate, push and enqueue acts steps (and its JSON carries `steps`), yet the same page cites spc-2610150728396006 step 4 in the spec sense. That is two senses in one document, and the glossary has no row for the second.

### 797. The glossary keeps bare "the loop" for the record loop and says abcd never owns a run loop; the agent catalog uses bare "the loop" for abcd's own implement loop.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-48fc2f98d14d93dc · ledger: iss-2610262038283527 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/loop.md:38` — “abcd never owns the run loop.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:40` — “the loop names each in turn and records the”

loop.md registers three senses, keeps bare "the loop" for the record loop, wants the others named in full, and says abcd never owns the run loop because an adapter supplies it. 01-agents uses bare "the loop" for the implement loop that `build` and `drain` run in abcd's own binary. That is a sense the glossary does not register and says abcd does not have.

### 798. The glossary makes "memory" an alias of memory note; the configuration chapter says unqualified "memory" means the repo-scope `.abcd/memory/` page store.

- class: terminology drift · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-0bc3faa2a8a3c4a4 · ledger: iss-2610262038299872 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/memory-note.md:5` — “aliases: ["memory"]”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1175` — “the brief says "memory" unqualified, it means the repo-scope store”

memory-note.md gives "memory" as the alias of a memory note, a short lesson kept in `memory.json`. 03-configuration says that when the brief writes "memory" unqualified it means the repo-scope store, the curated `.abcd/memory/` pages that `abcd library ingest` writes, and calls the notes a separate thing. A builder reading "memory" unqualified gets opposite stores depending on which page governs.

### 799. The memory-note entry says a promoted note goes into the project's rules; the configuration chapter puts promoted notes in the project's own `memory.json` layer.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-a89e833b5cea5c11 · ledger: iss-2610262038308994 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/memory-note.md:31` — “A note that has been recalled in several sessions is promoted into the project's rules”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:792` — “`memory.json` (the layer the prompt router recalls above the machine's”

memory-note.md's example has a note recalled across sessions promoted into the project's rules. 03-configuration says the project's memory notes live in `.abcd/memory.json`, a layer the prompt router recalls above the machine's `memory.json`, separate from `rules.json`. So promotion has two different destinations.

### 800. The surfaces register says library and memory are not one store under two names; the memory chapter's memory store holds the outside material the library ingests.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5512bc6932693807 · ledger: iss-2610262038319450 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:494` — “the two are not one store with two names: the library is for what a decision may need to cite”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:51` — “User-ingested PDF via `/abcd:library ingest <path>`”

04-surfaces/README separates the library (outside material a decision may cite) from memory (lessons an agent would otherwise relearn) and says they are not one store with two names. 07-memory's `.abcd/memory/` takes user-ingested PDFs, articles and transcripts through `/abcd:library ingest` as its page classes, so "memory" names the library's cited material there.

### 801. "persona" means a placeholder stakeholder from the personas registry, and also the name a session takes from a machine register.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a97494003fde2ed1 · ledger: iss-2610262038329713 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/persona.md:4` — “A placeholder stakeholder character drawn from the abcd personas registry”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:276` — “sets the session's persona name as its title (itd-2610111707085098)”

persona.md defines a persona as a placeholder stakeholder from the personas registry, used in press releases and design documents. 04-surfaces/README has the prompt router set the session's persona name as its title, and session-start reserve that name in the machine register. Agent sessions are not stakeholder archetypes, so one word names two concepts.

### 802. The library entry forbids "corpus" as a synonym; the surfaces register says "the corpus" and "the corpus verbs" for the library.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-a5b9f88a20151139 · ledger: iss-2610262038322994 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/library.md:6` — “forbidden_synonyms: ["corpus", "knowledge base"]”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:343` — “run in the host agent around the corpus verbs”

library.md lists "corpus" among the words that must not stand for the library. 04-surfaces/README describes the library page's steps as searching the corpus and running around the corpus verbs, and speaks of consulting the sources corpus, which is the substitution the entry forbids.

### 803. The oracle entry forbids "LLM" for the oracle; the adapters chapter names the oracle seam's native default "host-delegated LLM".

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-1a1f664cf6083c66 · ledger: iss-2610262038336864 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/oracle.md:6` — “forbidden_synonyms: ["LLM", "model", "bot", "AI", "chatbot"]”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:22` — “host-delegated LLM — abcd emits the prompt, the host's subagent dispatch runs it (adr-25)”

oracle.md lists "LLM" among the words that must not stand for the oracle. 02-adapters' seam table names the oracle seam's native default "host-delegated LLM", which is that substitution.

### 804. The glossary retires "phase" for dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves; the configuration chapter still schedules work into "a later phase".

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-c370fe4ab0eb5865 · ledger: iss-2610262038344053 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1215` — “Scheduled sync comes in a later phase (itd-13).”

phase.md is superseded: sequencing is now dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves, and unqualified "phase" carries only the retired sense. 03-configuration still sequences live work by it: scheduled sync comes in a later phase (itd-13), and so do schema migration and user-scope memory.

### 805. The memory chapter says the agent count stays at 15; the agent catalog ships eighteen.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-965eacd5c171d8a5 · ledger: iss-2610262038359555 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:158` — “The agent count stays at 15”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:18` — “Eighteen agent prompts ship in `agents/` today, in five groups:”

07-memory says the agent count stays at 15 and that the curator gains roles rather than peers. 01-agents says eighteen agent prompts ship in `agents/`. The two counts cannot both describe the roster.

### 806. The memory chapter says the lint contract §2 records library lint's warn-only exit-0 divergence; §2 records no divergence and says a warning raises the exit to 1.

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-85eb0d91ee3d9e03 · ledger: iss-2610262038368760 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:169` — “the recorded divergence from the standalone grammar”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:34` — “Raises the exit code to 1 on an otherwise-clean run”

07-memory gives `/abcd:library lint` a warn-only exit of 0 and calls it the recorded divergence from the standalone grammar, citing 06-lint §2. 06-lint §2 records no such divergence. Its severity model says a `warn` raises the exit code to 1 on an otherwise-clean run, so the record 07-memory depends on does not exist.

### 807. Universal patterns say abcd and the companion harness interoperate as two MCP servers; the build sequence says abcd's MCP front door is a design target.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-8afab655f6b6daf2 · ledger: iss-2610262038376261 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:73` — “when both are present, abcd and the companion harness interoperate as two independent MCP servers”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:108` — “a second thin door over the unchanged”

04-universal-patterns calls MCP the runtime contract: with both present, abcd and the companion harness interoperate as two independent MCP servers. 01-build-sequence marks the MCP front door as a design target, with `internal/surface/` holding only `cli` and `dashboard`. abcd cannot take part as an MCP server it does not have.

### 808. itd-1 says Audit Notes fill only from a hand-run audit; 01-agents says a build run audits automatically in the validate stage

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8a2f987a7be8f142 · ledger: iss-2610262038389473 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:45` — “Until that lands, a shipped intent's `## Audit Notes` is populated only when `/abcd:intent audit` is run by hand.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:156` — “A `build` run audits in the implement loop's validate stage, on the lane whose landing closes the intent's last open spec and before that lane lands”

itd-1 defers automatic invocation on the planned-to-shipped move and says that until it lands a shipped intent's Audit Notes are populated only when /abcd:intent audit is run by hand. 01-agents says a build run audits in the implement loop's validate stage before the lane that closes the intent's last spec lands. The audit cannot be both hand-run only and run by the build loop.

### 809. itd-1 says the SHIP/NEEDS_WORK/MAJOR_RETHINK review verdicts score plan and implementation reviews; 01-agents limits them to a packed lifeboat

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f72f62ab428645ba · ledger: iss-2610262038399413 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:47` — “which score *changes/runs* (oracle reviews of plans, implementations, completions; consumed by the native receipt schema validator)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:222` — “`{SHIP, NEEDS_WORK, MAJOR_RETHINK}` — assess a packed *lifeboat*.”

itd-1 says the review-verdict family scores changes and runs: oracle reviews of plans, implementations and completions. 01-agents, which itd-1 cross-references, says that family assesses a packed lifeboat only, and that the implement loop's reviewers use words of their own. So 'review verdict' covers two different scopes, and a builder cannot tell which verdicts a plan or implementation review returns.

### 810. itd-1 writes each audit's forensic copy under .abcd/logbook/; 04-universal-patterns says that name is retired and must not be re-minted

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5ed097e0e983496b · ledger: iss-2610262038393994 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:45` — “each run also writes a per-run forensic copy at `.abcd/logbook/audit/review-<ts>/report.{json,md}`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:94` — “Its root was once `.abcd/logbook/`; a 2026-07-12 adjudication moved run output to the local ephemeral tier and retired that name, which must not be re-minted”

itd-1 has every audit run write a per-run copy at .abcd/logbook/audit/review-< ts>/. 04-universal-patterns says the .abcd/logbook/ root was retired on 2026-07-12, run output moved to the local ephemeral tier, and the name must not be re-minted. A writer built from itd-1 would re-mint the retired namespace.

### 811. itd-1 cites lint code IL002 and points to 06-lint.md for it; 06-lint says the engine has no numbered codes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1a0d08947b0b51a8 · ledger: iss-2610262038415265 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:30` — “Lint code: `IL002` (delivered by spc-8 (predecessor store); see `05-internals/06-lint.md`).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “The engine carries no numbered code catalogue: rules are named, not numbered”

itd-1 names its drafts-to-planned hard block as lint code IL002 and points to 06-lint.md. 06-lint says the engine carries no numbered code catalogue and that rules are named in the JSON configs. The code itd-1 cites does not exist in the document it points to.

### 812. itd-5 keeps the candidate on a tie and says length is no tiebreak; 05-prompt-quality accepts a rewrite that ties and is more than 10% shorter

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-20ad23af547e97e7 · ledger: iss-2610262038415713 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:58` — “If the oracle variant scores better on the corpus, accept it; on a tie, keep the candidate. Length is not a tiebreak (see § Why).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/05-prompt-quality.md:127` — “accepts the reviewer's variant only if it scores at least as well and is more than 10% shorter”

itd-5 accepts the oracle's rewrite only if it scores better, keeps the candidate on a tie, and says length is not a tiebreak. 05-prompt-quality accepts the reviewer's variant when it scores at least as well and is more than 10% shorter. When a shorter rewrite ties, one rule locks the rewrite and the other locks the candidate, so the lock-time gate has two decision rules.

### 813. itd-5 calls the prompt linter lint_prompts; 05-prompt-quality calls the one shipped prompt-tree rule agent_contract

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ab4940e4499b0676 · ledger: iss-2610262038425929 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:23` — “`lint_prompts` validates set-membership against the `task_classes` enum in `internal/core/lint`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/05-prompt-quality.md:26` — “`agent_contract`, in `internal/core/lint`, is record-lint's dedicated rule for the agent-prompt tree.”

itd-5 says the lint_prompts check validates task_classes set-membership in internal/core/lint. 05-prompt-quality says agent_contract is record-lint's dedicated rule for the agent-prompt tree, and that the membership check is staged. One linter has two names, and the two documents also disagree about what it checks.

### 814. itd-5 preserves an oracle cascade it attributes to universal pattern § 7; 04-universal-patterns says the core imposes no cascade

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-088804ba9251593e · ledger: iss-2610262038431352 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:87` — “Adding `capability_scope` does NOT modify the oracle cascade”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:60` — “Guidance the adapter layer offers, never a cascade the core imposes.”

itd-5 says adding capability_scope leaves the oracle cascade unchanged. It cites § 7 as a 'fixed cascade' with an availability-driven fallback chain, and puts its selector above that cascade. 04-universal-patterns describes a native default that configuration overrides, and says the core imposes no cascade. The seam itd-5 promises to preserve is one the patterns page says does not exist.

### 815. itd-5 counts 14 (now 15) agents under its rule; 01-agents says eighteen agent prompts ship

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-af6ef4926a7aab85 · ledger: iss-2610262038443634 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:25` — “abcd ships all 14 (now 15) agents under this rule.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:18` — “Eighteen agent prompts ship in `agents/` today, in five groups:”

itd-5 says abcd ships 14 (now 15) agents under the discipline. 01-agents says eighteen agent prompts ship in agents/ today. The discipline's count of the roster it governs is wrong.

### 816. itd-5's lock-time pre-flight submits prompts to lifeboat-oracle; 01-agents' rosters have no such agent

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9c0120ee3ffcbb9d · ledger: iss-2610262038457611 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-5-prompt-quality-additions.md:21` — “the candidate prompt submitted to `lifeboat-oracle` for clarity-rewrite”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:23` — “`lifeboat-reviewer` (`disembark review`), `graveyard-interpreter`”

itd-5's one-shot pre-flight sends each candidate prompt to lifeboat-oracle for a clarity rewrite. In 01-agents the lifeboat agent that ships is lifeboat-reviewer, which feeds disembark review and does not rewrite prompts. Neither 01-agents' shipped list nor its design-target roster names a lifeboat-oracle, so the pre-flight depends on an agent no document provides.

### 817. itd-11 has lifeboat-oracle audit a lifeboat's output; 01-agents names the lifeboat auditor lifeboat-reviewer

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-83b7b389ee72b809 · ledger: iss-2610262038460690 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-11-pass-b-pitfall-mitigation.md:15` — “the lifeboat-oracle's audit catches and quarantines low-confidence Pass B output before it pollutes the brief”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:23` — “`lifeboat-reviewer` (`disembark review`), `graveyard-interpreter`”

itd-11 has lifeboat-oracle audit Pass B output and quarantine what fails before it reaches the lifeboat brief. 01-agents names the agent that audits a packed lifeboat lifeboat-reviewer, serving disembark review, and lists no lifeboat-oracle. The same role has two names.

### 818. itd-14 marks a prompt's version with a `## Prompt Version: X.Y` field; 05-prompt-quality requires semver prompt_version frontmatter

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-424f102ee6423667 · ledger: iss-2610262038472526 (filed)

itd-14 records a prompt's version in a `## Prompt Version: X.Y` body field. 05-prompt-quality requires a prompt_version frontmatter key holding a valid semver on every prompt, and agent_contract enforces it. The version marker has two names and two formats.

### 819. itd-14 keeps a changelog at agents/< name>/CHANGELOG.md; 01-agents keeps the changelog out of agents/, at .abcd/development/agents/

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ef029a806fca1870 · ledger: iss-2610262038484184 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:71` — “the roster's README and changelog, plain docs with no agent frontmatter, live at [`.abcd/development/agents/`] (../../agents/README.md) instead (iss-110)”

itd-14 puts one changelog per prompt at agents/< name>/CHANGELOG.md. 01-agents says the roster's changelog lives at .abcd/development/agents/, because the loader registers what sits in agents/ and that directory holds only prompts and their fixture directories. itd-14 puts the changelog where the agent-directory contract excludes it.

### 820. itd-81 puts each judge's calibration corpus at agents/< name>/corpus/; 01-agents says agents/ holds prompts and fixture directories and nothing else

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-911a73ce9cdc3f57 · ledger: iss-2610262038490693 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-81-judge-calibration.md:25` — “`agents/<name>/corpus/`, containing labelled cases of **both** classes:”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:68` — “`agents/` holds the prompt files and their per-agent fixture directories and nothing else.”

itd-81 requires each verdict-rendering agent to have a calibration corpus at agents/< name>/corpus/. 01-agents says agents/ holds the prompt files and their per-agent fixture directories and nothing else. The corpus location the discipline requires is excluded by the agent-directory contract.

### 821. itd-37 says Role 1 boilerplate detection runs at plan-review and ship time; 01-agents says the auditor's modification-grammar output is deferred and in no prompt or lint

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-06cab784fc133ace · ledger: iss-2610262038495354 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-37-modification-grammar.md:69` — “Role 1 boilerplate detection runs at plan-review and ship time”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:160` — “term-drift, PRD-fidelity and modification-grammar outputs the role was drawn with are **deferred**: none is in the shipped prompt or in any lint.”

itd-37 says every spec inherits Role 1 boilerplate detection, run at plan-review and at ship time. 01-agents says the modification-grammar output the auditor role was drawn with is deferred, and is in neither the shipped prompt nor any lint. A spec author would rely on a gate that does not run.

### 822. itd-37 defines the concreteness lint as numbered codes MG001 to MG003; 06-lint says the engine has no numbered codes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-71e74d6553bf2bd5 · ledger: iss-2610262038501901 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-37-modification-grammar.md:56` — “in the native intent lint with three codes:”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “The engine carries no numbered code catalogue: rules are named, not numbered”

itd-37 specifies its concreteness lint as three numbered codes, plus MG004 and VR001 elsewhere. 06-lint says the lint engine carries no numbered code catalogue and that rules are named in the JSON configs. Building itd-37 as written breaks the lint contract's naming rule.

### 823. itd-37 puts append-only pages into .abcd/memory/; universal pattern § 8 gives each namespace one lifecycle class and lists .abcd/memory/ as compounding-curated

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d05351831fdb0337 · ledger: iss-2610262038511722 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-37-modification-grammar.md:63` — “Writes append-only `spec_modification_grammar_<spec_id>.md` to `.abcd/memory/` with `source.class: spec_modification_grammar`.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:188` — “Lifecycle class is declared in the parent README of each artefact namespace.”

itd-37 writes append-only per-spec pages into .abcd/memory/, beside a compounding-curated per-domain page, and cites § 8 for both lifecycles. 04-universal-patterns § 8 declares one lifecycle class per artefact namespace in its parent README, lists .abcd/memory/ as compounding-curated, and has lint block a namespace whose behaviour disagrees with its class. One namespace cannot hold both of itd-37's classes under that taxonomy.

### 824. itd-10's destroy deletes a lifeboat and a logbook inside .abcd/; 03-configuration says neither namespace exists in any tree

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-db5e9428ce061d51 · ledger: iss-2610262038521887 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-10-purge-uninstall.md:16` — “AND the entire `.abcd/` namespace (including lifeboat, dev artefacts, logbook, and config)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1367` — “Three namespaces are deliberately absent from every tree: `voyage/`, which is user-scope and never committed; `logbook/`, retired in favour of the local tier's logs; and `lifeboat/`, because the lifeboat is out-of-tree output at an operator-chosen destination.”

itd-10's destroy removes the whole .abcd/ namespace, which it says includes a lifeboat and a logbook. 03-configuration says logbook/ is retired and lifeboat/ is absent from every tree, because the lifeboat is out-of-tree output. The deletion list names directories the configuration model says are never there.

### 825. itd-13's dev-sync curates entries into the issue ledger; 03-configuration says capture writes the ledger directly and the sync has nothing left to migrate there

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-06ba6997c3aac6e8 · ledger: iss-2610262038534481 (filed)

### 847. itd-57 unblocks a spec with a native `spec rm-dep`, but the spec verb registers only its bare board and `spec close`

### 851. itd-83's fallback for harnesses without hooks is a pointer in AGENTS.md's marked section, but the configuration page says a default install writes no marker block

### 853. itd-85 makes `abcd audit` a repository conformance check, but the agent catalogue reserves the top-level `/abcd:audit` for itd-16's hash-chain surface

### 854. itd-85's `abcd audit` checks whether a repository conforms, which the register already gives to `/abcd:lint`

Two verbs claim the same ground, and neither document draws a line between them.

### 859. The oracle-routing intent sends a step to a configured provider that can serve its tier, but the adapters page says a tier alone never reaches a provider

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-d106ee8cd8acaf45 · ledger: iss-2610262039253719 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:129` — “tier: it is reached by a role or a judgement type pointed at it, never by a tier”

itd-2609170822093401 matches the winning row's tier against the machine's connections and uses a provider wherever it is reachable and able to serve the tier, so economy rows run on a local server without anyone touching a row. The adapters page says a provider claims no tier: it is reached only by a role or judgement type pointed at it, and that role wins whatever tier the routing tables name. The two documents cannot both describe how a step reaches a provider, and the intent's central mechanism is the one the shipped adapter rules out.

### 860. The build intent arms auto-merge wherever the ruleset gates merges through a queue, but the land page says AM1 arms it only where a queue and a required approval both exist

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f36ea247f6e1b3d0 · ledger: iss-2610262039262634 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:62` — “A pull request with auto-merge armed where the ruleset gates it through a queue, a pull request left open where it does not.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/38-land.md:125` — “auto-merge is armed only where a merge queue gates the default branch and a”

Decision 3 of itd-2609201916151817 arms auto-merge on a pull request wherever the ruleset gates it through a queue. The land page says the shared merge gate follows ruling AM1, which arms auto-merge only where a merge queue gates the default branch and a ruleset requires a person's approval. A repository with a queue but no required approval is armed under the intent and left alone under the land page.

### 861. The consistency-pass hook runs rule checks over the whole corpus at commit time, but the lint contract's pre-commit tier lints only staged lines so that old findings never block

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2dd1ded1fda1c5f5 · ledger: iss-2610262039276483 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609291923559186-the-consistency-pass-runs-where-records.md:151` — “the rule checks cover the whole corpus; the model pass covers the staged records and their links”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:52` — “so a pre-existing finding on an untouched line never blocks a commit”

itd-2609291923559186 rules that its pre-commit hook runs the rule checks over the whole corpus and, under the 'stop' setting, refuses the commit and names the finding. The lint contract's design target for the pre-commit tier lints only the files a commit stages, filtered to the staged lines, so that a pre-existing finding on an untouched line never blocks a commit. The two documents draw the pre-commit lint tier with opposite scope: under 'stop', a finding in an untouched record blocks a commit that the lint contract says must not be blocked.

### 862. The memory-notes intent lets the status line write one fill file, but the configuration page says the status line writes nothing at all

### 863. The land page calls AM1's arming 'human mode', but the facilitator-mode intent rules that `human` arms nothing, even where the forge would hold the merge for approval

'Human mode' means arming under AM1 in one document and refusing to arm in the other.

### 864. The configuration chapter stages itd-50's audit loop as a per-intent frontmatter mode, while itd-50 rules that the loop is build's last stage for every intent, not a per-intent mode

### 874. itd-105 keeps every hook command calling `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/abcd` directly, with the bootstrap as the first SessionStart hook; the configuration chapter says every event's command is `sh` on a per-event shim and SessionStart is one chained command

### 879. The surfaces register gives the hidden hook verb six entrypoints, while the away-mode intent adds a Stop hook that runs `abcd hook stop`.
