Both cannot hold: either the hook verb has more than six entrypoints or the stop check is not one of them.

### 880. The README's `abcd rules` loads a machine-wide rules.json layer, which itd-3 explicitly rejects.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b3d22b75bf44cabe · ledger: iss-2610262039423717 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:283` — “the bundled default domains, then the machine's `~/.abcd.noindex/rules.json`, then the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-3-modular-rules-loader.md:41` — “Keeping a personal cross-repo rules file recreates exactly the”

The rules verb section says the loader reads the bundled domains, then the machine's `~/.abcd.noindex/rules.json`, then the checkout's `.abcd/rules.json`. itd-3, the shipped intent the README names as delivering `rules`, lists a global user rules file as explicitly rejected, because it recreates the scaffolding-outside-the-repo failure, and says the loader is per-repo only. itd-3 does not record the later reversal, so the two documents give opposite answers on whether a user layer exists.

### 881. 03-configuration makes the rules refresh event-driven with a 15-turn backstop; itd-3 forces a full re-inject every N turns, N defaulting to 5.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-e332ef7c41019880 · ledger: iss-2610262039439681 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:93` — “prompt-router refresh backstop (itd-3). The primary refresh is”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-3-modular-rules-loader.md:30` — “Signature-based dedup; force full re-inject every N turns (N defaults to 5, configurable).”

03-configuration's `rules.force_refresh_every_n` defaults to 15. It calls the primary refresh event-driven, on SessionStart and PreCompact, and says a domain that stays in force is never re-injected unchanged within a session. itd-3 specifies signature-based dedup with a forced full re-inject every N turns, N defaulting to 5, as the way to recover from compaction. The default and the refresh mechanism disagree.

### 882. 03-configuration says the shared tier holds 'the append-only decision log'; itd-2609151138388536 replaced that log with one file per decision.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-15b192a28d7a0ec9 · ledger: iss-2610262039442943 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:805` — “current orientation, the append-only decision log, the external-contribution runbook”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609151138388536-append-only-logs-conflict-on-every-merge.md:25` — “longer a line appended to the bottom of one shared file. It is a record with”

The three-tier table says `.abcd/work/` holds the append-only decision log. itd-2609151138388536 (shipped) retires `.abcd/work/DECISIONS.md` and says a decision is no longer a line appended to one shared file but its own record in `.abcd/work/decisions/`. A reader of the tier table would look for a single appended log that no longer exists.

### 883. itd-34 calls the three-role audit agent `intent-fidelity-reviewer`; 01-agents calls the same agent `intent-auditor`.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-eee897549482b295 · ledger: iss-2610262039443223 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:133` — “## `intent-auditor`: one agent, three roles”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:88` — “### `intent-fidelity-reviewer` shape-classification role (third role)”

Both documents describe one agent with three roles: single-document fidelity, cross-document fidelity and shape (kind) classification. itd-34 uses `intent-fidelity-reviewer` throughout. 01-agents' catalogue uses `intent-auditor`, and 05-prompt-quality says the agent was renamed. That gives one agent two names, and itd-34 does not map one to the other.

### 884. itd-34 ships a shape-classification role that runs from the pre-commit hook and `/abcd:intent shape`; 01-agents says the role is a design target with no `shape` sub-verb.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-923f527aa1cdb309 · ledger: iss-2610262039451705 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/01-agents.md:176` — “`shape` sub-verb is registered, and no cached suggestions exist for bare”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:90` — “It runs continuously via the pre-commit hook (writing findings to the latest report) and on-demand via `/abcd:intent shape`.”

itd-34 is in shipped/. Its scope says the third role runs continuously from the pre-commit hook and on demand through `/abcd:intent shape`, and that bare `/abcd:intent` shows cached suggestions. 01-agents says the kind-classification role is a design target, that no `shape` sub-verb is registered and that no cached suggestions exist. Both cannot be accurate: one is a shipped record promising a surface, the other is the catalogue saying it was never built.

### 885. itd-34 files shape findings under `.abcd/logbook/`, a name 04-universal-patterns retired and says must not be re-minted.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c9127c078b228674 · ledger: iss-2610262039463304 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:94` — “Its root was once `.abcd/logbook/`; a 2026-07-12 adjudication moved run output to the local ephemeral tier and retired that name, which must not be re-minted”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:90` — “Findings live at `.abcd/logbook/audit/shape-<ts>/report.{json,md}`.”

itd-34 says shape findings live at `.abcd/logbook/audit/shape-<ts>/report.{json,md}`. 04-universal-patterns says the log root was once `.abcd/logbook/`, that a 2026-07-12 adjudication moved run output to the local tier and retired the name, and it draws the shape reports at `audit/shape-<ts>/` under `.abcd/.work.local/logs/`. itd-34's decisions date from 2026-09-21, after the retirement, so it uses a retired name for a location the brief puts elsewhere.

### 886. itd-34 maps a standalone intent one-to-one to a flow-next spec; the surfaces register says an intent owns one or more specs in the native spec store.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1cf9980d6a5a4160 · ledger: iss-2610262039476904 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:275` — “an intent owns one or more specs”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:21` — “A standalone intent maps 1:1 to a flow-next `spec`”

itd-34's press release and lifecycle paths say a standalone intent maps 1:1 to a flow-next `spec`, planned through `/flow-next:plan`. The README's `spec` row describes the native spec store, where `spec close` ships an intent only when no open spec still names it, because an intent owns one or more specs. The two documents disagree on which store holds specs and on how many specs one intent can have.

### 887. itd-2610030810350727 says a question that breaks the layout rules is refused before it reaches the person; 04-universal-patterns says a question that is too tall is shown anyway.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6360503ecf105732 · ledger: iss-2610262039482748 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:18` — “rows limit is the exception: a question too tall for the narrow window is”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610030810350727-every-question-abcd-puts-to-a-person.md:32` — “A question that breaks these rules is refused before it reaches you, naming the part and the limit, so it is asked again properly.”

The intent's press release says any question that breaks the rules is refused before it reaches the person, naming the part and the limit, and that such a question reads at 80 columns without scrolling. 04-universal-patterns makes the rows limit an exception: a question too tall for the narrow window is shown, and the agent is told afterwards to keep the next one within it. Under the brief a question over the rows limit reaches the person; under the press release it cannot.

### 888. itd-4 ships a `dev-sync` migration of `.abcd/.work.local/issues.md`; 03-configuration says no `dev-sync` verb exists.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-936bba8318c0381e · ledger: iss-2610262039487315 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:1194` — “No `dev-sync` verb is registered on the binary,”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-4-issue-capture.md:46` — “`dev-sync` promotes existing `.abcd/.work.local/issues.md` entries to the structured ledger on first run after install”

itd-4's scope has `dev-sync` move existing `.abcd/.work.local/issues.md` entries into the structured ledger on the first run after install. 03-configuration says the whole `dev-sync` section is staged, that no `dev-sync` verb is registered and that the migration has nothing left to do. itd-4 is in shipped/, so it claims a delivered mechanism that the configuration chapter says does not exist.

### 889. 04-universal-patterns classes issue-ledger entries as immutable once created; itd-4's `capture resolve` moves an entry and adds a resolution note.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b7c9cceafff165be · ledger: iss-2610262039494979 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:195` — “capture issue-ledger entries (immutable post-create)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-4-issue-capture.md:36` — “move to `resolved/` with optional resolution note”

The lifecycle taxonomy puts capture issue-ledger entries in the append-only class: never modified after creation, old entries kept verbatim. itd-4 defines `capture resolve` as moving the record to `resolved/` with an optional resolution note, and gives every record an `updated` field. An entry that changes folder and gains text after creation is not immutable. The same table also lists the ledger as compounding-curated.

### 890. itd-40 says identity and lineage live directly in the history `index.json`; 03-configuration puts lineage in a separate file per repository under that key.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a8cc9f1f15e3d872 · ledger: iss-2610262039504627 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:441` — “root-commit SHA, and one identity-and-lineage file per repo under that key.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-40-folder-classification.md:42` — “the history `index.json` is the single registry; root-SHA identity and lineage live there directly.”

itd-40 says identity is not duplicated because the history `index.json` is the single registry, with identity and lineage held there directly, and it points to 03-configuration. 03-configuration says the store holds a registry keyed on the root-commit SHA plus one identity-and-lineage file per repository under that key. Lineage cannot be both directly in the index and in a separate per-repository file.

### 891. itd-40 has ahoy create `~/.abcd/history/`; 03-configuration says no reader ever reads the old `~/.abcd` name and that its presence stops every command.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-8e286d9acb92b47c · ledger: iss-2610262039519748 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-40-folder-classification.md:36` — “if `~/.abcd/history/` does not exist, the first `/abcd:ahoy install` creates it (directory + `index.json`) before registering the repo.”

itd-40 says that if `~/.abcd/history/` does not exist, the first `/abcd:ahoy install` creates it. 03-configuration says the home is now `~/.abcd.noindex/`, that only the stop check reads the earlier name `~/.abcd`, and that anything standing there stops every command until it is renamed. Followed as written, itd-40 creates the very path the brief treats as a stop. Other shipped intents repeat the old spelling.

### 892. itd-36 gives `principle-distiller` a curator role over memory ingest from external sources; 01-agents lists it as feeding only `disembark principles`.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-647b485434280a35 · ledger: iss-2610262039527135 (filed)

itd-36 (shipped) adds a curator role to `principle-distiller`: an external-source ingest pipeline as input, and typed `source:` frontmatter on every page it writes into `.abcd/memory/`. 01-agents puts `principle-distiller` among the lifeboat and release synthesis agents, each of which feeds one verb, and pairs it with `disembark principles` only. The README's agent table also has it serve `disembark` alone. The catalogue gives it no memory-curation duty.

### 893. `/abcd:memory` is itd-36's curated knowledge store with `ingest`, `ask` and `lint`, and also the README's command for short lessons agents keep.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4a3091aa9f4e301a · ledger: iss-2610262039522985 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-36-memory-unification.md:41` — “**`/abcd:memory` command** with sub-verbs `ingest` / `ask` / `lint`.”

itd-36's scope defines `/abcd:memory` as the command with sub-verbs `ingest`, `ask` and `lint` over the `.abcd/memory/` store, whose verbs have since merged into library. The README's register lists `/abcd:memory` as the notes command that keeps short lessons an agent would otherwise relearn, stored in `memory.json`. itd-36 records the merge but not the reuse of the name, so one name stands for two different stores with different verbs.

### 894. itd-2609212130136102 caps the person's default verb list at fourteen; the README says neither surface caps it and lists seventeen.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6a32678d30ca977d · ledger: iss-2610262039536939 (filed)

itd-2609212130136102 (shipped) says the person's default list holds at most fourteen verbs once it ships. ### 895. itd-2609231013154443 names `abcd changelog` as the release-page preview; the README says `changelog` merged into `launch` and is in neither help block.

itd-2609231013154443's scope gives the read-only preview as `abcd changelog`, or the `launch` dry run. The README says `changelog` is in neither help block because it merged into `launch` as its preview, and the merges of itd-2610090831227812 keep no old name as an alias. One document offers a verb the other says no longer exists.

### 896. itd-2609212113220149 requires the verb's sentence to be byte-identical on the list, the help and the plugin page; the README adds a 'use when' clause to two pages' descriptions.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-adfbaa8852fff11c · ledger: iss-2610262039556194 (filed)

itd-2609212113220149 says the sentence is rendered onto the command list, the verb's own `--help` and its plugin page, byte-identical, and that its test fails on any difference between the three. The README says a page that carries a host workflow adds one 'use when' clause after the sentence in its `description:`, that `library` and `ahoy` both do, and that the test sets the clause aside. Those two page descriptions are therefore not byte-identical to the sentence.

### 897. 'Status' names both the board's Now / Next / Later block and `/abcd:status` with its `## STATUS` block of announcements.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-2364a6c066cbd0ef · ledger: iss-2610262039567036 (filed)

itd-2609212103568351 rules that the Now / Next / Later block that replaced the roadmap 'is called status'. 39-status defines `/abcd:status` as the people's view of announcements, reservations and releases being cut on the shared remote, and gives the prompt hook a `## STATUS` block that carries those announcements. One word names two unrelated renders, so 'the status block' could mean either.

### 898. itd-34 says its subtype deferral mirrors the lint-code namespace pattern in 06-lint; 06-lint says the engine has no code catalogue.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-5b1c212fef9eb237 · ledger: iss-2610262039572342 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:14` — “The engine carries no numbered code catalogue: rules are named, not numbered”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-34-three-intent-kinds.md:109` — “This mirrors the lint-code namespace pattern in”

itd-34 justifies deferring a closed subtype enum by pointing to the lint-code namespace pattern in 05-internals/06-lint.md, where categories are added as intents introduce them. 06-lint says the engine has no numbered code catalogue, that rules are named rather than numbered, and that any literal list belongs in a generated region. The pattern itd-34 relies on is not in the document it cites.

### 899. itd-2609212137129937 bans 'maintainer' in every lint root, the command pages and rules included; 06-lint limits docs-lint to `docs/` and the repo-root prose.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ded0eb903972c859 · ledger: iss-2610262039584858 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/06-lint.md:10` — “lints `docs/` and the repo-root prose for change-narration”

itd-2609212137129937 (shipped) says the docs-lint banned-token list gains the word for every lint root, the command pages and the rules included. 06-lint says docs-currency (`abcd lint docs`) covers `docs/` and the repo-root prose, and that record-lint covers `.abcd/development/`. Neither root includes `commands/` or the rules files. Either those are lint roots and 06-lint understates the reach, or the ban does not cover them.

### 900. 03-configuration schedules work 'in a later phase'; itd-2609211913453478 retired phases as the unit of sequencing.

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-ec59b609a78be04c · ledger: iss-2610262039581980 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:428` — “Schema versioning and cross-version migration come in a later phase”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609211913453478-one-page-in-the-glossary-maps-abcd-s.md:55` — “Phases and milestones are retired; sequencing is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves”

itd-2609211913453478 rules that phases and milestones are retired and that sequencing is dependencies plus the lifecycle shelves. 03-configuration still says schema versioning and migration come in a later phase, that migrators are added if a later phase changes the shape, that scheduled sync comes in a later phase, and that cross-project memory pages are a later phase. It uses the retired unit as if it still sequences work.

### 901. 04-universal-patterns keeps multi-agent claims in `.abcd/coordination/` with local-only state; itd-2609091034175565 makes the reservation branch on origin the one record of who holds what.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-aa3490f2b7564025 · ledger: iss-2610262039590757 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/04-universal-patterns.md:139` — “Coordination state (file locks like `shape.lock`, multi-agent claims per itd-33) lives at `.abcd/coordination/`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609091034175565-nothing-tells-an-agent-that-a-record-it.md:211` — “nothing kept only on one computer (the local tier, a note on the desktop, same-account messaging) is the source of truth for who holds what.”

04-universal-patterns says coordination state, including multi-agent claims under itd-33, lives at `.abcd/coordination/`, with `active-work.json` and the locks kept local and gitignored. itd-2609091034175565 rules that nothing kept on one computer, the local tier included, decides who holds what, and that the reservation branch is the only transport. Both documents say where agent claims live, and they put them in different places.

### 902. 02-adapters sends spec-tied reviews to a native spec review store; itd-28 dropped that store, so the dated folders and gate receipts are the store.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7659910dd3ea55be · ledger: iss-2610262040004118 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/02-adapters.md:284` — “spec-tied reviews go straight to the native spec”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-28-rp-reviews-into-flow.md:112` — “the dated review folders and the gate receipts are the store”

02-adapters' RepoPrompt harvesting section says spec-tied reviews go straight to the native spec review store and are never swept, and its reviews reader reads spec-tied reviews beside the charter folders. itd-28's first decision drops the review store its scope described, so the dated review folders and the gate receipts are the store. Its third decision says no abcd verb files a dated folder. The brief names a store that the shipped intent removed.

### 903. itd-2609091034175565 says a person sees reservations through `abcd peers`; the README lists `peers` as a verb for agents and hosts only.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-9af1a1a49240b872 · ledger: iss-2610262040016204 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609091034175565-nothing-tells-an-agent-that-a-record-it.md:267` — “a person sees reservations through `abcd peers` and the record and board renders.”

itd-2609091034175565's decision 39 hides `reserve` from the person and says a person sees reservations through `abcd peers` and the record and board renders. The README puts `peers` in the agents-and-hosts block, whose rule is that only a command no person types belongs there, and hides that block's pages from a person's `/abcd:` menu. The verb named as the person's view is one the placement says no person types. The README now gives that view to `/abcd:status`.

### 904. itd-2610030720038073 says the stop names one rename command and abcd then runs as before; 03-configuration's stop also names a worktree repair.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-54c868b92cd7668a · ledger: iss-2610262040028651 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/03-configuration.md:706` — “the line names the rename, `mv ~/.abcd ~/.abcd.noindex`, and the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2610030720038073-abcd-keeps-its-home-folder-out-of.md:21` — “asks the person to rename ~/.abcd to ~/.abcd.noindex, naming the one command; after that, abcd runs as before.”

The confirmed press release says an existing install stops and asks the person to rename `~/.abcd` to `~/.abcd.noindex`, naming the one command, after which abcd runs as before. 03-configuration says the stop line names the rename and also a `git worktree repair` command that reconnects the worktrees moved with the store, and that `abcd ahoy` reports any store worktree still unlinked. The rename alone does not bring back the earlier state.

### 905. The surfaces register says the intent verb ships no grill sub-verb; shipped itd-42 scopes itself as a capability of an existing /abcd:intent grill

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bb32a3bf8f9b2685 · ledger: iss-2610262040034904 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:395` — “per-session output are command-shaped, and the `intent` parent ships no `grill`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-42-coherence-aware-grill.md:71` — “this is a capability of the existing `/abcd:intent grill`, not a sibling verb.”

The README states that grill's design target is promotion to a sub-verb of /abcd:intent and that the intent parent ships no grill sub-verb. itd-42, in shipped/, scopes its coherence tier as a capability of the existing /abcd:intent grill, with renamed flags, and rules out a sibling verb. The grill sub-verb cannot both exist for itd-42 to extend and be unshipped.

### 906. The README requires a flat commands/ directory where a plugin-named subdirectory breaks every verb; itd-46 edits the intent page at commands/abcd/intent.md

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0e1fc9a21c45b69c · ledger: iss-2610262040034442 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:50` — “Update `abcd-cli/commands/abcd/intent.md`”

The README says commands/ is flat on purpose, because a verb in a subdirectory named after the plugin registers as /abcd:abcd:< verb>, which makes every documented /abcd:< verb> an unknown command. itd-46 puts the intent command page at abcd-cli/commands/abcd/intent.md, which is that subdirectory. The page cannot sit there if the directory is to stay flat.

### 907. The help register names the verdict ingest `intent audit ingest`; itd-80 names it `intent review ingest`

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f9ce9d52438c2a5c · ledger: iss-2610262040043356 (filed)

The README's help table lists `intent audit ingest` beside `intent consistency ingest` as the verbs agents and hosts call. itd-80, which delivered the fidelity-verdict ingest, names it `abcd intent review ingest`. That is two names for one verb, and someone building from itd-80 would type a verb the help does not list.

### 908. The README ships an intent only when no open spec still names it, because an intent owns one or more specs; itd-80's reconcile ships the linked intent whenever its spec closes

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-bafba7ff86574416 · ledger: iss-2610262040053417 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-80-intent-lifecycle-automation.md:34` — “on spec close, detect the linked intent via the immutable link, move it `planned → shipped` with an atomic same-filesystem rename”

The README's spec row says a spec close ships the linked intent only when no open spec is left naming it, since an intent owns one or more specs. itd-80 says that on spec close the reconcile finds the linked intent through the link and moves it from planned to shipped, which assumes one spec per intent. When an intent has two specs, closing the first ships it under itd-80 but not under the README.

### 909. The README's hook row says session-end only stages the transcript and session-start files it away; itd-89 says session-end calls history.Capture, which redacts and files it

The operator-internal verbs table says `session-end` stages the session's own transcript and `session-start` files both staged transcripts away. itd-89 says the session-end verb takes the transcript path and calls history.Capture, which redacts the transcript, so the session is stored as it ends. The two put the redact-and-file step on different hook events.

The shape role cannot be both live and unbuilt.

01-agents cites 04-universal-patterns § 7 for the rule that the oracle seam is one interface with a native default and opt-in shapes, never a fixed cascade the core imposes. itd-6 cites the same section as a fixed cascade and says its RP MCP, then Codex CLI, then in-session subagent cascade is and stays availability-driven. The same section cannot both rule out and establish a fixed cascade.

### 913. The adapters chapter says the RepoPrompt route opens a new chat for each reviewer; itd-6 requires re-reviews to stay in the same RP chat, never a new one

02-adapters says the RepoPrompt adapter runs one MCP session per review and sends `new_chat: true` when the tool declares it, so each reviewer starts fresh. itd-6 says a re-review after fixes must stay in the same RP chat, never `--new-chat`, and carries the chat_id from one call to the next. A route that always opens a fresh chat cannot keep a re-review in the same chat.

### 914. The adapters chapter says every lifeboat source reader implements probe → extract → copy; itd-95 says every adapter implements Section, Tier and Probe

02-adapters says disembark reads a repository through source readers, each implementing the `probe() → extract() → copy()` contract. itd-95 adds an open-questions adapter that implements the same `Source` interface every other adapter does, which it gives as `Section()` / `Tier()` / `Probe()`. The two documents give different contracts for the same set of disembark source adapters.

### 917. The configuration chapter keeps transcripts in a user-scope store under ~/.abcd.noindex/transcripts; itd-89 files them in a local per-repo store

### 918. The configuration chapter treats ~/.abcd as the retired home, read by no reader; itd-76 puts the sources corpus at ~/.abcd/sources/ by default

Creating the corpus where itd-76 says would halt every abcd command.

### 921. Universal patterns call itd-60 a planned draft that is not yet built; itd-60 is shipped, and its gate refuses at spec close

04-universal-patterns describes the doc-fidelity pass as planned under a draft itd-60 at intents/planned/ and not yet built, and plans its log-tier layout as a later addition. itd-60 sits in shipped/ and says `abcd spec close` refuses per intent while the brief lags the surface it delivered. The gate cannot be both unbuilt and enforcing at the close.

### 922. The lint contract says rules are named, never numbered; itd-43 says a `GL002` lint catches regressions

### 923. The lint contract calls the docs-currency gate `abcd lint docs`; itd-60 calls the same gate `abcd docs lint`

That is two invocations for one verb, and only the lint sub-verb is the gate.

### 925. The memory chapter gives the prompt router a refresh every N prompts; the verification matrix says the refresh is event-driven and nothing counts prompts.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0d833404537bfe51 · ledger: iss-2610262040213900 (filed)

### 926. The memory chapter makes the in-tree repository store memory's primary home; the glossary says a memory note stays on the person's machine until it is promoted.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-c43c122782de6446 · ledger: iss-2610262040221402 (filed)

### 929. The build sequence says itd-27's grilling is now the planning interview; the glossary README keeps /abcd:intent grill as a live itd-27 design target.

### 930. The internals index gives /abcd:grill a design target of promotion to /abcd:intent grill; the build sequence says the grill is superseded by itd-94's planning interview.

### 931. The out-of-scope page says a later intent enters work by being scoped into a phase; the build sequence says phases are retired and their documents are history.

### 932. The loop glossary says abcd never owns the run loop; the build sequence says abcd's own loop ships through abcd build without the seam.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-14a34222fb852a7f · ledger: iss-2610262040273336 (filed)

The build sequence says a native Go loop is the fallback, and that the loop which shipped runs on the intent key without the seam, through abcd build. A loop that ships inside abcd is a run loop abcd owns.

### 933. The spec glossary says specs are driven to completion by the pluggable run seam; the build sequence says the run seam does not ship.

### 934. The spec glossary defines a spec as broken into tasks; the step glossary forbids 'task' for the unit below a spec.

The spec entry's definition breaks a spec into ordered tasks, and its body says numbered tasks. The step entry makes the step the unit below a spec and lists 'task' and 'sub-task' as forbidden synonyms. So the glossary's own definition of spec uses a word the glossary forbids.

### 935. The record entry and the record-families page use 'record family' for two different sets.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-3031eb3efc669510 · ledger: iss-2610262040295570 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record.md:32` — “One lifecycle-bucketed set of records of a single kind”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:4` — “The one page that maps abcd's record families (intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release, status)”

The record entry defines a record family as a lifecycle-bucketed set of filed, identified records of one kind, pointing at the four families embark writes (ADRs, issues, intents, specs). The record-families page uses the same phrase for intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release and status. That list leaves out ADRs and includes step, bundle, release and status, none of which is a filed record with its own id. One name covers two sets.

### 936. 'position' names a cold-reading question in reading-position and a record's how-soon axis in record-families.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-608abd7ec23ce5fb · ledger: iss-2610262040300326 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/reading-position.md:5` — “aliases: ["reading position", "position"]”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/record-families.md:30` — “The *position* (how soon) is rendered from it as Now / Next / Later and is never stored.”

reading-position registers bare 'position' as an alias for the question a cold reading answers (widening, entailment, comparative, detection). record-families uses 'position' for a record's how-soon axis, rendered as Now / Next / Later. Both entries are in the core context, so one word names two concepts.

### 963. The glossary says abcd never owns the run loop; the build intent makes abcd's own verb that loop.

loop.md defines the run loop as the receipt-gated iteration over ready work and states flatly that abcd never owns it, a pluggable adapter supplying it. itd-2609201916151817 makes `abcd build`/`abcd implement` exactly that loop, run by abcd's own binary over a state file, verifying each lane's receipt before advancing. - end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610222215485265-abcd-drain-run-from-a-plain-terminal.md:79` — “The driver is a loop inside `abcd drain`, entered only by `--drive`”

loop.md says abcd only defines the run-loop contract and an adapter supplies the loop itself. itd-2610222215485265 decides that the driver which works through ready issues lane by lane is a loop inside the `abcd drain` verb, not an adapter. The draft builds the loop the glossary says abcd never owns.

### 965. The glossary keeps 'step' in the build loop for a spec's piece only; the build intent uses it for one invocation of the loop.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-259609c8848ec806 · ledger: iss-2610262040551548 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:21` — “every invocation reads the state, does one step, writes the state and exits”

step.md fixes that in the build loop the word names the spec's step and nothing else, and that one `implement step` call performs a stage, not a step. The build intent's press release says each invocation 'does one step', using the word for one loop advance (a stage), the sense the glossary rules out.

### 966. The glossary makes planning the product thinker's sign-off and never unattended; the build intent adds `--auto-plan`, which plans with no human.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-defe297e14e1f8c4 · ledger: iss-2610262040570378 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:68` — “it lets the planning path run without a human”

plan.md defines moving a draft to planned/ as the product thinker's sign-off on the acceptance criteria, never run unattended and never inferred. itd-2609201916151817 decision 6 adds an agent path, `implement --auto-plan`, that takes a draft through planning with no human and replaces the sign-off with recorded decisions and review receipts. The two documents disagree on whether planning can ever happen without the sign-off.

### 967. The glossary says signing off a dependency is never the technical facilitator's; the Terminal-interview intent records the technical facilitator signing one off.

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610030810370060-a-person-can-run-abcd-s-interviews-in-a.md:79` — “the technical facilitator, signing off a new dependency”

technical-facilitator.md lists dependency sign-off among the acts that are the product thinker's, never the facilitator's, and product-thinker.md says the same. itd-2610030810370060 decision 5 records golang.org/x/term being adopted as a new direct dependency on the technical facilitator's sign-off. A dependency cannot be signed off by a role the glossary says has no authority to do it.

### 968. A person's preferences have two user-level homes: the memory chapter's `~/.abcd.noindex/memory/` pages and the memory-notes intent's `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json`.

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610091918433290-an-agent-working-in-an-abcd-managed.md:64` — “The machine's `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json` holds personal notes”

07-memory.md sends personal preferences and cross-project lessons to the user-scope page store `~/.abcd.noindex/memory/`, curated by principle-distiller. itd-2610091918433290 puts personal notes, which the glossary describes as a person's preferences and lessons, in `~/.abcd.noindex/memory.json`, written by agents. Neither says which store a personal preference belongs in, so the same knowledge is claimed by two stores with different writers and lifecycles.

### 969. The glossary sends a promoted memory note into the project's rules; the intent keeps promoted notes in `.abcd/memory.json`, apart from the rules people curate.

memory-note.md's example says a note recalled across sessions is promoted into the project's rules. itd-2610091918433290 puts promoted notes in the project's `.abcd/memory.json`, states that agents write memory.json while people curate rules.json, and keeps the two files separate. A promoted note cannot end up in both places.

### 970. 'status' is the glossary's Now/Next/Later record family, and the announcements intent gives the same name to `abcd status`, a view of announcements, reservations and release cuts.

record-families.md defines the status family as the Now / Next / Later view computed from the shelves, the gate and the build's state. itd-2609151838312703 decision 21 names `abcd status` as the view of everyone's announcements, reservation holders and releases being cut, saying a board rename frees the word. The glossary still ties 'status' to the Now/Next/Later view, so one name now covers two different views.

### 971. The routing intent says nothing reads the oracle choice today; the verification matrix has close read the intent-auditor's own oracle role and send it to a provider.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4d7535cea77c9969 · ledger: iss-2610262041018201 (filed)

Per-role routing that is read cannot also be a single value that nothing reads, and the matrix's `oracle.roles` key and the intent's routing table name the same per-agent choice two ways.

### 993. The cold-reading draft only ever reads a design document, never code; the glossary's detection position reads the shipped tree against the claim record.

reading-position.md defines four positions for a cold reading, one being detection: where the shipped tree is in tension with the claim record. itd-86 says a cold reading's target is a design document, keeps code out of scope, and takes exactly one document. ### 1018. The step intent says `implement step` and the spec's Steps section share one word; the step glossary entry says `implement step` performs a stage, not a step.

### 1021. The loop glossary entry says abcd never owns the run loop; the shipped pacing intent describes the loop abcd's own build, drain and implement verbs run.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-aec7d73c7343fbc3 · ledger: iss-2610262041445723 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/loop.md:38` — “abcd never owns the run loop.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609201925079472-an-autonomous-implementation-run-paces.md:20` — “A run started with `abcd build` (or `abcd drain`, or the `abcd implement` loop they hand over to)”

The loop entry says abcd only defines the run-loop contract (iterate, gate on a receipt, guard) and that a pluggable adapter supplies the loop itself. The shipped pacing intent describes a run started with `abcd build` or `abcd drain` and handed to the `abcd implement` loop. That run opens lanes, writes next_eligible_at into its own state file, checkpoints and refuses an early restart. This is a loop the abcd binary owns and runs, with no adapter. Someone building from the glossary would treat a native loop as forbidden, which contradicts what shipped.

### 1022. The memory chapter says the prompt router is a binary sub-command, not a script in hooks/; the shipped rules-loader intent scopes it as hooks/prompt_router_hook.py.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-1677a08239531db0 · ledger: iss-2610262041454448 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-3-modular-rules-loader.md:30` — “`hooks/prompt_router_hook.py`”

07-memory states that itd-3's prompt router is a sub-command of the abcd binary reached through the hook manifest, and explicitly not a script file in hooks/. itd-3's scope defines the router as the Python file hooks/prompt_router_hook.py. The two documents disagree about what the shipped router is and where it lives.

### 1023. The verification matrix says the rules-loader refresh is event-driven and nothing counts prompts; itd-3 refreshes in full every N turns.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c89b936d0f833a9f · ledger: iss-2610262041455139 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:73` — “The refresh is event-driven rather than turn-counted”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-3-modular-rules-loader.md:30` — “Signature-based dedup; force full re-inject every N turns (N defaults to 5, configurable).”

The matrix's dedup row says the refresh is event-driven rather than turn-counted. Only SessionStart and PreCompact clear the dedup ledger, and nothing counts prompts. The shipped itd-3 scope promises a full re-injection every N turns, with N defaulting to 5 and configurable. A gate written from the matrix would fail the behaviour itd-3 promises, and the reverse is also true.

### 1024. The provenance chapter says the source-hash registry is durable and only partly regenerable; itd-36 scopes it as regenerable.

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-36-memory-unification.md:48` — “source-hash registry at `.abcd/memory/.sources_index.json` (regenerable per the lifecycle taxonomy)”

09-provenance-substrate classifies .abcd/memory/.sources_index.json as durable source metadata that is only partly regenerable. It says fields about a discarded original cannot be rebuilt by a crawl, and that this supersedes the blanket 'regenerable' classification. itd-36's scope still files the same registry as regenerable under the lifecycle taxonomy. A builder following itd-36 could drop and rebuild a file that the substrate says it cannot rebuild.

### 1025. /abcd:memory names the memory-note command in the glossary, but itd-36 names the curated knowledge substrate with ingest, ask and lint.

One command name and one word refer to two different concepts, and a reader of the shipped intent will reach for sub-verbs that the command does not have.

### 1032. In the glossary a spec lives in abcd's native spec store; itd-34 maps each intent to a flow-next spec planned through /flow-next:plan.

### 1037. itd-2609150819445595 says every spec close mints an owed receipt; the verification matrix says only the shipping close does, and a build run ingests its verdict at that close.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c22a8e854f562e41 · ledger: iss-2610262041582285 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:56` — “and ingests that verdict at the close rather than leaving it owed”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609150819445595-a-debt-nothing-lists-owed-fidelity.md:41` — “Every `spec close` mints an owed receipt in the same change”

The owed-review intent's first decision depends on the premise that every `spec close` mints an owed receipt in the same change. The matrix's intent-lifecycle row says three things: an earlier close of a multi-spec intent moves nothing, only the close that ships an intent makes its audit owed, and a build run audits before landing and ingests the verdict at the close rather than leaving it owed. Some closes therefore mint no owed receipt, and the intent's reason for never gating on owed reviews rests on a premise the matrix contradicts.

The record-families page has no decision row. The shipped decisions intent makes every decision 'a record with an id', allocated through the same seam that mints captures, intents, specs and ADRs, and minted by `abcd decide` as dcn- records. The glossary's closed list of record kinds does not cover the family this intent created.

The interview-context embark entry says both shipped forms of the planning interview ask one thing at a time, not in rounds. The shipped question-layout intent rules that parts of one thing, such as the criteria of one feature, are put as tabs, up to four per screen. ### 1043. The memory chapter places abcd's user-level home at ~/.abcd.noindex/; itd-40 names ~/.abcd/history/index.json as the sole user-scope registry.

### 1047. itd-42 extends an existing `/abcd:intent grill` sub-verb; the build sequence says intent has no grill sub-verb at all.

### 1048. itd-42 records coherence findings in a grill report and a PRD behind the GR002 gate; the verification matrix says no grill report, no PRD and no GR* code exist.

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-42-coherence-aware-grill.md:61` — “Coherence questions and grounded conflicts are recorded in the Phase 1 `grill-report.{json,md}` alongside the existing question stream”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:78` — “`intent` registers no `grill` sub-verb, no PRD or grill report is written anywhere”

itd-42 writes coherence questions and grounded conflicts into the Phase 1 grill-report.{json,md}, has the Phase 2 PRD reflect them, and makes the full grill the default at 'the existing GR002 no-PRD gate'. The matrix's Grill row says intent registers no grill sub-verb, no PRD or grill report is written anywhere, and no GR* code exists in any tree. The artefacts itd-42 delivers into, and the gate it relies on, are ones the matrix says are absent.

### 1049. itd-46 lists `ship` and `grill` as existing intent sub-verbs that keep requiring an id; the build sequence says neither exists.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-265503fe264de4bf · ledger: iss-2610262042088869 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:75` — “`refine`, `grill`, `plan`, `ship`, `review`, `reclassify`, `link`, `resolve`, `wontfix`, `promote` continue to require their target's ID.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:99` — “so there is no `intent ship`. There is no `grill` sub-verb”

itd-46 calls the rule that `grill`, `plan`, `ship` and the other mutating sub-verbs continue to require their target's id an already-correct shape it leaves alone, which assumes those sub-verbs exist. The build sequence says an intent ships as the close-hook of `abcd spec close`, so there is no `intent ship`, and there is no `grill` sub-verb. The two documents describe different `/abcd:intent` surfaces.

### 1050. itd-46 calls bare-invocation-renders-status a universal abcd convention; the skills chapter says it is a convention and not a universal.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-65a1647b992a96bf · ledger: iss-2610262042091628 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:18` — “The bare command (zero arguments) keeps doing what the universal abcd convention says it must: shows status and help, never mutates state.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/08-skills.md:66` — “That is a convention rather than a universal”

itd-46 grounds its bare form on the universal abcd convention that a bare command shows status and help. 08-skills says the status-and-help render on bare invocation is a convention rather than a universal, and points to the surfaces index for the places where a parent prints usage instead. Someone building from itd-46 would assume every bare command renders status, and the brief says that is not so.

### 1051. itd-48 lands its consistency and shape reports under `.abcd/logbook/audit/`; the build sequence says `.abcd/logbook/` is retired and guarded by a detector.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-0efead12ebbe0746 · ledger: iss-2610262042109861 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-48-intent-fidelity-reviewer-roles-2-3.md:77` — “Reports land at `.abcd/logbook/audit/consistency-<ts>/report.{json,md}`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:176` — “`.abcd/logbook/` is a retired location, held retired by an armed detector”

itd-48 sends Role 2 reports to .abcd/logbook/audit/consistency-< ts>/ and Role 3 reports to .abcd/logbook/audit/shape-< ts>/. The build sequence says .abcd/logbook/ is a retired location, held retired by an armed detector that fails the build if any non-test Go source under internal/ names it, and that runtime output goes to the gitignored local tier (iss-73). Building the report path itd-48 states would trip that detector.

### 1052. itd-48 says Role 3 kind classification ships and `/abcd:intent shape` becomes a working surface; the verification matrix lists the shape-classification role as staged.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-76502cb6e28014c9 · ledger: iss-2610262042115843 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-48-intent-fidelity-reviewer-roles-2-3.md:24` — “With all three roles live, `/abcd:intent consistency` and `/abcd:intent shape` move from documented command surface to working command surface.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:80` — “the shape-classification role that would propose a reclassification”

itd-48's press release says the intent ships Role 3, and that with all three roles live `/abcd:intent shape` becomes a working command surface. The matrix's Three intent kinds row marks as staged the shape-classification role that would propose a reclassification. A shipped intent cannot have delivered a role the matrix says has no shipped surface. itd-48's Decisions narrow it to the consistency pass, but its press release and scope still claim Role 3.

### 1053. The agent that audits intents is called `intent-fidelity-reviewer` in itd-48 and `intent-auditor` in the internals index.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6fe4e9eb7c2681c9 · ledger: iss-2610262042125545 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-48-intent-fidelity-reviewer-roles-2-3.md:24` — “`intent-fidelity-reviewer` agent grows from one `role` to three”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/README.md:29` — “When `intent-auditor` matures, brief-skeleton presence checks would land alongside its existing intent-vs-implementation checks.”

itd-48 names the agent that holds Role 1 per-intent fidelity, and gains the cross-document and kind roles, `intent-fidelity-reviewer`. The internals index gives the name `intent-auditor` to the agent with the existing intent-vs-implementation checks. With two names for one agent, a reader cannot tell whether there is one prompt or two.

### 1054. The verb that ingests a fidelity verdict is `abcd intent review ingest` in itd-80 and `abcd intent audit ingest` in the verification matrix.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-b109411096afc769 · ledger: iss-2610262042134366 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-80-intent-lifecycle-automation.md:32` — “`abcd intent review ingest` ingests a verdict”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:56` — “`abcd intent audit ingest` writes the returned verdict into the intent's own Audit Notes”

In itd-80, `abcd intent review ingest` ingests the Role 1 verdict that an `intent-fidelity-reviewer` agent returns into the intent's Audit Notes. The matrix's Intent lifecycle hook row writes the same returned verdict into the intent's Audit Notes with `abcd intent audit ingest`, routed through the `oracle.roles.intent-auditor` role. One act and one agent each carry two names.

### 1055. itd-6 keeps a re-review in the same chat for every backend, the in-session subagent included; the verification matrix says consecutive host-delegated calls are independent dispatches.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-cf2d5a09bdf350f1 · ledger: iss-2610262042130595 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:45` — “Same rule applies whether the backend is RP, Codex, or in-session subagent (in-session uses `Task` with continuation prompts).”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:34` — “Two consecutive calls are independent dispatches, so the audit-fix loop re-primes context every iteration”

itd-6 makes it a rule that a re-review after fixes MUST stay in the same chat, and applies the rule to the in-session subagent through continuation prompts. The matrix's default host-delegated oracle row says two consecutive calls are independent dispatches, so the audit-fix loop re-primes its context on every iteration. The default backend cannot both carry on the earlier conversation and start fresh each time.

### 1056. itd-6 rules out direct provider API integrations and puts RP MCP first in the oracle cascade; the build sequence ships an opt-in OpenAI-compatible provider and makes the host the default.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5646a7eccee82f47 · ledger: iss-2610262042143519 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:54` — “Direct OpenAI / Google / Anthropic API integrations — out of scope; route everything through RP”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:35` — “`openaiapi`, the opt-in OpenAI-compatible provider an agent's oracle role can be pointed at”

itd-6's scope routes everything through RP, puts direct OpenAI, Google and Anthropic API integrations out of scope, and keeps a three-transport cascade with RP MCP preferred. The build sequence lists `openaiapi`, an opt-in OpenAI-compatible provider an agent's oracle role can be pointed at. It also makes review host-delegated by default, with native, CLI, API and MCP adapters opt-in. So a direct API adapter exists that itd-6 says abcd never has, and the default is the host rather than RP.

### 1057. itd-60 is sequenced as a rung of Phase 8; the phase entry says roadmap phases run 0–7, and it retires the phase.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-74f3affd7ac6d54e · ledger: iss-2610262042159336 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-60-doc-fidelity-anti-drift.md:28` — “Phase 8 — the brief is the shipped state”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/phase.md:43` — “Roadmap phases run 0–7 and the brief's plumbing-phases run 0–6”

itd-60 places itself in 'Phase 8 — the brief is the shipped state' and its Decisions say it is sequenced as Phase 8. The phase glossary entry says roadmap phases run 0–7, and it marks the phase superseded as the sequencing layer on 2026-09-21. Either a ninth phase exists that the 0–7 numbering leaves out, or itd-60's sequencing points at a phase the glossary does not recognise.

### 1058. itd-67 picks the bump tier from phase completion and writes the version into plugin.json; the version entry keeps the working tree unversioned and derives the version from impact.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-f652bc07912593e8 · ledger: iss-2610262042162078 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:47` — “auto-selects the bump tier (patch/minor/major) via the brief §4 phase-completion detection, writes the new version into `plugin.json`”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/distribution/version.md:22` — “The working tree stays unversioned; the version lives only in the cut artifact and its tag”

itd-67 has `launch ship` choose the bump tier through the brief's phase-completion detection and write the new version into plugin.json, which it calls the single source of the installed version. The version entry, which names itd-67 as its origin, says the version comes from the impact of what shipped and lives only in the cut artifact and its tag. It also says the working tree stays unversioned, and the phase whose completion itd-67 would detect is retired. Both the source of the bump and the place the version lives disagree.

### 1059. itd-67 builds the changelog from git tags, commit and spec history and the launch report, and lets a gate append to it; the release entry composes it from records that reached a terminal folder.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d746792ff452a028 · ledger: iss-2610262042174713 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:48` — “generated from the canonical history (git tags + commit/spec history + launch report) — never hand-curated prose”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/distribution/release.md:29` — “composes its changelog from the records that reached a terminal folder”

itd-67 generates the changelog from git tags, commit and spec history and the launch report. It also makes the changelog the place where itd-65's doc-history gate appends the change narration it strips from doc bodies. The release entry says `launch ship` composes the changelog from the records that reached a terminal folder. A changelog built from records has no room for lines taken from commit history or for prose a gate appends.

### 1060. itd-73 makes any breaking intent a major bump and a cut with nothing additive a patch; the version entry bumps the minor for a breaking change before 1.0 and derives no version for an empty cut.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-895b1d6ea1745549 · ledger: iss-2610262042183674 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-73-derived-versioning.md:30` — “any `breaking` → major, else any `additive` → minor, else patch”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/distribution/version.md:30` — “pre-1.0, a breaking change bumps the minor), and an all-internal or empty cut derives none”

itd-73's rule is any breaking intent gives a major bump, else any additive one gives a minor, else a patch, and it leaves pre-1.0 semantics out of scope. The version entry says that before 1.0 a breaking change bumps the minor, and that an all-internal or empty cut derives no version. For a 0.x release with a breaking intent, or a cut with nothing user-facing in it, the two rules give different versions.

### 1061. itd-76 calls its log of which source influenced which decision 'the provenance ledger'; the ledger entry keeps that name for another sense and calls this one 'the sources ledger'.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-efa64e6dd16787bd · ledger: iss-2610262042193372 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-76-source-provenance-ledger.md:18` — “abcd manages this with a personal corpus and a provenance ledger, guarded mechanically”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/ledger.md:29` — “Origin, grounds and disposition stamped at the point of commitment | **the provenance ledger**”

itd-76's append-only JSONL ledger records which source influenced which decision. The ledger glossary fixes one spelling for each sense. 'The provenance ledger' is origin, grounds and disposition stamped at the point of commitment. Source-to-decision provenance for the local sources corpus is 'the sources ledger'. itd-76 gives one sense's name to the other.

### 1062. itd-76 puts abcd's user-level home at `~/.abcd/`; the memory chapter puts the user scope under `~/.abcd.noindex/`.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-dd148aace909232c · ledger: iss-2610262042201742 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-76-source-provenance-ledger.md:18` — “abcd's user-level home, `~/.abcd/sources/` by default, itself a no-remote git repository”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/05-internals/07-memory.md:14` — “`~/.abcd.noindex/memory/` | **Personal preferences** and cross-project principles that have no single repo home”

itd-76 keeps the local-only corpus in abcd's user-level home, at ~/.abcd/sources/ by default. The memory chapter's two-scope table puts the user-level store at ~/.abcd.noindex/memory/. The two documents give different roots for the same user-level home, so a corpus built from itd-76 ends up outside the directory the brief treats as the user scope.

### 1063. itd-88 writes the packer as `disembark <repo> to <dest>`; the disembark entry writes it as `abcd disembark pack <source-repo> <dest>`.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-160d24114622ba31 · ledger: iss-2610262042208017 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-88-lifeboat-coverage-experiment.md:41` — “The packer (`disembark <repo> to <dest>`), embark, and the round-trip”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/disembark.md:4` — “`abcd disembark pack <source-repo> <dest>` reads a source repository without writing to it”

itd-88's scope names the packer that comes after the probe and coverage aggregate `disembark <repo> to <dest>`. The disembark glossary entry defines the same act as `abcd disembark pack <source-repo> <dest>`. That is two command forms for one pack operation, so the documents disagree on what to type.

### 1064. itd-89 files captured transcripts in a local per-repo store; the build sequence keeps the transcript store outside every checkout, at the user level.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6ae91ea37aa7ef33 · ledger: iss-2610262042214474 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-89-start-the-transcript-clock.md:18` — “abcd redacts the transcript and files it in the local per-repo store”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/01-build-sequence.md:82` — “lives outside every checkout at the user level, so a repo tracks none of it”

itd-89 says the SessionEnd hook files the redacted transcript in the local per-repo store. The build sequence says the native transcript store lives outside every checkout at the user level, so no repo tracks any of it, and that pulling it into a checkout's local tier is a per-machine opt-in. The default home of the store differs between the two.

### 1065. itd-94 has the agent run `abcd intent plan` as the person's sign-off; the plan entry has the human run it and says it is never inferred from consent.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-45277ccff902257e · ledger: iss-2610262042222565 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-94-an-intent-that-is-not-planned-cannot-be.md:23` — “Only then does the agent run `abcd intent plan` — your sign-off act”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/core/plan.md:63` — “offer the planning interview and let the human run `plan`”

itd-94 says that once the person has confirmed the interview, the agent runs `abcd intent plan` as their sign-off act. The plan entry says the invocation itself is the product thinker's sign-off, is never run unattended and is never inferred from consent. Its worked example is to offer the planning interview and let the human run `plan`. The two documents disagree on who carries out the sign-off.

### 1066. A fidelity review that cannot run because no backend is reachable is 'deferred' in itd-53 and 'owed' in the verification matrix.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-38505a3b26d8251c · ledger: iss-2610262042237923 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-53-review-queue-auto-drain-fidelity-gate.md:35` — “No-backend behavior: entries stay `deferred` (not failed), so a headless run never blocks on an unreachable backend.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/brief/06-delivery/02-verification-matrix.md:56` — “otherwise the audit stays owed until the host runs it”

itd-53 says queue entries stay deferred, not failed, when no review backend is reachable. The matrix says that when no provider connection is reached the audit stays owed until the host runs it, and other documents call this an OWED receipt. Two state names describe one condition.

### 1067. The audit verb is the hash-chain umbrella in itd-16 and a repo-conformance check in itd-85

- class: naming conflict · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-bc4937c79eb895cb · ledger: iss-2610262042244924 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-16-hash-chain-merkle-audit.md:23` — “`/abcd:audit` is the *whole*; specific verifications register as sub-verbs that share the substrate”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-85-audit-verb.md:16` — “a read-only check that tells you, in one command, whether a repository follows the working conventions”

itd-16 makes /abcd:audit an umbrella whose bare form shows the chain head and whose sub-verbs are chain and lifeboat. itd-85 makes bare abcd audit a read-only check of whether a repository follows the working conventions. Both cannot own the same verb: built as written, the bare invocation means two unrelated things, and one draft's sub-verb registry collides with the other's rule set.

### 1068. The glossary's detection reading compares the shipped tree with the claim record; itd-86's cold reading detects contradictions inside one document

- class: terminology drift · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-13128cf40d3fc4b7 · ledger: iss-2610262042256389 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/position.md:17` — “the detection pass (gaps between the shipped tree and the claim record)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-86-cold-reading-surface.md:29` — “A surface that takes exactly one target document and produces candidate detections against the constraints visible in that document alone.”

The position entry fixes the detection position of a cold reading as gaps between the shipped tree and the claim record. itd-86 names a cold reading that takes exactly one document and produces detections only against that document's own constraints. The same instrument name and the same word, detection, are given an incompatible object, so someone building from itd-86 would build a different instrument from the one the ledger glossary defines.

### 1069. The glossary forbids calling a cold reading a review; itd-90 says the cold reading reviews a document

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-fe7a580813a9259b · ledger: iss-2610262042269640 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/cold-reading.md:25` — “Do not call a cold reading a review or an audit: a review weighs and recommends, and a reading is forbidden both.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-90-brief-interview-for-the-blanks.md:40` — “That surface *reviews* a document for internal contradictions and is deliberately denied context.”

The cold-reading entry lists review as a forbidden synonym and says a review weighs and recommends, which a reading may not do. itd-90 describes the cold reading of itd-86 as a surface that reviews a document, using the forbidden word for the very instrument the entry defines.

### 1070. The glossary keeps disposition apart from the issue ledger's resolved and wontfix; itd-87 calls resolved and wontfixed entries dispositioned

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-736424e371fdf8bf · ledger: iss-2610262042279476 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:25` — “Do not reuse the issue ledger's open, resolved and wontfix.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-87-recurrence-escalation-in-capture.md:31` — “Matching an incoming capture against **dispositioned** entries (`resolve`, `wontfix`), not merely against open ones.”

The disposition entry says a disposition is not a resolution and must not reuse the issue ledger's open, resolved and wontfix. itd-87 uses dispositioned to mean exactly an issue resolved or wontfixed, so the term carries two senses across the record.

### 1071. Disposition has four states in the glossary; the deferred-finding discipline gives it three different words

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-33a66a4b7f27f321 · ledger: iss-2610262042284906 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:4` — “in one of four states: accepted, rejected, declined or held”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2610141956319695-a-deferred-finding-is-its-own-captured.md:35` — “In a release receipt the three states are the three words of the finding's `disposition`, spelled exactly”

The glossary defines a disposition as one of accepted, rejected, declined or held (and, for scope conditions, survived, narrowed, falsified or untested). The deferred-finding discipline makes disposition a release-receipt field whose only words are fixed, invalid and deferred. One field name now carries a third vocabulary the glossary does not register.

### 1072. Regime is a reading's licence (generative, explicative, evaluative, registrative) in the glossary; itd-142 names four question regimes with other values

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4caff5ff9e9e159f · ledger: iss-2610262042289741 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/regime.md:4` — “naming what it may produce and what the ingest verb refuses or flags: generative, explicative, evaluative or registrative”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-142-the-brief-creation-interview-abcd.md:60` — “Four question regimes — narrative / options / entailment / defaults”

The regime entry fixes the term to the licence a reading holds, with exactly four values. itd-142 uses regime for interview question kinds (narrative, options, entailment, defaults), one of which also borrows the entailment position's name. The same term has two incompatible value sets.

### 1073. The glossary calls the phase a retired sequencing unit; the rehearsal discipline builds its rungs on live phases

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-23b9bc79ca1fe3f2 · ledger: iss-2610262042291241 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/position.md:25` — “Do not call a position a phase (the retired sequencing unit) or a step (a landable piece of a spec); those are delivery vocabulary.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-196-a-capability-is-rehearsed-end-to-end.md:40` — “The cumulative rung is what turns a phase into something more than a list of merged intents”

The position entry says a phase is the retired sequencing unit. itd-196's second and third rungs are defined per phase (what the phase can deliver so far, the phase's close), and it calls turning a phase into a runnable demonstration a deliverable. A discipline cannot be enforced against a unit the glossary has retired.

### 1074. itd-192 decides verdicts by whether this phase wires a criterion, a unit the glossary calls retired

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-4d639ded95e9180b · ledger: iss-2610262042302710 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/position.md:25` — “Do not call a position a phase (the retired sequencing unit) or a step (a landable piece of a spec); those are delivery vocabulary.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-192-an-acceptance-criterion-whose-producer.md:16` — “is judged by whether this phase wires it, not by whether the narrowing was disclosed”

The position entry calls the phase the retired sequencing unit. itd-192's single deciding question is whether this phase wires the criterion, so its verdict rule depends on the retired unit for its scope.

### 1075. itd-41 proposes phase plans as its whole capability; the glossary says the phase is retired

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7fb3edf14d0b0a6c · ledger: iss-2610262042314589 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/position.md:25` — “Do not call a position a phase (the retired sequencing unit) or a step (a landable piece of a spec); those are delivery vocabulary.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-41-phase-negotiator.md:16` — “Ask abcd to phase a set of intents and it works backwards from what each phase should make true, proposes an ordered set of phases”

itd-41's negotiator phases a set of intents and proposes an ordered set of phases with phase acceptance bullets. The position entry calls the phase the retired sequencing unit. The draft presupposes a unit that the glossary records as no longer in use.

### 1076. The glossary forbids calling a reading's position a step; itd-143 calls the widening reading the Step 2 reading

- class: terminology drift · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-039e3daeb4d8a01e · ledger: iss-2610262042329594 (filed)
