### 1104. The disposition glossary entry fixes four states; itd-180 calls the same disposition vocabulary five-state.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c17b8090c669a94e · ledger: iss-2610262042575392 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:4` — “in one of four states: accepted, rejected, declined or held.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-180-a-cold-reading-s-findings-land-as.md:28` — “five-state vocabulary whose availability varies by position”

The glossary defines a disposition as written 'in one of four states: accepted, rejected, declined or held', and says an undispositioned item is outstanding, which is never a state. itd-180 describes the same disposition record as drawn from 'a five-state vocabulary' (and 'five states' in its scope) while naming only those same four values. An implementer sizing the enum, or a lint counting the states, cannot satisfy both counts, and neither document names a fifth value that would reconcile them.

### 1105. The glossary reserves 'disposition' for the researcher's response to a reading item; itd-82 uses it for a drain run's per-issue outcome.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6605e36ade33f075 · ledger: iss-2610262042571852 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:4` — “The researcher's recorded response to one reading item, written as a separate record keyed to the item”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:52` — “every issue's disposition (pull request number, draft id, flag with home or reason”

In the ledger bounded context a disposition is 'the researcher's recorded response to one reading item, written as a separate record keyed to the item', with four named states, and the glossary forbids mixing it with issue-ledger vocabulary. itd-82's drain summary records 'every issue's disposition' as a pull request number, a draft id, a flag, ineligible, skipped or stopped. The same word now names two unrelated things that both live on the issue ledger side (reading dispositions are filed under the issues tree), so a reader of a drain summary or a ledger query cannot tell which sense a 'disposition' carries.

### 1106. 'declined' is a reading-item disposition state in the glossary and a capture-triage grounds value in itd-179.

- class: naming conflict · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-3baa805a2785b4e7 · ledger: iss-2610262042580667 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/disposition.md:4` — “in one of four states: accepted, rejected, declined or held.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-179-the-reasoning-behind-what-was-pursued-no.md:22` — “`deferred`, `declined` — and the grounds name the conjecture being acted”

The glossary makes 'declined' one of the four disposition states (the widening proposal was admissible and the researcher chose otherwise) and asks that disposition vocabulary not be mixed with the issue ledger's. itd-179 gives the readiness gate and capture's triage routes a grounds vocabulary of 'pursued', 'deferred', 'declined', where 'declined' means a triage choice on an issue or intent. One token names two different acts on two different record kinds, so a reader meeting 'declined' on a ledger record must know which vocabulary wrote it.

### 1107. The glossary defines warm as what a cold reading must never see; itd-199 defines warmth as how much a reader is given.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f9c92a6f7f4af372 · ledger: iss-2610262042593698 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/brief/glossary/ledger/warm.md:17` — “names what a cold reading must not see and what the researcher keeps”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-199-a-reading-is-about-something-narrower.md:19` — “because warmth is how much a reader was given and nothing else”

warm.md defines warm as the researcher's reserved reasoning and the ledger material it works on (dispositions, admissions, manifests, the lapse log), and says warm 'names what a cold reading must not see'. itd-199 names a 'warm' preset that is 'cold' plus a delta of scope and states that 'warmth is how much a reader was given and nothing else', so a 'warm' reading is a wider reading of admissible material that still sees no warm material. The term means 'withheld from the reader' in one document and 'more of what the reader may see' in the other.

### 1108. itd-192's verdict rule turns on 'this phase'; itd-24 records that phases are retired and the release is the unit.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-01a24050a18f6a8d · ledger: iss-2610262043005827 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-192-an-acceptance-criterion-whose-producer.md:25` — “Does this phase wire it?”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:90` — “phases are retired, so `<phase-id>` reads as the release tag”

itd-192 decides between MET_WITH_CONCERNS and NOT_MET by one question, 'Does this phase wire it?'. itd-24 records the ruling that 'phases are retired' and that a phase now reads as a release tag. The discipline still keys its test on a retired sequencing unit and does not say whether 'this phase' now means the release, the intent's spec or something else, so an auditor applying it has no defined scope to judge wiring against.

### 1109. itd-196's cumulative and closing rehearsal rungs are defined over a phase; itd-24 records that phases are retired.

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-20e5dde37a9867c7 · ledger: iss-2610262043017551 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-196-a-capability-is-rehearsed-end-to-end.md:32` — “Run what the PHASE can deliver so far”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:90` — “phases are retired, so `<phase-id>` reads as the release tag”

itd-196 defines its second rung as running 'what the PHASE can deliver so far' and its third as one full run 'at the phase's close', and calls the cumulative rung what turns a phase into more than a list of merged intents. itd-24 records that phases are retired and the release is the unit. The discipline's two most important rungs are keyed on a unit that no longer exists, so when the cumulative run starts, and what the closing run must cover, are undefined.

### 1110. itd-26 names the knowledge-ingest verb '/abcd:memory ingest'; itd-39 records that 'memory' is now the agents' notes command.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-700bb2ff1a143895 · ledger: iss-2610262043026422 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-26-loot-oss-vendor.md:70` — “`/abcd:memory ingest` for knowledge”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-39-scope-aware-memory-retrieval.md:78` — “Since the verb split, `memory` is the agents' notes command”

itd-26 builds loot on a provenance substrate it shares with knowledge ingest, which it names '/abcd:memory ingest'. itd-39 records that since the verb split 'memory' is the agents' notes command, and that the source store is reached as 'library ingest', 'library ask' and 'library lint'. The name itd-26 builds on now points at a different command, and the surface it means has another name, so an implementer following itd-26 would wire loot to the wrong verb family.

### 1111. The sources-corpus draft names its ingest, consult and lint 'source add', a consult verb and a corpus lint; itd-39 says the store is already reached as library ingest, ask and lint.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-637125c56f80c63a · ledger: iss-2610262043030522 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609292108089653-ingesting-a-source-and-consulting-the.md:43` — “is refused at `source add` and”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-39-scope-aware-memory-retrieval.md:79` — “its store is now reached as `library ingest`, `library ask` and `library lint`”

itd-2609292108089653 proposes moving ingest and consult into the binary as new verbs: a consult verb, a quality check that refuses a keyword stub 'at source add', and 'a corpus lint'. itd-39 records that the same store is already reached as 'library ingest', 'library ask' and 'library lint'. One surface has two sets of names, and a builder taking the draft at its word would add a second verb family beside the one itd-39 says exists.

### 1112. itd-1 names the agent that writes criterion verdicts 'intent-auditor'; itd-50 names it 'intent-fidelity-reviewer'.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6d85b7da1097148b · ledger: iss-2610262043043502 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:17` — “emitted by the `intent-auditor` agent's single-document role”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-50-loop-toward-acceptance.md:25` — “the `intent-fidelity-reviewer` records a `NOT_MET` verdict”

itd-1 states that every shipped intent's per-criterion verdicts are 'emitted by the intent-auditor agent's single-document role'. itd-50, whose whole loop is driven by those verdicts, says 'the intent-fidelity-reviewer records a NOT_MET verdict'. Two names are used for the one agent the loop depends on, and the second carries the 'review' word the audit was renamed away from, so a builder of itd-50 has to guess which agent the loop calls.

### 1113. itd-1 fixes the audit at four verdict states; itd-50 adds UNACHIEVABLE as a fifth terminal audit outcome.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-95caed7079f0d1bb · ledger: iss-2610262043043610 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-1-acceptance-gates.md:46` — “four states, lifted from PAUL. Binary pass/fail loses information; four states preserve nuance without exploding.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-50-loop-toward-acceptance.md:52` — “A new terminal audit outcome distinct from `NOT_MET`”

itd-1 fixes the escalation states at 'four states' (MET, MET_WITH_CONCERNS, NOT_MET, INCONCLUSIVE) for both per-criterion and overall verdicts, and argues four keep nuance without exploding. itd-50 introduces 'a new terminal audit outcome distinct from NOT_MET', UNACHIEVABLE, and its decisions apply it to a criterion judged unmeetable. Either the audit's verdict vocabulary has four values or it has five; the discipline that governs every audit is not amended, so the Audit Notes writer and the loop would disagree on what a verdict can be.

### 1114. itd-11 calls the lifeboat check 'the lifeboat-oracle's audit'; itd-125 consolidated that oracle/audit/review triple into 'review'.

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7f05cfd9966d06ed · ledger: iss-2610262043053279 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-11-pass-b-pitfall-mitigation.md:15` — “the lifeboat-oracle's audit catches and quarantines low-confidence Pass B output”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-125-the-lifeboat-verdict-says-what-it-is.md:22` — “produced by an oracle, holding a review verdict — three words for one thing.”

itd-11 has 'the lifeboat-oracle's audit' catch and quarantine low-confidence Pass B output. itd-125 records that the lifeboat verdict 'used to be called an audit, produced by an oracle, holding a review verdict' and that the verb, flag, artefact and prose now all say review. The draft still uses two of the three retired words for the same check, so a builder would reintroduce the naming itd-125 removed.

### 1115. itd-107 keeps the strict merge policy because ids minted on two branches can collide; itd-114 says such ids never collide.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-a4e14cc3a9ed0fd8 · ledger: iss-2610262043063912 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-107-autonomous-routines-assemble-from-one.md:138` — “the only place a record id minted concurrently on two branches”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-114-abcd-mints-collision-proof-record-ids.md:21` — “minting the same instant on different branches produce different ids”

itd-107 forbids relaxing the strict status-check policy on the ground that the merged-result run is 'the only place a record id minted concurrently on two branches' becomes visible, because the mint lock does not span checkouts. itd-114 makes every id collision-proof by construction with no coordination, so two agents 'minting the same instant on different branches produce different ids'. One premise is false; the routine template would carry a justification the shipped id scheme has removed.

### 1116. itd-115 keeps the strict merge gate to catch duplicate ids from parallel sessions; itd-114 says ids are collision-proof with no coordination.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-f85b029a07199952 · ledger: iss-2610262043071551 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-115-abcd-managed-repos-merge-prs-without-the.md:24` — “strict merge gate stays intact: it is what catches a duplicate record id minted”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-114-abcd-mints-collision-proof-record-ids.md:19` — “mints is collision-proof by construction, with no coordination between”

itd-115 states that the strict merge gate 'is what catches a duplicate record id minted by two parallel sessions' and must never be traded away. itd-114 states that every id abcd mints is collision-proof by construction, with no coordination between agents. If itd-114 holds, the gate catches no such duplicate; if itd-115 holds, itd-114's guarantee does not. The merge-queue design rests on a failure the shipped mint says cannot happen.

### 1117. The delegated-payload draft refuses a payload that names no model; itd-166 records a missing served model as a reason, never leaving it out.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-463bc206bdf2ee90 · ledger: iss-2610262043089096 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609180517121254-every-payload-a-host-hands-back-from-a.md:15` — “and the ingesting verb refuses one that does not”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-166-each-run-should-record-the-model.md:18` — “Whatever the route cannot show is written down as unpinned or self-reported, never left out and never guessed.”

itd-2609180517121254 requires every payload a host hands back from a delegated step to name its model, and 'the ingesting verb refuses one that does not'. itd-166, which covers a role run through the host as well as runners and providers, says 'whatever the route cannot show is written down as unpinned or self-reported, never left out', and its decisions record an absent served model as 'not reported' rather than failing the call. For the same case, a host-delegated answer that names no model, one record refuses the ingest and the other records the gap and goes on.

### 1118. itd-109 and itd-50 both define how a human's verification of an intent's criteria is recorded before shipping, as a receipt and as not a receipt.

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-de2212f476ae8152 · ledger: iss-2610262043093810 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-109-a-two-part-verification-suite-for-abcd.md:23` — “a human walks them, and their verdicts land in the”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-50-loop-toward-acceptance.md:101` — “in the product thinker's words, not a separate receipt”

itd-109 has a human walk the criteria that cannot be automated, with 'their verdicts land in the same receipt through the same verb', and shipping an intent reads those receipts and refuses on a pending manual verdict. itd-50 rules that 'hand verification is a grounds entry in the product thinker's words, not a separate receipt', taken after the machine criteria read MET. Both records claim the same moment and the same act and record it in incompatible forms, so the ship gate cannot read both.

### 1119. The deferral discipline says every confirmed finding is fixed, invalid or captured, with no exception; the model-matrix run keeps confirmed check findings out of the ledger.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5ed9f071ab1ea9c1 · ledger: iss-2610262043101146 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-2610141956319695-a-deferred-finding-is-its-own-captured.md:20` — “A deferral is always a capture. There is no exception.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610161733316518-a-product-thinker-who-wants-to-know.md:323` — “copy's findings are kept in the run's own record, nothing reaches the issue ledger”

itd-2610141956319695 states that 'a deferral is always a capture. There is no exception': every finding a review confirms ends fixed, invalid, or captured as its own open issue. itd-2610161733316518 has a person judge each check copy's findings valid or not, then keeps them in 'the run's own record, nothing reaches the issue ledger'. A real defect a doc-fidelity copy finds and the person confirms is then neither fixed, invalid nor captured, which the discipline says cannot happen.

### 1120. The brief-realisation draft treats the brief as the target design in the present tense; itd-147 sequences the brief as the shipped state.

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-a321c6e560e493e7 · ledger: iss-2610262043106501 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610040817105016-a-product-thinker-reads-their-brief-as.md:19` — “A product thinker reads their brief as the target design, in the present tense”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-147-the-brief-s-surface-chapters-are-a.md:99` — “the brief is the shipped state, with itd-60 as the”

itd-2610040817105016 records the product thinker's ruling that a product thinker reads the brief 'as the target design, in the present tense', with intents shown as realising each section. itd-147 is a delivery rung of the phase whose rule is that 'the brief is the shipped state', generating each chapter's surface block from the shipped command tree and marking an unbuilt surface as unbuilt. A brief written as target design in the present tense is exactly the drift itd-147's generated blocks and currency rule exist to stop, so a builder cannot satisfy both definitions of what the brief is.

### 1125. itd-79 requires every press-release quote's persona to be the role's registered name; itd-198 attributes its quote to an unnamed role.

### 1130. itd-191 assigns selection to 'the maintainer', a word itd-2609212137129937 removed in favour of naming the product thinker or the facilitator

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-509be2a63c2576a2 · ledger: iss-2610262043197794 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-191-the-selection-criteria-are-a-declared.md:20` — “combining characterisations into a choice is the maintainer's act”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212137129937-abcd-s-own-text-names-the-product.md:21` — “the word maintainer leaves the vocabulary”

The discipline says combining characterisations into a choice is the maintainer's act, while the shipped intent rules that the word maintainer leaves the vocabulary and that every use names the product thinker or the technical facilitator. The standing selection rule therefore leaves unstated which of the two people makes the choice, which is the ambiguity the shipped intent exists to remove.

### 1131. itd-109 lets 'the maintainer' record a disposition, where itd-2609212137129937 requires naming the product thinker or the facilitator

- class: terminology drift · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-09229528449657ac · ledger: iss-2610262043202769 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-109-a-two-part-verification-suite-for-abcd.md:29` — “verdict refuses the move unless the maintainer records a disposition”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212137129937-abcd-s-own-text-names-the-product.md:39` — “rewritten to the product thinker (what to build, adoption, rulings) or the technical facilitator (how, gates, mechanics)”

The draft's gate refuses a ship, a plan completion or a cut unless the maintainer records a disposition; the shipped intent rewrites every such use to the product thinker (rulings) or the technical facilitator (gates, mechanics). The draft does not say which of the two may answer its gate, so a builder cannot tell whose act the disposition is.

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609212137129937-abcd-s-own-text-names-the-product.md:54` — “Everywhere abcd writes, each use names the role it meant; a lint bans the word after”

The draft requires another maintainer's agreement in a repository with more than two maintainers, but the shipped intent ruled that each use names the role it meant and that a lint bans the word afterwards. The draft mixes the two named roles with an undefined count of maintainers, so who must agree is not stated in the vocabulary the record allows.

### 1133. itd-1 calls the single-document fidelity auditor intent-auditor; itd-34 calls the same agent intent-fidelity-reviewer

One agent carries two names across the two records, so a reader cannot tell whether the shape-classification role belongs to the auditor the verdict pipeline dispatches.

### 1134. itd-34 routes a standalone intent to a flow-next spec, while itd-37 places the spec template in abcd's native Go binary

itd-34 states that a standalone intent maps 1:1 to a flow-next spec and is planned through /flow-next:plan and plan-review; itd-37 says every spec carries its Modification Grammar section through the native spec template in the Go binary. The two name different spec stores and planning paths for the same promotion, so a builder cannot tell which one intent plan mints into or which template carries the inherited gates.

### 1135. itd-81 requires binary verdicts from every judging agent; itd-28 locks reviewers to the three-valued SHIP / NEEDS_WORK / MAJOR_RETHINK enum

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-605aa8215d29eb0d · ledger: iss-2610262043240944 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-28-rp-reviews-into-flow.md:65` — “the canonical review verdict enum, shared by every oracle adapter”

itd-81 covers every reviewer and auditor that renders a verdict and puts binary verdicts in scope, with severity structural rather than scaled. itd-28 locks the canonical review verdict enum, shared by every oracle adapter, at three values. A review agent cannot satisfy both: its verdict is either binary or one of the three.

### 1151. itd-2609091034175565 hands reservation tombstone deletion to itd-118, whose scope covers PR branches and local residue only

### 1153. itd-1 calls the Role 1 fidelity agent intent-auditor; itd-48 calls the same agent intent-fidelity-reviewer

### 1155. itd-1 has a repeat review replace the one Audit Notes block in place; itd-80 appends each ingested verdict, keyed on its receipt

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-ac075eab622bb8c8 · ledger: iss-2610262043417816 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-80-intent-lifecycle-automation.md:36` — “appends idempotently (keyed on the receipt id) to `## Audit Notes`”

itd-1 says the writer keeps a single machine-fenced review block that a repeat review replaces, so the section never collects stale blocks and git history holds earlier reviews. itd-80 says the ingest appends to Audit Notes and is idempotent only per receipt id, so a second review with a new receipt adds another block. The section cannot both hold one replaced block and gain one block per receipt.

### 1156. itd-81 requires binary verdicts from every verdict-rendering agent, the intent auditor included; itd-80 ships that reviewer with four-state verdicts

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c4501af4b0d0dd1d · ledger: iss-2610262043429522 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-81-judge-calibration.md:102` — “Binary verdicts. Severity is structural (a FIX-FIRST list vs a NOTES list)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-80-intent-lifecycle-automation.md:19` — “per-criterion verdicts (MET / MET_WITH_CONCERNS / NOT_MET / INCONCLUSIVE)”

itd-81's rule covers every agent that renders a verdict and names intent-auditor. It puts binary verdicts in scope and carries severity in structure. itd-80 ships that same reviewer emitting MET / MET_WITH_CONCERNS / NOT_MET / INCONCLUSIVE for each criterion. A four-valued verdict per criterion is not binary. Either the shipped reviewer breaks the discipline, or the discipline does not cover the agent it names.

### 1157. itd-37 gives Role 1 the job of spotting spec boilerplate at plan-review; itd-48 defines Role 1 as grading a shipped intent's criteria against delivered reality

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c9590045e90b9fc6 · ledger: iss-2610262043436609 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/disciplines/itd-37-modification-grammar.md:69` — “Role 1 boilerplate detection runs at plan-review and ship time”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-48-intent-fidelity-reviewer-roles-2-3.md:24` — “`Role 1` (per-intent fidelity) grades a shipped intent's acceptance criteria against delivered reality”

itd-37 has Role 1 judge a spec's Modification Grammar for boilerplate, at plan-review and again at ship time. itd-48 defines Role 1 as per-intent fidelity: it grades a shipped intent's acceptance criteria against what was delivered. A plan-review judgement of spec prose happens before anything is delivered, so it is not the Role 1 that itd-48 defines. Either Role 1 has a second job that no shipped record gives it, or the boilerplate check has no owner.

### 1158. itd-142 takes brownfield coverage from embark probe; itd-88 ships the coverage report as disembark probe

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-c4d6254eb411a70d · ledger: iss-2610262043446144 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-88-lifeboat-coverage-experiment.md:18` — “abcd ships `/abcd:disembark probe <repo>` — point it at any repository”

itd-142 fills the brief interview in advance from 'embark probe' coverage. itd-88 makes /abcd:disembark probe the verb that reads a repository and reports what each section can be grounded from. The coverage a brownfield interview needs comes from the disembark probe, so a builder following itd-142 would wire the interview to the wrong probe.

### 1159. itd-142 says the tool never recommends; itd-42 lets the grill pre-pass recommend an answer in prose

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d4b0bd6cc4d151cb · ledger: iss-2610262043456762 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-42-coherence-aware-grill.md:94` — “the pre-pass may recommend one with its reason in the prose beside the question, never as a marked option”

itd-142 states that at a conjectural question the tool never recommends. itd-42's ruled decision lets the coherence pre-pass recommend one of the standard answers, with its reason, in the prose beside the question. It forbids only a marked option. These cannot both be abcd's interview stance: one forbids any recommendation, and the other allows one in prose.

### 1160. itd-142 says abcd ships zero skills; itd-43 still treats the grill SKILL.md as a live surface to rewrite

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-142-the-brief-creation-interview-abcd.md:13` — “Command-shaped, because it mutates state — abcd ships zero skills”

itd-142 makes the interview a command because abcd ships zero skills. itd-43 lists the grill SKILL.md boundary message among the surfaces its prose sweep rewrites. It does not mark that file moot, as it does other files that are absent from the tree. The record cannot both say abcd ships no skills and keep a grill skill file as a surface to maintain.

### 1161. itd-25's dredge promote calls /abcd:intent new; itd-46 replaced the new sub-verb with quoted-text create

itd-25 has dredge promote create its intent draft by calling /abcd:intent new. itd-46 shipped quoted-text create, which files the intent with no new sub-verb. On the surface itd-46 shipped, the verb itd-25 calls is gone.

### 1162. itd-25 says agents are host-delegated by default with RepoPrompt opt-in; itd-6 keeps RP MCP as the preferred first backend in the oracle chain

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-be4985647b154de9 · ledger: iss-2610262043470447 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-25-dredge-cross-corpus-synthesist.md:43` — “Oracle backend chain (same as other agents): host-delegated by default, with the opt-in RepoPrompt adapter and Codex CLI as configured alternatives”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:41` — “RP MCP (preferred) → Codex CLI subprocess (alternative for non-Mac / no-RP users — RP is macOS-only) → in-session subagent (final fallback)”

itd-25 says the oracle chain that agents share is host-delegated by default, with RepoPrompt and Codex CLI as opt-in alternatives. itd-6's scope keeps a three-transport chain where RP MCP is preferred and the in-session subagent is only the last fallback. The two records disagree on which backend an agent reaches first.

### 1163. itd-19 sets the oracle backend from the project's stage; itd-6 has ahoy lock it based on whether RP is reachable

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-7ddc6f90a3aef2f1 · ledger: iss-2610262043485833 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-19-stage-aware-behaviour.md:31` — “oracle=in-session (fast iteration)”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:43` — “If reachable: lock `oracle.backend = "rp"`. If not: lock `oracle.backend = "codex"` (if Codex CLI present)”

itd-19's stage profiles have ahoy set oracle=in-session for an Autonomous project, and rp or rp+codex for other stages. itd-6 has ahoy test whether RP is reachable and lock oracle.backend to rp when RP answers, falling back to codex or in-session only when it does not. For an Autonomous project where RP is reachable, one record writes in-session and the other locks rp.

### 1164. itd-2609301918174237 sends the auditor and consistency pass to remote providers; itd-6 rules out direct provider API integrations

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6f09cbea0d28fd45 · ledger: iss-2610262043494574 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2609301918174237-a-provider-off-this-machine-takes-a-file.md:19` — “The intent auditor, the consistency pass and the release composer could never run on a paid provider, because a provider call carries no tools and nothing built what they read.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:54` — “Direct OpenAI / Google / Anthropic API integrations — out of scope; route everything through RP”

itd-2609301918174237 assumes abcd sends helper work, including the intent auditor and the consistency pass, to a provider that runs it. That provider can be paid or not, but it is not on this machine. itd-6 puts direct OpenAI / Google / Anthropic API integrations out of scope and routes everything through RP. Sending work to a remote provider is exactly the direct integration itd-6 excludes.

### 1166. itd-85 names the repo-conformance check `abcd audit`; itd-124 says the conformance check is `abcd lint` and `audit` is reserved for something else

The draft itd-85 promises a verb `abcd audit` whose job is checking a repository against the working conventions. The shipped itd-124 says exactly that job is `abcd lint`, and that the word `audit` returns to meaning 'did we do what we said', with `/abcd:audit` reserved for hash-chain fidelity checks. One name is given to two different concepts: building itd-85 as written would put the conformance check back under the name itd-124 took it away from.

Both drafts claim the same verb for unrelated jobs, and neither mentions the other.

### 1169. The build loop arms auto-merge whenever the ruleset gates through a queue; the facilitator-mode intent says that by default abcd never arms or queues a pull request

- class: premise contradiction · severity: major · finding_ref: cfk-cad55990057f7808 · ledger: iss-2610262043535279 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609201916151817-one-verb-takes-a-single-intent-from.md:62` — “A pull request with auto-merge armed where the ruleset gates it through a queue, a pull request left open where it does not.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610150602547271-a-repository-declares-whether-its.md:21` — “person, a ready pull request waits for them: abcd never queues it or arms”

itd-2609201916151817 decision 3 makes the merge target depend only on the repository's ruleset: auto-merge is armed whenever a queue gates the branch. itd-2610150602547271 makes `human` the default mode for a fresh install and says that in this mode abcd never queues a pull request or arms auto-merge on it. Its merge gate is the function the build loop must ask. Built as written, the loop would arm auto-merge in exactly the repositories where the mode intent forbids it.

### 1170. itd-82 says merging the drain's pull requests is a human gate by design; itd-2610150602547271 says that in auto mode a ready pull request merges with no human step

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-95a5c8e5d359310c · ledger: iss-2610262043542024 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:58` — “Merging pull requests, planning promoted drafts, writing decision records: human gates by design.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610150602547271-a-repository-declares-whether-its.md:145` — “in `auto`, a ready pull request merges with no human step.”

itd-82 lists merging pull requests as a human gate by design, outside what the drain may do. itd-2610150602547271 lets a repository declare `auto`, in which the merge gate that the build loop (and so the drain's issue lanes) asks queues or arms the merge with no human involved. Under `auto`, the drain's pull requests merge without the human gate itd-82 says is built in.

### 1180. itd-44 writes ADRs under a next-free ordinal; itd-114 makes every minted id collision-proof across branches

### 1184. itd-87 escalates a finding that matches a resolved or wontfixed record as a new entry; the consistency pass marks such a finding addressed and files nothing

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-87-recurrence-escalation-in-capture.md:17` — “the ledger no longer quietly folds it into the closed entry. It escalates: a new entry, citing the closed one”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2609291923559186-the-consistency-pass-runs-where-records.md:87` — “fix is marked `addressed` on the report, naming the record, and files”

itd-87 says a finding that matches an entry already resolved or wontfixed must not be folded into the closed entry: it becomes a new entry citing the closed one, because the recurrence is evidence that the closure may be wrong. itd-2609291923559186 G1 says that when a consistency finding's record is already resolved or won't-fix, the report marks it `addressed` and files nothing. The two give opposite rules for the same event in the issue ledger.

### 1185. itd-86 says the cold reading's target is a design document and not code; itd-184 makes the detection reading the shipped tree against the claim record

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-19bb3b7a364b5066 · ledger: iss-2610262044082114 (filed)

itd-86 defines the cold reading's detection as reading one design document against the constraints visible in it, and puts reviewing code out of scope. itd-184's Detection definition reads the shipped tree, which includes source and tests, against the claim record. The two disagree on what the detection reading's object is.

itd-97's scope promises a per-repo mode declaration with the values duo and solo, duo the default. itd-2610150602547271 implements the same declaration as `facilitator.mode` with the values `human` and `auto`. itd-97 notes in passing that these are aliases, but its declared values and the declared key's values still differ, so one setting has two vocabularies.

itd-30 has `intent-fidelity-reviewer` read both press releases and design fictions against delivered reality. itd-24 says judging delivered reality against an intent's criteria is the intent auditor's job. The two documents use different names for the same agent, and a builder of itd-30 would look for an agent that does not exist under that name.

### 1188. itd-24 says abcd is single-developer or pair shaped; itd-99 says the product thinker can be a team

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:65` — “abcd is single-developer-shaped (or pair-shaped); team retrospective patterns belong elsewhere.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-99-a-team-of-product-thinkers-decides-as.md:19` — “The product thinker can be a team.”

itd-24 leaves team retrospectives out of scope on the premise that abcd is single-developer-shaped, or at most pair-shaped. itd-99's premise is that the product thinker role can be held by a team of several people, each with their own thinking session and recorded dissent. The two state incompatible assumptions about how many people abcd is built for.

### 1189. itd-99 has a team of product thinkers write independently before anything is merged; itd-2610091016262335 has the team edit the brief live, each seeing the others' changes

- class: scope leakage · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-5eb84d467ecb5ee2 · ledger: iss-2610262044119054 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-99-a-team-of-product-thinkers-decides-as.md:60` — “captured independently — thinkers do not see each other's answers before”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610091016262335-the-product-thinker-and-the-technical.md:21` — “everyone edits the brief together, seeing each other's changes as they type.”

itd-99 covers how a team of product thinkers authors the 'why': each writes in isolation without seeing the others' answers, then abcd collates, and real-time collaboration tooling is out of scope. itd-2610091016262335 covers the same ground with the opposite method: the team edits the brief together during a call, each person seeing the others' changes as they type. The two records claim team brief authorship with incompatible models and do not reference each other.

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/drafts/itd-2610222029228127-a-person-away-from-their-computer-can.md:19` — “A person away from their computer can follow every abcd session's checklist and answer the questions that would stop its work from their phone.”

itd-2610032150577708 shows the product thinker what is waiting on them on their phone, and records a ruling that it cannot answer abcd's questions ('answer on Tailscale' was declined). itd-2610222029228127 covers the same ground, the person's phone showing what is waiting on them, but its purpose is answering the questions that would stop a session, through a separate web app. The two records give contradictory answers to whether abcd's questions can be answered from the phone, and neither refers to the other.

### 1191. itd-2610222029228127 sends a private shared copy of every checklist through abcdev.app; itd-2610091010348892 rules that abcd never runs a server holding project content

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-2610091010348892-anyone-who-opens-abcdev-app-finds-the.md:70` — “abcd never runs a server that holds or serves project content; anything that needs one is offered only through a partner who runs it.”

itd-2610222029228127 sends each session's full checklist beyond the computer to a private shared copy, giving abcdev.app as the example host. itd-2610091010348892 records the product thinker's ruling that abcd never runs a server that holds or serves project content, and that anything needing one goes through a partner. It also reduces abcdev.app to a community site. Keeping checklists on abcdev.app is the kind of hosting that ruling forbids.

The routing intent never records that exception, so the two disagree on whether the fallback always applies.

### 1195. The dependency graph says severity inheritance decides what to build first, but build next picks readiest first and explicitly not most-important-first

### 1202. The recurrence draft says the ledger folds a match into the closed entry, but the shipped matcher always writes a new record and links it as a duplicate

### 1209. Tier routing sends a row to a provider that can serve its tier, but the shipped adapter rules that no provider serves any tier

### 1210. `status` names the Now/Next/Later record family in the glossary and the people's view of announcements and reservations in the planned verb

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-2609211913453478-one-page-in-the-glossary-maps-abcd-s.md:39` — “intent, spec, step, bundle, issue, release, status (Now / Next / Later)”

It describes the store as a minimal floor: link, status-by-directory, reconcile. As written, that store has none of the three things itd-57 builds on: the dependency edge, the `rm-dep` verb and the skipping selector.

### 1235. Shipped itd-48 says Role 2 findings are only reported and a person acts on them; itd-2609291923559186 adds an automatic mode that fixes mechanical contradictions in the commit

It sets itself apart from the grill, which it says checks criteria only. itd-42 says the grill still questions vague terms and hidden assumptions, on top of its new coherence tier. Both surfaces claim an intent's unstated premises, and itd-55's line between itself and the grill ignores the questioning of hidden assumptions that itd-42 delivered.

itd-44 says the plan path reads `suggested_kind` through `_choose_candidate_kind` and routes only `_PLAN_CANDIDATE_KINDS`. ### 1239. itd-3 explicitly rejects a personal cross-repo ~/.abcd/rules.json; itd-117 ships exactly that user-scope rules file

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-3-modular-rules-loader.md:41` — “explicitly rejected. Keeping a personal cross-repo rules file recreates exactly the”

itd-3 records a global ~/.abcd/rules.json as explicitly rejected and rules the loader per-repo only, because a personal cross-repo rules file recreates the scaffolding-outside-the-repo failure. itd-117 introduces a user-scope rules layer in that same file, injected into every repository abcd manages, and does not record that it reverses itd-3. The two records cannot both describe the loader's layers: one says the user layer is rejected by design, the other says it exists between the bundled defaults and the repo file.

### 1240. itd-39 reuses the rules loader's context brackets from itd-3, but itd-3's loader defines no brackets

itd-39 rules that memory recall shares the rules loader's context brackets (itd-3), with no thresholds tuned separately for memory. itd-3's hook keyword-matches the prompt against each domain's recall list and injects every matching rule; its scope has no gating by remaining context budget and no FRESH, MODERATE or DEPLETED bracket. The dependency points at a mechanism the intent it names never provides, so either itd-39 must build the brackets itself or another record must supply them.

### 1251. itd-187 holds two assemblies byte-identical with only the manifest excluded; itd-2609020625402599 puts a per-run stamp naming the run in every bundle

itd-187 states the amnesia identity relation as byte-equality of the assembled input with the manifest excluded, so one state assembled twice must be byte-identical. itd-2609020625402599 makes every reading assembly carry a per-run stamp naming its kind and its run. Two assemblies are two runs, so their assembled inputs differ in that stamp. The relation itd-187 states fails unless a second exclusion is added, and itd-187 does not name one.

### 1258. itd-50 relies on a drainer that runs queued reviews at a safe boundary; itd-53 ruled out any boundary-hooked autodrain

itd-50 makes the drainer that runs queued reviews at a safe boundary its substrate. itd-53 is that drainer, and its decision 1 replaces the boundary drainer with one bounded command run once by the autonomous run's batch 0, with no boundary-hooked autodrain. As ruled, itd-53 cannot supply what itd-50 says it depends on.

### 1259. itd-53 calls loop-toward-acceptance a facilitator-elected policy riding on its drainer; itd-50 ruled the loop is build's last stage, not a per-intent mode

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-50-loop-toward-acceptance.md:98` — “not a per-intent mode; every intent the run ships goes through it.”

itd-53 defers the facilitator-elected loop-toward-acceptance policy to itd-50 and says it rides on itd-53's drainer. itd-50's decision 1 makes the loop the last stage of `build`, not a per-intent mode, with every intent the run ships going through it. A loop that every shipped intent goes through is not one the facilitator elects per intent, and it does not depend on itd-53's drainer.

### 1260. itd-94 has autonomous drain runs implementing intents; itd-82 defines drain as working issues only and leaves picking intents to `abcd build next`

'Drain' means two different runs, and itd-82's drain never reaches the intent gate that itd-94 credits it with.

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-6-rp-mcp-only-integration.md:54` — “Direct OpenAI / Google / Anthropic API integrations — out of scope; route everything through RP”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-166-each-run-should-record-the-model.md:18` — “A role run through the host, a command-line runner or a provider connection names the model it requested”

itd-6's scope puts direct OpenAI, Google and Anthropic API integrations out of scope, routes everything through RP, and also rules out spawning subprocesses. itd-166 ships receipts for roles run through the host, a command-line runner or a provider connection (opencode, OpenRouter, local servers). Those are the direct routes itd-6 excludes, so the two cannot both describe how abcd routes model calls.

### 1262. The verdict verb is `abcd intent review ingest` in itd-80 and `abcd intent audit` in itd-123

- class: naming conflict · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-607753d8b8340a88 · ledger: iss-2610262045156888 (filed)

itd-80's shipped scope names the verb that ingests a fidelity verdict `abcd intent review ingest`. itd-123 renames it, so that `abcd intent audit` emits the same per-criterion verdicts. One verb has two names, and anyone who types the name itd-80 gives gets a verb that has been renamed.

### 1263. The agent that grades shipped intents is `intent-fidelity-reviewer` in itd-48 and 'the intent auditor' in itd-24

itd-48 names the agent that grades shipped intents, and gains the consistency and kind roles, `intent-fidelity-reviewer`. itd-24 gives the same job, judging delivered reality against each intent's criteria, to the intent auditor. That is two names for one agent definition, so a reader cannot tell which file holds the role.

### 1264. itd-6 still calls the lifeboat verdict pass lifeboat-oracle and re-audit; itd-125 renamed it a review so that one word names it

That keeps the oracle and audit names itd-125 retired.

### 1265. itd-42 defers full-body comparison of intents to itd-39; itd-39 recalls keyword-matched memory pages and compares no intent bodies

- class: sequencing impossibility · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-066f49d040b2cb15 · ledger: iss-2610262045183188 (filed)

Nothing in it loads or compares intent bodies, so the deferral points at an intent that does not cover it.

### 1266. itd-67 picks the release bump by phase-completion detection; itd-24 records that phases are retired and the release is the unit

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-d231d328ae6fadb6 · ledger: iss-2610262045198472 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:47` — “`/abcd:launch ship` auto-selects the bump tier (patch/minor/major) via the brief §4 phase-completion detection”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-24-reflect-command.md:90` — “phases are retired, so `<phase-id>` reads as the release tag”

itd-67's `launch ship` auto-selects the bump tier through the brief §4 phase-completion detection. itd-24 records the ruling (adr-2609212115255771) that phases are retired, with a phase read as a release tag. A bump that depends on detecting phase completion has nothing left to detect.

### 1267. itd-46 says quoted text alone creates a capture; itd-82 requires a remedy field on every new issue

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-4e40104d42a8d32d · ledger: iss-2610262045199145 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:20` — “Quotes mean create. That's the whole rule for both commands.”
- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-82-drain-ledger-triage.md:44` — “and requires it of every new issue (ruling BX3 of 2026-09-29)”

itd-46 makes quoted text the whole create path for capture and intent: quotes mean create, and that is the whole rule for both commands. itd-82 has capture require the remedy field of every new issue (ruling BX3). Quoted text with no remedy can no longer create an issue, so quotes alone are no longer the whole rule for capture.

### 1268. itd-94 has the agent run `abcd intent ready itd-93` with no other argument and read its verdict; itd-179 makes `intent ready` refuse without a grounds argument

- class: premise contradiction · severity: minor · finding_ref: cfk-6f64f4eb9f9cbfe2 · ledger: iss-2610262045201587 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-179-the-reasoning-behind-what-was-pursued-no.md:27` — “A grounds argument on `intent ready` and on the capture triage routes”

itd-94's readiness flow runs `abcd intent ready itd-93` with no other argument and acts on the NOT READY verdict, with exit 1 a journaled SKIP for drains. itd-179 adds a grounds argument on `intent ready` and on the capture triage routes, refused when absent. Under itd-179 the invocation itd-94 describes is refused before any verdict comes back.

### 1269. The lifeboat packer is `disembark pack <repo> <path>` in itd-24 and `disembark <repo> to <dest>` in itd-88

itd-24 has `/abcd:disembark pack <repo> <path>` pack the voyage's retrospectives into the lifeboat. itd-88 names the packer `disembark <repo> to <dest>`. These are two invocation shapes, a `pack` sub-verb against a positional `to`, for one packing command.

### 1270. itd-124 keeps 'audit' for checking a promise and 'lint' for checking form; itd-65 calls its docs-lint row the documentation-auditor

itd-124 rules that a lint checks form with no model and no judgement, and that audit means checking whether we did what we said. itd-65's warn-tier `documentation-auditor` row runs the docs-lint engine, a deterministic form check, under the word itd-124 keeps for checking promises.

### 1271. itd-46 says sub-verbs act on existing records and quoted text creates; itd-2609020625400194 adds a capture sub-verb that creates a new record from quoted text

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-bb69e2f64535cdb4 · ledger: iss-2610262045235833 (filed)
- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-46-abcd-intent-quoted-text-create-symmetric.md:18` — “The three invocation shapes are crisp: bare → status, quoted text → create, sub-verb [+ID] → act on existing.”

itd-46 sets the invocation shapes: bare is status, quoted text creates, and a sub-verb with an id acts on an existing record. itd-2609020625400194's `abcd capture surprise --occasioned-by <id>` with quoted text creates a new surprise record through a sub-verb, and its id names the occasion, not an existing record to act on. `capture admit` likewise mints a new admission record.

### 1272. itd-46 lists `ship` and `review` among the intent sub-verbs; itd-121 says shipping an intent is a spec verb

- class: premise contradiction · severity: nitpick · finding_ref: cfk-cf95f9604a55271d · ledger: iss-2610262045246595 (filed)

- end B: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-121-type-the-id-get-your-next-move-abcd-id.md:21` — “every record names its own next verb, and nobody needs to know that shipping an”

itd-46 says `ship` and `review` remain intent sub-verbs that take the intent's id, and calls that shape already correct. itd-121 says nobody needs to know that shipping an intent is a `spec` verb (`abcd spec close`), and itd-123 has since renamed the per-intent review to audit. An intent `ship` sub-verb and shipping only through `spec close` cannot both hold.

### 1273. itd-3 has ahoy own a CLAUDE.md marker block; itd-2610030814013772 rules that projects carry no CLAUDE.md at all

### 1274. itd-3 rejects a user-level rules.json outright; itd-2610030720038073 records that every managed project's block names the home's top-level rules.json

itd-3 lists a global ~/.abcd/rules.json as explicitly rejected and the override as per-repo only. itd-2610030720038073, answering from the code, says each managed project's block names the home's top-level rules.json, which is that same personal cross-repo layer. ### 1278. itd-40 names ~/.abcd/history/index.json as the sole user-scope registry; itd-2610030720038073 renames the home to ~/.abcd.noindex

### 1279. itd-2609231434459890 keeps the load-check limits in a settings file under ~/.abcd/; itd-2610030720038073 renames that home

### 1281. itd-34 says shape classification runs continuously in the pre-commit hook; itd-48 defers continuous pre-commit shape scanning

### 1287. itd-67 picks the bump tier by phase-completion detection and keeps the version in plugin.json; itd-73 derives it from shipped intents' impact on an unversioned tree

### 1288. itd-67 makes the changelog the reroute target for itd-65's doc-history gate; itd-65 supersedes the reroute whole

- end A: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/itd-67-installable-versioned-plugin.md:48` — “change-narration that gate strips from a doc body is appended here”

itd-67 says change-narration the doc-history gate strips from a doc body is appended to the changelog. itd-65 records that the reroute criterion is superseded whole, because a gate cannot append prose to a changelog nothing hand-writes and the change reaches the changelog through its record. The appending path itd-67 relies on does not exist under itd-65.

itd-2609231013154443 leaves intents with impact: internal out of the release page. itd-73 defines the impact classification on every intent as exactly additive, breaking or fix, and derives the version from those three. ### 1292. itd-2609212103565953 starts each step's lane only after the previous has merged; itd-2609201925079472 runs independent steps' lanes side by side

itd-2609212103565953 says the build runs one lane per step in order and the next step's lane starts after the previous has merged. itd-2609201925079472 rules that a run works in parallel up to its ceiling, with the lanes of steps that do not need each other running side by side and a step's needs opted out per step. The step loop's ordering rule differs between the two shipped records.
